title: fix(mesh): decode NodeInfo and MeshPacket with the official field numbers (#238)
body:
Closes #238.

### What was wrong

In Mesh > BLE, nodes that came from the radio's node database showed `20731d ago` and an SNR such as `114710017334578600000000000.0`, and had no position or battery until a fresh packet arrived. `parseNodeInfo` did not use the field numbers in mesh.proto, and the MeshPacket metadata was off by one in the same way. The unit tests built frames with the same wrong numbers, so they passed. The full field list is in #238.

### What changed

- `parseNodeInfo` uses the official layout: num=1, user=2, position=3, snr=4 (float), last_heard=5 (fixed32), device_metrics=6, hops_away=9. Fields 7, 8, 10 and 11 (channel, via_mqtt, is_favorite, is_ignored) are skipped by wire type. The alternates it carried are removed: user at 4, position at 5, snr at 7, num as fixed32, last_heard as a varint. I scanned every revision of mesh.proto in the protobufs history. Of those alternates only snr at 7 ever existed in a real revision: 1.x firmware, until 2022-03-20, where last_heard was field 4. That layout uses field 4 for a different value, so it cannot be decoded next to the current one, and the app talks to 2.x firmware.
- `parseMeshPacket` reads rx_time=7, rx_snr=8, hop_limit=9 and rx_rssi=12. It used to read rx_time from 8, rx_snr from 9 and hop_limit from 10, so a live position packet stamped "last heard" with the bits of a float. The field 16 branch (an sint32 RSSI) is removed, because field 16 is `public_key`.
- "Last heard unknown" is a real state. `MeshNode.lastHeardEpoch` is `Long?`, and a missing or zero `last_heard` stays null instead of becoming the parse time. The node list, topology list and detail sheet show a dash (`relativeTime` and `formatLastHeard` already treated 0 that way, and now take null). The CoT converters leave `<last_heard>` out. `upsertNode` keeps a known value when a later NodeInfo has none. A live position packet with no rx_time is stamped with the phone's clock.
- Node-database positions are now read, so the contact built from a node carries `last_heard` as `receivedAtMs` (capped at now). Without it, a position last heard days ago would show as "just now" on the map. This goes beyond the field-number fix. It is one line in `MeshtasticCoTConverter` plus its tests, and easy to drop.
- `DeviceMetrics.battery_level` above 100 means external power (telemetry.proto), so it is shown as "powered" instead of "101%". Battery was never decoded from NodeInfo before, so this would have appeared as soon as the number was fixed.
- `MeshtasticManager.dispatchFrame` is `internal` so tests can feed it FromRadio frames.

### Audit against the official protos

Field numbers and wire types, one message at a time.

| Message | Matched | Did not match | Changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| FromRadio | id=1, packet=2, my_info=3, node_info=4, config=5, config_complete_id=7, channel=10 | none | none |
| MyNodeInfo | my_node_num=1 | none | none |
| NodeInfo | num=1, user=2 | position, snr, last_heard, device_metrics and hops_away were read from other numbers or not at all | rewritten to the official numbers |
| MeshPacket, decode | from, to, channel, decoded | rx_time, rx_snr and hop_limit one number off, field 16 read as RSSI | fixed |
| MeshPacket, encode | to, channel, decoded, id, hop_limit, want_ack | none | none |
| Data | decode portnum, payload. encode portnum, payload | encode writes want_response to 5 (it is 3) | not here, see #240 |
| Position, User, DeviceMetrics | latitude_i, longitude_i, altitude. long_name, short_name, role, and id, is_licensed in set_owner. battery_level | DeviceMetrics was never reached, NodeInfo expected it at 10 | reached through field 6, above 100 shown as "powered" |
| Config, Channel, ChannelSettings, ChannelSet | device=1, position=2, lora=6 and the fields used inside them (role, rebroadcast_mode, position_broadcast_secs, use_preset, modem_preset, region). Channel index, settings, role. ChannelSettings psk, name, uplink, downlink. ChannelSet settings=1 | none | none |
| AdminMessage, ToRadio | get_channel_request=1, get_owner_request=3, get_config_request=5, responses 2, 4, 6, set_owner=32, set_channel=33, set_config=34. ToRadio packet=1, want_config_id=3. TCP frame 0x94 0xC3 plus length | none | none |
| TAKPacket (port 72) | TAKPacket, Contact, Group, Status, PLI and GeoChat as used | none | none |
| TAKPacketV2 (port 78) | callsign=3, latitude_i=6, longitude_i=7, altitude=8 (sint32), uid=14, stale_seconds=16, cot_type_str=23, remarks=24, marker=35, and Marker kind, color_argb, readiness, iconset | none | none |
| TAKMessage (port 72 fallback, shared with the iOS app) | the CotEvent numbers | the Detail numbers differ from the TAK protocol's detail.proto (contact=2, group=3, precisionLocation=4, status=5, takv=6, and Contact endpoint=1, callsign=2) | none, see below |

Enum values used by the app were compared as well: Role, ModemPreset, RegionCode (0 to 26), RebroadcastMode, Channel.Role, Team, MemberRole, Marker.Kind and the portnums 72 and 78.

### How it was checked

Unit tests only. This change has not been run against a radio.

- The unit suite went from 855 tests to 899, with no failures (9 skipped, as before).
- The two NodeInfo tests that encoded the old layout now use the official numbers. The new tests build frames from the official numbers with a small writer (`ProtoMsg`), one case per field: snr from 4, last_heard from 5, position from 3, battery from device_metrics 6, hops_away from 9, and that channel, via_mqtt, is_favorite and is_ignored are not mistaken for anything. Others cover the MeshPacket fields, an unknown last heard in the node table, the CoT converter, and the path from a FromRadio frame to the node list.
- 27 of the new and corrected decoding tests fail against the old parser.
- The numbers were compared with mesh.proto, telemetry.proto, config.proto, channel.proto, admin.proto, apponly.proto, atak.proto and portnums.proto at v2.7.26 (the firmware on the radio where this showed up) and at the current head. The audited messages have the same numbers in both; the newer revision only adds fields.

### To check on a radio

- Connect over BLE and open Mesh > BLE. Nodes from the node database should show a real age (or a dash if the radio never heard them), an SNR in dB, hop counts, battery, and a position when the node has one. There should be no five-digit "Nd ago".
- A node on USB power without a battery should read "powered".
- With auto-publish to TAK on, node-database nodes with a position should appear on the map, and the age label should show when they were last heard.

### Not changed

- `Data.want_response` is written to the wrong field, which is why device settings writes probably never reach the radio. The one-line fix is not in this PR on purpose: on its own it would let partial configs through. Details and the plan are in #240.
- The TAKMessage Detail numbering above. It is shared byte for byte with the iOS app, so it needs a decision on both sides.
- The iOS client appears to use the same NodeInfo layout. I only read it.
- MeshCore nodes still default last heard to the advert time or now. That is a different protocol and was left alone.
- `Position.time` is the position's own timestamp and is not read. The contact age uses `last_heard`, which can be newer than the position it labels.

title: fix(mesh): make the Meshtastic BLE link recover after a drop (#203)
body:
The Meshtastic BLE link not coming back after a drop (#203, phase B). Phase A (#218) added the diagnostics; this is the fix, worked out on a bench with a Heltec V3 (firmware 2.7.26) and a Pixel 6a (Android 17). Four separate causes turned up, each reproduced on that hardware.

**1. The reconnect loop could stop making attempts.** The client kept one Nordic `BleManager` for its whole life and reset it with `close()` between attempts. `close()` does not reset the library's "operation in progress" flag (the line is commented out in `BleManagerHandler.close()`), so when it is called while a request is in flight, every later `connect()` is queued behind a request that never finishes. That is what happened after a connect that timed out with the GATT link already up: Nordic had issued `gatt.disconnect()` and was waiting for the callback, and our failure path closed the manager first. From then on the log shows `BLE auto-reconnect: retrying ... (attempt N)` every 40 s with no `connectGatt` in between, until the app is force-stopped. The trigger on the bench was a stale pairing (phone still bonded, radio no longer has the keys: `encryptionChangeCallback: status=6`, bond state BONDING), which is also what a firmware update that clears the radio's bond store leaves behind.

Now every connect attempt gets its own `BleManager` (`Link`), and a link is never reused once it has failed or dropped. Callbacks from a link that is no longer the current one are ignored, and the current link and the connection state change under one lock.

**2. A wait on a request could hang forever.** Nordic clears its queue without calling done or fail on the requests in it when a link goes down, drops the request in flight when a pairing fails, and after a read times out it keeps that read in flight and runs nothing queued behind it. The auto-reconnect loop awaits the handshake write inline after each connect, so one write lost that way would end reconnecting for good. Every wait on a request now ends when the link ends (`BleLinkAwaits`) and has a deadline of its own. A read or write that gets no answer of any kind ends the session, so the loop starts a new one instead of sitting on Connected with a blocked queue. The loop also caps one attempt, as a second line of defence.

**3. Android answered from a stale service cache.** For a bonded radio without robust caching Android keeps the service table on disk and skips discovery on later connects (`Using cached database without robust caching`, `Service discovery is skipped`). The bench board had run MeshCore before: the phone kept returning three cached services, none of them Meshtastic, and every attempt ended in `Device is not supported`. A firmware update that changes the GATT table would leave the same kind of stale copy. The first service list on a link is no longer trusted: a cache refresh is queued as the first init request, Nordic discovers again, and only that result decides. If the refresh cannot run, init continues with the first list.

**4. RSSI reads were stalling everything else.** The poll loop asked for RSSI every second on the same request queue as the reads and writes. After an RSSI read was issued on a link that was going down, the phone answered none of the RSSI reads in the next session until Bluetooth was restarted, and Nordic waits a full second for each unanswered one. So after a reconnect there was a one second stall in front of every frame. RSSI is now sampled every 10 s, right after a read that came back empty, one request at a time, and not again on that link once a read goes unanswered.

Also in here:

- **`fromNum` had the wrong UUID** (`...aa7547de15e6`; the firmware's `src/BluetoothCommon.h` says `...aa7547e34453`). The characteristic was never found, so its notifications were never enabled and the link ran on the once-a-second poll alone. The unit test asserted the same typo. iOS has the same value and gets its own PR.
- **The BLE log no longer contains radio traffic.** Nordic prints every value it reads and writes in hex. Those are FromRadio and ToRadio frames (channel keys, positions, messages), and the log is what "Copy diagnostics" puts on the clipboard for a bug report. Each value is now reduced to its size, in Logcat and in the copied text. 0.44.0 has the unredacted form; the how-to on #203 has been edited to say so.
- Deadlines count idle time rather than time since the start, and a pairing does not count against them, so entering the PIN is not cut off and neither is the setup that follows it. One pairing may take 60 s.
- Nordic's own connect retry is gone: its timer cannot be cancelled and could open a GATT client on a link that was already retired. The manager retries a connect that failed on a stack error before the link was up (status 133 and its relatives), twice, 300 ms apart.
- The handshake (want_config) is written by the connect itself, on the link that attempt brought up, and a session it could not be delivered on is dropped instead of kept.
- A pairing that fails on a session ends the session (Nordic drops the request in flight at that point without a callback), and so do services that are invalidated under a live session. The reconnect loop then starts a new one.
- Deadlines run on `uptimeMillis`, like the delays behind them, so a wait is not charged for time the phone was asleep. Each step a connect gets through (link up, a service discovery, the cache refresh) starts its limit again.
- The failure row carries a hint when the client knows what to do (radio not answering, pairing waiting, Bluetooth off, not a Meshtastic device). Android raises a pairing request triggered by an app as a notification, not a dialog, so the pairing hint says where to look.
- The last failure stays visible after the link recovers; its relative time says how old it is. A streak of identical failures restarts after a session. Drops that Android ends itself, and Bluetooth being switched off, are recorded now.
- The scan list uses the name the radio advertises now, not the one Android remembers for the address (the board showed up as `MeshCore-...` on main).
- The "Reconnecting, attempt n" row only shows while it is retrying. It used to read "attempt 0" on a link that was up.
- Each BLE log line carries its attempt number (`#3 Connected to ...`).
- The BLE pane starts the connect on the manager's scope, so leaving the pane does not cancel it.

**Checked on the bench (Pixel 6a, Android 17; Heltec V3, firmware 2.7.26).** The table and the first list were run on builds of the first commit on this branch (8cd83d6) and of the working states that led up to it; the reboot run was on exactly that commit. title: fix(service): connection service survives Android's limits and a server that drops on accept (#223, #229)
body:
Closes #223, closes #229

Three crashes in the foreground service that holds the server and mesh links open in the background. All three were reproduced on an Android 16 emulator before the change and are gone after it.

**Root cause.**

- **#223, the two Play vitals crashes.** The service ran as `dataSync|location`. Android 15 gives `dataSync` six hours of background time a day and then calls `onTimeout()`. The service did not implement it, so the process was killed with `ForegroundServiceDidNotStopInTimeException`, and the `START_STICKY` restart then died in `onStartCommand` with `ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException` ("Time limit already exhausted"). The limit applies even though the service also holds the `location` type.
- **#229.** `OmniTAKApp` starts the service 750 ms after a link reports Connected and calls `stopService()` when every link is Disconnected. A server that accepts the connection and drops it around that moment makes the stop land between `startForegroundService()` and the service's `startForeground()`, which is fatal (`ForegroundServiceDidNotStartInTimeException`).

**Fix.**

- The service runs as `location` alone when location is granted. That type has no time limit and is what keeps GPS flowing with the screen off. `dataSync` stays as the fallback: for a user who denied location, and for a start from the background, where the location type is refused. The manifest still declares both types.
- `onTimeout()` stops the service and posts a one-off notice, "OmniTAK paused in the background".
- A refused foreground start stops the service quietly instead of crashing, in `onStartCommand` and at the `startForegroundService()` call.
- `MainActivity.onResume` asks the app to start the service again when a link is up. That is the one moment a start is always allowed, and it also moves the service to the `location` type right after that permission is granted.
- `StartStopGate` parks a stop that arrives while a start is in flight; `onStartCommand` carries it out after it has entered the foreground. Starts are counted, and a start that is never delivered stops blocking after 10 seconds.

**Reproduction and check (emulator, Android 16, debug builds).** The limit was shortened with `adb shell device_config put activity_manager data_sync_fgs_timeout_duration 30000` and the app connected to a plain TCP stand-in server.

| Case | main (0.44.0) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Location granted, app in the background past the limit | service `types=0x9`; crash at about 33 s, second crash on the sticky restart | service `types=0x8`; still in the foreground at 70 s, no crash |
| Location denied, app in the background past the limit | same two crashes | `onTimeout` logged, service stopped, notice posted, process alive; service back (`types=0x1`) and notice cleared on return to the foreground |
| Server drops each connection 0.85 s after accept, 4 launches | 4 of 4 crash | 0 of 4 crash; the service enters the foreground and stops |

**Tests.** `TAKConnectionServiceTypesTest` (4): the type candidates, including that `dataSync` is never combined with another type. `StartStopGateTest` (8): parked stop, a newer start cancelling it, two starts in flight, refused start, the delivery window, a system restart with nothing issued.

`./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest` passes: 867 tests, 0 failures, 9 skipped (the skips already exist on main).

**Verification still needed.**

- A real device over a real six hours has not been run; the emulator check shortens the limit instead.
- One path was not exercised: `startForegroundService()` allowed from the background (battery optimisation off) and then every type refused. By AOSP's ordering the obligation to call `startForeground()` is cleared when the call is made, before it can throw, so stopping afterwards is safe. The app did not reconnect in the background on the emulator, so the case never arose.
- Play Console: the foreground service declaration already covers `location` and `dataSync`, and both stay in the manifest, so nothing should need changing there. Worth a look at the declaration before the release.
- With "Report my position" off (#227) and location granted, the service still claims the `location` type. That is a product decision for when #227 lands.

title: fix(position): hold PPLI until a live fix replaces the restored one (#205)
body:
Closes #205

**Root cause.** Three things, all in how the position the app sends is chosen.

1. The position restored from the last session was an ordinary `SelfFix`. `SelfFixPersistence.restoredFixOrNull` rebuilt it, `LocationProvider.seedFromPersisted` put it into the same `fix` flow as live GPS, and the only thing marking it as restored was NaN accuracy and zero speed, which a live fix without accuracy also has. `SelfPositionBroadcaster` sends `manualFixProvider() ?: locationFix.value`, so as soon as any server, Meshtastic or MeshCore link came up (the first send is immediate) the old position went out as PPLI. On the wire `time` and `stale` are always "now" and `how` is `m-g`, so receivers saw a stale position as a fresh one. Sends are timer driven (every 30 s), so the first live fix could then wait up to 30 s, and in that time other operators saw the old position, stamped as fresh, before the live one replaced it.
2. A second leak path: when the in-memory fix was still null, the broadcaster fell back to the persisted `selfLat`/`selfLon` prefs and sent those the same way.
3. `UserPrefsStore.ensureSelfUid()` read the uid outside the DataStore edit. Two first-run callers (the broadcaster when a link connects, the chat screen, a marker drop, mission sync) could each read blank, each mint an `ANDROID-<uuid>`, and each return its own while only the last writer's uid stayed on disk. I confirmed the uid does persist on first run (the issue's last bullet); the race is the only gap there.

**Fix.**
- `SelfFix` gets `restored: Boolean = false`. Only `restoredFixOrNull` (the seed path) sets it.
- `SelfFixPersistence.newerOf` now also decides by provenance: a live fix always replaces a restored one and a restored seed never displaces a live one, whatever the timestamps say. Without this a seed stamped in the future (device clock moved back) would pin itself as the current fix and PPLI would stay held while live GPS kept arriving.
- `LocationProvider.offerFix` now merges with `update {}`. The seed is offered from `appScope` (Default dispatcher) while GPS callbacks land on the main looper, so the old read-then-write could let the seed overwrite a live fix that arrived in between.
- `SelfPositionBroadcaster.broadcastOnce` skips the tick (server and mesh) while the only fix is a restored one, and logs that once per held episode. The prefs fallback is deleted, so persisted `selfLat`/`selfLon` are now only the store the map's restored seed is rebuilt from. A manual position (`manualFixProvider`) is the operator's deliberate choice and is never held.
- After a held or fix-less tick the loop now waits for a live fix instead of sleeping the whole interval, so the first real position goes out immediately and the 30 s cadence restarts from that send. The wait is still bounded by the interval, so a manual drop or a changed pref is picked up on the normal tick. This covers the "no persisted fix at all" first-run case too.
- `UserPrefsStore.ensureSelfUid()` now reads and writes inside a single DataStore edit (with a plain read fast path once a uid exists). `UserPrefsStore` gains an `internal` constructor taking a `DataStore<Preferences>` so the store can be tested on the JVM; `UserPrefsStore(context)` is unchanged for callers.

Behaviour change to be aware of: with no GPS at all (permission denied, indoors) nothing is sent until there is a live fix or a manual position. The restored position is still drawn on the map (dimmed when stale), it just is not transmitted.

Out of scope, possible second cause of duplicate markers: on other phones the operator's own radio is ingested as a separate `MESHTASTIC-<hex>` contact unless it runs the TAK role (`MeshNode.isTakPaired`, used in `MapScreen.kt` for the paired-radio filter). That is independent of this change.

Also not changed, found while tracing who reads the fix: `MultiUasRegistry` is built with `operatorFix = { locationProvider.fix.value }` (`OmniTAKApp.kt`), and UAS follow-me (`UASManager.startFollowMe`) steers the drone to whatever that returns. A restored fix now counts as "a fix" there. `SelfFix.restored` makes it easy to gate (`takeUnless { it.restored }`), but that is a drone-behaviour change I did not want to fold into a PPLI fix; flagging it for a decision.

**Tests.**
- `SelfPositionBroadcasterFixSourcingTest`: `broadcasts_persisted_position_when_fix_null` asserted the behaviour being removed, so it is inverted (`never_broadcasts_persisted_prefs_position_when_fix_null`); new `holds_restored_fix_until_live` (server and mesh), `sends_immediately_on_first_live_fix` (virtual time: held at start, still held at +10 s, live fix sends with no time passing, next send 30 s after it), `sends_immediately_when_first_fix_ever_arrives`.
- `SelfPositionBroadcasterManualFixTest`: `manual_position_still_broadcasts_while_gps_fix_is_only_restored`.
- `SelfFixPersistenceTest`: flag round trip (`restore_flags_the_fix_as_restored`, `live_fix_is_not_flagged_restored`, `persist_then_restore_round_trips_through_the_flag`) and the provenance rule (4 tests, including the clock-skew cases).
- `UserPrefsStoreSelfUidTest` (new, real file-backed DataStore): mint once and persist, later calls return the same uid, an existing uid is never replaced, eight concurrent first-run callers all return the persisted uid, other prefs untouched. I ran the new tests against the old code first: the four new broadcaster tests (hold, both immediate-send cases, manual-while-restored), the inverted prefs-fallback test and the concurrent uid test all failed there. The flag and provenance tests in `SelfFixPersistenceTest` and the other four uid tests were green in that run, because the data-model change was already in place when I ran it.

`./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest --max-workers=2 -Dorg.gradle.jvmargs="-Xmx2560m -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8" -Dkotlin.daemon.jvm.options=-Xmx1536m`: 871 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors (9 skipped, the same ones as on main: `GeoTIFFParserTest`, `DeepLinkEnrollTest`).

**Verification still needed.** I did not run this on a device or emulator; the checks below are for the maintainer.
- Restart case: get a GPS fix, force-stop the app, relaunch somewhere with no GPS and connect to a server. Logcat tag `SelfPositionBroadcaster` should show "PPLI held" once and no PPLI at the server; the map still shows the dimmed restored puck. Get a fix: PPLI should go out within a couple of seconds of the first live fix, not up to 30 s later, and the position on a second device should replace the old one rather than sit next to it.
- Same with a Meshtastic radio and no server (mesh PPLI path).
- Manual position: with only a restored fix, drop a manual position from the self marker sheet. It should still broadcast; "resume GPS" should go back to holding.
- First run on a fresh install: open Chat while connecting a server and compare the uid in the logcat line "Starting PPLI broadcast" with the sender uid of the first chat message.
- Known gap, not changed here (from reading the code, not observed): only `MapScreen` calls `LocationProvider.start()`. After a service-only restart (the foreground service restarts the process, no UI) nothing requests live GPS, so PPLI now stays held until the app is opened. Before this change it would have sent the restored position instead. If that case matters, starting location from `startAppBroadcaster` is the follow-up.

title: fix(onboarding): keep Skip and the bottom button clear of the system bars (#221)
body:
Closes #221

**Root cause.** `OnboardingFlow` is rendered straight from `MainActivity`'s `Surface`, outside `AppNav`'s Scaffold, and `MainActivity` calls `enableEdgeToEdge`. Nothing on that path consumes the system-bar insets, so the root `Box` was laid out under the status bar and the navigation bar. Skip (`Alignment.TopEnd`, `padding(top = 16.dp, end = 8.dp)`) landed inside the status bar, where on the Pixel Fold from the report it did not take taps. The bottom controls (`padding(bottom = 48.dp)`) had a fixed 48 dp of clearance that knows nothing about the real navigation bar or taskbar height.

**Fix.** The root `Box` keeps `fillMaxSize()` and the dark `background`, then applies `windowInsetsPadding(WindowInsets.safeDrawing)` after the background in the modifier chain. The fill still runs edge to edge behind the bars; only the content is inset. Skip now sits below the status bar or cutout, and Continue / Back sit above the navigation bar or taskbar. The existing fixed paddings are unchanged, so everything moves by the inset sizes and nothing else.

`safeDrawing` rather than `statusBarsPadding()` + `navigationBarsPadding()` (what #89 used for the map chrome) so a side display cutout in landscape is covered as well. It is the same mechanism and the same outcome on a portrait phone.

**Tests.** None added. This is a layout-only change with no logic to unit test, and the project has no Robolectric or Compose UI test setup, so a test here would assert nothing real. Existing suite, run once before pushing:

`./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest --max-workers=2 -Dorg.gradle.jvmargs="-Xmx2560m -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8" -Dkotlin.daemon.jvm.options=-Xmx1536m`

Result: 855 tests, 0 failures, 9 skipped (the skips are pre-existing, in `DeepLinkEnrollTest` and `GeoTIFFParserTest`).

The first run of the suite had one failure that is unrelated to this change: `RegionDownloaderTest.downloads_every_tile_in_region_and_writes_to_cache` (`expected:<7> but was:<5>`). That test's `CountingSink` is a plain `HashMap` written from `Dispatchers.IO` threads, so it can lose writes when the machine is starved of CPU (this one was). It passed on the immediate rerun of the whole suite.

**Verification still needed.** I did not run the app, so none of the on-screen behaviour is observed. On a device with edge-to-edge enforced (the Pixel Fold outer display from the report, Android 17), from a fresh install or after clearing app data so onboarding shows:

- Skip is fully below the status bar on every page and a tap on it opens the map. A `uiautomator dump` should now put the Skip bounds below the status bar's bottom edge (about 132 px on the outer display; the report had it at y 77..135 px).
- Continue / Get Started and Back clear the navigation bar in gesture navigation and in 3-button navigation.
- On the Pixel Fold inner display (taskbar visible) the bottom button and Back are not under the taskbar.
- Landscape: nothing sits under a side cutout or the navigation bar. The page content block still has its fixed 80 dp top / 220 dp bottom paddings, which I did not change, so check that the content still fits.

title: fix: prevent keyboard focus trap in SyntaxHighlightedTextEditor (#511)
body:
## Overview

Fixes #511.

Addresses WCAG 2.1.2 ("No Keyboard Trap") and aligns with official Android Developer and Desktop interaction guidance by providing keyboard escape and focus traversal mechanisms for `SyntaxHighlightedTextEditor`.

## Changes

1. **Escape Key Handling (`Key.Escape`):**
   - Intercepts hardware `Key.Escape` in `previewKeyModifier` to clear focus via `FocusManager.clearFocus()` when enabled.
   - Added `escapeKeyClearsFocus: Boolean = SyntaxHighlightedTextEditorDefaults.ESCAPE_KEY_CLEARS_FOCUS` parameter to `SyntaxHighlightedTextEditor`.
   - Added `SyntaxHighlightedTextEditorDefaults.ESCAPE_KEY_CLEARS_FOCUS = true`.
2. **Reverse Focus Traversal (`Shift+Tab`):**
   - Intercepts `Key.Tab` when `isShiftPressed` is true and moves focus backwards via `focusManager.moveFocus(FocusDirection.Previous)` instead of inserting spaces.
3. **Forward Focus Traversal (`Ctrl+Tab`):**
   - Intercepts `Key.Tab` when `isCtrlPressed` is true and advances focus via `focusManager.moveFocus(FocusDirection.Next)` even when Tab indentation interception is enabled.
4. **Unintercepted Tab Pass-through:**
   - When `tabKeyInterceptionEnabled = false`, plain `Tab` passes through to allow normal focus traversal.
5. **KDoc & Official Documentation Links:**
   - Linked to Android official documentation:
     - [Keyboard Navigation](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/touch-and-input/keyboard-input/navigation)
     - [Desktop Keyboard Interaction](https://developer.android.com/design/ui/desktop/guides/interaction/keyboard)
     - [Compose Focus Behavior](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/touch-input/focus/change-focus-behavior)
6. **Sample App:**
   - Added an "Escape clears focus" toggle chip to `LiveEditorSection` to test and demonstrate the behavior interactively.
7. **Testing:**
   - Added JVM unit tests in `SyntaxHighlightedTextEditorDefaultsTest`.
   - Added Robolectric tests in `SyntaxHighlightedTextEditorRobolectricTest` verifying `Escape`, `Shift+Tab`, and `Ctrl+Tab` handling.
   - Added connected Android test in `SyntaxHighlightedTextEditorTest` run on the live emulator verifying hardware Escape key clears focus.
   - Updated public API baseline with `./gradlew apiDump`.
   - Updated `CHANGELOG.md` under `[Unreleased]` -> `### Fixed`.

## Verification

- `./gradlew formatKotlin lintKotlin apiCheck` - PASSED
- `./gradlew :compose-highlight:assembleDebug :sample:assembleDebug :compose-highlight:test` - PASSED
- `./gradlew :compose-highlight:connectedAndroidTest -P android.testInstrumentationRunnerArguments.class=dev.hossain.highlight.ui.SyntaxHighlightedTextEditorTest` on `Pixel_10_Pro_XL(AVD)` - PASSED

title: fix: harden hidden WebView settings and origin restrictions
body:
## Summary

Hardens the hidden, offscreen `WebView` instance managed by `WebViewManager` in accordance with official Android security recommendations and best practices (#497).

## Changes

1. **Disable unused file and content access:**
   - Set `settings.allowFileAccess = false` and `settings.allowContentAccess = false`.
   - Local assets are served over HTTPS via `WebViewAssetLoader`, so filesystem (`file://`) and ContentProvider (`content://`) access are unneeded and disabled to prevent unsafe file exposure.
   - Reference: [Android Developers - Webview unsafe file inclusion](https://developer.android.com/privacy-and-security/risks/webview-unsafe-file-inclusion)
2. **Block outbound network loads:**
   - Set `settings.blockNetworkLoads = true`.
   - Prevents any outbound network calls from the WebView, ensuring it strictly processes bundled local assets.
   - Reference: [WebSettings.setBlockNetworkLoads](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/webkit/WebSettings#setBlockNetworkLoads(boolean))
3. **Disable Safe Browsing overhead on trusted internal WebView:**
   - Set `settings.safeBrowsingEnabled = false` on API 26+ (`Build.VERSION_CODES.O`).
   - For an offscreen WebView serving bundled local assets only, Safe Browsing adds unnecessary initialization delay and telemetry overhead.
   - Reference: [WebSettings.setSafeBrowsingEnabled](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/webkit/WebSettings#setSafeBrowsingEnabled(boolean))
4. **Prevent unexpected navigation:**
   - Implemented `WebViewClient.shouldOverrideUrlLoading` returning `true` to abort any navigation away from the bundled `bridge.html`.
   - Reference: [WebViewClient.shouldOverrideUrlLoading](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/webkit/WebViewClient#shouldOverrideUrlLoading(android.webkit.WebView,%20android.webkit.WebResourceRequest))
5. **Origin restriction in request interception:**
   - In `WebViewClient.shouldInterceptRequest`, verify `request.url.scheme == "https" && request.url.host == "appassets.androidplatform.net"`. Return an HTTP 403 Forbidden `WebResourceResponse` for any other scheme or origin.
   - Reference: [WebViewAssetLoader](https://developer.android.com/reference/androidx/webkit/WebViewAssetLoader)
6. **Strict Content Security Policy in `bridge.html`:**
   - Added `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline';">`.
7. **Documentation and Tests:**
   - Added KDoc references and links to official Android documentation in `WebViewManager.kt`.
   - Added `WebViewManagerSecurityTest.kt` verifying hardened `WebSettings`, navigation blocking, origin validation, and 403 Forbidden responses.

Closes #497

title: fix: prevent horizontal scroll reset on state restoration in code composables
body:
Resolves #509

### Summary

In `SyntaxHighlightedCode` and `StreamingSyntaxHighlightedCode`, horizontal scroll position unexpectedly reset to 0 whenever the composables recomposed following state restoration (such as screen rotation/configuration change) or viewport re-entry in a `LazyColumn`.

### Root Cause

- In `SyntaxHighlightedCode`: `LaunchedEffect(code) { scrollState.scrollTo(0) }` executed unconditionally on initial composition and following state restoration, discarding the restored scroll offset from `rememberScrollState()`.
- In `StreamingSyntaxHighlightedCode`: `previousCode` was tracked with plain `remember { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }`. Following configuration change, `previousCode` reset to `null`, causing `isAppend` to evaluate as `false` and triggering `scrollState.scrollTo(0)`.

### Solution

1. In `SyntaxHighlightedCode`: Track `previousCode` using `rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(code) }` and only trigger `scrollState.scrollTo(0)` when `code != previousCode`.
2. In `StreamingSyntaxHighlightedCode`: Track `previousCode` and `previousLanguage` using `rememberSaveable`. Initial composition and state restoration preserve the restored scroll position, while code stream changes reset scroll to 0 as intended.
3. Added Robolectric unit tests using `StateRestorationTester` for both composables verifying that:
   - Horizontal scroll offset survives `emulateSavedInstanceStateRestore()`.
   - Horizontal scroll offset resets to 0 when code content changes.
   - Streaming token appends do not reset scroll offset.

### Verification

- `./gradlew formatKotlin` passed.
- `./gradlew lintKotlin` passed with 0 violations.
- `./gradlew apiCheck` passed with binary compatibility verified.
- `./gradlew :compose-highlight:test` passed all JVM unit tests.
- `./gradlew :compose-highlight:assembleDebug :sample:assembleDebug` compiled successfully.
- `npx markdownlint-cli CHANGELOG.md` passed with 0 errors.

title: fix: guard against silent highlightAuto fallback on unknown or blank languages
body:
## Summary

Guards against silent `highlightAuto` fallback in `bridge.html` when an unknown, empty, or misspelled language string is passed to `HighlightEngine.highlight()` or `highlightToHtml()`.

Resolves #508.

## Background & Fix Details

- **Prior behavior:** `highlightCode()` in `bridge.html` set `block.className = lang` and invoked `hljs.highlightElement(block)`. If `lang` was unknown (such as typo `"kotlinn"` or empty `""`), Highlight.js treated the element as having no language class and silently triggered `highlightAuto()` across all 190+ bundled grammars.
  - This incurred a **56x slowdown** (measured: 254 ms vs 4.5 ms on a 160-line Kotlin sample).
  - Held the engine `Mutex` during auto-detection, stalling all concurrent UI code blocks.
  - Contradicted the documented contract that `spanCount == 0` indicates an unsupported language.
- **Fix:**
  - Validates `lang` via `hljs.getLanguage(lang)`.
  - When unrecognized or blank, immediately returns escaped plain text (`{ error: false, html: escapeHtml(code), unsupported: true }`) without running `highlightAuto`.
  - Delegates directly to `hljs.highlight(text, { language: lang, ignoreIllegals: true }).value`, eliminating DOM textContent/innerHTML round-trip overhead.
  - Callers desiring automatic language detection continue to use `HighlightEngine.highlightAuto()`.

## Tests & Verification

- **Bridge validation:** Updated `scripts/validate-bridge.sh` and added automated semantic Node.js contract checks verifying valid language, alias resolution, unknown language escaping, and blank language guards.
- **Unit & Android tests:**
  - Added Robolectric test in `HighlightEngineRobolectricTest` asserting unsupported language returns `spanCount == 0`.
  - Updated `HighlightEngineTest` asserting unknown and blank languages return unhighlighted text with `spanCount == 0` and zero `hljs-` spans.
- **Full verification passed:**
  - `./gradlew formatKotlin`
  - `./gradlew lintKotlin`
  - `./gradlew apiCheck`
  - `./gradlew :compose-highlight:assembleDebug :sample:assembleDebug`
  - `./gradlew :compose-highlight:test`
  - `./scripts/validate-bridge.sh`
  - `npx markdownlint-cli CHANGELOG.md`

title: fix: remove broad consumer R8 keep rules to allow code shrinking
body:
## Summary

Removes broad `-keep public class` rules from `consumer-rules.pro` to allow downstream consumer applications to shrink unused `compose-highlight` code, composables, and theme factories when R8 shrinking is enabled.

Resolves #492.

## Background & Verification

- **Current behavior:** The packaged `consumer-rules.pro` contained blanket rules keeping every public class and interface in `dev.hossain.highlight.ui.*` and `dev.hossain.highlight.engine.*`. This populated R8's `seeds.txt` with 354+ library entries, preventing downstream apps from stripping any public APIs even if unused.
- **Reflection & JNI audit:** Verified that `compose-highlight` does not use Java reflection, JNI, `@JavascriptInterface` callbacks, or reflective serialization.
- **Shrinking measurements with `:sample:assembleRelease` (R8 enabled):**
  - Library seeds in `seeds.txt`: **354 -> 0**
  - Shrunk / dead-code eliminated library members in `usage.txt`: **395 members** stripped (unused `copy$default`, `componentN`, unused theme factories, and uncalled helpers).
  - Downstream consumers using only `SyntaxHighlightedCode` can now freely shrink `StreamingSyntaxHighlightedCode` and `SyntaxHighlightedTextEditor`.

## Verification checklist

- [x] `./gradlew formatKotlin`
- [x] `./gradlew lintKotlin`

title: fix: preserve streaming highlight spans on mid-stream engine failures
body:
## Problem

Code review of the recently added `StreamingSyntaxHighlightedCode` / `rememberStreamingHighlightedCode` found three issues in the streaming highlight pipeline:

1. **Mid-stream failures flash the whole block to plain text** - `onFailure` reset the snapshot to `null`, discarding all preserved spans. A transient failure (e.g. `HighlightException.Timeout` while the WebView is busy) during active token streaming visually reset every already-colored line back to unstyled text, defeating the span-transfer feature.
2. **No explicit ordering guard between overlapping highlight runs** - the newline-triggered immediate run is untracked and can overlap a throttle/debounce job. Safety depended entirely on the engine fair `Mutex` serializing calls in launch order - an implicit cross-module invariant.
3. **Unused `LocalContentColor` import** in `StreamingSyntaxHighlightedCode.kt`.

## Solution

- `executeHighlight` now keeps the last successful snapshot on failure; the next debounce/throttle cycle retries with newer text. `lastHighlightedText` is intentionally left unchanged on failure so text that already has a valid snapshot is deduped.
- Added a monotonic `runId` guard: a result (or failure) from a superseded run can never overwrite a newer run\s snapshot or re-fire callbacks (`onHighlightComplete` / `onError`). The engine\s serialized-execution assumption is now an enforced invariant rather than an implicit one.
- Removed the unused import.
- Updated the `onError` KDoc on `rememberStreamingHighlightedCode` to describe the preserved-spans failure behavior.

## Testing

- Added `midStreamHighlightFailurePreservesPreviouslyHighlightedSpans` to `RememberStreamingHighlightedCodeRobolectricTest`: drives two sequential highlight runs through `ShadowWebView` (run 1 succeeds, run 2 fails with a null JS result) and asserts the returned `AnnotatedString` still carries run-1 spans on the unchanged prefix while the new token text renders immediately.
- **Revert-checked**: the new test fails against the old `highlighted = null` behavior and passes with the fix.
- The ordering guard is not directly testable through `ShadowWebView` (the engine mutex prevents two concurrently pending JS callbacks); it is covered implicitly by the full suite.
- `formatKotlin`, `lintKotlin`, `markdownlint-cli CHANGELOG.md`, full `:compose-highlight:testDebugUnitTest`, and both `assembleDebug` builds pass.

## Notes

- No public API signature changes; behavior-only fix within `@ExperimentalHighlightApi` surface.
- CHANGELOG updated under `[Unreleased]` -> `### Fixed`.

title: fix: trim trailing newline from code block text to prevent extra line in docs
body:
## Summary Fixes an issue where an extra trailing empty line is rendered at the bottom of Kotlin code blocks across the Zensical documentation site (`https://hossain- khan.github.io/android-compose-highlight/`). ### Root Cause When Pygments (`pymdownx.highlight`) renders Markdown code blocks into HTML (`
...
`), `block.textContent` almost always includes a trailing newline (`\n`). When `docs/javascripts/shiki-kotlin.js` passed `block.textContent` directly to Shiki's `codeToHtml()` without trimming, Shiki treated that final newline as an extra line break and generated an empty `` at the end of the code block. Combined with `pre[data- shiki] code .line { display: block; min-height: 1.45em; }` in `shiki-kotlin.css`, this caused a `1.45em` tall blank line to appear at the bottom of every Kotlin code block box. ### Solution - **`docs/javascripts/shiki-kotlin.js`**: Call `.trimEnd()` on `block.textContent` before passing the code string to `codeToHtml()`, preventing the creation of the trailing empty line span. Added an explanatory inline comment. - **`CHANGELOG.md`**: Added entry under `[Unreleased] -> ### Fixed`.

title: fix: resolve runtime, plugin loading and build issues
body:
- Repository
   - Ignore `enckey/` and `.kotlin/`, remove `app/release.zip`
 - Build / CI
   - Remove unused kapt plugin, use the Gradle wrapper version on CI
   - Sign release builds when `KEYSTORE_FILE` is set. The release workflow decodes it from secrets: `KEYSTORE_BASE64`, `KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`, `KEY_ALIAS`, `KEY_PASSWORD`. Without them, the release APK stays unsigned as before.
   - Add PluginCore unit tests (`PluginResolver`, `Version`, `FileUtils`)
 - Runtime
   - ProjectImpl: shut down the project thread pool on stop/destroy. `setTimeout`/`setInterval` now run in the project scope and are cancelled with it.
   - PluginLoader: resolve dependencies in topological order, and compare required versions against the dependency's version. Skip plugins that have missing or incompatible required dependencies, or circular dependencies. Plugin load errors no longer abort startup.
   - NotificationListener: deliver notifications without actions to `onNotificationPosted` (StarLight's own notifications are excluded). Key chat rooms by room id and refresh them on each message.

   - Fix the ApplicationSession re-init guard, the update install permission intent, `Version.newerThan` and the JobLocker parent race

   - Declare the `specialUse` foreground service type, and handle the foreground service start restriction

   - Remove the duplicate FileProvider, stop exporting internal activities

title: fix(ext): smooth one-clock Breathing pacer with a 4-3-2-1 phase count (0.3.2)
body:
## What

Anti: "the breathing in and out thing should be a smooth thing that has the counting down properly". The Breathing pause (block page AND the in-page gate overlay on all seven platforms) now grows smoothly over the whole 4s inhale, shrinks over the whole 4s exhale with ease-in-out sine motion, and counts each phase down 4, 3, 2, 1 in the circle's centre, landing on 1 as the phase ends.

## Root cause of the jank

Each surface ran the circle and its numbers off **two clocks**:

- **Block page (`BreathingView`)**: scale was derived from a `setInterval` countdown that decremented React state every 100ms, smoothed by a `transition: transform 100ms linear`. The result was an 80-step staircase per phase with linear motion that reversed at full speed at each phase boundary (a bounce, not a breath). Each re-render restarted the transition at irregular timer intervals.
- **In-page overlay (`content/overlay.ts`)**: toggled `.nudge-overlay__breath--in` on a 200ms `setInterval` under a 4s `cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)` CSS transition. The first toggle landed ~200ms after mount, so the circle started late and lagged its own "Breathe in" label. Every phase toggle could be up to 200ms off, and the curve was asymmetric (fast start, slow end).

## Fix

- `src/core/breathing.ts` (pure): `breathFrame(elapsedMs, totalMs)` gives `{phase, phaseSecondsLeft, level (eased sine), progress, totalSecondsLeft, done}`. Over a full cycle the level is one continuous cosine with zero velocity at every turn. `breathVisual` maps level to transform scale, or to opacity under reduced motion.
- `src/ui/breathingClock.ts`: ONE requestAnimationFrame clock per pause. It advances ACTIVE time only, so it is frozen while the tab is hidden and adds at most 250ms per frame (no burst of catch-up motion). It emits frame 0 synchronously so the first paint is already correct, and `stop()` cancels the rAF and removes the listener.
- Both surfaces write `style.transform`/`opacity` directly every frame (composited only, no CSS transition left to race) and touch text only when a value changes. In React, the driven properties stay OUT of the JSX `style` so the once-a-second re-render cannot reset them.
- `prefers-reduced-motion`: the circle stays still and its opacity breathes; the countdown is unchanged.
- Pause length and the `COMPLETE_PAUSE` flow are unchanged. Completion fires off the same clock.

## Tests

- **Layer L1 (pure)**: `tests/core/breathing.test.ts` covers the phase/count table at every boundary (0, 999, 1000, 3999, 4000, 7999, 8000, ...), the 4-3-2-1 sequence, a mid-phase end landing on 1, done/total/progress, a **class invariant that no 1ms step in 3 cycles moves the circle more than a sine can**, easing at the turn, mirror symmetry, the reduced-motion visual, and the frame-step clamp.
- **Driver**: `tests/ui/breathingClock.test.ts` covers the synchronous first frame, many frames per second (not a per-second tick), the phase turning exactly at 4s, stopping after done, hidden-tab freeze with no catch-up jump, `stop()` cleanup, and reduced-motion passthrough.
- **Surfaces**: blockPage 4-3-2-1 plus monotonic-growth test; overlay first-paint and count test, plus a dispose-stops-the-clock test.
- **e2e (real Chrome)**: on the block page, rAF-sampled scale must change on most frames with no per-frame jump over 0.05 and the count must tick. On the Instagram Reels Breathing gate, the in-page circle must animate every frame.
- `npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test`: 1498 passed (42 new). The pause and instagramGate e2e specs: 10/10 locally under xvfb.

Visual check: 400ms frame series across a full inhale/exhale on both surfaces, in `~/Pictures/screenshots/nudge-ext-breathing-{blockpage,overlay}-*.png` (+ `-sheet.png` contact sheets).

Release: extension 0.3.2 (package.json; WXT derives the manifest version from it), CHANGELOG entry, CLAUDE.md lesson.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(ext): @ in URL path looped the block page into 'internal error' (0.3.1)
body:
**Bug:** `youtube.com/@handle` showed "Nudge hit an internal error blocking this page" whenever YouTube was in force.

**Root cause:** `extractDomain` cut userinfo at the first `@` anywhere in the URL, so `https://www.youtube.com/@antiraedus` parsed to host `antiraedus`, which returned null. DNR redirected youtube.com correctly. The block page then resolved no rule and answered ALLOW, bounced back, got redirected again, and the loop guard gave up. Usage on `/@handle` and TikTok `/@user/video` pages was also never counted.

**Fixes**
- `domainMatcher`: look for userinfo only inside the authority.
- `GET_BLOCK_CONTEXT`: an ALLOW recompiles DNR before answering. Dynamic rules persist across restarts and sleep, so a stale rule set now heals instead of looping.
- `applyRules`: serialized. A browser start runs bootstrap twice, and concurrent recompiles could stack or collide rule ids.

**Tests:** 5 new regression tests, each verified failing with its fix reverted. Full unit suite: 1456/1456. Lint and typecheck clean.

title: fix(#53): the second leaker was the ViewModel's own thread pool racing resetMain()
body:
Closes #53 (second leaker).

**Layer L1 + rule (f)/(e):** the offender is a JVM-unit-test race, so the regression test is a pure JVM counterfactual pair (`MainDispatcherResetLeakTest`) plus two source-level absence gates. The prescribed class-boundary `JUnitCore` gate was built, measured at **0 of 158 classes, twice**, and dropped — see below.

## The offender

`HomeBlockedTileTest` — both victim and leaker. Not `CrashSafeScopeTest`, which the 2026-09-27 fix already drains.

`Dispatchers.resetMain()` is not a neutral cleanup in a JVM unit-test fork. With no Android main looper, it restores `MissingMainCoroutineDispatcher`, whose `isDispatchNeeded` **throws** rather than returning false — so it arms a trap for any coroutine of the finished test still alive on `Dispatchers.Main`.

`HomeViewModel` named `Dispatchers.IO` in `flowOn` at two points in its `uiState` chain, putting part of a `viewModelScope` chain on a real thread pool that no `TestScope` waits for. The pool thread finished after `@After`, tried to resume its `Dispatchers.Main` continuation, and took the throw as a `CompletionHandlerException` with no `CoroutineExceptionHandler` in its context. `kotlinx-coroutines-test`'s process-global `ExceptionCollector` queued it, and the next `runTest` anywhere in the fork died at its first line with `UncaughtExceptionsBeforeTest`.

Full cause chain, from the CI probe output:

```
kotlinx.coroutines.CompletionHandlerException   [thread DefaultDispatcher-worker-6, context Dispatchers.Main,
                                                 job StandaloneCoroutine{Cancelled}]
Caused by: IllegalStateException: Module with the Main dispatcher had failed to initialize
    at MissingMainCoroutineDispatcher.isDispatchNeeded  <- TestMainDispatcher.isDispatchNeeded
    <- resumeCancellableWith <- ScopeCoroutine.afterCompletion
Caused by: RuntimeException: Method getMainLooper in android.os.Looper not mocked
```

## How it was found

It does not reproduce locally. A class-boundary hunter (every test class through `JUnitCore`, drain the global collector before and after each) found **0 leakers across 158 classes** at a 400 ms settle and again at a **40 second** settle; 8 single-CPU runs of the two victim classes were clean; both full local suites showed only the known, drained `CrashSafeScopeTest.kt:146` leak. The local suite takes 52 s, the CI job 3 m 54 s — the race only loses on a slow runner.

So it was instrumented **where it happens**: `LeakProbeHandler` (a `CoroutineExceptionHandler` via `META-INF/services`) pushed to a branch, `./gradlew test` run 12× in parallel on `ubuntu-latest`. **1 of 12 failed** (~4 % per suite run, matching two occurrences in three weeks), and because Gradle attributes a fork's stderr to the test that was *running*, the probe printed under the **offender's** name rather than the victim's.

## The fix, in layers

1. **Root cause — the dispatcher is injected.** `di/DispatcherModule` provides `@IoDispatcher CoroutineDispatcher = Dispatchers.IO`; `HomeViewModel`, `BackupViewModel`, `StatsViewModel`, `WillpowerViewModel` and `AppDetailViewModel` take it, and `StatsViewModel.polled()` (a companion helper, so it cannot read an instance property) takes it as a parameter. Production behaviour is unchanged. A test now hands in its own test dispatcher, so the whole chain runs on the test scheduler on the test's own thread and **no background worker exists to lose the race to.**
2. **Second layer — `MainDispatcherRule`.** A `TestWatcher` that installs the dispatcher in `starting()` and does `resetMain()` + `LeakedCoroutineExceptions.drain()` in `finished()`, which runs *after* the class's own `@After`. Six test files migrated onto it.
3. **Gates that discover rather than list.** `ViewModelDispatcherContractTest`: no `*ViewModel.kt` under `ui/` contains the token `Dispatchers.` (absence over a walked set, rule (e)) plus both of `HomeViewModel`'s steps on the parameter. `LeakedCoroutineExceptionsContractTest`: no test file contains `Dispatchers.setMain(` except the rule and the gate itself.
4. **Behavioural counterfactual — `MainDispatcherResetLeakTest`.** A live `Dispatchers.Main` coroutine carried across `resetMain()` must leak into the global collector; the identical coroutine **joined first** must not. The pair makes the assertion about the *order* (rule (d)), and it asserts the property that hurts (queued in the collector) rather than which internal kotlinx branch produced it.
5. **Diagnosability, so the next one costs one log read.** `exceptionFormat = FULL` on the test tasks — `UncaughtExceptionsBeforeTest` attaches the exception that actually leaked as a **suppressed** throwable, and Gradle's default `SHORT` printed one line and threw it away, which is why this cost two investigations. Plus `STANDARD_ERROR` for attribution, `release.yml` uploading test reports on failure, and `LeakProbeHandler` kept in the tree behind `-Dnudge.leakprobe=1`.

## Not done, deliberately

The reopening comment asked for a class-boundary `JUnitCore` gate and an `@After` rule that fails the leaking test itself. The boundary gate was built and **measured blind to this defect** (0/158, twice); shipping it would mean running all 2044 tests a second time inside one test for a gate with a demonstrated blind spot. A JUnit4 `RunListener` is not registerable from `build.gradle.kts` in Gradle's JUnit4 executor. And nothing inside the offending class can fail on this — the throw happens on a pool thread after the test has ended. So the invariant is enforced where it is decidable: in the source, by making the shape unwritable (rule (a)), with one deterministic behavioural counterfactual for the mechanism.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `./gradlew test lintDebug` (`--rerun-tasks`) | **PASS** — 2044 debug + 2044 release, 0 failures (was 2038; +6 new tests) |
| 10× `testReleaseUnitTest --rerun` | **10/10 green** |
| 12× `./gradlew test` on `ubuntu-latest`, probe armed, **before** the fix | **1 of 12 failed**, unaccounted `CompletionHandlerException` attributed to `HomeBlockedTileTest` |
| 12× `./gradlew test` on `ubuntu-latest`, probe armed, **after** the fix ([run](https://github.com/astraedus/nudge/actions/runs/36535256133)) | **12/12 green**; all 72 probe hits accounted for (48 = `CrashSafeScopeTest`'s deliberate F7 leak, 24 = `MainDispatcherResetLeakTest`'s own), **0 unaccounted** |
| Counterfactual: `Dispatchers.IO` back in `HomeViewModel` | `ViewModelDispatcherContractTest` **FAILS**, naming `HomeViewModel.kt` |
| Counterfactual: hand-written `Dispatchers.setMain` back in a test | the new gate **FAILS**, naming that file |
| Counterfactual: both of `CrashSafeScopeTest`'s drains removed | `GlobalCollectorNotLeakedTest` **FAILS** |

That last one also **corrected a claim in `docs/testing-strategy.md`**: removing only the `@After` drain leaves the gate **green**, because the in-test `assertTrue(…, drain())` already consumes the leak. Delete-the-guard-by-hand is a proof only if you delete *every* guard covering the property — recorded in rule (f) and in `tasks/lessons.md`.

title: fix(#64): presence cancels an absence, placed in SittingTracker, not in EventClassifier or the grant
body:
Closes #64.

## The placement assumption, stated up front

The fix goes in **`SittingTracker`**, because that class already owns the one question this bug is
about — *is the user still in a sitting with app X* — and the away clock it owns is the thing that
was wrong. The two other places it could plausibly have gone are both worse:

- **`EventClassifier`** — promoting a click or a scroll to `ForegroundSignal.AppWindow` would have
  been a one-line change and would have worked. It is also exactly the mistake #5, #7, #19 and #28
  all were: teaching the "what is on screen" answer a second meaning so that a downstream consumer
  gets the behaviour it wants. `AppWindow` means a window came forward. A scroll is not that.
- **`PassthroughManager`** (e.g. refreshing `lastTime` on interaction) — that is a time-based expiry
  on the grant by another name, and the class doc explains at length why there is deliberately none.

So: the classifier keeps telling the truth, the grant keeps having no clock of its own, and the
sitting model gains one new input — which is where the defect actually is.

## What was wrong

`SittingTracker.awaySinceMs` is a one-shot timestamp, started by the first foreign `AppWindow` and
cancelled only by an `AppWindow` for the sitting's own package. But `AppWindow` means *a window
transition happened*, not *the user is here* — `EventClassifier` returns `NotForeground` for
everything that is not a window change. A user actively using their app without changing windows
(scrolling, reading, typing) therefore had **no way to contradict an absence they were not having**.

One ordinary sub-flow — a Chrome Custom Tab from Reddit, "open with" from Files, a share sheet, a
permission dialog — armed a fuse with no expiry. If the return did not arrive as a window event
(#58 measured that exact delivery flakiness on the bench Pixel 3, same gesture, same build), the
clock kept burning and the user's next in-app navigation, minutes later, was read as a return from a
two-minute absence: grant revoked, block back, while they sat exactly where they had been.

The app was contradicting itself throughout — `InteractionCounter` was counting those same taps and
scrolls as *what the user did inside app X*. One question, two opposite answers, which is the same
split #54 found between enforcement and counting.

## What changed

`SittingTracker.onInteraction(packageName, nowMs)` routes a `VIEW_CLICKED` / `VIEW_SCROLLED` carrying
the sitting's package through the **same** "the user came back" branch `onAppWindow` uses (extracted
as `onEvidenceOfPresence`), not through a rule of its own:

| interaction | away clock | result |
|---|---|---|
| sitting's app | running, under the window | cancelled, sitting survives — the reported bug |
| sitting's app | running, past the window | sitting ENDS as a window event would end it — **no bypass opened** |
| another app, or no sitting | anything | nothing |

A stray event from a backgrounded app can therefore only ever revoke **sooner**, never grant.

Wired in the service's interaction branch, under the synthetic-click guard (a tap we performed for
the Following steer must not prove the user is present) and before the counter is told, so a sitting
that ends resets the counter's sources before this same event is counted.

## Layer (docs/testing-strategy.md)

**L1, pure unit**, plus a source-level contract clause for the wiring.

L1 is the right layer because the defect is a pure-model one: the model accepted only one kind of
evidence and the missing kind is representable in the model's own types. It is reproducible with
four calls and no device.

The contract clause is not a substitute for it — it answers a different question. A pure-model fix
nobody calls is a silent no-op with a green suite, and a click classifies as `NotForeground`, so it
reaches no branch that would otherwise touch the sitting. The existing
`every sitting-model call from the service uses the monotonic clock` test already **discovers**
`onInteraction` from `PassthroughManager`'s signatures and fails if there is no call site passing
`sittingClock()`; the new clause adds only the position (under the synthetic-click guard, before the
counter).

**L6 (bench device) is owed and NOT done** — the Pixel 3 is offline tonight. Test cases are filed in
`~/ops/routes/nudge/tasks.md` with n>=3 trials per build and an A/B against a main build, because
#58's pass/fail spread is what a one-shot check on an intermittent bug is worth.

## Counterfactual

Verified by neutering `onInteraction` to `return SittingEvent.Unchanged` and re-running:

```
SittingTrackerTest > an interaction after a display timeout the user returned from closes the absence FAILED
SittingTrackerTest > an interaction after a genuine absence still ends the sitting FAILED
SittingTrackerTest > an interaction in the app cancels an away clock a sub-flow armed FAILED
PassthroughTest > a completed hold survives a sub-flow when only the scrolling proves the user came back FAILED
PassthroughTest > an interaction arriving after a real departure revokes rather than rescues FAILED
75 tests completed, 5 failed
```

The two tests that still pass with the fix removed are the ones that should: `pre-fix, nothing the
user did inside the app could reach the away clock` and `without that evidence the same sub-flow
revokes the hold six minutes later` assert the OLD behaviour on the path that did not change, so
they also prove the fixed tests are not passing because a sub-flow quietly stopped arming the clock
at all.

## Tests

`./gradlew test`: **1942 passed, 0 failed** (debug + release unit variants), +9 vs before.
`./gradlew lintDebug`: clean.

New:
- `SittingTrackerTest` ×6 — the reported case, the pre-fix counterfactual, no-bypass, foreign-app
  inertness, cannot-start-a-sitting, and the #54-family display-timeout variant.
- `PassthroughTest` ×3 — the same story at the grant level through the real `EventClassifier`, its
  counterfactual, and the bypass direction.
- `EventDispatchOrderContractTest` ×1 — the wiring, its position, and the synthetic-click guard.

## Not closed, and filed rather than hidden

If the fuse is armed spuriously and the user then goes past the return window without touching the
app at all, their next touch or navigation still ends the sitting. The complete fix is to verify the
foreign app is *still* in front rather than inferring it from one event —
`UsageEvents.Event.getTaskRootPackageName()` (API 29+). That `docs/BACKLOG.md` entry already existed
and is now annotated as promoted by #64.

## Docs

`docs/architecture/accessibility-event-pipeline.md` (the sitting section + the test table),
`docs/BACKLOG.md`, and an `## [Unreleased]` CHANGELOG entry — no version bump and no tag here, since
the device gate has not run.

title: fix(release): Play notes must not ship a half word or raw markdown
body:
Two store-facing defects in `publish-to-play.sh`'s release-note extraction, both found while previewing v1.18.2's notes before shipping them.

**1. The 500-char Play cap was applied as a hard slice, so the live listing ended mid-word.** v1.18.2's first draft would have shipped `...no block screens, no delays, no daily limits, an` to the store. It now cuts back to the last complete **sentence**, with a last-whole-word + ellipsis fallback for a single bullet long enough to contain no sentence end at all.

Whole-string parameter expansion, **not** sed: the notes are multi-line, and a line-oriented `s/[^.!?]*$//` strips the tail of *every line* rather than the tail of the text. That was the first attempt and it mangled the whole block — the comment in the diff says so, because the sed version is the one that looks obviously right.

**2. The CHANGELOG is markdown and the store field is plain text**, so markup shipped verbatim. v1.18.1's **live** notes currently read:

> ...while he was still in the app, reading client messages ([#54](https://github.com/astraedus/nudge/issues/54)). He had not gone anywhere...

Issue parentheticals are now dropped entirely (a bare issue number means nothing to a store reader and eats the char budget), any other link keeps its text, and emphasis/code markers are stripped.

## Verification

Previewed 1.18.2, 1.18.1 and 1.17.3 through the extraction block lifted verbatim out of the script (not a paraphrase of it). All three now end on a complete sentence in clean plain text, 360-434 chars:

- **1.18.2** — 415 chars, ends `...because it had never finished starting up.`
- **1.18.1** — 434 chars, the `([#54](...))` parenthetical gone, ends `...thirty seconds of reading is enough.`
- **1.17.3** — 360 chars, `(#35, asked for by a user...)` kept as plain text (the link is inside a larger parenthetical, so only the link flattening applies — which reads correctly).

`bash -n` clean. No behaviour change to AAB resolution, preflight, or the release call.

title: fix: guard the accessibility service teardown against an uninitialised foregroundClock (#57)
body:
## The bug

`onDestroy` called `stopForegroundTimeTicker` unconditionally, and that read `private lateinit var foregroundClock` — a field only `onServiceConnected` assigns. Any teardown of a service that never completed a connect threw `UninitializedPropertyAccessException` **out of `onDestroy`**, Android wrapped it as *"Unable to stop service"* and filed the component under `Crashed services:`, which per AOSP is **never retried**. Every rule then became a silent no-op with nothing shown to the user. Reachable from install-over / `MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED`, a force stop, a memory-pressure kill and rebind (BACKLOG F8 records this service churning on the bench device under exactly that), or a fast permission toggle.

**Pre-existing**, as the issue says: four traces in the bench Pixel's dropbox, three tagged v54 (1.18.1) and one v53 (1.18.0). Not caused by #54, only found while QAing it — where it presented as "the block screen just did not appear" and cost several rounds chasing a phantom regression in unrelated code.

## The fix, in two layers

The field guard alone only fixes the field, so:

1. **Every `lateinit` teardown can reach is guarded**, in the shape `hideAllOverlays` already used (`if (::field.isInitialized)`).
2. **`onDestroy` runs every statement through a new `ServiceTeardown`**, which contains and reports each step's failure by name. A throw in teardown can buy nothing — nothing after it can observe a failure — and it was costing both the crashed-service state *and the steps below the throw*: before this, the uninitialised clock on the third line meant `serviceScope` was never cancelled and all three overlay managers kept a dead service as their context. `Throwable`, not `Exception`: a `NoSuchMethodError` from an API-level mistake (a bug class this repo has shipped) leaves the service equally crashed. Containment makes ordering the only thing left to get wrong, so the two load-bearing orderings are pinned by test: instance cleared **first**, scope cancelled **last**.

## The audit you asked for

Teardown surface: `onDestroy` (the only one that runs our code). **`onUnbind` is not overridden** and `onInterrupt` has an empty body — neither reads anything. The eight `lateinit` fields are `webClock`, `webSessionUsageProvider`, `autoKickWebTimeHandler`, `interactionHandler`, `timeRemainingHandler`, `autoKickExecutor`, `autoKickTimeHandler`, `foregroundClock`.

**Found a second one, not just the reported field.** `onDestroy`'s call closure is `{onDestroy, stopForegroundTimeTicker, endWebSession}`, and `endWebSession` reads `webClock.isRunning` **even when `activeWebSessionKey` is already null** (`&&` does not short-circuit that way round), plus `webSessionUsageProvider.browserPackage`. It would have thrown in exactly the same place the moment the clock above it was fixed. Both now guarded.

Also checked and clean:

- **The two broadcast/observer paths cannot fire pre-connect.** `screenOffReceiver` and `imeSettingObserver` are `by lazy` and registered at lines 933/943 of `onServiceConnected`, *after* every `lateinit` is assigned (828-917). `screenOffReceiver` reaches `hideAllOverlays`, whose two `lateinit` reads were already guarded.
- **Nullable derefs in `onDestroy`**: `grayscaleActiveForPackage` is null-checked, `entryPoint` is a lazy Hilt lookup, `contentResolver` is platform-provided post-`onCreate`. All are inside contained steps now regardless.
- **Unguarded `lateinit` reads elsewhere** (`onAccessibilityEvent`, `tickForegroundTime`, the DataStore collectors) are reachable only from paths that `onServiceConnected` itself starts, so they cannot run before assignment. The contract test scopes itself to the teardown closure for exactly that reason.

### The issue's second half: "a crashed service must not be able to look enabled"

**Checked rather than assumed, and it already holds.** `ProtectionStatus.isAccessibilityServiceConnected` reads `AccessibilityManager.getEnabledAccessibilityServiceList` — the server-side bound list, which a crashed service is absent from — so `ProtectionCheck` raises the "blocking has stopped" alert on its next cycle, and the settings string (which survives a crash) is only ever read as *intent*. That is the design the `mCrashedServices` retraction in `service-lifecycle-and-watchdog.md` produced, and this bug is the first real-world case it was built for; `ServiceLifecycleContractTest` already pins it. One observation, filed here rather than fixed: `instance = this` is set at the TOP of `onServiceConnected`, before the fields, so a partial connect would leave `NudgeAccessibilityService.isConnected()` reading true — but that function has **no production callers** (only a doc reference in `AccessibilityStatusProvider`), so nothing user-facing hangs off it. Moving it is a semantic change to the connection signal and not worth bundling into a crash fix.

## Tests

**Layer L3** (pure lifecycle decision, per `docs/testing-strategy.md`). The service is not JVM-constructible — `android.app.Service`'s framework methods are stubs in the unit-test `android.jar` — which is why the step runner was lifted out of it, exactly as the issue suggested.

- **`ServiceTeardownTest`** (5): a step throwing `UninitializedPropertyAccessException` does not escape and is reported; a failing step does not skip the steps after it; an `Error` is contained too; a failing *reporter* does not escape either; a succeeding step reports nothing.
- **`ServiceTeardownContractTest`** (3): the invariant is **DISCOVERED, not listed**, as the issue asked ("a hand-list will rot"). It parses the service, computes which functions `onDestroy` can actually reach (bare calls only, so `teardown.step(` and `entryPoint.x()` do not pollute the closure), and requires a guard for every `lateinit` any of them touches; plus that `onDestroy` holds nothing but `ServiceTeardown.step` statements; plus a parser self-check, so a regex that silently matched nothing cannot make the other two pass vacuously. A new field, or a new call added to `onDestroy`, is covered the day it is written.

### Counterfactuals (all three verified, each reverted after)

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| Remove `::foregroundClock.isInitialized` | `every lateinit reachable from onDestroy is guarded` **FAILED** |
| Remove the `try`/`catch` in `ServiceTeardown` | all 5 `ServiceTeardownTest` tests **FAILED** |
| Add one bare statement to `onDestroy` | `onDestroy runs every statement through the contained teardown runner` **FAILED** |

`./gradlew test` **1932 passed / 0 failed** (1924 before, +8). `./gradlew lintDebug` **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**, no new findings.

## Also

- `CHANGELOG.md` 1.18.2, `versionCode` 54 — 55, `versionName` 1.18.1 — 1.18.2.
- `docs/architecture/service-lifecycle-and-watchdog.md` gains the section the issue asked for, as the sibling of the existing F7 "the coroutine scope cannot take the process down".
- No device QA needed for the logic (pure teardown, JVM-tested); a post-merge smoke check on `main-latest` confirms `Crashed services:{}` survives permission toggles and a force-stop.

Closes #57
