title: Fix refetchPolicy(CacheFirst) not falling through to network on cache miss
body:
When a watcher is configured with `refetchPolicy(FetchPolicy.CacheFirst)`, it never hits the network on a cache miss during refetch — it silently behaves like `CacheOnly`.

The cause is the "reset first" block in `refetchPolicy()`:

```kotlin
// Reset first
refetchOnlyIfCached(true)  // should be false
refetchNoCache(false)
```

The analogous `fetchPolicy()` function resets to `onlyIfCached(false)`, and each restrictive branch flips the flag back to `true` as needed (`CacheOnly`). The refetch variant resets to `onlyIfCached(true)` instead, and since the `CacheFirst` branch is a no-op (`this as T`), the flag stays `true`. `DefaultFetchPolicyInterceptor` then skips its `chain.proceed(request)` network call because `request.onlyIfCached` is `true`, so the watcher only ever emits the cache response.

This PR flips the reset to `false` to match `fetchPolicy()`. `CacheOnly` still sets it back to `true` explicitly. `NetworkOnly` already flips it off via the mutual-exclusion logic in `refetchNoCache()`. `NetworkFirst` and `CacheAndNetwork` use their own interceptors that do not consult `onlyIfCached`.

### Reproduction

The added `WatcherTest.cacheFirstRefetchPolicy` test pins the expected behavior: with a `CacheFirst` refetch policy, after `cacheManager.clearAll() + publish(ALL_KEYS)`, the watcher emits the `CacheMissException` and then the network response. Without the fix it times out waiting for the network response.

Data-driven source engine, adaptive tablet and foldable UI, and older-Android crash fixes
body:
## Summary

Moves Android to the data-driven source engine that web and the desktop clients already use, makes the UI adaptive for tablets and foldables, and fixes the crashes on Android versions older than the developer devices.

Base branch `nyora-root` is the tree the `Nyora` root repository pins (v2.1.6 plus the unified backup and identity work). `main` holds the v2.6–v2.7.3 Play lineage; this branch upgrades databases from both, but merging the two lineages is a separate decision (30 conflicting files against `main`).

### Sources
- New `:engine` Android library compiles the `nyora-data-driven` checkout (`data/` submodule, branch `android-sources-2026-09-20`, 49 engines) against `android.jar`; the QuickJS bundle, JavaScript OTA worker and `quickjs-kt` are removed.
- Catalogue loading with daily refresh from the pinned data branch; canonical `data:<id>` identities; legacy 64-bit manga ids shared with desktop and web; native adapters for MangaFire, the MangaNato family, ToonTop and MANGA Plus; Madara chapter-list recovery.
- Migrations 32→33→34 upgrade `JS_` (v2.1.6) and `DD_` (v2.6–v2.7.3) sources and engine-id manga ids; backups and cloud sync map ids through the same helpers.

### Adaptive UI
- System density and font scale are respected again (fixes the oversized UI report).
- Window size classes drive sheet, FAB and settings-pane decisions; tablets get the rail layout; book and tabletop postures keep details panes and reader pages clear of the hinge.

### Crash fixes
- API 35 frame-rate call under an API 34 guard (crash on every activity start on Android 14).
- `Bitmap.Config.HARDWARE` on Android 6/7 in the translator.
- Encrypted preferences at process start now fall back on keystore failures.
- Display-cutout inset consumption below API 30; dangling `DownloadsActivity` manifest entry.

## Verification
- 208 unit tests green (`-PversionName=2.8.0`); zero `NewApi` in Kotlin for both modules (22 pre-existing app lint errors remain).
- Instrumented migration tests on Android 7: all five migration cases green.
- Resizable emulator (phone, tablet, desktop, book and tabletop postures, density 560 / font 1.3) and Android 7 emulator (launch, explore, read, translate) with no fatal exception.
- A real v2.7.3 database transplanted into this build upgrades to schema 34 with favourites and history intact.

## Before release
1. Push the data submodule branch (`git -C data push origin android-sources-2026-09-20`) and merge it into the data repository's `main`; then remove `.github/data-bootstrap` as the script header documents.
2. Bump `versionName`/`versionCode` above 2.7.3 / 27300.

Full record: `docs/android-data-driven-migration-2026-09-20.md` in the `Nyora` repository.

title: fix: privacy, network, and updater hardening + build modernization
body:
## Context

This is a body of work that had been sitting uncommitted in the working tree. I reviewed all 48 files and it turned out to contain several genuine defect fixes rather than just cleanup, so it is split into reviewable commits by theme. Nothing here is new code written for this PR — it is existing work, reviewed, grouped, and verified.

## Defect fixes

**The configured server URL did nothing** (`NetworkModule`) — Retrofit was built against the compile-time `API_BASE_URL`, so a self-hoster who pointed the app at their own server in Settings still had every `/api/v1` request go to the default host. The interceptor now rewrites scheme/host/port/path-prefix to the configured base.

**The pairing code leaked to third parties** (`NetworkModule`) — `Accept` and `X-TV-Code` were attached to *every* request on the shared client, so the pairing code was sent to third-party IPTV and EPG hosts. Now scoped to FireVision API requests only.

**Credentials in plaintext** (`AppPreferences`) — Xtream-derived guide URLs embed username and password, and were stored in plaintext `SharedPreferences`. Moved to `EncryptedSharedPreferences` with a one-time migration that removes the plaintext copy.

**Device-scoped identifier** (`FavoriteRepositoryImpl`, `StreamMetricsRepositoryImpl`) — identity was `Settings.Secure.ANDROID_ID`, which is shared across apps signed by the same key and not user-resettable. Replaced with a random per-install UUID, so it identifies the install and clears on uninstall.

**Updater could stall forever** (`AppUpdater`) — three separate paths to a permanently stuck "downloading" UI: starting a second download orphaned the first receiver while overwriting `downloadId`; `getColumnIndex` returns `-1` rather than throwing, so `getInt(-1)` crashed inside the receiver; and an empty cursor fell through without ever invoking `onState`. Also, both ViewModels tore the receiver down from `onCleared`, killing in-flight downloads whenever the user left Settings.

**Refresh/sync races** (`ChannelRepositoryImpl`, `FavoriteRepositoryImpl`) — the scheduler, pull-to-refresh, and startup sync all call these; two interleaving refreshes both fetch and both write the channel table, so a partial write can land after the complete one. `Mutex` each.

**Uncancellable polling** (`PinnedHttpClient` + pairing call sites) — pairing polls with blocking `execute()`, which ignores coroutine cancellation, so leaving the screen left the request running and the socket held. Adds suspend `get`/`post` over `suspendCancellableCoroutine`.

**Locale-dependent countdown** — `String.format` without a locale renders Arabic-Indic numerals under `ar-*` in a layout expecting ASCII. Pinned to `Locale.ROOT`.

**The unit test suite could not compile** (`SettingsViewModelTest`) — missing two constructor args, which failed the whole `testDebugUnitTest` source set. `testDebugUnitTest` therefore could not run on `main` at all. Fixed, plus `ChannelRepositoryImplTest` now mocks the `AppPreferences` object (it reads `SharedPreferences` statically, unavailable on the JVM).

## Also included

- **Refactor/lint** — Activity Result API in `TvSetupActivity`, dead pre-API-28 branches removed (minSdk is 28, so they were unreachable), unused locals and three dead nav lambdas dropped, `modifier`-before-default parameter ordering, AutoMirrored icon variants so `Article`/`MenuBook` flip under RTL, `mipmap-anydpi-v26` → `mipmap-anydpi` (byte-identical; the qualifier is redundant at minSdk 28).
- **Build** — compileSdk/targetSdk 34 → 36, kapt → KSP for Hilt/Room (meaningfully faster; kapt runs a full Java APT round over generated stubs), hardcoded coordinates consolidated into the version catalog.

## Two things worth a deliberate look

1. **The lint `disable` set** in `app/build.gradle.kts` silences `AndroidGradlePluginVersion`, `GradleDependency`, `UnusedResources`, `PrivateResource`, `VectorPath`, `IconLauncherShape`, `IconDipSize`. These are advisory rather than correctness checks, but it is a real narrowing of lint coverage — reviewable on its own merits, and easy to drop from this PR if you would rather not take it.
2. **The SDK 36 + KSP migration** is isolated in its own commit so it can be reverted independently of the fixes.

## Verification

- `assembleDebug`, `lint`, and `testDebugUnitTest` all green.
- Full suite runs and passes: **47 test classes, 0 failures** — including `SettingsViewModelTest` (16 tests), which could not execute before this branch.
- The EPG-URL migration and the identifier switch both change persisted state; worth a manual pass on an install that already has an Xtream playlist configured.

title: fix: settings busy-state UX, update download hang, channel long-press flow
body:
Three TV UX/correctness fixes, one commit each:

## 1. Settings tabs no longer reset to Connection
The section rail selects on focus. Busy states (Check for Updates, Update Now, Check Liveness, Clear Cache) swapped the focused button out of composition, dropping focus back to the first rail item and snapping the pane to Connection. All busy-state rows now keep one persistent button with the spinner inside it and guarded clicks — nodes are never removed or disabled mid-action.

## 2. In-app update no longer stuck at "Downloading..."
`ACTION_DOWNLOAD_COMPLETE` comes from the Download Provider app, not the system UID, so the `RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED` receiver never received it on Android 13+ — the APK downloaded but the installer never launched. Now registered `RECEIVER_EXPORTED`; safe because the receiver validates the download id, queries DownloadManager for real status, and verifies the APK signature before install.

## 3. Channel long-press opens only the context menu
Long-pressing a channel opened the context menu at 600ms while OK was still held; the menu focused its first row and the next auto-repeat key-down clicked it — toggling favorite and dismissing the menu instantly. The card now opens the menu on key release, and menu rows require a fresh press (repeat-count-0 down, then up) so held-over keys can't click through. Menu persists until you pick Favorites/Multiview or press Back.

## 4. Multiview channel picker no longer crashes on large playlists
The picker composed every channel eagerly (`forEach` in a scrollable Column) — thousands of focusable rows built in one frame while 2–4 panes decode video, which kills low-end boxes. Now a bounded `LazyColumn` (only visible rows compose) that opens at the pane's current channel instead of the top.

## Testing
- `./gradlew assembleDebug` + Android lint pass (pre-commit hook).
- On device: Settings → About → Check for Updates / Update Now and Channels → Check Liveness / Clear Cache keep the current tab; long-press a channel card → menu opens on release and persists.
- Note: signature verification means a debug build will refuse a release-signed update APK — test the full update flow on a release build.

title: fix: make player menu reachable on remotes without a MENU button
body:
## Problem

On Android TV / Google TV the audio & subtitle panel could never be opened: the quick-actions bar (which holds the **Audio/Subs** button) was only summoned by the MENU key, and those remotes don't have one. Fire TV's ☰ button was the only way in.

Separately, the quick-actions bar auto-popped over the video on every player entry and zap, and a one-line key-hints toast showed on the first launches — both flagged as bad UX.

## Changes

- **New "Menu" remappable key action** that summons + focuses the quick-actions bar, same as the MENU key. Selectable for D-pad up/down, left/right, and Hold OK in Settings → Player Controls.
- **D-pad ◀▶ now defaults to Menu** — it previously duplicated the ▲▼ zap action, so nothing is lost. Users who explicitly picked "Zap" for left/right keep their saved setting.
- **Quick-actions bar no longer auto-shows on TV** on player entry or zap; it appears only when summoned. Mobile keeps its tap-to-show chrome; the now/next info bar is unchanged.

title: fix: keep Xtream credentials out of stored stream URLs (URL templating)
body:
## Summary
Closes #50 — the residual finding from the #49 security review. Xtream live URLs (`/live/{user}/{pass}/{id}.m3u8`) embed credentials by protocol and were persisted verbatim in the Room DB and TIF provider data.

Imported stream URLs now store `{username}`/`{password}` placeholder tokens instead of real credentials. The new `StreamUrlTemplate` resolver substitutes them from `EncryptedSharedPreferences` at use time. Non-templated URLs (M3U, paired server) pass through unchanged.

## Consumers threaded
- **PlayerScreenEffects** — live playback resolves before building stream slots (proxy URLs get the resolved form)
- **MultiviewScreen** — per-pane players resolve at `setMediaItem`
- **FireVisionTvInputService** — resolves at tune time; `ChannelManager` now writes the credential-free template into `TvContract`, so credentials also stop leaking into the system TV database
- **ChannelHealthScanner** — resolves before probing (`@ApplicationContext` now injected; unit test updated)
- **ChannelThumbnailExtractor** — resolves before HLS manifest fetches

Existing installs self-heal on the next channel sync: `refreshChannels()` rewrites all Room rows from the templated import, and the TIF sync rewrites provider data.

## On-device verification (Android TV emulator, API 34, mock Xtream panel with auth-gated HLS)
- **Room DB**: all channels store `.../live/{username}/{password}/{id}.m3u8`; byte-level scan of DB + WAL found zero credential occurrences
- **Live playback**: stream renders; server log shows the resolved credentialed request arriving at request time
- **Multiview**: two panes streaming concurrently, both manifests fetched with resolved credentials
- **TIF**: sync inserts the 4 channels into `TvContract` (rows receive the templated `streamUrl` verbatim); input service registered
- **Health scanner**: background probe hit never-played channels with resolved credentials
- `./gradlew assembleDebug` + unit tests pass; pre-commit lint passes

## Residual
- System-TV tune-in (`FireVisionTvInputService.resolve()` at playback) could not be exercised on the emulator (no Live Channels app) — worth a quick spot check on a real Fire TV. It is the same one-line resolve verified in the other consumers.
- The EPG URL (`xmltv.php?username=&password=`) is inherent to the Xtream protocol and out of scope per the issue.

fix: add EnclosingMethod to proguard-rules.pro to prevent Gson TypeToken crash
body:
## Problem

Production crash on release builds (Crashlytics, v1.1 build 2):

```
Fatal Exception: java.lang.IllegalStateException:
TypeToken must be created with a type argument: new TypeToken<...>() {};
When using code shrinkers (ProGuard, R8, ...) make sure that generic signatures are preserved.
```

R8 strips the `EnclosingMethod` bytecode attribute during shrinking. Gson uses this attribute to resolve the generic type argument when the `new TypeToken<T>(){}` anonymous subclass pattern is used. Without it, `TypeToken.getTypeTokenTypeArgument()` throws at runtime.

## Root Cause

`app/proguard-rules.pro` had `-keepattributes Signature` but was missing `-keepattributes EnclosingMethod`.

## Fix

Added two lines to the Gson section in `app/proguard-rules.pro`:

- `-keepattributes EnclosingMethod` - preserves the attribute R8 was stripping, allowing Gson to resolve generic type arguments at runtime
- `-keep class * extends com.google.gson.reflect.TypeToken` - prevents R8 from merging or eliminating anonymous TypeToken subclasses

## Test Plan

- Build release APK: `./gradlew assembleRelease`
- Verify no Gson-related R8 warnings in build output
- Install release APK on Fire TV device/emulator and exercise the channel list load to confirm Gson deserialization completes without crash

Fixes: FIR-30

title: fix: use setup-gradle for Gradle caching in CI
body:
## Summary

Every `Run tests` CI job emits:

```
[warning]Path Validation Error: Path(s) specified in the action for caching do(es) not exist, hence no cache is being saved.
```

Root cause: the `run-tests` job in `code-checks.yml` runs inside `container: ubuntu:24.04`. The `actions/cache` steps in `.github/actions/common-setup/action.yml` target `~/.gradle/wrapper` and `~/.gradle/caches`, which resolve to a container-local home dir that does not match where Gradle actually writes its caches in CI. `actions/cache` validates the paths at save time, finds nothing, warns, and skips the save. The Gradle cache is therefore never persisted between runs (the audit estimates ~8min added to `:check` each time).

## Fix

Replace the two manual `actions/cache` steps with a single `gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v6.1.0` step. This action:

- Auto-detects `GRADLE_USER_HOME` correctly on both host runners and container jobs.
- Uses Gradle-aware cache keys (no manual `hashFiles` glob to maintain).
- Is the Gradle-team-recommended approach and supersedes the older manual `actions/cache` pattern.

Pinned to `50e97c2cd7a37755bbfafc9c5b7cafaece252f6e` (`#v6.1.0`), the same SHA already used by `gradle-wrapper-validation.yml`.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

The build also surfaces:

> Consider enabling configuration cache to speed up this build

That requires Gradle code changes to verify all tasks are config-cache compatible, so it's out of scope here. Tracked as a separate follow-up.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI runs without the `Path Validation Error` warning
- [ ] Second CI run on this branch reports a cache hit (`gradle/actions/setup-gradle` logs `Restored Gradle User Home from cache`)
- [ ] All existing jobs (`build-modules`, `build-docker-image`, `run-tests`, `regression-synthetic-replay`) still pass

title: Add daily agentic workflow to auto-fix security alerts via PR
body:
Introduces a GitHub Agentic Workflow that runs daily (weekdays) to detect open Dependabot and code scanning/malware alerts and automatically opens a pull request updating the affected dependencies to their minimum safe patched versions.

## Workflow behavior
- **Triggers**: Daily weekday schedule (`10:16 UTC, Mon–Fri`) + `workflow_dispatch`
- **Alert sources**: Dependabot alerts + code scanning alerts (via GitHub MCP `dependabot` + `code_security` toolsets)
- **Dependency resolution**: Updates versions in `gradle/libs.versions.toml` (primary); falls back to grepping individual `build.gradle.kts` / `buildSrc/` for inline declarations
- **PR output**: Prefixed `[security]`, labeled `security` + `dependencies`, lists CVE/GHSA IDs, old→new versions, max 3 concurrent PRs

## Security posture
- Agent job is strictly read-only; all write operations go through `safe-outputs` (never direct `write` permissions)
- Network access scoped to `java` ecosystem (Maven/Gradle registries) + `defaults`

## Files
| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `.github/workflows/security-alerts-fix.md` | Agentic workflow definition (frontmatter + agent prompt) |
| `.github/workflows/security-alerts-fix.lock.yml` | Compiled GitHub Actions YAML — do not edit manually |
| `.gitattributes` | Marks `*.lock.yml` as linguist-generated with `merge=ours` |

title: Fix: exported component access should be restricted with appropriate permissions
body:
## :page_facing_up: Context
[Sonar reported issue](https://sonarcloud.io/project/issues?id=infinum_android-sentinel&issues=AY69dgmkqpIEknBs3OF1&open=AY69dgmkqpIEknBs3OF1&tab=code)
This PR fixes that issue.
Feel free to add an additional review(s)

## :pencil: Changes
Since Sentinel activity is marked as `android:exported="true"` other apps can start that activity. And that is good, this is one of the ideas for Sentinel. Sonar finds this potential security issue because we don't define a mechanism by which apps that can open Sentinel should be "restricted".
To improve upon this I added custom permission that has `protectionLevel` **signature**. Meaning: only apps that are signed with the same certificate as Sentinel will be able to start Sentinel. This is perfect for our use case because Sentinel comes with apps.

Also, I ran into some compilation issues due to all modules/tools using the same package so I renamed one constant object in the Timber tool. Since this PR is not big I squeezed those changes here.

There's not much here, just try opening Sentinel in one app that uses lib.

## Description 📑

- New composite GitHub Action (.github/actions/popcorn/action.yml) — runs `popcornParent` Gradle task, posts markdown error report as a PR comment on failure, and deletes it on success.

- Architecture refactor: new `AnalyseArchitectureUseCase` — replaces the `PopcornTaskHelper` class by moving all orchestration logic (checking modules, logging, report generation, error triggering) into the domain layer. The use case accepts a list of `TargetModule` objects and an optional error report path.

- `CheckArchitectureUseCase` simplified — now takes `TargetModule` (which includes rules) instead of separate `internalDependencies` + `rules` parameters.

- `GenerateReportUseCase` changed — now accepts `Map<String, CheckResult>` instead of a single `ReportInfo`, enabling batch report generation for multiple modules. Report output now supports multiple modules concatenated.

- `ReportDataSource` and `PopcornGuineapigRepository` — changed from single `ReportData` to `List<ReportData>`.

- Removed skipped rules support — `AnalysisTableResultEnumData.SKIPPED `removed, along with all related logic (`ReportInfo`, `toAnalysisTableList()` extension, `skippedRules` parameter, the `SKIPPED` markdown mapping).

- Presentation layer cleanup — `PopcornTaskHelper.k`t, `ArchitectureViolationErrorsExt.kt`, `TargetModuleExt.kt` deleted; their logic moved to `TargetModule.toString() `override and `CheckResult.Failure.toString().`

- New `Logger` interface in domain layer, with adapter in `PopcornParentTask` that bridges to Gradle's logger.

- Gradle & wrapper upgrade — Gradle 8.4 → 8.12, updated gradlew/gradlew.bat scripts, version bumped to 3.1.7.

- New tests — `AnalyseArchitectureUseCaseTest`, `FakeCheckArchitectureUseCase`, `FakeGenerateReportUseCase`, `FakeLogger`; existing tests updated for the new signatures; `ReportInfoExtTest` deleted (no longer relevant).

title: Fix LocalContext resource queries in Compose by migrating to colorResource
body:
## Fix Lint Errors - LocalContext Resource Queries ✅

### Plan:
- [x] Understand the issue: Replace `context.getColor()` calls with Compose's `colorResource()` API in EcgPlot.kt
- [x] Fix all 5 instances of `context.getColor()` in EcgPlot.kt
- [x] Convert Compose Color to Android Color int using `.toArgb()` for MPAndroidChart compatibility
- [x] Fix composable invocation error by reading colors in composable context
- [x] Verify no other files have similar issues
- [x] Request code review - No issues found ✅
- [x] Run security checks with CodeQL - No issues found ✅

### Changes Made:
- Replaced `import androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalContext` with `import androidx.compose.ui.res.colorResource` and `import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.toArgb`
- Removed `val context = LocalContext.current` from the composable function
- **NEW**: Read all color resources in the composable body (lines 28-32) before the AndroidView
- **NEW**: Use the pre-computed color values in the `update` lambda to avoid composable invocation errors

### Colors Fixed:
1. `R.color.backgroundLight` - ECG line color in dark theme
2. `R.color.backgroundDark` - ECG line color in light theme
3. `R.color.r_peak` - R-peak marker color
4. `R.color.v_beat` - V-beat marker color
5. `R.color.s_beat` - S-beat marker color

### Why This Approach?
Using `colorResource()` instead of `context.getColor()` follows Jetpack Compose best practices:
- Properly integrates with Compose's recomposition system
- Handles configuration changes automatically
- Supports theme changes more effectively
- Allows Compose to track resource changes

The color resources are read in the composable body (where `@Composable` functions can be called) and then used in the non-composable `update` lambda. This avoids the composable invocation error while still following best practices.

The `.toArgb()` conversion is necessary because MPAndroidChart requires Android `Color` int values.

### Security Summary:
- Code review completed: No issues found
- CodeQL security scan: No vulnerabilities detected
- All changes maintain existing functionality while improving code quality

## Lint Error Fix - Completed ✅

- [x] Understand the lint error: LocalContextGetResourceValueCall in EcgPlot.kt
- [x] Replace `context.getColor()` calls with `colorResource()` in EcgPlot.kt
- [x] Fix composable context error: Move `colorResource()` calls to composable body

- [x] Remove unused `LocalContext` import
- [x] Verify no other similar issues exist in the codebase
- [x] Request code review
- [x] Address review feedback

## Summary

Fixed the Android Lint error `LocalContextGetResourceValueCall` and subsequent compilation error by correctly using `colorResource()` in the composable context.

### Changes:
- **Lines 28-32**: Extract all color resources in the composable body using `colorResource().toArgb()`
- **Lines 74-75, 85, 91, 97**: Use the pre-computed color Int values in the `update` lambda

### Why This Approach:
1. `colorResource()` is a `@Composable` function and can only be called from composable context
2. The `update` lambda in `AndroidView` is NOT a composable context
3. Solution: Call `colorResource()` in the composable body, convert to Int, then use those values in the lambda
4. This fixes both the lint error (no `LocalContext.current.getColor()`) and the compilation error (no composable calls in non-composable context)

title: Fix release-only UI freeze: keep DataStore proto classes for R8
body:
## Summary
Fixes the release-build freeze/ANR (and startup crash) caused by R8 stripping fields that AndroidX DataStore's vendored protobuf accesses reflectively.

- **Reverts** the temporary `isMinifyEnabled = false / isShrinkResources = false` workaround in `app/build.gradle.kts` — minification stays **on**.
- **Adds** keep rule in `app/proguard-rules.pro`:
  ```
  -keep class androidx.datastore.preferences.PreferencesProto$** { *; }
  ```

## Root cause
`androidx.datastore.preferences.protobuf.MessageSchema` finds the generated proto class's private backing field `preferences_` **by name at runtime**. R8's shrinker deleted/renamed that field, so the first DataStore `Preferences` read threw:
```
java.lang.RuntimeException: Field preferences_ for <obf> not found.
    at androidx.datastore.preferences.protobuf.MessageSchema...
```
Debug builds were never minified → always worked; the release build froze/crashed.

## Verification (on physical device, release APKs)
| Config | Result |
|---|---|
| minify+shrink, `-dontobfuscate` | works |
| minify+shrink, obfuscate on, `-dontoptimize` | crashes with field-not-found |
| full minify + keep rule (this PR) | **works** |

Verified: app boots, navigation responsive, Auto Wallpaper Updates toggle persists and regenerates wallpaper, no crash.

## Issue
Closes #97 (full analysis + stack trace commented there).

title: Fix auto wallpaper toggle, wallpaper sort, and home-list active-first ordering
body:
## Summary

Three fixes in the wallpaper/list flow:

### 1. Auto Wallpaper Updates toggle now applies the wallpaper (#94)
- `SettingsViewModel.setAutoWallpaperEnabled()` previously only persisted the flag to DataStore — toggling did nothing visible.
- Now, after a successful write with `enabled == true`, it calls `updateWallpaper()` to immediately generate and set the wallpaper from current pending tasks.

### 2. Wallpaper task cards follow the user's selected sort (#93)
- `WallpaperGenerator` hardcoded cards to HIGH → MEDIUM → LOW priority.
- It now reads the saved `SortOption`/`SortDirection` from DataStore and orders the drawn pending tasks the same way as the tasks list.
- Sorting logic extracted to shared `core/util/TaskSorter.kt`, used by both `TasksViewModel` (list) and `WallpaperGenerator` (wallpaper). Completed tasks are still excluded from the wallpaper.

### 3. Home list: active tasks first when status filter is "All" (#96)
- With status filter = **All**, incomplete (active) tasks now always render above completed tasks, with the selected sort option/direction applied within each group.
- Active/Completed filters and priority filter composition are unchanged.

## Tests
- `TaskSorterTest`: due-date (asc/desc, null-due handling), priority asc/desc, created-date, title case-insensitive, immutability.
- `SettingsViewModelTest`: enable → generates wallpaper; disable → no update; failed write → no update.
- `TasksViewModelOrderingTest`: All → active-first ordering; descending sort per group; Active filter; Completed filter; priority filter composition.

Verified: `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest assembleDebug` passes.

Closes #93, #94, #96

title: Fix R8 optimization, reminder scheduling, and persist sort preference
body:
## Summary
Fixes 2 issues found while investigating the Play Console R8 warning and missing notifications, plus 2 UX improvements.

### 1. R8 optimization (Play Console warning)
The app's shrink rate was ~11% because of blanket `-keep` rules that kept entire packages. The real culprit was the library modules' `consumer-rules.pro` files (shipped inside AARs and merged into the app's R8 run), not just `app/proguard-rules.pro`.

**Changes:**
- `app/proguard-rules.pro` — trimmed to only what reflection/codegen needs
- `data/consumer-rules.pro` — was keeping all data packages + Retrofit/Moshi (unused); now only Room `@Entity` + `RoomDatabase` subclasses
- `domain/consumer-rules.pro` — was keeping all models/usecases/repos; now empty (all direct references)
- `core/consumer-rules.pro` — was keeping `core.**` + Compose; now empty

**Results:** classes 18,704 → 3,636 (−80.6%), methods 133,886 → 18,097 (−86.5%), APK 4.1 MB → 1.9 MB. Zero R8 warnings.

### 2. Reminder notifications never scheduled for new tasks (pre-existing bug)
`addTask` returned `Result<Unit>`, so the new task's ID never reached the ViewModel — `savedTaskId` stayed `null` and `scheduleReminder()` was skipped. The reminder flag was saved to the DB (showing "Reminder enabled") but no WorkManager work was ever enqueued, so no notification ever fired.

**Changes:**
- `TaskRepository.addTask` / `AddTaskUseCase` — return `Result<String>` (created task ID)
- `TaskRepositoryImpl` — return the created task's ID
- `AddEditTaskViewModel.saveTask` — capture the new task ID and pass it to the reminder scheduler

### 3. Sort preference not persisted (UX fix)
Sort option/direction reset to Due Date on every app restart.

**Changes:**
- `UserPreferencesRepository` + impl — persist `sort_option` / `sort_direction` in DataStore
- 4 new use cases (`Get`/`SetSortOption`, `Get`/`SetSortDirection`)
- `TasksViewModel` — restores persisted sort on init (guard prevents initial DataStore emission from overriding a user's selection) and writes through on every change/toggle/reset

### 4. Scope-based delete dialog (UX improvement)
The toolbar delete button opened a single "Clear Completed" confirmation. It's now a selection dialog with live task counts.

**Changes:**
- `TaskDao` — explicit `deleteAllTasks`, `deleteCompletedTasks` (renamed from misleading `deleteAllTask`), `deleteIncompleteTasks`
- `TaskRepository` + impl — 3 explicit delete methods
- New `TaskDeleteScope` enum (ALL / COMPLETED / INCOMPLETE) + `DeleteTasksUseCase`
- `TasksViewModel.deleteTasks(scope)` — cancels pending WorkManager reminders for affected tasks (fixes stale notifications after toolbar delete), keeps the 2s progress overlay, refreshes wallpaper + widgets
- `TasksScreen` — redesigned dialog: X close icon, selectable option cards ("Completed" / "Incomplete") with live counts, disabled state when a scope is empty, ✓ badge on selection, and a red destructive action button that adapts its label ("Delete Completed" / "Delete Incomplete" / "Delete All Tasks") and stays disabled until a scope is selected
- `TasksViewModel` — exposes `taskCounts` StateFlow for the dialog

### Verification
- Unit tests pass
- Release APK installed on device: Hilt DI, Room read/write, navigation, task creation all work — no crashes, no ClassNotFound/NoSuchMethod
- Reminder flow verified end-to-end: WorkManager job enqueued, `ReminderWorker` executed, notification posted
- R8 obfuscation confirmed working (single-letter class names visible in logs)
- Delete dialog verified on device with live counts (12 tasks → Completed 4 / Incomplete 8)

title: Fix Play Store release notes upload

title: Fix/live result on tall narrow screens
fix: show live result on tall screens below the sw360dp floor
body:
Compact mode is picked purely from resource qualifiers, and every layout that shows the result view is gated behind an sw qualifier. A device whose smallestWidth lands under 360dp therefore falls through to base layout/, which hides the result — no matter how much vertical space it has.

A OnePlus 11R (1240x2772 @ 560dpi) resolves to sw354dp/h792dp: it misses the sw360dp floor by 6dp and gets compact mode with 792dp of height.

Add an unqualified layout-h500dp/ so the height qualifier can apply on its own. Wider devices are unaffected — sw-qualified configs still win the smallestWidth step and eliminate this one before height is evaluated.

Verified on a OnePlus 11R: the result view is now in the hierarchy and updates live as the expression is typed.

title: fix: keep @HiltAndroidApp class in R8 to prevent release crash
body:
## Summary

- Adds a ProGuard keep rule for classes annotated with `@HiltAndroidApp`
- Fixes a crash on app launch in release builds where R8 was breaking Hilt's `GeneratedComponentManagerHolder` instanceof check

## Root Cause

When R8 minification was enabled, it could rename or inline Hilt-generated superclasses. At runtime, `ActivityComponentManager.createComponent()` checks `application instanceof GeneratedComponentManagerHolder` — if Hilt's generated `Hilt_MainApplication` class was affected by R8, this check fails with:

```
IllegalStateException: Hilt Activity must be attached to an @HiltAndroidApp Application.
```

## Fix

Added to `proguard-rules.pro`:
```proguard
-keep @dagger.hilt.android.HiltAndroidApp class * { *; }
```

Closes #72

## Test plan

- [ ] Build a release APK (`./gradlew assembleRelease`) and verify it launches without crashing
- [ ] Run unit tests: `./gradlew test`

On Android 16 (API 36), theme attribute resolution is stricter and throws an `InflateException` instead of failing silently.

title: Fix negative base exponentiation for even exponents
body:
Fixed incorrect calculation when raising negative numbers to even powers. The calculator was incorrectly returning negative results for expressions like `(-2)^10`, which should evaluate to positive values according to mathematical rules.

## Problem
When calculating `(-2)^10`, the calculator returned `-1024` instead of the correct answer `1024`. This occurred because the `solvePower` function always applied a negative sign to results when the base was negative, regardless of whether the exponent was even or odd.

## Solution
Modified the `solvePower` function in `NumberFormat.kt` to implement correct mathematical rules:

- **Negative base + even exponent = positive result** (e.g., `(-2)^10 = 1024`)
- **Negative base + odd exponent = negative result** (e.g., `(-2)^3 = -8`)
- **Positive base + any exponent = positive result** (existing behavior preserved)

The fix uses `BigDecimalMath.pow(num1.abs(), num2, precision)` to calculate the absolute result, then applies the correct sign based on exponent parity using `num2.remainder(BigDecimal.valueOf(2))`.

## Key Changes
- Updated power calculation logic to handle negative bases correctly
- Added support for fractional exponents with negative bases
- Preserved existing behavior for positive bases and special cases (exponent 0, 1)
- Added comprehensive test coverage with 14 new test cases

## Test Cases Added
```kotlin
// Core issue case
assertEquals("1024", roundMyAnswer(getResult("(-2)^10", deg))) // Even: positive

// Additional coverage
assertEquals("-8", roundMyAnswer(getResult("(-2)^3", deg)))   // Odd: negative
assertEquals("4", roundMyAnswer(getResult("(-2)^2", deg)))    // Even: positive
assertEquals("1", roundMyAnswer(getResult("(-1)^2", deg)))    // Edge case
assertEquals("-1", roundMyAnswer(getResult("(-1)^3", deg)))   // Edge case
```

Fixes #55.

title: fix(update): 自建更新节点跟随服务端迁移改用 HTTPS
body:
## Summary

- Fixes #115 — `IllegalStateException: CLEARTEXT-only client` crash on the update-check background thread.
- 自建更新元数据入口 `http://yyh163.xyz:10000/` 之前被单独授予 `ConnectionSpec.CLEARTEXT`（仅明文）连接规格。服务端已迁移到 HTTPS 后，该端口只讲 TLS，客户端却仍以「仅明文」的连接规格去连接，OkHttp 判定无法满足 TLS 需求，抛出未捕获的 `IllegalStateException("CLEARTEXT-only client")`，导致更新检查所在的后台线程崩溃。
- 将 `SELF_HOSTED_UPDATE_BASE_URL` 改为 `https://yyh163.xyz:10000/`，并移除现已多余的明文连接特例（`buildUpdateMetadataConnectionSpecs`、`isAuthorizedCleartextMetadataUrl`、`SELF_HOSTED_UPDATE_VERSION_URL`），所有更新节点统一走 `buildUpdateConnectionSpecs()`（仅 `MODERN_TLS`/`COMPATIBLE_TLS`）。
- `isExpectedUpdateMetadataResponseUrl` 的重定向来源校验相应简化为只允许 HTTPS。
- `UpdateRepository.createApi()` 去掉了对每个节点单独设置连接规格的多余调用（现在所有节点共用 base client 的 TLS-only 规格）。

## Issue #115 验收清单

- [x] 添加针对（现已改为 HTTPS 的）自建端点的正常请求测试 —— `UpdateClientTlsRegressionTest`：使用真实 `OkHttpClient` + `MockWebServer`（TLS 证书）验证统一的 TLS-only 连接规格可以正常完成自建端点请求。
- [x] 添加 HTTP → HTTPS（协议切换）相关测试 —— 同一测试类中：a) 端到端复现根因，`ConnectionSpec.CLEARTEXT`-only 客户端连接真实 TLS 服务端会立即失败；b) 验证跟随同源 HTTPS 跳转时统一连接规格仍能正常完成请求；c) `UpdateNetworkPolicyTest` 中的重定向来源校验测试已改为断言拒绝协议降级（https → http）。
- [x] 添加 self-hosted endpoint 不可用时的 fallback 测试 —— 此前已有 `UpdateEndpointFailoverTest.自建服务失败后继续从 GitHub Raw 获取更新` 覆盖，本次又补充一条节点抛出 `IllegalStateException` 时同样按策略 fallback 的用例。
- [x] 确认 `IllegalStateException` 不会导致进程崩溃 —— 新增 `UpdateEndpointFailoverTest.自建端点抛出 IllegalStateException 时按策略继续 fallback 而不会逃逸`，验证我们自己的调度逻辑（`resolveUpdateInfoFromEndpoints`）会把该异常当作普通节点失败处理并继续下一个节点，不会让其穿透到调用方。**补充说明**：OkHttp 异步 `enqueue()` 内部对非 `IOException` 的 `Throwable` 会在其自身的 Dispatcher 线程池线程上重新抛出（这是 OkHttp 自身机制，不受调用方 try/catch 影响），因此真正防止本次崩溃的关键是**根因修复本身**（消除连接规格与协议不匹配的场景），而不是任何一层 catch 块——这也是本 PR 选择直接改用 HTTPS、而不是仅靠异常处理兜底的原因。
- [ ] 在 Android 16 / API 36 真机或模拟器回归更新检查 —— 需要真实设备/模拟器，当前沙盒环境无法完成，请在 CI 或本地设备上验证。

## Test plan

- [x] 更新 `UpdateNetworkPolicyTest.kt`：移除针对已删除明文特例的用例，改为断言所有更新节点均为 HTTPS，并将重定向校验测试改为 HTTPS 场景。
- [x] 新增 `UpdateClientTlsRegressionTest.kt`（真实 OkHttp + MockWebServer + TLS 证书）与 `UpdateEndpointFailoverTest.kt` 中的 `IllegalStateException` fallback 用例。
- [ ] `./gradlew :feature:update:testDebugUnitTest`（当前沙盒环境无法访问 Google/AGP 插件仓库，未能在本地执行；已逐个对照 OkHttp/MockWebServer/okhttp-tls 4.12.0 的实际字节码核对过所有新增测试用到的 API 签名，但仍请在 CI 中确认实际编译与运行通过）。
- [ ] Android 16 / API 36 真机或模拟器回归更新检查流程。

title: fix(import): 修复只上一周的课程识别/显示失败 (#109)
body:
关闭 #109

## 问题

从教务系统（正方/新正方、强智、青果、kingosoft）导入课表后，**只上一周**的课程（"形势与政策"是典型例子）会静默丢失。

## 根因（一条链路上的多处 + 两个渲染缺陷）

| # | 位置 | 问题 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `common_parser_utils.js` `extractWeeksStr` | 唯一不带"周数"前缀的分支是"区间"正则，要求两个短横连接的数字，单周永远匹配不上；贪婪 `[^\s]*` 还会吞进节次文本 |
| 2 | `common_parser_utils.js` `parseWeeks` | 按 `-` 拆区间前只去 `周()` 不去节次文本：`"9周(1-2节)"` → `"91-2节"` → `91..2` 空区间 → `weeks=[]` → 整行被丢。区间课带垃圾数据存活，形成"只有单周课消失"的现象。也只去 `周` 不去 `第` |
| 3 | `zhengfang.js` `parseOldTimeRanges` | 把 `,` 当 `-`，`"1,3,5周"` 被拆成多段，`ranges` 分组数既非 1 也非 2 → 整行被丢 |
| 4 | 所有解析器 | 丢弃候选行时无任何日志/诊断 |
| 5 | `QiangZhiApiEngine` | `parseAndAddCourse` 用严格 `toIntOrNull`，`"5周"`/`"第5周"` 直接被拒；`parseApiCourses` 单/双过滤把偶数周里误标"单"的单周课过滤成空 |
| 6 | `TimetableLayoutEngine` | 每个 `(星期,起始节次)` 格子只吐一门课，单周课与整学期课占同格时，即使在它上课那一周也不显示 |
| 7 | `TimetableScreen` | 用全局 `settings.totalWeeks` 判定假期页，单周课落在第 N 周且 N > totalWeeks 时会被假期页挡住、周次选择器也选不到 |

Kotlin 侧 `splitWeeks`/`buildWeekRange` 本身正确（`[9]` → `WeekRange(9,9,0)`），未改逻辑，只补测试。

## 改动

**JS 解析器**：重写 `parseWeeks`（先剥离括号/`第`/节次噪声再拆区间，容错写反的区间，钳制 `1..53`，去重排序）与 `extractWeeksStr`（周数上限 `[0-9]{1,2}`、去掉贪婪捕获、新增 `"周次:5"` 和独立单周分支）；`zhengfang.js` 删除与 common 逐字节相同的本地副本改用加固版；`parseOldTimeRanges` 区分 `-` 与 `,`；新增 `reportDropped(reason)` 诊断（仅固定短码，不含页面内容），`ScriptEngine` → `ImportViewModel` 汇总成"N 条记录被跳过"提示。`common_parser_utils.js` 加载失败时不再硬跑解析器。

**强智 Kotlin 引擎**：`parseWeekString` 截断括号后缀；`parseAndAddCourse` 改用它；单/双过滤改为非破坏性（过滤后为空则保留原周次）。

**课表渲染**：`prepareRawDisplayList` 本周有效课程从"取第一门"改为"全部吐出"，交给已有的重叠簇分栏逻辑并排显示；`maxWeeks` 取 `settings.totalWeeks` 与课程最大结束周的较大值。

**测试**：新增 `feature/import/src/test/js/parse_weeks.test.cjs`（纯 Node 零依赖，50 条断言），Gradle 任务 `:feature:import:jsParserTest` 挂在 `testDebugUnitTest` / `check` 上，CI 自动执行。新增 `SplitWeeksTest`（7）、`QiangZhiApiEngineWeekTest`（3）JVM 单测。

**文档**：`parser_contribution_guide.md` 补单周约定 / 空 weeks 会被丢弃 / `reportDropped` 用法 / JS 测试位置；README 提示改内置解析器需同步云端同名脚本。

## 验证

- `:feature:import:jsParserTest`（50/0）+ `testDebugUnitTest`（import 10、timetable 2、domain 9 全过）+ `lintDebug` + `assembleDebug` 本地全绿。
- 反馈者未提供页面代码，本次按全面防御处理；若仍有个别格式无法识别，导入页现在会提示被跳过的条数，便于二次反馈。

## 注意

- **第 6 项的视觉变化**：以前被隐藏的同格重叠（含误导入的重复课）现在会渲染成更窄的并排卡片。
- 修改的是内置兜底解析器；云端同名脚本（`server/html/scripts/js/`，不在本仓库）需同步打相同补丁或提升版本号。

title: fix(startup): 修复冷启动白屏闪退（App Startup 与 WorkManager 初始化竞态）
body:
问题现象：部分机型（iQOO/OriginOS）打开 App 极大概率白屏后闪退，
小米真机与模拟器无法复现。

根因：
WidgetSyncInitializer 通过 androidx.startup 在 InitializationProvider.onCreate()
中执行，该时机早于 Application.onCreate()。它把初始化工作抛到
CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Default) 中，且 dependencies() 返回 emptyList()，
未声明对 WorkManagerInitializer 的依赖。

WorkManager 挂载在同一个 InitializationProvider 上，于是后台线程调用
WorkManager.getInstance() 与主线程执行 WorkManagerInitializer 形成竞态。
当后台线程先到时，因 DawnApp 未实现 Configuration.Provider，
getInstance() 抛出 IllegalStateException；该协程既无 try/catch
也无 CoroutineExceptionHandler，异常冒泡至默认
Thread.UncaughtExceptionHandler，直接杀死进程。

竞速结果取决于冷启动瞬间主线程的调度情况，因此表现为“概率性”且强依赖 ROM。

另外，启动主题 Theme.DawnCourse 继承自 android:Theme.Material.Light.NoActionBar，
既非 Theme.SplashScreen 后代也未声明 postSplashScreenTheme，
导致 installSplashScreen() 无法接管启动窗口，进程被杀前用户看到的是白色
windowBackground，即“白屏”。

修复内容：
- WidgetSyncInitializer 声明依赖 WorkManagerInitializer，消除初始化竞态；
  并挂载 CoroutineExceptionHandler + SupervisorJob，杜绝异常杀进程
- WidgetSyncManager.scheduleUpdate/cancelUpdate 增加 runCatching 兜底
- registerTimeChangeReceiver 改用 ContextCompat.registerReceiver 并显式声明
  RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED，修复 targetSdk 34 下动态注册缺少导出标记的问题
- 新增 Theme.DawnCourse.Starting（继承 Theme.SplashScreen）作为启动主题，
  并补充 values-night 主题与 windowBackground 颜色，消除深浅色模式启动白屏
- DawnTheme 对 dynamic*ColorScheme() 增加兜底，OEM ROM 缺失 system_* 资源时
  回退内置配色，避免首帧组合崩溃
- MainActivity 将 getPackageInfo 移出 composable 作用域，避免每次重组
  在主线程重复发起 Binder IPC

title: fix(startup): 修复 iQOO/OriginOS 冷启动白屏闪退（App Startup 与 WorkManager 初始化竞态）
body:
## 背景

部分机型（iQOO / OriginOS）打开 App **极大概率白屏后闪退**，小米真机与模拟器无法复现。

## 根因

1. **冷启动初始化竞态**：`WidgetSyncInitializer` 经 `androidx.startup` 在 `Application.onCreate()` 之前执行，`dependencies()` 返回空列表、未声明对 `WorkManagerInitializer` 的依赖。后台线程 `WorkManager.getInstance()` 与主线程 `WorkManagerInitializer` 形成竞态；后台线程先到时，因 `DawnApp` 未实现 `Configuration.Provider`，`getInstance()` 抛 `IllegalStateException`，协程无 `try/catch` 也无 `CoroutineExceptionHandler`，异常冒泡至默认 `UncaughtExceptionHandler` 直接杀进程。结果强依赖 ROM 调度，表现为「概率性」。
2. **启动白屏**：启动主题 `Theme.DawnCourse` 继承自 `android:Theme.Material.Light.NoActionBar`，既非 `Theme.SplashScreen` 后代也未声明 `postSplashScreenTheme`，`installSplashScreen()` 无法接管启动窗口，进程被杀前用户看到的是白色 `windowBackground`。
3. **动态取色首帧崩溃**：`dynamic*ColorScheme()` 读取约 65 个 `system_*` 系统资源，部分第三方 ROM 缺失会抛 `Resources.NotFoundException`，直接让首帧组合崩溃。

## 改动

| 提交 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `6c80086` fix(startup) | `WidgetSyncInitializer` 声明依赖 `WorkManagerInitializer` 消除竞态 + `CoroutineExceptionHandler`/`SupervisorJob`；新增 `Theme.DawnCourse.Starting`（继承 `Theme.SplashScreen`）+ `values-night` + 显式 `windowBackground`；`DawnTheme` 对 `dynamic*ColorScheme()` 加 `runCatching` 兜底；`registerTimeChangeReceiver` 改用 `ContextCompat.registerReceiver` 显式 `RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED`；`MainActivity` 把 `getPackageInfo` 移出 composable 作用域 |
| `a285c97` fix(widget) | 小组件后台协程异常不再升级为进程崩溃 |
| `1f1d24c` fix(crash) | 新增本地崩溃捕获（`CrashReporter`，不联网、不上报，下次启动弹窗展示）；补齐 `ReminderReceiver` / `SilenceReceiver` / `WebDavAutoSyncWorker` 等启动路径无兜底崩溃点 |
| `74e9fc5` fix(deps) | 移除无用的 SQLCipher 依赖；`ScriptEngine` 加固 QuickJS 16KB 页对齐容错 |

## 真机验证（iQOO Z1 / V1986A / Android 12 / Funtouch 13）

- 冷启动 ×10（浅色）：10/10 存活，无白屏，无 `FATAL EXCEPTION`
- `pm clear` 后首次冷启动 ×6（深色，最易触发竞态的场景）：6/6 存活
- `files/crash/last_crash.txt` 从未写入
- WorkManager Job 已调度且 `4x successful_finish` —— 确认已越过原先抛异常的 `getInstance()`
- 启动主题 → 课表页在浅色/深色下均正常渲染，无白屏闪烁
- 开启「动态取色 (Material You)」后重启：正常，无崩溃

> 白屏闪退在 iQOO Z1 上无法再复现。

## 合并方式

按 issue 作者要求：**开放审核 + 等 CI，手动合并。**

This ensures JavaScript running within the WebView cannot access `content://` URIs, reducing the risk of exposing protected content through a malicious or compromised page.

In this file, the only relevant piece of information is the use of a `webView` instance around line 744, which implies there is code (not shown) that creates/configures this WebView, likely via `AndroidView` earlier in `ImportScreen.kt`. Since we cannot see that block, but we can edit anywhere in this file, we should add a small helper function that hardens a `WebView` and then call it immediately after the `WebView` is created (in the existing AndroidView factory). That way, existing functionality is preserved and only security-related defaults are tightened.

title: fix: resolve AGP 7.x crash (#16) and AGP 8 config/cleanup/runtime issues (#17)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #16 and #17.

### Issue #16 — AGP 7.x crash (`onVariants$default` NoSuchMethodError)

**Root cause:** `Agp8Compat.isAgp8OrHigher()` detected "AGP 8+" by checking whether `com.android.build.api.instrumentation.AsmClassVisitorFactory` exists on the classpath — but that class has existed **since AGP 7.0**. On AGP 7.2.2 the check returned `true`, so the plugin entered the Instrumentation-API branch and invoked `AndroidComponentsExtension.onVariants`, a Kotlin method with default arguments whose synthetic `onVariants$default` bridge does not exist on AGP 7.x → `NoSuchMethodError`.

**Fix:** judge by the real AGP version (`com.android.Version.ANDROID_GRADLE_PLUGIN_VERSION`, major >= 8) instead of class presence. AGP 7.x now correctly falls back to the Transform-API branch.

### Issue #17 — AGP 8.7.0 config error + runtime StackOverflow + leftover junk code

Three distinct problems:

1. **Unknown property `generatedMethodCount`** — the extension's property names did not match the docs / `toString()` output:
   - `generatedMethodCount` vs real `generatedClassMethodCount`
   - `isAutoAdapted` vs real `isInsertCountAutoAdapted`
   - `isSkipJarFilesProcessing` / `isSkipJars` vs real `isSkipJar`
   - `mapperFile` vs real `mapper`
   - `obfuscationDictionary` vs real `obfuscationDict`

   Added backward-compatible alias getters/setters for all of them, and fixed `toString()` to print the real property names.

2. **Runtime `StackOverflowError`** (the repeating `com.filter.jobhunting.*` call stack) — on the AGP 8 branch, `CodeGuardClassVisitorFactory.isInstrumentable()` never excluded the plugin's **own generated decoy classes**, so those classes were instrumented again and their methods were injected with calls to each other, forming endless recursion. Added `AppCodeGuardConfig.isGeneratedClass()` and skip generated classes in `isInstrumentable()`.

3. **Generated junk code was never cleaned up on AGP 8** — the AGP 8 branch had no cleanup step (the AGP 7 branch does it in `transformTask.doLast`). Added a cleanup `doLast` on the `transform<Variant>ClassesWithAsm` instrumentation task, and fixed two path bugs in `AppCodeGuardConfig` that prevented deletion:
   - `getDeleteDir()` concatenated `mainDir + baseDir` without a separator (produced `.../codeguard/javacom/...`)
   - `batchDeleteGenClass()` derived the lookup key by searching for `src/main/java` in the file path, which no longer exists since generated classes moved to `build/generated/...` (commit 744ef0f)

## Verification

- 75 unit tests pass (14 new cases covering the aliases, `isGeneratedClass`, and AGP version detection)
- `:app:assembleDebug` builds successfully on AGP 8.0
- Generated decoy classes are packaged into the APK while their source files under `build/generated/codeguard/java` are deleted after the build
- Cleanup log confirms correct keys and paths: `batchDeleteGenClass, key => com.dorck.app.obfuscate.f.y.k.Ah is exist: false`, `deleteGenClass dir succeed: .../codeguard/java/com/dorck/app/obfuscate/f/`

title: Fix local file server: MIME types, reliable Range seeks, registry bound
body:
## Summary
- Serve real MIME types by file extension (mp4/mkv/avi/mov/ts/mp3/flac/...) instead of always `application/octet-stream` — some TVs refuse unknown content types
- Loop `InputStream.skip()` until the requested Range offset is fully skipped: a single `skip()` call may skip fewer bytes than requested, which started the HTTP body at the wrong offset and produced a corrupt stream after a seek
- Bound the token registry with an LRU cap of 64 entries — each cast mints a new token and the previous unbounded map leaked one entry per cast for the whole process lifetime

## Test plan
- [x] `./gradlew test lint assembleRelease` green locally
- [ ] Manual: cast a local mkv/mp4 and seek — needs a real TV

title: fix(engine): distinguish missing model from engine failure
body:
## Description

A background engine prewarm with no model on disk published `SttEngineState.Failed`, so the keyboard blanketed itself with **"Speech recognition could not start — Try loading the model again, or cancel to return"** and offered a Retry that could never succeed.

This fires at **onboarding step 3**, where the keyboard first becomes the active IME and the model download is still two steps away. Every new user hits a hard error before doing anything wrong. Found while validating #41 on an emulator (see #111).

```kotlin
val modelPath = modelManager.getModelPath(activeModelKey)
if (modelPath == null) {
    providerSlot.markFailed(activeModelKey)          // -> SttEngineState.Failed
    Timber.w("Engine prewarm failed: active model is not downloaded")
```

### Changes

- **`SttEngineState.ModelMissing`**, distinct from `Failed`. A missing model is a setup state, not an error. `prewarmActiveModel` publishes it through the new `SttProviderSlot.markModelMissing` and logs at info: `Engine prewarm skipped: model=%s is not downloaded yet`.
- **`PendingMicGate`** treats `ModelMissing` as *not pending*. Prewarming again cannot download a model, and leaving the intent pending would silently start recording on the next unrelated `Ready`.
- **The overlay no longer appears for a background prewarm.** It surfaces only when the user actually taps the mic, and then shows "No voice model yet / Download a voice model to start dictating." with a dismiss button and no useless Retry.

Strings added in EN and FR.

### Scope

This narrows but does not close the silent mic-tap problem: a tap with a missing `RECORD_AUDIO` permission or an unbound controller is still silent, and the keyboard still writes no log line for either. #112 stands.

## Validation

Pixel 4 API 29 emulator, clean install, Dictus enabled and selected at onboarding step 3 with no model downloaded:

- **Before:** the "Speech recognition could not start" overlay covered the keyboard on arrival at step 3.
- **After:** no overlay on arrival; the log reads `[I] Engine prewarm skipped: model=tiny is not downloaded yet`. Tapping the mic shows the "No voice model yet" panel, dismissible.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests pass (`./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`) — two added: `PendingMicGateTest.missing model neither prewarms nor keeps the intent pending`, `SttProviderSlotTest.undownloaded model publishes model-missing state, not a failure`
- [x] No new lint warnings — deferred to CI on this PR
- [x] Tested on device (emulator, screenshots in #111)

Refs #111

title: fix(ui): centre the bottom nav bar on the screen axis
body:
## Description

The bottom navigation bar was not centred on the screen axis: the middle tab sat about 14px left of centre, and the whole row shifted as the selected pill changed width.

`Arrangement.SpaceEvenly` distributes the *gaps* between items, not the items themselves. "Home", "Models" and "Settings" have different text widths, so equal gaps do not put the middle tab on the centre axis.

Each tab now occupies an equal 1/3 cell (`Modifier.weight(1f)`) and centres its pill inside it, so the middle tab is exactly centred regardless of label length. This matters beyond English: in French the labels are "Accueil" / "Modèles" / "Réglages", which drifted by a different amount.

## Validation

Pixel 4 API 29 emulator, screen width 947 in screenshot space:

- **Before:** Home 201, Models 456, Settings 726 — centre axis 473, so the middle tab was off by 17.
- **After:** Home 183, Models 473, Settings 762 — middle tab exactly on the axis, outer tabs symmetric at ±290.

title: fix(release): support validated beta tags
body:
## Problem

`v1.2.0-beta.1` currently becomes `PATCH=0-beta` and aborts Bash arithmetic, so the proposed beta cannot be built. Direct GitHub-expression interpolation would also make a naive parser repair unsafe.

## Approach

- add a strict standalone tag parser for final and `beta.N` tags
- derive monotonic Android codes with 1–998 reserved for beta and 999 for final
- reject malformed, oversized and Android-out-of-range values before arithmetic
- pass the tag through a quoted environment variable and validate it before decoding signing material
- add deterministic boundary/rejection tests

## Verification

- `.github/scripts/test-derive-android-version.sh` — PASS
- `git diff --cached --check` — PASS
- added-line security scan — clear
- first fresh review found expression injection and integer-overflow blockers; both fixed
- second fresh adversarial review: PASS, including shell-like/newline/10,000-digit inputs and boundary ordering

## Risk / exclusions

No tag, signing build, release, upload or public distribution was triggered. Existing final releases keep their versionName; future versionCodes intentionally move to a wider monotonic namespace above published code 10100.

Closes #105
Refs #33

## Summary

- leave Bluetooth SCO, communication mode, media controls, and output routing untouched
- fall back to Android default routing if no built-in input is exposed or the preference is rejected
- log only preference status and routed device type, never device names/addresses

`AudioCaptureManager` used `AudioSource.MIC` with platform-default input routing. With a connected headset, OEM/default behavior could select a low-quality Bluetooth SCO microphone even though Dictus intends iOS-parity built-in-mic capture quality.

## Verification

Exact commit `e1027bfc0c41dc0a07421e2464026593b40406bf` / exact APK installed on Pixel 4 (`flame`), Android 15, ARM64. Real microphone capture logged:

`inputPreference=BuiltInMicPreferenceAccepted, routedType=15`

This change affects only the recorder's preferred **input** device. It does not claim an acoustic comparison, Bluetooth playback/ducking result, wired-headset result, or media-key validation. Android can reject a preferred input; that case safely retains platform routing and is tested.

title: fix(recording): reject clips shorter than 500ms
body:
## Summary

- add a single 500 ms recording-duration policy for the 16 kHz capture pipeline
- reject sub-500 ms clips before model download/provider initialization
- stop `AudioRecord`, await the capture loop's final read, then snapshot samples
- cover below-boundary, exact-boundary, above-boundary, and delayed-final-read behavior

Closes #13

## Why

Whisper can hallucinate on extremely short clips. iOS accepts recordings from 0.5 s while rejecting anything shorter; Android previously sent every non-empty clip to STT. The capture shutdown also needed synchronization so the final blocking read could not race the 8,000-sample threshold.

## Verification

fix: support OAuth/Sign-in-with-Google popups on both engines
body:
Fixes #14

## Problem

"Sign in with Google" (and other OAuth/SSO flows) open their consent screen in a popup via `window.open()` / `target="_blank"`. Neither browser engine surfaced that popup, so sign-in could never complete — the site then falls back to a generic "cookies required" message (the symptom reported in #14 on System WebView).

- **System WebView** (the engine in the report): never overrode `WebChromeClient.onCreateWindow`, so the popup was silently dropped.
- **GeckoView**: `onNewSession` loaded the popup URL into the *main* session, navigating the page away and destroying the `window.opener` relationship the flow needs.

## Fix

Both engines now open a **real popup window** and surface it to the host:

- `WebViewManager` enables `setSupportMultipleWindows(true)` + `javaScriptCanOpenWindowsAutomatically`.
- `SystemWebViewEngine` overrides `onCreateWindow` (spawns a popup `WebView`) and `onCloseWindow` (dismisses it).
- `GeckoViewEngine.onNewSession` returns a **new unopened child `GeckoSession`** (per the GeckoView contract) built from the parent's settings, so it inherits the `contextId` and shares cookies/storage with the opener; `ContentDelegate.onCloseRequest` dismisses it.
- New `BrowserEngineCallback.onShowPopup`/`onClosePopup` and `BrowserEngine.closeTopPopup()`.
- `WebViewActivity` hosts popups as full-screen overlays. For System WebView popups it **re-applies the per-app isolation profile** so sign-in cookies land in the app's own store (Android 13+). Back-press dismisses the topmost popup first.

## Tests

Verified on a real arm64 emulator (incl. a real GeckoView runtime):

| Test | Engine | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `systemWebView_windowOpen_showsPopupOverlay_andBackDismisses` | Real System WebView | ✅ |
| `geckoView_windowOpen_showsPopupOverlay` | Real GeckoView (skips on CI via `assumeTrue(isInstalled())`) | ✅ |
| `popupHostingContract_showsAndRemovesOverlay` | Fake engine (shared host wiring) | ✅ |

Plus `ExternalSchemeTest` unit tests. `detekt`, `lintDebug`, `testDebugUnitTest` (+ Konsist) and `verifyRoborazziDebug` all pass.

## Note

Google additionally blocks OAuth inside embedded WebViews by user-agent (`disallowed_useragent`) for some sites; that is independent of this popup fix and would need a Custom Tab path if it surfaces.

title: fix(#268): add security on media file name
body:
This pull request changes the way media files uploaded from the gallery are set. 

Normally, the method `lastPathSegment` called from an URI object retrieves the last segment from the path, that is, the file name itself with extension. However, users reports showed that on certain phones (apparently Xiaomi), this method returns the full file path instead, resulting in subsequent errors when uploading medias from gallery.

We add a `substringAfterLast("/")` on the `uri.lastPathSegment` to make sure that only the file name is used.

Tested on two Xiaomi phones that experienced the bug : it seems fix
plus one other phone : no regression.

Fixes bug #268

title: Fix/compat text field crash
body:
## Summary

Fixes `KPCompatBasicTextField` production IME crash and two follow-up issues after the Foundation `BasicTextField` → platform `EditText` switch: keyboard not reopening on already-focused `FocusRequester` (Search “X” / clear), and text looking smaller than Compose because font scale was applied twice and `fontFamily` was ignored.

Public `KPCompatBasicTextField` API is unchanged. Android hosts do not need caller-side `view == null` guards.

### Technical Details
- Skip `KeyboardActions` when host lifecycle is below `CREATED` **or** the `EditText` is detached (`isAttachedToWindow`). Clear the editor-action listener and lifecycle ref in `AndroidView.onRelease` so delayed IME `Handler` callbacks cannot reach a destroyed Fragment (`viewLifecycleOwner` / `getView() == null`).
- Compose `hasFocus` and already-focused `requestFocus()` reshow the platform IME (`SHOW_IMPLICIT` via `safePost`). First focus still goes through `requestFocusAndShowKeyboard`; already-focused path avoids a double `safePost`. Empty-text `update` no longer forces IME (last-character delete must not pop the keyboard). Search clear remains `FocusRequester.requestFocus()` + empty value.
- `TextStyle.fontSize` is applied as Compose `toPx()` + `COMPLEX_UNIT_PX`. `fontFamily` / weight / style / synthesis resolve through `LocalFontFamilyResolver` with a safe `as? Typeface` cast. Style snapshot uses `fontFamily ==` and tracks `FontSynthesis`.

## Relevant domains

### Search
- Changes made: Compat editor used by Search header (`KPCompatBasicTextField`) no longer delivers IME Search after `onDestroyView`; “X” / `FocusRequester` reshows IME; font size/family match Compose.
- Reason: Crashlytics `IllegalStateException` on IME Search after view destroy; clear-button IME no-op; visual mismatch vs Foundation field.
- Impact: Any screen hosting this component (Search, Home, PDP, Category) gets the same lifecycle and IME behavior without app-side API changes.

## Structure

### Architecture
- Compose `AndroidView` + `SelectionAwareEditText` bridge (existing). Lifecycle-gated IME actions; focus forwarded from Compose `FocusRequester` / `onFocusChanged(hasFocus)` to platform `InputMethodManager`.
- Pure style mapping: `FontFamily.Resolver` → Android `Typeface`; size in px to match Compose density + fontScale.

### Dependencies
- No new dependencies
- No removed dependencies
- No version catalog bumps in this MR

## Unit tests

### Test Coverage Analysis
- Test Files Added/Modified:
  - `app/src/androidTest/java/compat/KPCompatBasicTextFieldInteractionTest.kt`
- Test Scenarios Covered:
  - IME Search when lifecycle is `DESTROYED` does not invoke `KeyboardActions`
  - IME Search when `EditText` is detached (lifecycle still `RESUMED`) does not invoke `KeyboardActions`
  - `FocusRequester` shows IME
  - Already-focused `FocusRequester` after IME hide reshows IME
  - Clear text + `FocusRequester` (Search X order) reshows IME
  - `fontSize` 16.sp matches Compose `toPx()` on `EditText.textSize`
  - `FontFamily.SansSerif` applied as `Typeface.SANS_SERIF`

## Notes
- Verify on device: Search IME Search after leaving the screen (no crash); tap X with field focused and keyboard hidden (text clears, IME returns); font size vs previous Foundation field at non-default system font scale.
- No screenshots in this MR (IME / lifecycle behavior).

## 📝 Pull Request Description

### What does this PR do?
Fixes an issue where `KPDropdown` was incorrectly triggering `onClick` during scroll gestures. The component now uses an overlay-based gesture detection approach that properly distinguishes between tap and scroll/drag interactions while maintaining full `interactionSource` compatibility.

- [x] Screenshot tests were not affected
- [ ] Screenshot tests were updated
- [ ] New screenshot tests were added

**Screenshot Changes Explained:**
N/A

---

## 🐛 Bug Fix Details

### Root Cause Analysis
The original implementation used `interactionSource.interactions.collect` to detect clicks:

```kotlin
interactionSource.interactions.collect {
    when (it) {
        is PressInteraction.Release,
        is PressInteraction.Cancel -> onClick.invoke()
    }
}
```

**Problem:** `PressInteraction.Cancel` is emitted during scroll gestures (when the user presses down on the dropdown and drags away). This caused `onClick` to be triggered unintentionally while scrolling through a list containing dropdowns.

**Additional complexity:** Simply removing `Cancel` handling didn't work because `BasicTextField` + `readOnly=true` emits `Cancel` instead of `Release` on long press (likely due to text selection attempt), breaking long press functionality.

### How was it fixed?
Replaced the `interactionSource` collection approach with an overlay-based gesture detection:

1. Added a transparent `Box` overlay on top of `KPOutlinedTextField`
2. Used `pointerInput` + `detectTapGestures` to handle touch events
3. `tryAwaitRelease()` returns `true` only when finger is lifted on the component (tap), `false` when dragged away (scroll)
4. Manually emit Press/Release/Cancel to `interactionSource` to maintain backward compatibility for visual feedback states

```kotlin
Box(
    modifier = Modifier
        .matchParentSize()
        .pointerInput(enabled, interactionSource) {
            if (!enabled) return@pointerInput
            detectTapGestures(
                onPress = { offset ->
                    val press = PressInteraction.Press(offset)
                    interactionSource.emit(press)

                    val released = tryAwaitRelease()
                    if (released) {
                        interactionSource.emit(PressInteraction.Release(press))
                        onClick()
                    } else {
                        interactionSource.emit(PressInteraction.Cancel(press))
                    }
                }
            )
        }
)
```

### Bug Fix Testing
- [x] Bug reproduction scenario
- [x] Edge cases specific to the bug
- [x] Regression testing

**New/Updated Tests:**
- `dropdown_singleClick_triggersOnClickOnce` - Normal click works
- `dropdown_longPress_triggersOnClickOnlyOnce` - Long press works
- `dropdown_pressAndDrag_doesNotTriggerOnClick` - Drag doesn't trigger onClick
- `dropdown_scrollGesture_doesNotTriggerOnClick` - Scroll doesn't trigger onClick
- `dropdown_multipleClicks_eachTriggersOnClickOnce` - Multiple clicks work
- `dropdown_pressWithoutCompletion_doesNotTriggerOnClick` - Incomplete press doesn't trigger
- `debugTest_whatInteractionsAreEmittedDuringLongPress` - Verifies interactionSource emissions

### Bug Fix Screenshots/Videos

**Before:**
Scrolling through a list with `KPDropdown` items would accidentally trigger `onClick`, opening the dropdown unexpectedly.

**After:**
Scroll gestures no longer trigger `onClick`. Only deliberate taps (finger lifted on the component) trigger the callback.

body:
## 📝 Pull Request Description

### What does this PR do?
<!--- Provide a clear and concise description of what this PR accomplishes -->
This PR adds interactionSource parameter to `KPDropdown` and sets a default. Default behavior is handling click and longClick. Also removed the `clickable` call from modifier because that seems to be unnecessary. But a peer review would be nice.

Unfortunately this change introduces a breaking change. We needed to move `onClick` parameter above the `Modifier` parameter because it's a required parameter and needed for `interactionSource`. Since this API was tagged with `ExperimentalKompostoApi` I couldn't see any reason to not change this. 

Also added some behavioral tests in order to test interactions.
