title: Fix Private DNS not turning back on after leaving a blacklisted network
body:
If you turn Private DNS on, connect to a wifi network that's in your blacklist (so it gets auto disabled), then leave that network, DNS should turn back on. In some cases it doesn't.

The app saves your preferred DNS mode once, the first time you open it, and uses that saved value to restore after leaving a blacklisted network. If your actual preference changes after that first launch, the restore can end up using the old saved value instead of your current one.

This updates it to save your preference every time you toggle DNS yourself, so the restore always reflects your latest choice. Added a test covering that scenario, plus making sure the auto blacklist path still doesn't touch it (that one's only supposed to affect the current network, not your global setting).

title: fix: let npm install packages built for Android
body:
The `.npmrc` the app writes on every launch set `os[]=linux` and `os[]=android`. npm's `os` setting takes one string, and the two lines gave it the array `linux,android`, which npm-install-checks compares with each entry of a package's `os` list by `===` and never matches. Every optional dependency whose `os` list names a platform it supports was skipped, including the android-arm64 bindings of Rollup, Rolldown, Lightning CSS and oxlint, and a Vite 8 project stopped at "Cannot find native binding". Only packages whose list merely excludes platforms, such as `sass-embedded-unknown-all` (`!android`, `!darwin`, `!linux`, `!win32`), got through.

Changes:

- `FirstRunSetup.createNpmWrappers` writes `os=android` instead of the two `os[]` lines. npm runs with `process.platform` reading `linux` (`platform-fix.js`, which the `npm` shell function opts into with `VSCODROID_PLATFORM_FIX=1`), so leaving `os` unset would pick linux builds that declare no libc, which do not run here, and still no binding for rollup, rolldown or lightningcss, whose linux builds declare a libc npm cannot detect here.
- The old `os[]=linux` and `os[]=android` lines stay owned, so the first launch after an upgrade removes them. Left in place after the new line, they would reopen the array and npm would read `android,linux,android` (measured with npm 10.8.2 and 11.16.0).
- Only the exact `os=android` line is owned. An `os=` the user sets with `npm config set` is carried through after it, and npm takes the last value of a repeated key, so the user's choice still wins.
- `BashrcAtomicityTest`: the owned-keys and fresh-file cases now expect `os=android`; new cases pin the migration of a file an earlier release wrote and the carry-through of a user's `os`.
- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md`: React and Vite steps that run on the device (create-vite, and the template's `dev`, `build`, `preview` and `lint` scripts rewritten to start Vite and oxlint through `node`), which npm and npx forms fail and why, a Dev Server Preview step that names such a `dev` script, and a correction that esbuild does not install.
- `docs/DEVICE_TEST_CHECKLIST.md`: the Vite dev server start row (PF-9) runs Vite through `node` instead of `npx vite`, which exits 126.
- CHANGELOG entry under Fixed.

Every optional package whose `os` list names `android`, and whose `cpu` list allows arm64, now installs, not only the four bindings above. The libraries among them (Rollup, Rolldown, Lightning CSS, oxlint) load and work. The programs among them still cannot run from the app's storage, so they fail when run:

- `sass-embedded` gets `sass-embedded-android-arm64` and tries to run its Dart binary. It used to get `sass-embedded-unknown-all`, which excludes android and is no longer picked, and stop in its pure JS fallback with "sass --embedded is unavailable in pure JS mode.". Plain `sass` works either way.
- Linux builds whose `os` list also names android now land: `@turbo/linux-arm64` (`android`, `linux`), a 34 MiB executable, and `@sentry/cli-linux-arm64` (`linux`, `freebsd`, `android`). turbo's launcher maps android to linux and spawns that binary, so turbo started through `node` now fails when the exec is refused, where before it failed in its own just-in-time `npm install`. `@sentry/cli`'s postinstall exits 0 once the platform package resolves; before, it downloaded the binary and ran `--version`, which the app's storage refuses, so a project depending on it now installs and fails only when `sentry-cli` runs.
- None of the packages checked installs worse than before. Which packages land was measured on the host with npm 11.16.0 and `process.platform` forced to linux, as on the device; what sass-embedded, turbo and sentry-cli do after installing is read from their code (and for sass-embedded run on the host), not run on a device.

Still failing after this change, unchanged by it: anything that starts a package's program from the app's storage, which Android refuses to execute. That covers `npx <tool>`, `npm create`, `npm init <initializer>`, and `package.json` scripts such as `"dev": "vite"`, which npm starts through the file in `node_modules/.bin`; all exit 126 with `Permission denied` (`/usr/bin/env: bad interpreter: Permission denied` when the program is a `#!` script). esbuild still does not install, because its install step executes its binary (`spawnSync ... EACCES`), and Vite 7 and older fail with it. The guide documents the `node node_modules/...` form for the first group.

Verification:

- `./gradlew --offline :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug`: 2643 tests pass, lint reports no new issues. Against the previous `FirstRunSetup`, four `BashrcAtomicityTest` cases fail; the migration case reports `os[]=linux\nos[]=android\nregistry=https://x.example/\nos=android` where one `os=android` is expected.
- Releases ship npm 11.16.0 (`scripts/download-npm.sh`); the emulator runs below used npm 10.8.2 from a local assets tree. On the host, with `process.platform` forced to linux, both versions pick the same packages for rollup, lightningcss and sass-embedded: no binding, no binding and `sass-embedded-unknown-all` with the old lines; `@rollup/rollup-android-arm64`, `lightningcss-android-arm64` and `sass-embedded-android-arm64` with `os=android`. Under 11.16.0 the create-vite 9.2.1 React template gets the rolldown, lightningcss and oxlint android bindings with the new file and none with the old.
- On an API 36 emulator, npm 10.8.2, in the app's own terminal (`untrusted_app`), with the old `.npmrc` and with the new one in fresh projects under `~/projects`:

| Package | Old `.npmrc` | `os=android` |
|---|---|---|
| React + Vite 8.3.2 | no binding; `node node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js build` fails, "Cannot find native binding" | `@rolldown/binding-android-arm64`, `lightningcss-android-arm64`; builds, dev server answers 200 |
| rollup | no binding; fails to load | `@rollup/rollup-android-arm64`; `node node_modules/rollup/dist/bin/rollup --version` prints v4.63.6 |
| lightningcss | no binding; fails to load | `lightningcss-android-arm64`; transforms CSS |
| esbuild | install fails (EACCES running its binary) | install fails (EACCES running its binary) |
| workerd (linux-only build) | not installed | not installed; with `os=linux` it lands and its launcher refuses `android arm64 LE` |

- The guide's React steps run end to end with the new `.npmrc`: create-vite 9.2.1 scaffolds, `npm install` adds the rolldown, lightningcss and oxlint bindings, `npm run build` and `npm run lint` pass, and `npm run dev` serves the page with 200.
- With a build of this branch over main (alongside two unrelated fixes), installed over the previous build on the API 33 and API 36 emulators: after setup `~/.npmrc` holds the `script-shell` line and `os=android`, with no `os[]` line, and `npm config get os` prints `android`. On API 36, `npm install rollup` in a fresh project exited 0 with `@rollup/rollup-android-arm64` installed, and `node node_modules/rollup/dist/bin/rollup --version` printed `rollup v4.63.6`.
- Not run: npm 11.16.0 on a device, and the guide's `preview` script, which starts the same `vite.js` as `dev`.

title: fix: keep a hidden keyboard hidden
body:
The keyboard guard holds the soft keyboard down with `inputmode="none"` on the editor's editing host until a tap on text. Once a tap had let it up, putting it away with Back or the navigation bar's hide key left the host focused and without `inputmode`, and Chromium raises the keyboard again for any touch on a focused editable element, so the next scroll of the file brought it back. A read-only file did not help either: File: Toggle Active Editor Read-only in Session stops edits, but a tap on text still raised the keyboard.

Changes:

- `MainActivity.injectKeyboardGuard` defines `window.__vscodroidKeyboardDismissed`, which clears `aimedAtText` and puts `inputmode="none"` back on every editing host that is not composing. `setupExtraKeyRow` calls it from `ExtraKeyRow.onImeVisibilityChanged` when the keyboard goes down, and only then. It only ever writes `inputmode="none"` and never refocuses, so it cannot raise the keyboard or loop with the guard, and after a keyboard the guard itself took down it writes nothing.
- The same script never lets the keyboard up for a read-only editor. `writable()` reads `aria-autocomplete`, which Monaco's ScreenReaderSupport sets to `"none"` on the EditContext host from the readOnly option and rewrites on every option change, and gates the three places that remove `inputmode` or refocus: `apply()`, `letTheKeyboardUp()` and the `focusin` handler. The textarea edit path, where the value is written only when the host is created, is not gated and behaves as before.
- `KeyboardGuardWiringTest` holds the Kotlin call to the keyboard going down, and checks the packaged `workbench.js`, when the tree is present, for the marker being written from the readOnly option and rewritten on an option change.
- `scripts/test-keyboard-guard.js` gains 10 cases, 53 in all.
- The `injectKeyboardGuard` KDoc said a tap inside the editor but off the text leaves the keyboard down, and a comment said the scrollbar raises it. With the editor focused, a tap under the last line raises it, and a tap on the scrollbar moves focus off the editor and leaves it down; both now say so.
- Technical spec section 5.2, the testing strategy row, a User Guide entry, two CHANGELOG entries, and checklist row KB-33, whose last step turns the phone while typing.

Impact:

- In a read-only file the soft keyboard no longer comes up, so the extra key row, which shows only with it, is out of reach there: no Shift with the trackpad to select. Copy and Select All stay in the long-press menu.
- Not covered: a keyboard that keeps a word composing after it hides, since the hold is never put back on a composing host, and a floating keyboard that reports no IME insets.
- On an API 36 emulator a rotation reports the keyboard down and, about 350 ms later, up again, so the hook puts the hold back in between. Measured there (Gboard 18.2): after turning to landscape and back the keyboard was up and the next letter landed at the caret. Switching keyboards with the globe key and leaving the app with the keyboard up may report the same down and up, and were not measured.

Verification:

- `node scripts/test-keyboard-guard.js`: 53/53. Against the guard on main, 45/53: the 8 new cases fail and the two controls, a writable editor and the textarea path, pass. Each of ten edits to the guard fails at least one case: each of the three `writable()` gates removed, its `editContext` test removed, `writable()` always true, and the hook keeping `aimedAtText`, skipping `applyAll()`, writing `inputmode` under a composing word or over one already `none`, or adding a blur and refocus.
- `KeyboardGuardWiringTest`: 8/8 with the packaged 1.139.1 tree. The marker case fails for each of five edits to a copy of `workbench.js`: the marker written as `"both"`, written from another option, not rewritten in `onConfigurationChanged`, not forwarded from the EditContext, and the readOnly option declared twice.
- `./gradlew --offline :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug`: 2643 tests, 0 failed, 0 skipped; lint reports no new issues. Every `lint.yml` Python gate, `device-test.sh --self-check` and all 13 `node scripts/test-*.js` pass.
- On an API 33 emulator with Gboard 12.4, running debug builds of this branch whose guard differs from the head only in comments: a tap under the last line put the caret there with the keyboard up; a tap on the scrollbar left it down, with focus off the editor; after a tap on a word, Back or the navigation bar's hide key, then a drag and a fling, left the keyboard down and a tap on a word raised it, while the same scroll with the hook replaced over DevTools raised it; Back while a word was underlined ended the word and the hold came back; typing after a tap while a word was underlined kept the text intact; turning the phone with the keyboard up never reported it down. With the file read-only in session, a tap on a word moved the caret with the keyboard down and a long press opened the menu with Copy and Select All; set writable again, a tap raised it. The Explorer's rename and New File boxes raised the keyboard as before.
- Again with a build of the final head over main (alongside two unrelated fixes), from an upgrade install: on the API 33 emulator (Gboard 12.4) Back and the hide key then a drag and two flings left the keyboard down and a tap on a word raised it; read-only in session held it down with the caret moving and the menu offering Copy and Select All, and writable again a tap raised it; Rename and New File raised it; a word retyped so it was underlined, then End and `x`, gave the line plus `x` with no suggestion list; and a rotation to landscape and back with the keyboard up kept it up, with the next letter at the caret. On a Pixel 10 API 36 emulator (Gboard 18.2.4) the Back, hide key and read-only sequences behaved the same, and after a rotation to landscape and back the keyboard was up and the next letter landed at the caret.
- Not measured: physical phones, `files.readonlyInclude` (it reaches the same editor option, read from the bundle), the Output panel (its editor is always read-only and is held the same way, read from the bundle), a hardware keyboard, floating or split keyboards, and keyboards other than Gboard.

title: fix: warn when shared storage hides a folder's files
body:
VSCodroid holds no storage permission, so Android lets it list every directory on shared storage and hides every file another app saved there. File > Open Folder and Add Folder to Workspace reach `/storage/emulated/0/...` and `/sdcard/...` by path, so such a folder opens with its subfolders and none of its files, with nothing on screen to say why. Open Folder from Device, the route that shows those files, was reachable only from the Command Palette and, one step removed, from Open Recent Folder.

- The bridge extension warns once per folder, on activation and when workspace folders change, for a workspace folder on shared storage (`/storage/emulated/<user>`, `/storage/self/primary`, `/sdcard`, `/mnt/sdcard`, or an SD card under `/storage/<id>`), and offers a button that runs **VSCodroid: Open Folder from Device**. The warning also says what that route leaves out: files over 50 MB and folders such as `.git` and `node_modules`.
- Not warned about: the app's own `Android/data/<package>/` at the top of a volume, matched in any case since shared storage ignores case, and device-folder copies under the app's files directory. Every file in them is visible. An `Android/data` deeper in a folder, such as `Documents/backup/Android/data/foo`, is warned about.
- Android's folder picker will not grant the top of a volume, its `Download` folder or its `Android` folder. For those the warning says to pick a folder inside instead, and the top of the storage is called "your device storage" rather than `0`.
- **Don't Show Again** silences a folder by path in the extension's global state, for a folder the user works in knowingly, such as one whose files the app made itself. Without it, a folder reopened at launch raised the warning on every start.
- **VSCodroid: Open Folder from Device** is added to the remote indicator menu, and the Explorer with no folder open gets a `viewsWelcome` entry linking to it, translated in all 14 bundles.
- The extension moves from 1.9.0 to 1.10.0 (directory, `package.json`, `MILESTONES.md`), so upgraded installs rescan its manifest.
- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md`: Opening Files and Folders said the dialog cannot reach Documents, Downloads or an SD card. It reaches them and shows none of the files other apps saved there. The section now says so, names the three ways to Open Folder from Device, says which folders the picker will not grant, and states what a device folder's copy leaves out. The VSIX steps are corrected the same way and no longer tell the user to grant the Download folder, where a browser usually saves.
- `docs/DEVICE_TEST_CHECKLIST.md`: SF-20 and SF-21 cover the warning, its buttons and the two new entry points.
- CHANGELOG entries under Added.

The Explorer still shows the mirror's hash (for example `8e440ff38c8e`) as the root name of a device folder. Showing the real name would need a workspace file or a renamed mirror, and either one touches `folderFromUrl`, adoption, `mirrorNameFor`, the reclaim pass and where workspace settings are written, so it is left for a separate change. The warning is in English, like the extension's other messages; only its manifest strings are translated.

Verification:

- `node scripts/test-bridge-relay.js` drives the real extension. At activation it shows one warning, for a shared-storage folder. It shows none for `Android/data/<package>` on the primary volume, an SD card, `/storage/self/primary` or in lower case, nor for a device-folder copy, a home project, `/storagebox` or a folder silenced earlier. The warning's button runs `vscodroid.openFolderFromDevice`. The stubbed `showWarningMessage` answers only with a button the call offered, so a warning without the button fails the test. Folders added later through `onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders` are warned about once each: `/sdcard`, `/mnt/sdcard`, `/storage/self/primary`, an SD card, a nested `Android/data`, the top of the storage and `Download`, and only the last two are sent to a folder inside. **Don't Show Again** adds the folder to the ones silenced before. Against the 1.9.0 `extension.js` the test fails with no warning shown.
- `SafBridgeManifestTest` pins the remote indicator entry and the Explorer welcome link; against the 1.9.0 manifest it fails.
- `./gradlew --offline :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug`, every `node scripts/test-*.js`, and the `lint.yml` Python gates pass.
- On an API 36 emulator, a debug build of the first commit went through the upgrade setup, removed `saf-bridge-1.9.0` and listed 1.10.0 in `extensions.json`. File > Open Folder on `/storage/emulated/0/Documents/<folder>` listed only its subfolder, then the editor showed the warning once, and its button opened Android's folder picker. A device folder copy reopened without a warning. The remote indicator menu lists Open Folder from Device first, and the Explorer with no folder open shows the new text and button, which also opens the picker.
- Again on the API 36 emulator, with a build of this branch's final head over main (alongside two unrelated fixes): File > Open Folder on `/sdcard/Documents/reviewtest` showed only `src` and `fresh.js` of its files, and the warning in its final wording with both buttons; **Open Folder from Device** opened the picker. The warning comes back on every reload or reopen of that folder, because each page load is a new session for the extension; **Don't Show Again** is what stops it, and was not run on a device. The pick-a-folder-inside variant and the volume matching were checked by the tests above only.

title: fix: keep a caret key from opening the suggest list
body:
With a soft keyboard that composes, End or a trackpad drag down while a word was underlined could open the editor's suggestion list where the caret landed. The drag's next Down then moved the list's highlight instead of the caret, and Enter could insert a suggestion instead of a new line.

The keyboard guard from #480 ends the composition in the same task as the key, just before the editor moves the caret. Monaco's suggest model answers the end of a composition by scheduling a quick suggestion 10 ms later, and the key's move (source `keyboard`, reason Explicit) left it alone while no list was open, so it fired at the destination.

Changes:

- `patches/0023-suggest-drop-quick-suggest-on-caret-move.patch`: in `SuggestModel._onCursorChange`, an Explicit cursor move with no suggestion session cancels the pending quick suggest timer. Typing (reason NotSet) still arms it; `deleteLeft` is NotSet too; mouse and tap moves were already cancelled by the early exit; an open session still refilters; Tab and tap accept cancel the model before an edit from source `suggest`.
- `patches/fingerprints.txt`: one row for the patch's early return, `this._triggerQuickSuggest.cancel();return`, which occurs 0 times in the shipped 1.139.1 `workbench.js` and once in a tree built with the patch.
- The technical spec's patch diagram and composition paragraph, the `injectKeyboardGuard` KDoc, and KB-31, which gains an End case and a drag case on a line ending in `alph`.

No changelog line: the list opened at the destination only since #480, which is unreleased, and its entry already describes the user-visible change.

The published `server-1.139.1` has to be rebuilt from this branch before the Build check can pass. Until then the fetched tree's manifest lacks 0023 and the new row fails, as it should.

Verification:

- `git apply --check` passes against `suggestModel.ts` at 04c0d99f (blob c85f338), and against upstream main, where `_onCursorChange` is unchanged.
- Server tree built locally in Docker from this branch: the type-check reports 0 errors and the build's Verify stage passes every gate, both 0023 checks included, with 22 patches in the manifest. Tarball `vscode-reh-web-linux-arm64-1.139.1.tar.gz`, sha256 `2fa844d46c9ae43c2e34a2897a32dc3c6fe714f8743d33e6c96be9ccc8a4c9c2`. Its `workbench.js` differs from the shipped one only in the new block and in the format of the build date string.
- `check-patch-fingerprints.py` fails the 0023 row against the currently shipped tree and passes it on the new one.
- The shipped and the patched bundles, each served from a local tree and driven in headless Chromium with the IME emulated over the DevTools protocol and the keyboard guard script from `MainActivity.kt` installed, screenshots checked:
  - End from composing `kiwi` in `kiwi delta charlie`: the shipped bundle opens `charlie2`, `charlie3`, `charlie4` at the line end; the patched one opens no list.
  - End then Enter: shipped turns the line into `kiwi delta charlie2`; patched starts a new line.
  - Three synthetic Downs from composing `charlie4`: shipped stops one line down with the list's highlight on `charlie3`; patched moves the caret three lines with no list.
  - The same in both: a tap on another line (no list), typing `charl` (list opens), a composition committed in place (list opens), Left with the list open (it refilters and stays), and Tab or a tap accepting a row under a recomposed word.
- `:app:testDebugUnitTest` (2611 tests, 0 failed, 0 skipped) and `:app:lintDebug` (no new issues); `test-keyboard-guard.js` 43/43, `test-composing-enter.js` 9/9, `test-arrow-edge-guard.js` 22/22; `check-plain-punctuation.py`, `check-checklist-totals.py`, `check-document-dates.py`, `check-build-steps.py`, `check-workflow-steps.py`, `check-patch-fingerprints.py --self-test`, and `git apply --stat` on all 22 patches.
- On a Pixel 7 Pro API 33 emulator with Gboard 12.4, which underlines the typed word, running a debug build of this branch over that locally built tree (the served `workbench.js` holds the new row's pattern once), two runs each: End from an underlined `kiwi` in `kiwi delta charlie` put the caret at the line end with no list, then or 1.5 s later, and `x` gave `kiwi delta charliex` on disk; three trackpad Downs from an underlined `charlie4` moved the caret line by line with no list at any step; quick suggestions still open once the word is committed (`charl`, space, Backspace); and Down, Down, Tab then `x` gave `alpha3x`, a tap on the `alpha2` row `alpha2x`. On a Pixel 10 API 36 emulator with Gboard 18.2.4, typing `charl` opens the list and Down, Down, Tab gives `alpha3x`.

title: fix: let quick input keys work while composing
body:
Since #477 the key row presses PgUp, PgDn, Home, End and the trackpad's Left and Right as real keys, and a real key pressed while Gboard still underlines the typed word carries `isComposing`, for which the workbench dispatches no keybinding. In the Command Palette and Quick Open, PgUp, PgDn, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End work only through keybindings, as does Right at the end of Quick Open's box, so they did nothing until the word was committed. Separately, with Shift alone latched on the row, neither the code-less Gboard Enter that #478 fills nor the Enter that replaces a composing one spent the latch when a keybinding accepted it, so the badge stayed lit and the next row key went out shifted.

- `MainActivity.injectComposingEnter`: a real, composing keydown of PageUp, PageDown, ArrowRight, or Home/End with Ctrl, in the quick input's own box (inside `.quick-input-widget`, outside any editor there) gets `isComposing` defined false in the capture phase, so `quickInput.pageNext`, `pagePrevious`, `first`, `last` and `acceptInBackground` run. Other keys, other targets, Quick Chat's chat input among them, and synthetic events keep the flag.
- Same script: with Shift alone latched, the code-filled Enter and the Enter that replaces a composing one spend the latch without applying it, as the modifier interceptor does with a lone Shift on every soft keyboard edit, so the row's poll drops the badge. Applying it would change the key: on Shift+Enter, Quick Open and the `#` symbol search do not open the highlighted item but add it to the last focused chat input, and on Gboard 12.4, whose editor Enter is filled too, Enter in a Python file would run the line in the terminal. An Enter that arrives with a `code` is unchanged.
- `scripts/test-composing-enter.js` goes from 9 to 26 cases: the quick input keys, the keys and targets left alone (an editor inside the quick input among them), synthetic events, and a Shift latched alone on a filled Enter, on a composing Enter's replacement and on one that has a code. `ComposingEnterWiringTest` checks that the packaged workbench still binds those keys and still builds `.quick-input-widget`.
- Docs: KDoc in `MainActivity`, `TextEntry.kt`, `KeyInjector.kt` and `ExtraKeyRow.kt`, `docs/04-TECHNICAL_SPEC.md`, the test tables in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/07-TESTING_STRATEGY.md`, a PgDn-while-composing step in KB-28, and Shift steps in KB-30 for the Command Palette, Quick Open and a Python file. The CHANGELOG entry from #477 and the user guide no longer say PgUp and PgDn move the caret in the Command Palette, where they page the list.

Verification: `node scripts/test-composing-enter.js` passes 26/26. Against the script on main the five quick input cases and the Shift cases fail, and each of these fails its own cases: assigning `code` or `isComposing` instead of defining it, applying Shift to the filled Enter or leaving the latch standing, spending it on an Enter that has a code, and dropping the trusted, quick input or editor check. In headless Chromium 151, with trusted keys sent over the DevTools protocol, a window capture listener added after the script, as the quick input adds the one that records Shift when it is first used, reads `shiftKey` false from the filled Enter while the latch is spent, and a composing PageDown or Ctrl+Home loses `isComposing` only in the quick input's own box. All 13 `scripts/test-*.js`, the `lint.yml` Python gates, `./gradlew --offline :app:testDebugUnitTest` (2612 tests, none skipped) and `:app:lintDebug` pass.

On a Pixel 7 Pro API 33 emulator with Gboard 12.4, which underlines the typed word, and a build of this branch over main, two runs each: with `rel` underlined in the Command Palette, PgDn moved the highlight down a page and PgUp back, Ctrl+End went to the last item and Ctrl+Home to the first; in Quick Open a trackpad drag right at the end opened the highlighted file behind the open picker. Gboard's Enter opened About once from the Command Palette, with and without Shift latched, and with Shift latched in Quick Open over an underlined file name it opened the file, added nothing to chat and left the badge dark with the keyboard still up (three runs). On a Pixel 10 API 36 emulator with Gboard 18.2.4, which does not compose, the same palette keys and the Shift Enter behave the same.

title: fix: close gaps in the arrow edge guard
body:
#477 made the trackpad's Left and Right real key presses, with a guard that cancels one at a text box's edge, where spatial navigation would otherwise move focus out of the box and drop the soft keyboard and the key row. The guard missed number and email boxes, boxes that stop the key's propagation, and, below WebView 149, an Alt press on a selection or on the editor's EditContext host. From 149 it cancelled Android's own Alt+Left/Right line moves in a text box with no text selected.

- Decide on the box: a capture listener on the window now adds a one-shot listener for the event to its innermost target, which runs after the box's own listeners and before the key bubbles to any container. The Problems, Output, Debug Console and Comments filters stop Left and Right on their container, and the chat model picker's filter on the input itself, which hid the key from the old window bubble listener while spatial navigation still moved focus. A key stopped in the capture phase, or with `stopImmediatePropagation` by one of the box's own listeners, still never reaches the guard, as it never reached the old one; in the 1.139.1 workbench every listener that stops Left or Right either way cancels the key first: the title bar's agent status roving focus, and a modal dialog moving focus between its buttons; neither acts on a text box.
- Number and email inputs have no selection API (`selectionStart` is null), so their caret cannot be read. Every unmodified Left and Right there is now cancelled, so a drag does nothing there, as before #477; Alt follows the Alt rule below. Such boxes are the Settings editor's number settings and the Search Editor's context lines box. With a hardware keyboard, Left and Right no longer move the caret inside such a box either; Home, End and a tap do.
- Android maps Alt+Left/Right to the line's start and end only from Chromium 149, and those commands always count as handled, so the Alt rule now applies only when the user agent's Chrome version is below 149 or unreadable. There it covers any caret position, a selection included, and the editor's EditContext host, where a horizontal drag with Alt latched moved focus out of the editor. From 149 a hardware keyboard's Alt+Left/Right moves to the line's start or end again, as in v1.4.0, and the key row's Alt drag now does too, where v1.4.0's announced Alt arrow did nothing in a text box.
- `docs/05-API_SPEC.md` no longer places `typeCharacter` beside `isTextEntry` and `NAVIGATION_KEYS`, since it is a private member of `KeyInjector`, and names the number box exception for pressed keys.
- The KDoc, `docs/04-TECHNICAL_SPEC.md`, `docs/USER_GUIDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/07-TESTING_STRATEGY.md` and KB-29 in `docs/DEVICE_TEST_CHECKLIST.md` describe the new rules, and `CHANGELOG.md` notes that a hardware keyboard's Left and Right no longer move the caret in a number box.

Verification:

- `scripts/test-arrow-edge-guard.js` now dispatches through the capture, target and bubble phases of a fake DOM, once per user agent: 45/45 pass. Against the guard on main 12 fail, and each commit's new cases fail on the commit before it. Twenty single changes to the guard (deciding in another phase, no `once`, no version gate or a gate at 150, Alt only on a collapsed caret, no EditContext host, no number or email box, the edges swapped and others) each fail at least one case.
- The guard in headless Chromium 151 with `--enable-spatial-navigation` and trusted key events: focus stays in a filter box whose container stops the key, and in a number box, whose caret no longer moves; with a Chrome 148 user agent, an Alt+Left that has no editing command keeps focus on an EditContext host and on a text selection. With the guard from main, each of these moved focus. In the same setup a stop in the capture phase, or by `stopImmediatePropagation` on the box, still lets focus move.
- `./gradlew --offline :app:testDebugUnitTest` (2611 tests) and `:app:lintDebug` pass, as do every `lint.yml` check and bundled JavaScript test.
- On Pixel 7 Pro API 33 and Pixel 10 API 36 emulators (WebView 153), with a build of this branch over main: trackpad drags past both ends of the Settings editor's Editor: Font Size number box, the Problems filter box and the Explorer rename box kept focus in the box, with the keyboard and the key row up (`mInputShown` true, `mServedView` the WebView), and the rename was cancelled with the old name. With Alt latched, a horizontal drag in the editor kept focus there.
- Not run on a device: a WebView below 149, a hardware keyboard's Alt+Left/Right from 149, and the chat model picker's filter, which needs Copilot chat.

title: fix: keep held-back fetches and own writes out of device copies
body:
An open held back by the free-space floor dropped the held-back files from the folder's sync record, so the next open with room set their older copies aside as `<name>.local-<time>` files and put them into the device folder, and on a provider with no modification times kept the stale copy until a save overwrote the device's newer version. Separately, the live device-edit guard took the time and size a provider reports right after a write as final, so on providers that settle them later a save left a `<name>.device-<time>` copy of a version the editor already held: on MTP and Nextcloud at every save after the first, on FAT cards behind the FUSE cache and on Round Sync at a save made after the provider settled, and on any of them at the first save after an open that fetched a write still settling. Both regressions are unreleased.

- `SafSyncEngine` phase 2: a fetch that is held back or fails carries the previous record line forward while the mirror copy still matches it, so the record, the reclaim verdict and the next open treat that copy as one the record vouched for.
- A held-back fetch whose device copy already holds the mirror's bytes is settled by a read that spends no disk: the file is recorded, given the device's time where the provider reports one, and left writable, instead of being refused every save and announced as not copied, or, where a coarser clock put the device's time before the save, as kept inside the app. This covers every unchanged file of a folder without timestamps, and a file saved and delivered in the previous session, whether the device stamped that write after the save or before it.
- The device-edit guard keeps the SHA-256 and length of the bytes each landed write streamed and of the copy the open fetched, hashed on the way through. When the stamp has moved and the device copy hashes to that digest as it is read, the stamp is re-baselined and the save goes ahead with no copy, also below the free-space floor. A reported length other than the kept one is taken as another app's edit without a read. A device copy that cannot be read, as on Nextcloud offline, still holds the save back.
- Tests: an open held back by the floor followed by an open with room, on a provider with and without timestamps; a file settled below the floor and reopened with room, which is neither read nor written; providers whose stamp settles after the write (row updated later, milliseconds then whole seconds, size updated later), with no other writer, after an open that fetched a settling write, with another app's edit, below the floor, and after a write-back that lands on its second attempt; a file deleted and made again in the editor; a save after a write whose stamp could not be read back; a device edit grown past the copy limit, which is not read at each save.
- Docs: the changelog says the other app's version is normally kept and moves the two device-folder entries from Security to Fixed. The user guide states the guard's limits: a same-size change in a folder that reports no times or keeps a file's old time, a rare spare copy when a folder changes a file's time on its own, and saves held back in an offline network folder. Checklist rows SF-18 and SF-19 cover the late-stamp providers and the low-storage reopen.

On a provider whose stamp moves after a write, each save whose stamp moved at the length this app wrote now reads the document once to hash it: an MTP transfer, or a Nextcloud download once its cache is gone. Where the stamp is final at close nothing extra is read. The sync record format is unchanged and the digests live in memory only.

Verified with `./gradlew --offline :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug` (2635 tests, 0 failures; lint reports no new issues) and the Python gates in `lint.yml`, including `check-checklist-totals.py`, `check-plain-punctuation.py`, `check-document-dates.py` and `check-toolchain-claims.py`. Against the engine from `main`, 16 of the 449 storage tests fail: the eight held-back open cases and the eight late-stamp cases. The cases with another app's edit and with an unreadable device copy are controls that pass either way, the two guard-branch tests each fail when the branch they cover is removed, the retried write-back case fails when one digest is shared across both attempts, the reopen-with-room case fails when either settle leaves the mirror file's own time, and the copy-limit case fails when the guard hashes regardless of length. On a Pixel 10 API 36 emulator, with a device folder on the emulator's own storage and a build of this branch over main, two saves in a row left no `.device-` file, a save after the file was changed from the device side kept `a.txt.device-<time>` holding the device's text while `a.txt` took the editor's, and closing and reopening the folder added no `.local-` file (two runs, a.txt and b.txt). That storage reports final stamps at once, so it does not exercise the late-stamp providers: SF-18 still needs an MTP device or a Nextcloud folder, and SF-19 storage filled below 150 MB.

title: build: tighten release checks and fix stale figures
body:
Several build and release checks missed the case they exist for, patch 0022 depends on an upstream behavior that 1.140.0 changes while every gate stays green, a few comments and documents described code that has since changed, and the install sizes were measured on a 1.139.1 tree that can no longer ship.

- `build-vscode-oss.yml`: the publish job takes a concurrency group per server version, queued rather than cancelled, so two publishes of one version can no longer leave the release notes, the asset and the moved tag naming different builds. The workflow comment and the CI table in CONTRIBUTING say the release notes are the provenance record and how a clone refreshes a moved `server-*` tag.
- New `scripts/check-editcontext-sync.py`: fails when `nativeEditContext.ts` stops calling `_updateEditContext` directly from its content listener or `onCursorStateChanged`, which 0022's pre-edit copy depends on and upstream 1.140.0 defers to `prepareRender`. `build-vscode-oss.sh` runs it on the patched tree after the Patches stage; `check-patches-apply.sh` runs it on the upstream source before applying anything, so an earlier patch that stops applying cannot hide it, and exits 1 once all patches apply if it failed; when a patch fails as well, the report's closing paragraph names both. A source file that is there but cannot be read exits 2, "could not run", rather than 1. `lint.yml` runs its `--self-test`, and it is in the `assets-` cache key as `check-build-steps.py` requires. The 0022 header, CONTRIBUTING, docs/07 and the release plan's patch-drift row name it.
- Lint: `OutdatedLibrary`, `PlaySdkIndexDeprecated`, `PlaySdkIndexNonCompliant` and `PlaySdkIndexVulnerability` are informational, so a non-blocking Play SDK Index label on a pinned dependency no longer fails every build through `warningsAsErrors`. Lint has no override that keeps a blocking label on those four an error, so a blocking one is informational too (its message still says it blocks publishing); `RiskyLibrary`, reported only for a blocking critical issue, still fails. `check-lint-baseline.py` refuses a lint block that drops the four.
- `check-patch-fingerprints.py`: a row can require its pattern N times by ending the bundle field in ` xN`, covered by `--self-test`. Patch 0022's rows now fail when the suffix copy, the assignment the patch moves out of the `if`, or the comparison with the live buffer is reverted. The fingerprint comment, the checker's docstring and docs/04 say why the pre-edit row needs two matches: the text that tells the second copy apart starts with a renamed identifier.
- `check-checklist-totals.py` reads the release plan's row IDs by shape, so a citation whose whole checklist section has gone is refused instead of skipped, and GPL-2, BSD-3 or the tail of FR-DEV-06 is not read as one. The release plan names `docs/DEVICE_TEST_CHECKLIST.md` where it cites rows.
- `docs/DEVICE_TEST_CHECKLIST.md`: new KB-32 runs the three suggestion sequences that corrupted a line before 0022 (a tap inside a word, mid-word, and past the end of the line), with a keyboard that does not compose.
- `test-process-monitor-extension.js` raises the agent-host tree at the warning tier as well as the error tier, and asserts each offers only Show Details. Its fixture comment says why the default budget is not the shipped one.
- The `ApplySharedPref` suppressions in NodeService, ProcessManager and FirstRunSetup suppressed nothing, since every write uses `edit(commit = true)`; they are gone, and the comments say lint flags `Editor.commit()` but not the KTX form and name the tests that keep those writes committed.
- Sizes for the pruned 1.139.1 tree: about 738 MB free and 603 MB extracted (575 MiB, `EXTRACTED_ASSET_BYTES` 603,414,041), about 800 MB with both toolchains, in README, the user guide, the site, the SRS (703 MiB free to unpack), PF-1, the `installedExtractionBytes` KDoc and FirstRunSetup's class KDoc. The Gradle fingerprint task comment gives eight bundles, a 436 MiB server tree and 0.14 s. The mxc-sdk reclaim comment gives the 19 MB the released 1.133.0 tree held.
- Comments and docs: the process monitor's budget comments, the toolchain note in `device-test.sh` (TC-4 and TC-9, not the removed TC-5), and the node self-check fixture sentence in docs/07.

Verified with `./gradlew --offline :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug` (2,611 tests, no lint issues) and every gate `lint.yml` runs. Lint was also run against a Play SDK Index carrying an outdated label on asset-delivery 2.2.2: a non-blocking label failed with two `OutdatedLibrary` errors before the change and gives two informational hints after. The 0022 rows pass on the shipped server tree and were run against copies of its `workbench.js` with one change reverted at a time, each with the patch regenerated by `git diff`: the old rows passed six of the eight, the new rows fail all but the caret length, which differs only in a renamed local. The new self-check cases and the warning-tier test were each run against the code with the fix removed and failed.

`check-editcontext-sync.py` passes on upstream's `nativeEditContext.ts` at 1.139.1 and on main, and fails on 1.140.0 naming both callers, before and after 0022 is applied. `check-patches-apply.sh 1.140.0` now prints that failure before 0003 stops applying (without the change it reports only 0003), and `check-patches-apply.sh 1.139.0` passes. With the checker stubbed to exit 1 and 2, the drift check exits 1 after "All 21 patches apply" and 2 as "could not run". Its `--self-test` fails the three drift cases with the check disabled, and its read cases fail against the previous reader: an unreadable file exited 1 and an undecodable one raised. The checklist citation self-check was run against the previous pattern, which reported GPL-2, BSD-3 and DEV-06 as missing rows. The server build itself was not run.

The workflow concurrency key is checked against GitHub's context availability for `jobs.<job_id>.concurrency`; the workflow file still passes `check-workflow-steps.py`, which does not read concurrency. The race itself needs two dispatches to exercise.

title: fix: check each jshell argument for --execution
body:
The jshell wrapper in `toolchain-env.sh` adds `--execution local` unless the caller chose an engine, and it decided that by searching `" $* "` for `" -ex"`. A value with a space before `-ex` (`--class-path "lib -extra/x.jar"`, `"My -experiments/a.jsh"`) counted as a choice, so jshell fell back to its default engine and failed to launch it; under an IFS that does not start with a space (`IFS=$'\n\t'` in a strict-mode script, or an empty IFS), a later `--execution` went unseen and jshell refused the option given twice.

- `ToolchainManager.regenerateEnvFileLocked()`: the generated `jshell()` function tests each argument for an `-ex` or `--ex` prefix instead of searching the joined command line, so a value that merely contains ` -ex`, or the IFS in force, no longer sways it. The loader call, the `-J` options and the argument order are unchanged.
- `ToolchainEnvFileTest`: the bash harness is shared by the existing jshell test and two new ones. One covers paths that hold ` -ex`, `IFS=$'\n\t'` and an empty IFS with a later engine option, and arguments that hold `-ex` past their first character. The other runs a plain `jshell` after an engine choice under `set -u` and checks that the caller's shell is left without `arg` or `chosen`, so the flag cannot carry over to a later call.
- `scripts/device-test.sh`: the hand-written jshell sample in `--self-check` follows the new shape, and now carries the VFORK option the generator already emits.
- The comment above the generated function gave `lib/jspawnhelper` as the reason the default engine cannot start, but the wrapper's VFORK option bypasses it. It now says the engine's second JVM is `bin/java` under filesDir, which no launch mechanism can exec.

Existing installs need no action: `toolchain-env.sh` is regenerated from `toolchains.json` on every launch (the `SplashActivity` repair pass) and whenever the editor returns to the foreground (`MainActivity.onStart`). A terminal that is already open keeps the old function until a new shell starts.

An option value that itself starts with `-ex`, such as `--startup -extras.jsh`, still reads as an engine choice; telling the two apart would mean reimplementing jshell's option parser.

Verified:

- The first new test fails against the previous generator (no `--execution local` for either path, `--execution` passed twice under both IFS values) and passes with the change. The second fails when the `local` declaration is dropped or narrowed, and, under bash 5, when the flag is declared without a value.
- `./gradlew --offline :app:testDebugUnitTest`: 2613 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped. `:app:lintDebug`: no new issues.
- `bash scripts/device-test.sh --self-check`: 13 passed, 0 failed. `python3 scripts/check-plain-punctuation.py`: ok.
- The generated file, unmodified, sourced through `.bashrc` in an interactive shell and through `BASH_ENV` (`bash -c`, and a `set -euo pipefail` script) in bash 5.2 and 5.3 with a stub at `/system/bin/linker64`. The unit tests run it in bash 3.2 on macOS and bash 5 on CI. Not run on a device, where bash is 5.3.

title: fix: end a composition before the editor moves the caret
body:
With a soft keyboard that composes, which shows the word being typed underlined (Gboard 12.4, for example), moving the editor's caret while a word is still underlined garbles the line, and autosave writes the result to disk. Chromium keeps an EditContext composition's range where it was when the page moves the selection ([crbug 379170477](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/379170477)), so the keyboard's next edit lands on the old range. End while `kiwi` was underlined in `alpha delta kiwi charlie` left `alpha delta charlie charlie`, a tap on an empty line followed by `cha` typed `cchcha`, and Down, Down, Tab on `alp` in a suggestion list, then `x`, left `alpha3xha3ha3`. #479 fixed the editor's own bookkeeping; this part is in the browser, which no patch to the editor can reach.

Changes:

- `MainActivity.injectKeyboardGuard` ends the composition, by blurring and refocusing the composing EditContext host in the same task, from a window capture `keydown` for the arrows, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown, Tab, Backspace and Delete, and from the editor's own `-monaco-gesturetap` and `-monaco-gesturecontextmenu`. Only a focused host with an `editContext` that the script already tracks as composing is touched, and `inputmode` is left alone.
- It ends the composition before the editor handles the key or the tap, except where an open suggestion list takes it. Ending a composition makes the list refilter and highlight its first row again, so Up, Down, PageUp and PageDown that move the highlight end nothing, and Tab accepting the highlighted suggestion or a tap on a row end it after the list has acted, from a listener added during the capture phase, with a zero timeout as a fallback.
- `scripts/test-keyboard-guard.js` extracts the script and drives it in a fake DOM that dispatches through the capture, target and bubble phases (43 cases; 16 pass against main). It runs in `lint.yml` and `release.yml`, and `check-build-steps.py` requires it in both.
- Docs: the technical spec, a new device checklist row KB-31, the testing strategy counts and the CONTRIBUTING script table. The changelog gains one line, and the trackpad entry #477 added twice under Security is kept once, under Fixed.

Limits: the word is committed as typed, so a Japanese keyboard commits the kana unconverted. A caret moved by a command such as Undo, Find or Go to Line, or by an extension, is not covered, and neither is Enter accepting a suggestion. Chords the list also binds, such as Shift+Tab or Ctrl+Down, end the composition first and can reset the highlight. After an accept the list can reopen with the accepted word as its only row; the text is unaffected.

Verification, with the debug APK built from this branch over the main server tree:

- Pixel 7 Pro API 33 emulator, Gboard 12.4, which composes; each case twice, text read back from disk. Down, Down, Tab gives `alpha3x`; a tap on the `alpha2` row gives `alpha2x`; Up from the first row wraps the list and keeps the word composing. End, Home, PgUp, the trackpad in all four directions, Tab, a tap and Down on a single suggestion, Backspace at the start of a line, a tap on another line or the same line, and a long press all leave the text intact, and the long press still opens the menu with the keyboard up. Typing, Gboard's suggestion strip, a double tap, the Command Palette and the Explorer's rename box never trigger it, and the keyboard never hides. On main the same sequences on the same emulator and keyboard give the corrupted text above.
- Pixel 10 API 36 emulator, Gboard 18.2.4, which does not compose: the guard never fires, and typing, the suggestion strip, End, the trackpad, a tap on a word, the suggestion list cases, the key row, the Command Palette with Gboard's Enter, a long press and a double tap all give the expected result.
- `node scripts/test-keyboard-guard.js`, the other self-checks, the repository gates, the JVM suite and lint pass locally.

Not run: keyboards other than Gboard, Korean and Chinese input, a hardware keyboard, Enter or PageDown in the suggestion list, and physical devices.

title: fix: keep the editor's IME buffer in step with the model
body:
Typing in the editor with a soft keyboard could corrupt the line and autosave would write it: a word came back reversed after F1 and Escape (`upgrades` became `upgradessedargpu`), tapping a Gboard suggestion after moving the cursor or tapping a word garbled the text, and on a keyboard that composes (Gboard 12.4) End or a trackpad drag while a word was underlined looped (`alpha delta charlieeeee...`). VSCodroid's own page scripts are not involved: with all of them kept from installing, every case still corrupted.

The cause is in Monaco's native EditContext, which mirrors the model line into the browser's buffer and turns each `textupdate` back into a type command. Three steps of that round trip assume the buffer holds only what Monaco wrote; it also holds the keyboard's edits, which the keyboard reads back.

Changes, as patch `0022-editcontext-buffer-and-caret-sync.patch` against `nativeEditContext.ts`:

- `_updateEditContext` replaced `[0, length of the previous write)`. Blink has already applied the keyboard's edit when `textupdate` fires, so every character it added stayed after the new line (typing `kiwi` left the buffer `kiwiiwik`). The buffer is now compared with and replaced whole.
- `_emitTypeEvent` copied the text between the caret and the update range from the live buffer, at offsets of the text before the edit. It now copies from the line last written, which those offsets describe.
- The caret delta ignored that copied text, so a selection-only update (Gboard sends one before committing a suggestion) put the caret past the keyboard's selection and its next delete removed the wrong characters. It is now measured from the text actually typed.
- Three `fingerprints.txt` rows, one per fix, so a rebase that drops one fails its row; the technical spec's patch diagram and a CHANGELOG line.

Not fixed: Chromium keeps a composition's range when the page moves the selection during it (crbug 379170477), so on a keyboard that composes, a key that moves the caret while a word is underlined still rewrites that word once. The same three lines are unchanged on microsoft/vscode main.

The published `server-1.139.1` was rebuilt from this branch (run 36670309353, tag on d4d744bd), so the Build check now passes; before the rebuild it failed on the manifest and the three new rows, as it should. After merging, the workflow is dispatched once more from main.

Verification with the real build:

title: fix: let Gboard's Enter accept in quick input boxes
body:
With Gboard, Enter did nothing in the Command Palette, Quick Open and every input box an extension opens (for example VSCodroid: Open in Browser); the box stayed open until the user tapped a result. In a single-line input Gboard sends its action key as a keydown with `key` Enter and `keyCode` 13 but an empty `code`, and the workbench resolves keybindings from `code`. Quick input accepts only through the `quickInput.accept` keybinding, and the scan-code mapper falls back to `keyCode` for arrows and a few editing keys but not for Enter, so the key matched nothing. The Explorer's New File and Rename boxes were unaffected because they test `keyCode` themselves.

Gboard 18 never composes Latin words in these boxes, so every Enter took this path. Gboard 12.4 only reached it when no word was underlined; a composing Enter was already rewritten by the existing composing-Enter script.

Changes:

- `MainActivity.injectComposingEnter`: the same window capture listener now gives a non-composing, code-less Enter `code` "Enter" with `Object.defineProperty`, and leaves the real event otherwise untouched. It skips the fill while the key row has Ctrl or Alt latched, because the row builds that chord from the `beforeinput` that only follows an unhandled Enter. The editor is not excluded, since its rename box is such an input.
- `scripts/test-composing-enter.js` runs the page script under node: the fill, the Ctrl and Alt guards, an Enter that already has a `code`, other keys, and the composing path. It fails on main (3 of 9 cases) and runs in `lint.yml` and `release.yml`.
- Technical spec, testing strategy, CONTRIBUTING and a device checklist row (KB-30).

Behaviour change: on Gboard 12.4 the editor's and terminal's Enter also arrive without a `code` and are now filled, so Enter keybindings inside the editor (accepting a suggestion, accepting a symbol rename) match there, as they already did on Gboard 18 and on a desktop. On API 33 the find widget's Enter now moves to the next match instead of inserting a newline into the find box, and Settings search moves focus to the first result.

Verification:

- JVM suite 2611 tests, lint, and every `lint.yml` gate pass.
- Pixel 7 Pro API 33 (Gboard 12.4) and Pixel 10 API 36 (Gboard 18.2.4) emulators, debug build of this branch, real Gboard taps, with a read-only logger showing the keydown `code` after the fill:
  - The Command Palette ran Help: About.
  - Quick Open opened the file.
  - The Open in Browser box closed.
  - New File created exactly one file, and Rename committed once.
  - The find widget moved to the next match.
  - The editor took one newline per Enter, and the terminal ran `echo hi` once.
  - Ctrl latched on the key row still gave Ctrl+Enter (a line below in the editor, About once from the palette).
  - On API 33 a composing Enter in the palette ran once.

Not covered: a composing Enter in the find widget or Settings search on Gboard 12.4, which Gboard commits as text with no keydown at all; suggest and rename accept in the editor were not exercised on a device.

title: fix: send navigation keys as real key presses
body:
The trackpad arrows and the key row's Home, End, PageUp and PageDown were announced as synthetic keydown events. Those run the page's listeners but perform no default action, so they only worked where a handler does the moving, the editor and the terminal. In the Explorer rename box, the Command Palette or the find widget the caret stayed put, and inside an extension webview nothing arrived.

Changes:

- Left, Right, Home, End, PageUp and PageDown are dispatched as real `KeyEvent`s with the scan code a hardware keyboard sends and any latched modifier as meta state, falling back to the DOM event if the WebView refuses the press.
- Up, Down, Tab and Escape stay announced. A real key pressed while Gboard composes carries `isComposing`, and the workbench runs no keybinding for it, so a real Up or Down would stop the quick pick's highlight from moving. A real Tab moves focus, and the rename box commits on blur. A real Escape blurs the focused element once spatial navigation is on.
- A real arrow turns on WebView spatial navigation until the next touch, so a keydown listener cancels a Left at the start or a Right at the end of a text box when no handler used it, and any Alt+Left or Alt+Right on a collapsed caret. The key row blocks focus for its children, so an unused arrow cannot move Android focus into the pager and hide the keyboard.
- `scripts/test-arrow-edge-guard.js` runs the guard under node, in `lint.yml` and `release.yml`; the user guide, technical spec, architecture and device checklist describe the three routes.

Verification:

- JVM: the real-key set is pinned both ways (putting Up and Down back fails four cases, taking Left and Right out fails six), with meta state, scan codes and the DOM fallback on a refused press. The node test drives the guard through both edges, Shift with both selection directions, Alt, a handled key and a box with no caret, and each of ten deliberate breaks in the guard fails it. Full suite passes.
- Pixel 7 Pro API 33 emulator, Gboard 12.4, each row first on a main build as the control:
  - Rename box, composing: main leaves the caret, giving `helloX.txt`; this branch gives `helXlo.txt`.
  - Find widget: `alphaX` on main, `alpXha` here.
  - Command Palette, composing: dragging down still moves the highlight.
  - Dragging past either end of the rename box, and Alt with a drag, leave the box open and focused, with the keyboard up and nothing renamed.
  - Editor: Home, End, PgDn, Ctrl with a drag (word jump) and Shift with a drag (selection) behave as on a hardware keyboard.
  - Terminal: a left drag edits mid-line, Tab completes, and a vertical drag recalls history.

A separate, existing problem was seen on both builds and is not changed here: in the code editor, End or a horizontal drag while Gboard is still composing a word garbles the line.

title: fix: leave free space when opening a device folder
body:
Opening a device folder copied every document into the app's own storage with no free-space check; the pre-flight estimate only chose the wording of the notice afterwards. A folder larger than the free space drove the partition to zero for every app on the phone, where the mirror's own sync record can no longer be written either.

Changes:

- Each fetch into the mirror, including the device copy a repair sets aside, reads free space first and is held back below the app's low-storage line plus one maximum document, about 152 MB.
- A held-back document takes the existing failed-copy path, so the device copy stays protected from deletes and overwrites made in the editor, and the open ends with the "Not enough free space" notice. Reopening the folder once space is available fetches the rest.

Verification:

- JVM: a fetch below the floor is held back and announced as a space shortfall, a directory whose documents were held back stays on the device, a device copy is not fetched for a set-aside below the floor, and the pre-flight estimate still stops nothing. Full suite passes.
- Pixel 10 API 36 emulator with about 300 MB free and a folder of ten 40 MiB files: 4 files were copied, the toast read "Not enough free space: 6 files could not be copied into the editor", logcat showed the fetch stopping under 152 MB, and free space never fell below about 131 MB. Deleting the folder in the Explorer kept all ten files on the device. After freeing space, reopening through Open Recent fetched all ten with no notice.

title: fix: keep device edits made while a folder is open
body:
A device folder is read only when it is opened, and every save opens its document with `"wt"`. An edit another app made to the same file while the folder was open was therefore replaced by the next save, with no copy kept anywhere, and the user guide promised the folder stays in sync both ways.

Changes:

- `SafSyncEngine` remembers the modification time and size the device reported for each document when it last read or wrote it. A save into a document that has moved since first keeps the device copy beside it as `<name>.device-<time>`, the same set-aside an open already makes. If that copy cannot be made, the save stays in the mirror and the user is told, as for any write-back that does not reach the device.
- The memory lives only in the engine, never in the `.synced` record, and is scoped per mirror, so a folder switch that fails partway keeps the previous folder's guard.
- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` states the contract the code has: the device side is read when the folder opens, and a device-side change is kept as a `.device-` copy rather than overwritten.

Verification:

- JVM, `SafLiveDeviceEditTest`: a device edit set aside before the save, saves with no device edit leaving no copy, a set-aside that cannot be made holding the save back, a file replaced by rename, a provider with no clock, and a second folder keeping the first folder's guard. Removing the guard, the refresh after a write, the free-name loop or the per-mirror scope each fails the matching case. Full suite passes.
- Pixel 10 API 36 emulator, a folder on shared storage: a save with no device edit left no copy; after `echo` into the file from adb, the next save produced `notes.txt.device-<time>` holding the device text, shown in the Explorer, with `notes.txt` holding the editor's text; two further saves added no second copy; a `mv` over the file from the in-app terminal after another device edit made a new copy.

title: fix: sort lists case-insensitively
body:
String-keyed sorts (title, artist, album, name, composer, path) used Kotlin's natural String ordering, which compares by UTF-16 code unit. As a result uppercase letters (A-Z) sorted before all lowercase ones (a-z), so lowercase-named tracks, albums, and artists were pushed to the end of the list instead of their correct alphabetical position.

Apply .lowercase() to the string sort keys so ordering is case-insensitive, matching the existing convention already used in FolderSort, FolderHierarchySort, and GenreSort. This also makes the list panels' go-to-letter fast-scroller land correctly, since it groups sections by the case-folded first letter.

title: fix(cleaner): decode each URL component against its own delimiters
body:
## TL;DR

"Decode URL" decoded the serialized URL as one string, which can only apply the strictest structural rule everywhere — so an embedded target URL, the payload of every redirect wrapper and the whole point of the option, was displayed entirely unchanged. Decoding now happens per component on the parsed URL, each against the delimiters that actually apply to it, so a parameter value reveals its target while the path keeps its `%2F`. This also fixes "Extract URL", which re-serialized the encoded URL and so was never decoded at all.

## Notes

`CleanedUrl` carries the decoded form as `display`; `cleaned` stays encoded, because the change list and the matching of a change on the next pass are built from it.

Reported in https://github.com/leon-cleaning-services/leon/issues/49#issuecomment-5769390928.

## Testing

1. Enable "Decode URL" in settings.
2. Share `https://www.example.com/gp/r.html?U=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.example.com%2Fdp%2FB01%3Fref%3Dx`. The result must read `…?U=https://www.example.com/dp/B01?ref=x`.
3. Share `https://www.example.com/Hello%2FWorld?q=a%26b`. The `%2F` and the `%26` must stay escaped.
4. Enable "Extract URL" as well and repeat step 2 — the extracted URL must be decoded too.
5. Run `./gradlew :core-domain:jvmTest :shared:desktopTest`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(desktop): open URLs when Desktop.Action.BROWSE is unsupported
body:
## TL;DR

The Open button did nothing on Linux: `Desktop.getDesktop().isSupported(Desktop.Action.BROWSE)` returns `false` on Fedora (the JDK reaches for gio, which frequently isn't resolvable), so `DesktopUrlActions.open` returned early without doing anything. It now falls back to the platform's own URL opener — `xdg-open`, `open` on macOS, `rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler` on Windows.

## Testing

1. Install the RPM or run the AppImage on Linux (or `./gradlew :desktopApp:run`).
2. Clean a URL and press **Open** — the default browser must open it.
3. Same on the History and Settings screens, which use the same `UrlActions.open`.

title: fix(cleaner): keep the URL structure intact when decoding
body:
## TL;DR

"Decode URL" decoded every percent-escape in the whole cleaned text, including the ones that define the URL's structure (`%2F`, `%26`, `%3F`, `%20`, `+`, …), which could turn a path segment into an extra `/` or otherwise change what the URL addresses. `decodeUrl()` now takes a `keepStructure` flag that leaves those structural escapes in their original spelling while still decoding everything else, such as UTF-8 text; the display path in `Cleaner.clean()` now passes `keepStructure = true`, while the redirect-unwrapping `Decode.PercentDecode` step (which needs `%3A%2F%2F` to become `://`) is untouched.

## Testing

1. Share `https://www.some.site/?q=Hello%20M%C3%BCnchen` with Léon and enable "Decode URL" in settings.
2. The result should read `https://www.some.site/?q=Hello%20München` — `%20` stays intact, `M%C3%BC` decodes to `Mü`.
3. Run `./gradlew :core-domain:test`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(ui): tint the background image so it is visible in dark mode

title: fix(sanitizer): match domains against the complete host
body:
## TL;DR

`matchesDomainRegex` ended in `.*`, so the domain pattern only had to be a *prefix* of the host and every domain-specific sanitizer also matched lookalike hosts such as `example.com.evil.com`. The shared helper now requires the pattern to cover the host completely, and the individual sanitizer patterns — which the helper cannot fix on their own — are tightened alongside it.

Closes #795

## The shared helper

`matchesDomainRegex` no longer matches the whole string. It matches the pattern from the start and then checks that the match reaches the end of the host, which is the first `:`, `/`, `?` or `#` after the scheme:

```kotlin
val match = Regex("^(?:https?://)?(?:www\\.)?(?:$domain)").find(this) ?: return false
return match.range.last + 1 >= hostEndIndex()
```

- **Ports still match.** The host ends at `:`, so `https://example.com:8443/p` is matched by `example.com`, as before.
- **Patterns which reach into the path still work.** `google\.com/maps` produces a match *longer* than the host, which passes the check. Only patterns that stop short of the host end are rejected.

`matchesSubdomains` had the same hole plus a leading `.*`, which matched the domain anywhere at all — `https://evil.com/?u=feishu.cn` and `notfeishu.cn` both passed. It is now expressed in terms of the fixed helper as an optional chain of leading labels.

## The sanitizer patterns

Three defects, none of which the helper can catch:

| Problem | Sanitizers | Example that wrongly matched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unescaped `.`, matching any character | Netflix, Facebook, Wikipedia, GeoRiot | `https://target-georiot.com/Proxy-ashx` |
| Wildcard crosses the host boundary | AliExpress, Amazon, eBay, Google Search, LinkSynergy, Newegg, Flipkart, Wikipedia | `https://ebay.evil.com?u=/itm/1` |
| `containsMatchIn` on an unanchored pattern | YouTube Music, YouTube short URLs, Amazon products, MyDealz | `https://evil.com/?u=music.youtube.com` |

The third group is the most severe, because two of those sanitizers rewrite the URL rather than only stripping parameters. `AmazonProductSanitizer` turned `https://evil.com/?u=https://amazon.com/dp/B01` into `https://amazon.com/dp/B01/`, and `YoutubeMusicSanitizer` deleted `music.` out of the middle of a query string.

Two related changes came out of this:

- `MyDealzDomains.DOMAINS_REGEX` is now a pattern string for `matchesDomainRegex` instead of a `Regex` used with `containsMatchIn`, so both MyDealz sanitizers are anchored. Subdomains stay allowed.
- `LinkSynergySanitizer` never matched its own links: real ones are hosted at `click.linksynergy.com`, which the pattern rejected because it allowed no subdomain. It now matches, so the sanitizer actually runs.

### What is deliberately not fixed

Where a sanitizer covers a brand across all of its ccTLDs — `amazon\.[^/?#:]+`, `ebay\.…`, `google\.…` — `amazon.evil.com` is structurally indistinguishable from `amazon.com.br` without a public suffix list. Those wildcards are now confined to the host, but they still accept a lookalike. Since these sanitizers only strip parameters, a false positive is harmless while a false negative leaks tracking data, so the loose end is left loose on purpose. AliExpress is the exception: it has no multi-label TLD, so its pattern now rejects a dot in that position.

## Testing

No behaviour change is intended for any legitimate URL. Every pre-existing test passes untouched.

1. `./gradlew :core-common:test` — 14 tests, 5 new: lookalike hosts, the `@` user-information trick, ports, and `matchesSubdomains`.
2. `./gradlew :core-domain:test` — 250 tests, 33 new, one pair per tightened sanitizer: a real URL that must still match and the lookalike that must not.
3. By hand: share `https://substack.com.evil.com/p/article?r=1` with Léon — it must be left untouched, while `https://substack.com/p/article?r=1` is still cleaned.

_Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5)_

title: fix(sanitizer): keep the article reference of Substack URLs
body:
## TL;DR

Substack puts the article reference into the query string of `app-link` URLs, so removing all
parameters left links that no longer pointed at any article. The sanitizer now keeps
`publication_id`/`post_id`, matches every `*.substack.com` host instead of only `substack.com` and
`open.substack.com`, and rewrites the `open.substack.com/pub/<publication>` indirection to the
canonical publication URL.

## Notable decisions

* The fragment is now kept, since it references a section or comment of the article. Previously it
  was removed whenever the URL also had parameters, because `RegexFactory.AllParameters` matches
  everything from `?` onwards.
* The host is matched more strictly than `matchesDomainRegex` does: the path has to start with `/`,
  so `https://substack.com.example.com/p/foo` no longer matches. That mattered less while the
  sanitizer only trimmed parameters, but this one also rewrites the host.
* `substack.com/redirect/<uuid>?j=<blob>` links are deliberately left as they were. It is not
  publicly documented whether the `j` blob carries the destination or only the recipient, so
  dropping it stays the existing behaviour rather than a new assumption.
* A cleaned `app-link` URL stays opaque, because Substack only resolves it to the readable slug via
  a redirect and the app makes no network requests.

## Testing

1. Share `https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=89120&post_id=209203336&isFreemail=true&r=<reader>&token=<jwt>`
   with Léon. The cleaned URL must be
   `https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=89120&post_id=209203336` and must still open
   the article.
2. Share `https://open.substack.com/pub/fosspost/p/some-article?r=abc&triedRedirect=true`. The
   cleaned URL must be `https://fosspost.substack.com/p/some-article`.
3. Share `https://fosspost.substack.com/p/some-article?r=abc#comment-1`. The `r` parameter must be
   gone while `#comment-1` is kept.
4. Run `./gradlew :core-domain:test`.

---

This is my first open source contribution, so please say directly if anything here doesn't match
how you'd want it done. I use Léon every day, mostly on newsletter links, which is how I ran into
this — thanks for building and maintaining it.

The `bug` label applies, but I can't set labels from a fork.

title: fix: perform action after clean again when sharing identical text
body:
## Summary
- Sharing the exact same text/URL twice while Léon is already running was silently swallowed by value-equality checks all along the intent → state → StateFlow → composition chain, so the configured "action after clean" (e.g. opening the share menu) only fired once per distinct string.
- Each incoming `Intent` is now tagged with an id that is stable across activity recreation (e.g. configuration changes) but changes for every genuinely new intent, and the "already performed" bookkeeping moved from the Compose `remember` into `MainScreenViewModel` so it also survives configuration changes without re-firing the action.
- Also fixes a related defect where rotating the device while a result was on screen re-triggered the action after clean.

Fixes #775

## Root cause (verified by reproduction on-device)
1. `MainActivity` held `sourceText` as `mutableStateOf<String?>`, so assigning the same string on a repeat share triggered no recomposition.
2. `MainScreen`'s `LaunchedEffect(sourceText.value)` was keyed on the value, so it wouldn't relaunch either.
3. `MainScreenViewModel`'s internal `MutableStateFlow<String?>` doesn't re-emit an equal value.
4. `remember(uiState.result)` / `LaunchedEffect(uiState.result, …)` in `MainScreen` keyed on the `Result.Success` data class, which was structurally equal for a repeat.

`launchMode="singleTask"` keeps the process alive across shares, so all four gates held — which is why killing the app "fixed" it.

## Test plan
- [x] `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest` — new `MainScreenViewModelTest` covers: distinct ids for identical text, one-shot `consumeActionAfterClean` semantics, and the #775 regression (new id ⇒ action fires again for identical text)
- [x] `./gradlew spotlessCheck lintDebug`
- [x] Manual verification on emulator (API 36) with *Action after clean = Open share menu*: repeat-sharing the identical URL now reopens the share sheet every time; rotating with a result on screen no longer re-opens it; distinct URLs and normal navigation are unaffected
