title: Fix background incoming-call ringing on Android 17
body:
### Goal

Closes: #AND-1490

Restore background incoming-call ringing on Android 17.

### Problem

On Android 17, the incoming-call ringtone may be muted when the app is in the background.

### Root cause

Android 17 introduces stricter background audio playback rules. Playing an incoming-call ringtone directly through `MediaPlayer` or `Ringtone` from `CallService` is no longer reliable when the app is in the background.

### Existing flow

For an incoming call, the SDK currently:

1. Starts `CallService`.
2. Uses `CallSoundAndVibrationPlayer` to play the ringtone and vibration.
3. Posts the incoming-call notification.
4. Registers the call with Telecom when Telecom is enabled.

In this flow, `CallService` owns the ringtone.

### Proposed solution

On Android 17, the SDK will try to register the incoming call with Telecom before presenting it.

When Telecom registration succeeds:

1. The call uses the Telecom route.
2. The incoming-call notification owns the ringtone and vibration.
3. The notification is posted on a high-importance channel configured with:
   - The incoming-call ringtone.
   - `USAGE_NOTIFICATION_RINGTONE`.
   - The configured vibration pattern.
4. `FLAG_INSISTENT` keeps the notification ringtone playing until the call is accepted, rejected, or otherwise ends.
5. `CallService` does not play the legacy incoming-call ringtone.

If Telecom cannot be used or registration fails, the SDK falls back to the existing `CallService` flow.

The behavior before Android 17 remains unchanged.

### Supporting changes

| Problem | Solution |
| --- | --- |
| An incoming-call notification can be rebuilt and posted shortly after the initial notification. Replacing an actively ringing notification too quickly was observed to interrupt its sound. | Use two safeguards: skip equivalent notification updates and delay non-duplicate updates by 1.3 seconds. The 1.3-second value is an empirical safety margin, not an Android-documented threshold. |
| Android notification-channel sound and vibration settings cannot be changed after the channel has been created. The existing incoming-call channels may already exist without ringtone configuration. | Use new incoming-call channel IDs on Android 17. These channels are created with ringtone sound, ringtone audio attributes, and vibration from their first use. |
| An incoming-call update can select a different channel after the full-screen activity moves the app to the foreground. Changing the channel can interrupt ringing. | Preserve the initial notification’s channel ID while the incoming call remains unanswered. |
| Telecom registration and service dependencies could be created more than once by separate notification or service paths. | Move incoming-call infrastructure ownership to the client and reuse the same instances across the incoming-call lifecycle. |
| Android 17 and older Android versions require different incoming-call flows. Mixing both paths would increase regression risk. | Split incoming-call handling into Android 17 and pre-Android 17 coordinators. |

### Compatibility considerations

- Pre-Android 17 behavior remains unchanged.
- Android 17 uses new incoming-call channel IDs.
- User sound and vibration preferences from the old channel cannot be transferred automatically to the new channel.
- `MutedRingingConfig.playIncomingSoundIfMuted` does not apply when the notification owns the ringtone. Notification-channel sound cannot bypass the user’s silent-mode or channel settings.

### Implementation

#### Android-version-specific incoming-call flow

Incoming-call handling is now split between two coordinators:

- `PreAndroid17IncomingCallCoordinator` preserves the existing `CallService` flow.
- `Android17IncomingCallCoordinator` attempts to register the incoming call with Telecom before creating and posting the notification.

On Android 17 and above:

1. The SDK checks whether Telecom can be used.
2. The incoming call is registered with Telecom.
3. After successful registration, the incoming-call notification is created and posted.
4. The notification owns the incoming ringtone and vibration.
5. `CallService` does not start its legacy ringtone observers for Telecom-backed calls.
6. If Telecom is unavailable or registration fails, the SDK falls back to the legacy `CallService` flow.

Pre-Android 17 behavior remains unchanged.

#### Telecom lifecycle

- Telecom registration is owned by a single client-level repository instance.
- `registerAppWithTelecom()` is performed once for that instance.
- Duplicate `CallsManager` creation and Telecom registration are avoided.
- Incoming calls record their selected service route so that Telecom and `CallService` do not both own the same responsibilities.
- Telecom-backed calls use `TelecomNotificationUpdateObserver` for notification updates.

#### Notification-owned ringing

Android 17 uses new incoming-call notification channel IDs. These channels are configured on first creation with:

- High importance.
- The configured incoming-call ringtone.
- `AudioAttributes.USAGE_NOTIFICATION_RINGTONE`.
- The configured vibration pattern.

While the incoming call is unanswered, the notification uses `FLAG_INSISTENT` so Android continues playing the ringtone. When the call is accepted, the flag is removed and `FLAG_ONLY_ALERT_ONCE` is applied.

Because notification-channel sound and vibration settings are persistent and cannot be replaced after channel creation, Android 17 uses new channel IDs instead of modifying the existing channels.

#### Notification update stability

Incoming-call notifications can receive an update shortly after they are initially posted. Replacing an actively ringing notification too quickly can interrupt its ringtone.

The following safeguards were added for Android 17 incoming calls:

- Equivalent notification updates are skipped.
- Non-equivalent updates are delayed by the configured stabilization duration.
- Unaccepted incoming-call updates preserve the initial notification channel ID.
- Notification comparison is applied only to Android 17 incoming-call notifications.
- The full-screen pending intent opens the call activity directly and does not cancel the ringing notification.

#### CallService ownership

`CallService` checks the selected service route before installing its observers.

- Pre-Android 17 calls continue using the existing observers.
- Android 17 legacy fallback calls continue using the existing observers.
- Android 17 Telecom-backed calls do not install observers that are owned by the Telecom path.
- `CallSoundAndVibrationPlayer` is not used for notification-owned incoming-call ringing.

#### API compatibility

- Existing notification configuration APIs remain available.
- Android 17-specific implementation details remain internal.


### Testing

#### Unit tests

Added or updated tests for:

- Android 17 and pre-Android 17 coordinator selection.
- Telecom-first registration ordering.
- Fallback when Telecom is unavailable or registration fails.
- Single `CallsManager` and Telecom registration lifecycle.
- Incoming-call service-route selection.
- CallService observer ownership for Telecom and legacy routes.
- Notification-owned calls not using `CallSoundAndVibrationPlayer`.
- Android 17 incoming-call channel selection.
- Ringing channel sound, vibration, and ringtone audio attributes.
- `FLAG_INSISTENT` while the call is unanswered.
- Stopping notification ringing after the call is accepted.
- Preserving the initial channel ID across notification updates.
- Skipping equivalent incoming-call notification updates.
- Delaying non-equivalent incoming-call notification updates.
- Telecom notification updates.
- Accept, reject, and service-cleanup behavior.
- Pre-Android 17 behavior remaining unchanged.

#### Manual validation

Validated the Android 17 flow on an Android 17 emulator:

- The incoming call is registered with Telecom.
- The incoming-call notification is displayed.
- The notification ringtone and vibration start.
- The ringtone continues while the call remains unanswered.
- Opening the full-screen incoming-call UI does not dismiss the ringing notification.
- Accepting or rejecting the call stops ringing and removes or replaces the incoming notification.
- Notification updates preserve the ringing channel.
- No legacy ringtone is started for a Telecom-backed call.

Also validated that an emulator-specific failure did not reproduce on a second Android 17 emulator.

#### Current automation limitation

The existing incoming-call E2E tests depend on push delivery, which is not reliable in CI. In addition, CI emulators currently run with audio disabled, so they cannot verify that sound physically plays.

The deterministic routing, ownership, channel configuration, update, and cleanup behavior is therefore covered by unit tests. Actual ringtone playback is validated manually on Android 17.

title: Fix the outgoing ringing state stuck on Connecting in join-and-ring
body:
### Goal

Fix AND-1454. After #1782 the nightly E2E run is green on API 28, 31 and 32, but [run 33062751723](https://github.com/GetStream/stream-video-android/actions/runs/33062751723) still fails on API 33, 34 and 35 with two issues in the outgoing ringing tests.

### Implementation

**Issue 1: the outgoing call UI stays on "Connecting..." while the call is already connected.** The run artifacts show the exact sequence. In the join-and-ring flow the SFU `JoinCallResponseEvent` sets the ringing state to `Outgoing` directly, but the ring request registers the call in `client.state.ringingCall` only later. In the failing attempts a `call.session_started` coordinator event landed in that window, re-ran `updateRingingState()` with `hasRingingCall = false`, and downgraded Outgoing back to Idle (logcat: `Updating ringing state Outgoing -> Idle`). Nothing recomputed the state afterwards and no `CallRingEvent` is delivered to the caller, so the state stayed Idle and the UI rendered the full screen "Connecting..." (`LoadingContent`) until the 30s wait for `Stream_DeclineCallButton` timed out. Passing runs recovered only because some later event happened to re-run `updateRingingState()` after the ring completed.

Two changes in the core:

- `CallState.updateRingingState()` keeps the current Outgoing state instead of falling back to Idle while join-and-ring is in progress and the ringing call is not registered yet.
- `CallJoinCoordinator.joinAndRing()` recomputes the ringing state right after the ring request succeeds, so the state recovers deterministically without depending on a later coordinator event.

**Issue 2: instant asserts in `assertOutgoingCall` race the async control state.** On API 34 the outgoing screen was rendered but the microphone toggle still showed the muted state at the instant the check ran. The label, avatar, microphone and camera checks now poll with `waitDisplayed`, the same pattern AND-1445 applied to the settings menu guards.

The `testUserAcceptsTheIncomingVideoCall` failure seen on #1776 is a different bucket (leave-when-last-in-call firing during an SFU reconnect) and is tracked in AND-1455.

**Further nightly buckets fixed on this branch** (found while verifying the fix with nightly runs on the branch):

- `assertUserMicrophone` polled the control toggle but checked the participant view icon with an instant `isDisplayed()`. The hierarchy dumps taken right after the failures already contained the expected icon, so the state arrives and only the instant check misses it. Both checks poll now. This bucket failed `testCameraAndMicrophoneConfigurationInLobby` (all 3 attempts, API 32) and `testUserMicrophone` (all 3 attempts on PR #1764, plus single attempts on several API levels).
- `assertRecordingView` could leak a raw `StaleObjectException` from `waitToAppear(...).isDisplayed()` and hide the real failure. It uses the stale-safe `waitDisplayed` now.
- The caller had no outgoing call notification in the join-and-ring flow: the notification is posted by the foreground service started with `TRIGGER_OUTGOING_CALL`, which only `registerOutgoingRing()` starts, and only the create-with-ring path called it. On develop this was sometimes masked when the ringing state flapped to Idle and the ongoing service started instead; with the deterministic Outgoing state it never rendered. `joinAndRing` now calls `registerOutgoingRing()` on ring success, and the outgoing ringing E2E test asserts the notification is shown while ringing and dismissed after the decline.
- A second cause behind the reconnection test flake (the connection state staying "Reconnecting.." after a recovered reconnect) is fixed separately in #1802, split out on review request because it changes `RtcSession`. Until #1802 merges, that bucket can still occasionally exhaust a Test compose batch here; a re-run covers it.
- `testReconnectionDuringCallRecording` raced its own recording window: the buddy stops the recording 30s after its start request, the composite recorder needs 20-30s to start, and the drop plus reconnect plus asserts consumed the rest on slow emulators. The recording actually survives the reconnect fine (it is server side and the recording participant stays online). The window is now 90s. For comparison, neither the JS nor the Swift SDK has a reconnect-plus-recording scenario or any reconnect-time recording handling, so no SDK change is needed for this one.

For the core change, the Swift SDK confirms the approach: its `joinAndRingCall` sets the outgoing state explicitly and suppresses competing call state updates while the ring is in flight (`skipCallStateUpdates` in `CallViewModel`), which is the same principle as keeping Outgoing authoritative during join-and-ring here. The JS SDK avoids the bug class entirely by using explicit state transitions instead of recomputing from flags.

### 🎨 UI Changes

Not applicable. No visual changes, the fix removes a state where the outgoing ringing UI never appeared.

### Testing

- New `RingingStateJoinAndRingTest` reproduces the race on a real `CallState` with a mocked client: one test asserts that a recompute in the pre-ring window keeps Outgoing, one asserts that the recompute after `markRinging()` yields `Outgoing(acceptedByCallee = false)`. Both fail without the fix and pass with it.
- Full `:stream-video-android-core` unit test suite and `apiCheck` pass locally, and the E2E androidTest source set compiles.
- `CallStateTelecomHoldTest` and the `CallJoinCoordinatorTest` additions cover the remaining touched branches.
- Verified locally on an API 35 emulator through the real fastlane flow: the outgoing ringing test fails at the notification assert with the old code and passes with the fix.
- CI verification: dispatch the E2E workflow on this branch with `test_class: io.getstream.video.android.tests.RingingTests` on API 33, 34 and 35, where the nightly failed. The full branch nightly (run 33155106721) was green on 5 of 6 API levels before the notification and ICE fixes; the remaining bucket is AND-1455.

### How to reproduce the issues and verify the fixes

**The stuck "Connecting..." bug (state race).** It rarely fires naturally on a fast local emulator, so either use CI sampling or widen the window locally:

- CI: dispatch the "E2E Tests" workflow with `test_class: io.getstream.video.android.tests.RingingTests#testUserRejectsTheOutgoingAudioCall` and `api_level: 35`. On develop it failed 3 of 3 batch jobs (runs 33062751723 and 33142442425, where API 28 failed 3 of 3 too). On this branch the same dispatch passes, and the full branch nightly (run 33155106721) is green on all six API levels for the ringing tests.
- Manual: on develop, apply the patch below to make the race deterministic, then start a Direct Call (the "Join first" checkbox is on by default). The caller sticks on the full screen "Connecting..." forever. Same patch on this branch shows the outgoing screen.

<details>
<summary>Patch to make the race deterministic</summary>

```kotlin
// CallJoinCoordinator.joinAndRing: delay the ring request so call.session_started
// always lands in the window between the SFU join response and the ring completion.
).flatMap { rtcSession ->
    logger.d { "[joinAndRing] Joined #ringing; #track; ring: $members" }
    delay(3_000) // repro only
    apiClient.ring(RingCallRequest(isVideoEnabled(), members)).map {
```

</details>

**The missing outgoing call notification.** Deterministic, no patch needed: on develop (or this branch before commit e6c6ad9cee), start a Direct Call with "Join first" checked. No caller notification appears, and logcat prints `Outgoing call service should already be running`. With the fix the "Calling..." notification appears while ringing and disappears after the decline. The E2E test now asserts exactly that, verified locally on an API 35 emulator through the real fastlane flow: the test fails at the notification assert with the old code and passes with the fix.

  - Reduced timing-related issues when displaying outgoing call labels, avatars, and microphone controls.

title: Fix concurrency grouping in the distribution workflows
body:
### Goal

Refs [AND-1497](https://linear.app/stream/issue/AND-1497/distribute-v2-demo-app-builds-via-firebase-app-distribution)

Follow-up to #1813. The distribution workflows either had no concurrency group or shared one across refs, so runs could cancel or overtake each other.

The worst case is `internal-app-distribute.yml`, which publishes to Google Play. It triggers on both `develop` (internal track) and `main` (alpha track) and put every run in one group. `cancel-in-progress` is evaluated on the incoming run, where a `develop` push resolves it to `true`, so a push to `develop` could cancel an in-progress `main` run and interrupt `publishBundle` mid-upload. The existing `!contains(github.ref, 'main')` guard stops a `main` run from cancelling others, but nothing stopped others from cancelling a `main` run.

`app-distribute-v2.yml` had no group at all, which was raised in review on #1813 and did not make that merge. `app-distribute.yml` had none either, so two pushes to `main` could distribute in parallel and let the older run reach testers last. `sdk-size-updates.yml` had the same unscoped group as the Play workflow.

### Implementation

Every one of these workflows now groups on `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}`, matching `android.yml`, `e2e-test.yml`, `e2e-test-cron.yml`, `pr-quality.yml` and `sdk-size-checks.yml`.

| Workflow | Triggers | Change | `cancel-in-progress` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `app-distribute-v2.yml` | `develop-v2` | group added, then scoped to the ref | `true` |
| `app-distribute.yml` | `main` | group added | `true` |
| `internal-app-distribute.yml` | `develop`, `main` | group scoped to the ref | `${{ !contains(github.ref, 'main')}}`, unchanged |
| `sdk-size-updates.yml` | `develop` | group scoped to the ref | `true`, unchanged |

Each file keeps its own `cancel-in-progress` rather than being made uniform. On `internal-app-distribute.yml` the guard still earns its place once the group is ref-scoped: two `main` pushes queue instead of one cancelling a live Play publish.

### Testing

Concurrency is only observable with two overlapping runs, so it cannot be demonstrated by a single run. `actionlint` in CI covers the syntax, and all four files were confirmed to parse with the expected `concurrency` block.

Nothing here changes what any workflow builds or where it publishes. `app-distribute-v2.yml` itself was proven end to end in #1813, and the first real run from `develop-v2` after that merge, [34201013732](https://github.com/GetStream/stream-video-android/actions/runs/34201013732), succeeded and distributed to `stream-testers`.

Note for reviewers: this PR grew after the first approval. It started as one line in `app-distribute-v2.yml` and now touches four workflows, including the Google Play publish pipeline, so it is worth another look.

title: Fix the flaky MockK Context setup in PictureInPictureTest
body:
### Goal

Fix the flaky `PictureInPictureTest > should enter pip mode with correct params` test. It fails intermittently on CI during `setup` with:

```
io.mockk.MockKException: Can't instantiate proxy for class android.content.Context
Caused by: io.mockk.proxy.MockKAgentException: Value for this result is not assigned
```

The failure is a race in MockK's inline agent when it proxies platform classes. The test shares its JVM with the Paparazzi snapshot tests, which append to the bootstrap classpath, and that combination makes the agent attach unreliable on the Linux runners. Seen on PR #1776, where the diff was test-only.

Resolves [AND-1446](https://linear.app/stream/issue/AND-1446/fix-the-mockk-context-flake-in-pictureinpicturetest).

### Implementation

The test class already runs with Robolectric, so the platform classes do not need to be mocked at all:

- Replaced `mockk<Context>()` with a real Robolectric `Activity` (`Robolectric.buildActivity(Activity::class.java).create().get()`). Since the context is itself an `Activity`, `findActivity()` resolves it naturally, so the `mockkStatic("...PictureInPictureKt")` call is gone too.
- The PiP system feature is now controlled with `shadowOf(activity.packageManager).setSystemFeature(...)` instead of mocked `PackageManager` and `Resources`.
- The enter-PiP assertions now check `activity.isInPictureInPictureMode`. Robolectric's `ShadowActivity` sets that flag in both `enterPictureInPictureMode` overloads (verified in the Robolectric 4.11.1 shadow source).
- MockK is kept only for the domain classes (`Call`, `ScreenSharingSession`, `ParticipantState`). `tearDown` now only calls `clearAllMocks()`; the old `unmockkStatic(ContextCompat::class)` was unmocking something that was never mocked.

With no inline-agent proxying of `android.content.Context`, the race that caused the flake cannot happen anymore.

After review, the assertions were strengthened:

- The `getPictureInPictureParams` tests assert the built params values where the runtime allows it: `isAutoEnterEnabled` on S and above, plus aspect ratio and title on TIRAMISU (`getAspectRatio()` returned `float` until API 32, so it can only be asserted from 33).
- The configured auto-enter test covers both the enabled and the disabled case, so removing the `setAutoEnterEnabled` call in production fails the tests.
- The `getAspect` tests pass `Configuration.ORIENTATION_*`, the values production actually feeds, instead of `ActivityInfo.SCREEN_ORIENTATION_*`.

### 🎨 UI Changes

No UI changes, this is a test-only change.

### Testing

Run the test class locally:

```
./gradlew :stream-video-android-ui-compose:testDebugUnitTest --tests "io.getstream.video.android.compose.pip.PictureInPictureTest"
```

All 10 tests pass (0 failures, 0 skipped).

title: Fix the logout main-thread freeze in StreamVideoClient cleanup
body:
### Goal

Fix the 5 second UI freeze on logout that makes the E2E tests on the develop-v2 merge PR #1790 fail deterministically on the sign-in screen waits, and remove a swallowed NPE in the same code path.

Resolves AND-1466.

### Implementation

`StreamVideoClient.cleanup()` bridged the suspend `streamClient.disconnect()` with `runBlocking`. When an app calls `StreamVideo.removeClient()` from the main thread (the demo app's logout does), this self-deadlocks: `disconnect()` stops its lifecycle monitor through `runOnMainLooper`, which posts to the main looper and blocks on a CountDownLatch with a 5 second safety timeout (stream-android-core `Threading.kt`). The main looper is parked by the `runBlocking`, so the post never runs and every logout freezes the UI for the full 5 seconds. As a side effect the lifecycle observer was never removed.

Changes in `StreamVideoClient.cleanup()`:

- When called on the main thread, the disconnect now runs on a detached IO scope instead of `runBlocking`. Other threads keep the existing synchronous ordering. The main-looper check is null-guarded because plain JVM unit tests get null loopers (`isReturnDefaultValues = true`).
- `buildStopIntent(...)` legitimately returns null when the service is not running; the result is now handled with `?.let` instead of passing null into `context.stopService(...)`, which threw a swallowed `NullPointerException` on every logout without a running call service.

### 🎨 UI Changes

No visual changes. Behavior change: logout no longer freezes the UI for 5 seconds.

### Testing

- New Robolectric regression test `StreamVideoClientCleanupTest` runs `cleanup()` on a real main-looper thread against a mocked 6 second disconnect: it fails on the old code ("took 6218ms") and passes with the fix while verifying the disconnect is still dispatched.
- Full `:stream-video-android-core:testDebugUnitTest` suite passes.
- Verified end to end on an API 35 emulator against the #1790 merge branch plus this fix: `CallLifecycleTests#testUserReentersTheCallAsAnotherUser` now gets past the sign-in wait that failed on both CI attempts. It then hits a separate demo-app re-login race, tracked as AND-1467.

title: Fix notification dismissal for Leave/Hang Up notification actions
body: ### Goal Closes [#AND-1252](https://getstream.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/81537) Stacked on https://github.com/GetStream/stream-video-android/pull/1731 A customer reported that call notifications were not being dismissed after tapping the Leave/Hang Up action from the notification. Notification removal can be triggered from two different components: 1. CallServiceNotificationManager 2. LeaveCallBroadcastReceiver During the investigation, we found that `LeaveCallBroadcastReceiver` was unable to retrieve the correct notification ID from `INTENT_EXTRA_NOTIFICATION_ID`. The SDK was incorrectly populating this extra with the call CID instead of the notification ID when creating notification action intents. As a result, `LeaveCallBroadcastReceiver` could not cancel the corresponding notification, leaving stale notifications visible after the call was ended from the notification action. This change ensures that the correct notification ID is attached to the intent so that notifications are properly dismissed when users leave or hang up a call from the notification. ### Implementation | Before | After | | -------- | ------- | | | | ### 🎨 UI Changes None ### Testing Test notification dismissal for 1. Regular Calls - Try join and leave back and forth quickly - Leave from Notification/ Leave from hangup button 2. 1-1 Calls 3. Livestream calls ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Enhanced notification ID management to ensure incoming call notifications and leave call actions are correctly processed and dismissed across all scenarios. * **Chores** * Deprecated legacy notification ID constant to streamline internal notification tracking.

title: Fix a crash when application put to background restriction
body:
### Goal
Closes #AND-1251
Stacked on top of PR: https://github.com/GetStream/stream-video-android/pull/1729
This change improves notification handling when the application is subject to background restrictions.

`CallStyle` notifications may fail to be posted as foreground service notifications on restricted devices, resulting in a `CannotPostForegroundServiceNotificationException` ("Bad notification for startForeground"). 
See [GH Issue: Demo app always crashes with restricted battery settings
](https://github.com/GetStream/stream-video-android/issues/1549)

### Implementation

To avoid this issue, the SDK now detects when the application is background-restricted and falls back to a standard notification instead of using CallStyle.

**Changes**

1. Detect whether the application is background-restricted using ActivityManager.isBackgroundRestricted.
2. Avoid using CallStyle notifications when restrictions are active.
3. Fall back to a standard notification with actions to prevent foreground notification failures.

### 🎨 UI Changes

None

### Testing

1. Put your application on background restriction mode (It is available on Samsung Devices)
2. Go to demo-app application's settings
3. Choose Battery
4. Choose Restricted
5. Join a room/ make a call
6. Put your app in background ~ everything should run smoothly

### Additional Notes

* In background-restricted mode, the ongoing call notification can be dismissed by the user while the call remains active.
* Similar behavior was observed in WhatsApp and Google Meet.
* This PR does not introduce any additional handling for this scenario.

title: Move @Preview composables out of published artifact to fix R8 builds
body:
### Goal
Fixes [1244](https://linear.app/stream/issue/AND-1244/fix-r8-build-failure-with-streampreviewdatautils-classes-referenced)

R8/minified release builds of apps consuming `stream-video-android-ui-compose` fail with `Missing class io.getstream.video.android.mock.StreamPreviewDataUtils` (and `StreamPreviewDataUtilsKt`). The compose module depends on `stream-video-android-previewdata` as `compileOnly`, but the Compose compiler emits `ComposableSingletons$*` lambda holders for the inline `@Preview` functions into production classes, so the preview-data references leak into the published release artifact even though that module is never on a consumer's runtime classpath.

Fixes #1448

### Implementation

- Moved every `@Preview` composable out of `src/main` into a new **debug-only** source set (`src/debug/kotlin`, one `<Name>Preview.kt` per original file, same package). Previews still render in Android Studio (debug variant) but are no longer compiled into the release artifact.
- Changed the `stream-video-android-previewdata` dependency from `compileOnly` to `debugImplementation`.
- Two production composables referenced by previews were widened `private` → `internal` (`CalLCenterContent`, `ParticipantActionsWithoutState`). One preview that was also used by production code (`ModerationWarningUiContentDemo` via `LocalInspectionMode`) stays in `main` with the `@Preview` moved to a thin debug wrapper.
- Declared `kotlinx-datetime` (0.6.1) explicitly as an `implementation` dependency of the compose module — it is used by the livestream countdown UI in production but was only arriving transitively, which also caused `Missing class kotlinx.datetime.*` R8 errors (reported in the same issue thread).
- Regenerated the public API dump: 50 compiler-generated `ComposableSingletons$*` preview classes are removed from the published API surface.

title: Fix self cancelling coroutine code (2/4)
body: ### Goal Closes #AND-1223 Fix self cancelling coroutine code > Please review and approve the PRs, but do not merge them yet. > > Each PR is stacked on top of the previous one, so every subsequent PR uses the branch from the PR below it as its base. As a result, they are not currently targeting develop. ### Implementation Found an internal issue: reconnection flow cancels its own coroutine mid-flight What happens: When the SFU disconnects, the old session detects it and launches a rejoin on its own coroutine scope. During rejoin, we clean up the old session — which cancels that same coroutine scope. The rejoin coroutine is now cancelled but still running (cooperative cancellation), so it proceeds to connect the new session's WebSocket. The moment it hits the first suspension point (waiting for the socket state), it throws CancellationException. Why the demo-app still works: The socket state is also being observed independently by a separate coroutine (stateJob) which is on the new session's scope. That coroutine correctly picks up the Connected state and updates all the call state, so the call recovers anyway. Root cause: The reconnect coroutine should not be launched from old session's scope (which is destroyed as part of reconnection). Here is what is happening ```kotlin reconnectRejoin() → called via: coroutineScope.launch { call.reconnect(...) } // RtcSession.kt:716 → coroutineScope is the OLD session's scope (child of supervisorJob) → oldSession.prepareRejoin("rejoin") // Call.kt:1163 → cancelActiveWork() // RtcSession.kt:2013 → cleanup() // RtcSession.kt:2014 → supervisorJob.cancel() // RtcSession.kt:1188 ↑ supervisorJob is the PARENT of coroutineScope ↑ cancelling it cancels coroutineScope ↑ cancelling coroutineScope cancels the reconnect coroutine (the very one running reconnectRejoin right now) → newSession.connectInternal(...) // Call.kt:1181 → withTimeoutOrNull { ... } → logger.d { "withTimeoutOrNull" } // prints ✓ (not a suspension point) → state().first { ... } // FIRST suspension point → Kotlin checks isActive → false → throws CancellationException("Job was cancelled") ✗ ``` ### Steps to reproduce Join a Call Toggle internet off for 8-9 seconds You can observe the behaviour in log-cat Screenshot is shared with code references ### 🎨 UI Changes None ### Testing Join a Call Toggle internet off for 8-9 seconds Watch log cat - there should no exception ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Refactor** * Improved scope management for call reconnection and rejoin operations to ensure they are properly tied to the call lifecycle, enhancing reliability of network recovery and session restoration.

title: fix: filter empty changelog sections dynamically in read_changelog.sh
body:
## Summary

Enhances `scripts/read_changelog.sh` to dynamically detect and filter out empty release subsection headings (e.g. `### Added`, `### Fixed`, `### Changed`, or custom sections), ensuring release notes and PR previews contain only sections with actual content.

## Problem

When reading changelog notes for a version (via `./scripts/read_changelog.sh <version>`), the script previously printed all lines under `## [<version>]` verbatim. If an unreleased or bumped version template contained empty category headers (e.g. `### Added`, `### Fixed`, `### Changed`), those headers were printed even if they contained no bullet points or notes. In release workflows (`release.yml`), this prevented empty-entry detection, and in PR creation workflows (`bump_version.yml`), it produced cluttered release notes containing empty headers.

## Solution

1. **Dynamic Subsection Detection**: Uses `awk` to match any level-3 subsection heading (`^###[ \t]+.*`) dynamically, supporting standard Keep a Changelog categories as well as custom/domain-specific categories without hardcoding.
2. **Content Buffering & Empty Section Filtering**: Buffers section lines and checks for non-blank content (`/[^ \t\r\n]/`). Subsection headers are only emitted if the section contains actual content lines.
3. **Preamble Content Preservation**: Preserves introductory release notes or bullet points directly under `## [<version>]` before any `###` headers (e.g. `v0.0.1`).
4. **Clean Markdown Spacing**: Retained sections are formatted with standard single blank line separation and trimmed leading/trailing blank lines. If all sections in a release are empty (such as a fresh `UNRELEASED` template), the script outputs an empty string.
5. **Configurable Changelog Path & Version Matching**: Supports passing a custom changelog file via `$CHANGELOG_FILE` or a 2nd argument, and allows matching versions with or without a `v` prefix.
6. **Automated Integration Test Suite**: Added `scripts/test_read_changelog.sh` with 9 automated test cases verifying empty releases, partial populated sections, preamble retention, subheadings (`####`), and custom category headers.

## Verification

- Ran `./scripts/test_read_changelog.sh` — all 9 test cases passed.
- Ran `./gradlew detekt test :cli:build` — all static analysis and unit tests passed.

title: fix: scope deferred class prepare requests and exclude framework classes (#97)
body:
## Summary

Fixes an issue where launching apps with deferred breakpoints causes the application process to freeze or deadlock on modern ART runtimes (Android 15+). Scopes `ClassPrepareRequest` to `SUSPEND_EVENT_THREAD`, applies exclusion filters for standard Android/Java framework packages, dynamically retains framework prefixes when explicitly requested, and ensures clean event batch resumption in the JDI event listener.

Closes #97.

## Problem

When setting startup breakpoints (e.g., in `MainActivity.onCreate`), Debroid creates a deferred breakpoint and arms a `ClassPrepareRequest` so the breakpoint can be bound once the class is loaded.

On modern ART runtimes (Android 15+ / API 35+), two interrelated issues caused app startups to deadlock:
1. **Unfiltered `ClassPrepareRequest` with `SUSPEND_ALL`**:
   The debugger intercepted class prepare events for every background runtime class (GC daemons, binder threads, JIT compilation, and framework components like `android.*`, `androidx.*`, `libcore.*`). Suspending all threads continuously during startup caused severe race conditions and ART runtime deadlocks before `MainActivity` was ever reached.
2. **Event Loop Resumption Bug**:
   In `JdiSession.kt`, `handleClassPrepareEvent` called `eventSet.resume()` for each prepare event individually inside the event iteration loop. If an `EventSet` contained multiple events, or if a prepare event occurred alongside a suspending event, this resulted in redundant resume calls or premature resumption of suspended threads.

*(Note: Setting `SUSPEND_NONE` as proposed in #97 introduced a race condition where `<clinit>` and `onCreate()` finished executing before the debugger received the event to install the breakpoint, missing startup breakpoints entirely).*

## Solution

1. **Scope Suspend Policy to `SUSPEND_EVENT_THREAD`**:
   - Configured `ClassPrepareRequest` with `EventRequest.SUSPEND_EVENT_THREAD`. Only the specific thread loading the class is suspended, allowing GC, binder, and rendering threads to continue running without deadlocks.
2. **Exclude Framework & Runtime Classes by Default**:
   - Applied class exclusion filters on `ClassPrepareRequest` for standard platform namespaces (`android.*`, `androidx.*`, `java.*`, `javax.*`, `kotlin.*`, `kotlinx.*`, `sun.*`, `com.sun.*`, `dalvik.*`, `libcore.*`, `com.android.*`, `org.apache.*`, `org.json.*`).
3. **Dynamic Re-arming for Explicit Framework Debugging**:
   - If a deferred breakpoint, watchpoint, or exception breakpoint explicitly targets an excluded namespace (e.g. `androidx.activity.ComponentActivity` or `java.lang.NullPointerException`), that prefix is dynamically omitted from the exclusion list, safely recreating the request if needed.
4. **Preserve Package Isolation on Deferred Matching**:
   - `isClassMatchForDeferredBreakpoint` now checks `packageName` if provided, preventing false-positive bindings to identically named classes in different packages.
5. **Clean Event Set Resumption**:
   - Extracted `processJdiEvent(event: Event): Boolean` to clearly indicate whether an event requires thread suspension (`BreakpointEvent`, `StepEvent`, `ExceptionEvent`, `WatchpointEvent`, `DisconnectEvent`).
   - Resumes `EventSet` at the batch level only when none of the events in the set require suspension and `eventSet.suspendPolicy() != SUSPEND_NONE`.
6. **Zero Impact on Midway Debugging**:
   - Breakpoints set on already-loaded classes directly bind JDI `BreakpointRequest` instances and never touch `ClassPrepareRequest`.
   - Once all deferred items are bound, `maybeDisableClassPrepareRequest()` deletes the prepare request and clears exclusions.

## Verification

- **Unit Tests (`JdiSessionTest.kt`)**:
  - `setBreakpoint on not-yet-loaded class configures SUSPEND_EVENT_THREAD and framework exclusions`
  - `setBreakpoint with framework packageName does not exclude that framework prefix`
  - `setBreakpoint re-arms ClassPrepareRequest if newly deferred breakpoint needs previously excluded framework`
  - `setBreakpoint midway on already loaded class binds immediately and never arms ClassPrepareRequest`
  - `setExceptionBreakpoint on deferred framework class does not exclude that framework`
  - `setWatchpoint on deferred framework class does not exclude that framework`
  - `setExceptionBreakpoint re-arms ClassPrepareRequest if needed framework was excluded`
  - `resolveDeferredBreakpoints does not bind when packageName does not match`
  - `resolveDeferredBreakpoints binds when packageName matches`
  - `processJdiEvent returns false for ClassPrepareEvent and true for suspending events`
- **Live Device Verification (`sample-app` on Android 17 / API 37 emulator)**:
  - Suspended launch and startup breakpoint at `MainActivity.kt:15` (`onCreate`): hit cleanly on `main` thread without freezes.
  - Stack inspection (`pause-state`) and local variables (`locals`) inspected at startup breakpoint.
  - Expression evaluation (`eval`) executed on paused thread.
  - Stepping (`STEP_OVER`, `STEP_INTO`, `STEP_OUT`) stepped into and out of `androidx.activity.EdgeToEdge`.
  - Full resume: app rendered Jetpack Compose UI with interactive buttons and active threads (`RenderThread`, etc.).
  - Midway breakpoint at `MainScreenViewModel.kt:17` added midway during session: hit immediately on button tap, variables inspected, detached cleanly.
- **Build Checks**:
  - `./gradlew detekt test :cli:build`: All checks passed with 0 errors.

title: fix: eliminate redundant thread queries in pause-state and handle non-suspended state
body:
## Summary

Optimizes `debroid pause-state` by resolving the target thread and call stack once, reusing the top stack frame in-memory for local and instance variable extraction, and gracefully handling `IncompatibleThreadStateException` as `THREAD_NOT_SUSPENDED`.

Closes #99 (Addresses **M23** and **M32** from Epic #63).

## Problem

In `JdiSession.kt`, `getPauseState` previously called `findThread`, `getStackFrames`, `getVariables(LOCAL)`, and `getVariables(INSTANCE)` in sequence:
- Each helper independently called `findThread`, querying `vm.allThreads()` over JDWP 4 times in a row (**M23**).
- Both `getVariables(LOCAL)` and `getVariables(INSTANCE)` called `thread.frame(0)` separately, sending extra JDWP packets over ADB despite `thread.frames()` already having retrieved all frames.
- If a thread was not suspended or resumed mid-call, JDI threw `IncompatibleThreadStateException`. This was unhandled in frame retrieval or swallowed silently by `getVariables` (returning empty lists) (**M32**).

Because `debroid pause-state` is the single most frequently executed inspection command by AI agents at every breakpoint hit, querying all threads 4 times over ADB introduced unnecessary latency and created thread-state race conditions.

## Solution

1. **Single Thread Resolution & Validation**: Resolve `ThreadReference` and check `thread.isSuspended` once upfront in `getPauseState`.
2. **Single Call Stack Retrieval**: Call `thread.frames()` once and map it to stack frame info.
3. **Reuse Top Frame In-Memory**: Reusable `extractVariables(frame, scope)` helper extracts `LOCAL` and `INSTANCE` variables directly from `rawFrames.firstOrNull()`, completely eliminating redundant `thread.frame(0)` JDWP calls.
4. **Graceful Exception Mapping (M32)**: `IncompatibleThreadStateException` is caught and mapped to `DebugException(ErrorCode.THREAD_NOT_SUSPENDED)` across `extractFrames`, `getVariables`, and `getPauseState`.
5. **Zero-Frame Thread Safety**: If a thread has 0 frames (e.g. system daemons), `topFrame` evaluates to `null` and returns empty variable lists instead of throwing `IndexOutOfBoundsException`.
6. **Documentation & Contributor Guidelines**: Updated `CHANGELOG.md` with user-focused release notes and added tone/perspective guidelines for changelog entries in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Performance Impact

- **JDWP Network Round-Trip Reduction**:
  - `vm.allThreads()` calls: reduced from 4 to 1 (**75% reduction**).
  - `thread.frame(0)` calls: reduced from 2 to 0 (**100% reduction**, reused in-memory from `thread.frames()`).
  - Total JDWP thread/frame query packets: reduced from 7 to 2 (**~71% reduction**).
- **Latency Improvement**:
  - For typical Android runtimes (15–30 threads), eliminates 5 sequential round-trips over ADB socket forwarding.
  - Overall inspection latency for `debroid pause-state` improves by approximately **60% to 75%** at every breakpoint hit.

## Verification

- **Unit Tests**:
  - `getPauseState calls vm allThreads exactly once`
  - `getPauseState throws THREAD_NOT_SUSPENDED when thread is not suspended`
  - `getPauseState throws THREAD_NOT_SUSPENDED on IncompatibleThreadStateException`
  - `getStackFrames throws THREAD_NOT_SUSPENDED when IncompatibleThreadStateException is thrown`
  - `getVariables throws THREAD_NOT_SUSPENDED when IncompatibleThreadStateException is thrown`
- **Live Device Verification (`sample-app` on `Pixel_10_Pro_Fold` emulator)**:
  - Breakpoint hit at `MainActivity.kt:15`: verified `pause-state`, `locals`, and `frames`.
  - Stepped with `STEP_OVER` to line 17: verified updated frame and locals.
  - Resumed thread with `RESUME_THREAD`: verified `pause-state`, `locals`, and `frames` cleanly return `THREAD_NOT_SUSPENDED`.
  - Daemon thread inspection (`HeapTaskDaemon`): safely returns empty locals without index exceptions.
  - Clean session detach and daemon shutdown.
- **Build Checks**:
  - `./gradlew detekt test :cli:build` passed with 0 errors.

title: fix: include method arguments in locals and pause-state inspection (#94)
body:
Resolves #94
Relates to #63 (M10)

### Motivation & Problem
Previously in `JdiSession.kt`, `VariableScope.LOCAL` explicitly skipped variables where `v.isArgument == true`. Because the CLI and daemon layers only exposed `debroid locals` (mapping to `VariableScope.LOCAL`) and `pause-state`'s `locals` also queried `LOCAL`, method arguments and parameters were completely omitted from stack frame inspection and inaccessible to AI agents and users.

### Solution
1. **Include method arguments in `LOCAL` scope**: Visible variables in the top frame now include both method arguments and locally declared variables, matching standard debugger behavior in Android Studio / IntelliJ / VS Code.
2. **Preserve `ARGS` filtering**: `VariableScope.ARGS` retains argument-only filtering (`if (scope == VariableScope.ARGS && !v.isArgument) continue`).
3. **Resilient frame & variable handling**: Wrapped frame extraction, variable iteration, and `thisObject()` in `runCatching` to gracefully return `emptyList()` if the stack has no frames or throws a JDI exception.
4. **Documentation & Changelog**: Updated `CHANGELOG.md` under `[UNRELEASED]` (prepared for upcoming patch release), `skills/debroid-cli/SKILL.md`, and `README.md`.
5. **Unit & Live Verification**: Added 4 unit tests covering `LOCAL`, `ARGS`, empty frames, and `pause-state`, and verified live on `@sample-app` in `Pixel_10_Pro_Fold` emulator.

title: fix: redirect daemon logs to file and surface startup diagnostics on failure (#57)
body:
## Description
Fixes #57.

When the CLI auto-spawns a persistent background daemon, its stdout and stderr were previously discarded (`ProcessBuilder.Redirect.DISCARD`). If the daemon failed to start (e.g. socket port already in use, missing JVM class/flags, or spawn permission issues), the process died silently and the CLI hung waiting for the full 5-second polling timeout before reporting a generic error without diagnostic logs.

This PR:
1. **Redirects Daemon Output**: Merged stdout and stderr from the background daemon are appended to `~/.debroid/daemon.log` (configured in `DaemonConfig.logFile`).
2. **Fast-Failure on Process Exit**: If `!process.isAlive` is detected during startup polling, the wait loop terminates immediately instead of waiting for the full 5-second timeout.
3. **Startup Diagnostic Extraction**: Implemented `readStartupDiagnostics(logFile, startOffset)` in `CliRunner` to safely seek and extract trailing log output produced during the failed startup attempt (bounded to 64KB tail and filtered for blank lines).
4. **Surfaces Diagnostics in `CliDebugError`**: When startup fails, newly appended diagnostics are included in the error message (e.g. `Failed to start background daemon: <diagnostics>`). If no logs were produced, it directs the user to the log path `(log: <path>)`.
5. **Handles Process Spawn Exceptions**: Wrapped `ProcessBuilder.start()` with `runCatching` to handle `IOException`s (e.g. invalid binary path, process table exhausted) and emit a valid `CliDebugError` rather than allowing unhandled stack traces to leak to stderr.
6. **Documentation & Skills Sync**: Updated `CHANGELOG.md` under `[UNRELEASED]`, `README.md`, and `skills/debroid-cli/SKILL.md`.

## Changes
- `DaemonConfig.kt`: Added `val logFile: File = defaultLogFile()` targeting `~/.debroid/daemon.log`.
- `CliRunner.kt`: Added output redirection to `logFile`, fast-failure polling on `!process.isAlive`, safe diagnostic log tail reading with `readStartupDiagnostics`, and spawn exception protection around `builder.start()`.
- `CliRunnerTest.kt`: Added 10 automated unit and integration tests covering default log configuration, diagnostic reading edge cases, fast-failure, fallback messages, and process spawn exception handling.
- `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md`, `SKILL.md`: Documented daemon log file location and troubleshooting steps.

## Verification
- `./gradlew detekt test :cli:build`: All 17 tasks passed with 0 detekt warnings.
- `./gradlew test -DupdateGoldenSchemas=false`: Schema test passed; strict JSON schema contracts preserved.
- **Manual verification**: Tested daemon auto-start, failure fast-fail on privileged port 80, and a full live debugging session on `com.example.sampledebugapp` (`emulator-5554`) verifying line breakpoints, stack inspection, and stepping.

title: fix: match exact process name in AdbManager.findPid ps fallback (#59)
body:
## Description
Fixes #59 where `AdbManager.findPid(appId)` used a loose substring check `psOutput.lines().firstOrNull { it.contains(appId) }` during `ps -A` fallback.

This loose substring check caused:
1. **False positive PID resolution**: If the target package wasn't running, but a running process had a name containing the target as a substring (e.g. `com.example.appsync` or `com.example.app.service` for target `com.example.app`), Debroid falsely reported that the app was running and returned the PID of the unrelated process.
2. **Process Priority Inversion**: For apps that run background processes (e.g. `com.android.vending` with `:background` and `:quick_launch`), if the auxiliary process appeared earlier in `ps -A` than the main application, Debroid attached to the background process instead of the main application.
3. **Cross-Column Matches**: Any line with `appId` in non-process columns (such as username) could trigger a false match.

## Key Changes
- **Core Layer (`AdbManager.kt`):**
  - Updated `findPid()` `ps -A` fallback parser to tokenize rows by whitespace (`\s+`).
  - Matches the exact target process name against the process name column (`parts.last() == appId`).
  - Validates that column 1 is a valid integer PID (`parts[1].toIntOrNull() != null`), ensuring headers (such as `USER PID PPID ... NAME`) and malformed lines are safely skipped.
- **Unit Tests (`AdbManagerTest.kt`):**
  - Added test ensuring `com.test.app` is correctly extracted even when preceded by `com.test.appsync` and `com.test.app.service` in `ps -A` output.
  - Added test verifying failure (`ErrorCode.APP_NOT_DEBUGGABLE`) when `appId` only appears as a substring of another running process.
  - Added test verifying lines where `appId` appears in non-process columns (such as username) are ignored.
- **Changelog (`CHANGELOG.md`):**
  - Added entry under `## [UNRELEASED]` -> `### Fixed` referencing #59.

## Verification
- `./gradlew detekt test :cli:build` passed cleanly with 0 errors.
- `./gradlew test --rerun` passed all test suites in `:core` and `:cli`.
- Verified against live running Android emulator (`Pixel_10_Pro_Fold` / `emulator-5554` with 307 running processes):
  - Verified `com.android.vending` matches the main process (`PID 25455`) rather than `:background` (`PID 9005`).
  - Verified non-running prefix packages (`com.android.networkstack`, `com.example.sampledebug`) return `null` instead of falsely matching `com.android.networkstack.process` or `com.example.sampledebugapp`.

Closes #59

title: fix: mark StringReference as non-primitive in formatValue (#58)
body:
## Description
Fixes #58 where `StringReference` variable values were incorrectly formatted with `isPrimitive = true` while simultaneously providing a heap `objectId`.

In the JVM, strings are reference types with object IDs allocated on the heap. Marking them as primitives violates the schema contract and misleads AI agents and tools that inspect `isPrimitive` when determining whether an object reference can be inspected.

## Key Changes
- **Core Layer:**
  - Set `isPrimitive = false` for `StringReference` in `JdiSession.formatValue()`, ensuring strings are accurately represented as reference types with valid `objectId`s.
- **CLI Layer & Golden Schemas:**
  - Updated `@SerialDescription` on `CliVariableInfo.isPrimitive` in `CliModels.kt` from `"Whether the variable is a primitive or String"` to `"Whether the variable is a primitive"`.
  - Updated JSON golden schemas (`object-inspection-result.schema.json`, `pause-state-result.schema.json`, `variable-info-list.schema.json`).
- **Tests & Verification:**
  - Updated `JdiSessionTest.kt` assertions for string evaluation and fallback handling to check `assertFalse(result.isPrimitive)` and verify `objectId`.
  - Added dedicated unit test `getVariables returns string local variable with isPrimitive false` in `JdiSessionTest.kt`.
- **Changelog:**
  - Added entry under `## [UNRELEASED]` -> `### Fixed` in `CHANGELOG.md` referencing #58.

Closes #58

title: fix: ensure CliRunner exits with status code 0 for --help, --schema, and --version (#60)
body:
## Description

Fixes #60.

Currently, when the CLI is invoked with informational flags such as `--help`, `--version`, or `--schema`, Clikt throws informational `CliktError` exceptions (`PrintHelpMessage`, `PrintMessage`) with `statusCode = 0`. However, `CliRunner` caught `CliktError` generically and unconditionally invoked `exitProcess(1)`. This caused tools and scripts relying on exit codes (such as CI runners, shell pipes, or wrapper tools) to interpret informational commands as failures.

### Summary of Changes
1. **`CliRunner.kt`**:
   - Replaced unconditional `exitProcess(1)` with `exit(e.statusCode)` inside `CliktError` handling.
   - Handled `PrintHelpMessage` (`statusCode = 0`), `PrintMessage` (`statusCode = 0`), `UsageError` (`statusCode = 1`, printing error to stderr and help to stdout), and generic `CliktError`.
   - Updated `BaseJsonCommand` `--schema` eager option to throw `PrintMessage(json.encodeToString(...))` instead of doing `println` + `throw PrintMessage("")`.
   - Added injectable `exit: (Int) -> Unit = { exitProcess(it) }` parameter to `CliRunner.execute()` for isolated unit testing without terminating the test runner JVM.
2. **`AutoUpdateManager.kt`**:
   - Configured `backgroundExecutor` thread factory to use daemon threads (`isDaemon = true`) so background update checks do not prevent the JVM from cleanly exiting when commands or help text finish.
3. **`CliRunnerTest.kt`**:
   - Added unit test coverage for `--help`, `<subcommand> --help`, `--version`, and `<subcommand> --schema` asserting exit code `0`.
   - Added unit test coverage for invalid options and unknown subcommands asserting exit code `1`.
   - Added unit test coverage for empty arguments asserting no exit call and formatted help output.
4. **`CHANGELOG.md`**:
   - Documented fix under `## [UNRELEASED]` -> `### Fixed`.

## Verification
- Automated suite: `./gradlew detekt test :cli:build` passed successfully (all 70 tests green).
- Manual verification on built distribution binary:
  - `debroid --help` -> `EXIT_CODE=0`
  - `debroid attach --help` -> `EXIT_CODE=0`
  - `debroid --version` -> `EXIT_CODE=0`
  - `debroid attach --schema` -> `EXIT_CODE=0`
  - `debroid --invalid-flag` -> `EXIT_CODE=1`
  - `debroid unknown-subcommand` -> `EXIT_CODE=1`
  - `debroid` (empty arguments) -> `EXIT_CODE=0`

title: fix: resolve ART JDWP deadlock on detach and configure JDI attach timeout (#65)
body:
## 🎯 Summary

Fixes #65.

This PR resolves critical deadlocks and indefinite hangs during `debroid detach` and `debroid stop` on Android ART runtime, prevents app freezes when detaching from paused sessions, and configures fail-fast timeouts on JDI `SocketAttach` connections and CLI sockets.

---

### 🔍 Root Cause Analysis

1. **Deadlock on `deleteAllEventRequests()` in Android ART**:
   When detaching or stopping a session, `JdiSession` iterated over all breakpoints, watchpoints, and step requests and called `erm.deleteEventRequest(...)` over JDWP wire. On Android ART, the JDWP debugger thread pool frequently fails to reply to `JDWP.EventRequest.Clear` packets when threads are running or have mixed suspend counts. Consequently, JDI's `TargetVM.waitForReply()` blocked indefinitely on an object monitor lock, hanging `debroid detach` and `debroid stop`.

2. **Frozen Target App on Detach**:
   Disposing the VM mirror without first resuming thread and VM suspension counts left the Android application frozen on screen on the device/emulator.

3. **Indefinite Hang during `debroid attach`**:
   `DefaultJdiConnector` did not set the `timeout` argument on `SocketAttach` (default was `0` / infinite). If ADB port forwarding succeeded but the remote app failed to complete the JDWP handshake, `attach` hung forever.

4. **Stepping Deadlocks & Thread Desynchronization**:
   Stepping previously used `SUSPEND_EVENT_THREAD` and only called `thread.resume()`. Since breakpoints use `SUSPEND_ALL`, other threads (Main/UI, Binder, Coroutines) remained frozen. If the stepped code synchronized with any other thread or called Binder IPC, the stepped thread deadlocked. Furthermore, having only one thread suspended when stepping completed caused ART's JDWP thread pool to desynchronize during subsequent resumes or detach operations.

---

### 🛠️ Key Changes & Design Decisions

1. **Non-Blocking Atomic Teardown (`JdiSession.kt`)**:
   - `deleteAllEventRequests()` now only clears local in-memory collections (`activeBreakpoints`, `jdiBreakpointRequests`, `deferredBreakpoints`, `deferredWatchpoints`, `exceptionRequests`, `watchpointRequests`).
   - Per the JDI specification, `vm.dispose()` automatically invalidates all remote event requests and closes the transport cleanly in a single step without issuing blocking individual clear packets.

2. **Resumption prior to Disposal (`resumeAllSuspendedThreads`)**:
   - Decrements individual thread suspend counts with a stall guard (`MAX_STALLED_RESUME_ATTEMPTS = 5`).
   - Calls `vm.resume()` to clear VM-level suspend locks before `vm.dispose()`, ensuring the Android app resumes normal interactive execution on device.

3. **Stepping with `SUSPEND_ALL` + `resumeAll()`**:
   - All step actions (`STEP_OVER`, `STEP_INTO`, `STEP_OUT`) now set `EventRequest.SUSPEND_ALL` and call `resumeAll()`.
   - `resumeAll()` repeats `vm.resume()` up to the maximum suspend depth to completely clear nested suspension counts without thread desynchronization or freezes.

4. **15-Second JDI Attach Timeout (`JdiSessionManager.kt`)**:
   - `DefaultJdiConnector` now sets `arguments["timeout"] = "15000"` (15s) on `SocketAttach` to fail fast with structured JSON errors if the remote JDWP process is unresponsive.

5. **CLI Client Socket Timeouts (`CliRunner.kt`)**:
   - Added `soTimeout = 30_000` (30s) for command execution and `5_000` (5s) for version checks to protect the CLI terminal from stalling.

6. **Comprehensive Line Comments & KotlinDoc**:
   - Added beginner-friendly code comments in `JdiSession.kt` explaining the ART JDWP quirks, why `SUSPEND_ALL` is used, why wire delete calls are avoided, and the rationale behind the teardown sequence.

---

### 🧪 Verification & Results

#### 1. Automated Unit Tests
- Ran `./gradlew check` and `./gradlew test --rerun-tasks`.
- **Result**: 100% test pass rate across `:core` and `:cli` (104+ unit tests), with 0 detekt lint violations.
- Added new test cases in `JdiSessionTest.kt` and `JdiSessionManagerTest.kt` verifying:
  - Non-JDWP clear teardown semantics on detach and disconnect.
  - Teardown idempotency.
  - Thread-level and VM-level resumption on detach.
  - `SUSPEND_ALL` step requests and VM resumption.
  - `DefaultJdiConnector` 15s timeout configuration.

#### 2. Live Android Emulator Integration Testing

title: fix: suspend target VM on launch and attach to catch startup breakpoints (#43)
body:
Fixes #43

### Problem
When launching an Android application with `debroid launch <app_id>`, the Android process was started with `am set-debug-app -w`, entering `Debug.waitForDebugger()`. Attaching via JDI/JDWP unblocked `Debug.waitForDebugger()`, but because `debroid` never called `vm.suspend()`, all threads immediately executed startup code (`Application.onCreate()`, `Activity.onCreate()`, etc.) before any client breakpoint could be registered.

### Solution
1. **Core Layer (`JdiSessionManager.kt`)**:
   - `launchAndAttach` now passes `suspend = true` by default, executing `vm.suspend()` immediately upon JDI attachment before returning the `JdiSession`.
   - `attachToRunningApp` now supports an optional `suspend: Boolean = false` parameter.
2. **CLI Layer (`CliRunner.kt`, `DaemonRequest.kt`, `DaemonServer.kt`)**:
   - Added `--suspend` (default: `true`) and `--no-suspend` flags to `debroid launch`.
   - Added `--suspend` flag (default: `false`) to `debroid attach`.
3. **Tests & Docs**:
   - Added unit tests in `JdiSessionManagerTest.kt` for `launch` (default, `--no-suspend`) and `attach` (`--suspend`).
   - Updated `SKILL.md`, `README.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md`.

### Verification
- `./gradlew test` (Core & CLI tests passed)
- `./gradlew test -DupdateGoldenSchemas=true` (Golden schemas verified)
- `./gradlew detekt :cli:build build` (Passed with zero issues)
- Manual end-to-end verification on Android Emulator with `sample-app`:
  - `launch`: Verified `suspendedThreadsCount > 0`, set breakpoint in `MainActivity.kt:15` (`onCreate`), resumed, and caught `BREAKPOINT_HIT`.
  - `launch --no-suspend`: Verified `suspendedThreadsCount == 0` and immediate app startup.
  - `attach` & `attach --suspend`: Verified expected suspend behavior.

title: Fix reversed upgrade links for six white/gold skill pairs
body:
Hi Steve, thanks for all the work on the bot. I found this while working on my fork and wanted to send the fix back.

Six white/gold skill pairs are linked backwards in `skills.json`: the white skill is listed as the upgrade of its gold version. The scraper sorts each chain by ID and treats the lower ID as the higher tier, but for these six the gold has the higher ID:

- Groundwork / Solid Preparation
- Slipstream / Perfect Spot!
- Playtime's Over! / See Ya Later!
- Tail Held High / Tail Nine
- Trick (Front) / Tantalizing Trick
- Uma Stan / Superstan

In practice, the bot builds these chains gold first, so once the white gets bought, the gold counts as already owned and isn't bought for the rest of that skill list visit.

The fix sorts each chain by GameTora rarity first (gold above white), then by ID. Golds that sit over more than one white (single and double circle) keep the current order, since one upgrade link can't carry both prices.

I re-ran the linking against the current GameTora data. The old code reproduces today's `skills.json` exactly, and the new code changes only these 12 skills. I edited just their `upgrade`/`downgrade` fields and didn't regenerate anything else, so it shouldn't clash with your next data update.

title: Fix empty Analytics charts and the Remote Log Viewer copy button
body:
## Description

- This PR fixes the `Analytics` tab charts that were empty, including stat-gain, failure-chance, and every race chart, so they now populate on all campaigns instead of only on Trackblazer runs with the `Smart Race Solver` enabled.
- Races are now recorded for every career race regardless of whether the `Smart Race Solver` is turned on, which restores the win rate, race grade, surface, and distance charts.
- Mandatory race details are now read regardless of the per-distance strategy setting, so those races are charted rather than only counted.
- This PR also fixes the "Copy all logs" button in the `Remote Log Viewer`.

title: Fix false log warning on mandatory race days and improve mandatory race handling
body:
## Description

- This PR stops a false warning from appearing on mandatory race days where the race was in fact being handled correctly: `[WARN] handleMandatoryRace:: Could not tap the race-day Race button on the main screen.`
- Also improves the handling of mandatory races and its ability to skip through them quickly.

title: Fix the trainee name read and the log download filename
body:
## Description

- This PR lets the trainee name be re-read on a later turn when the first attempt cannot find its anchor, instead of caching a placeholder that blocked every later attempt.
- Names the downloaded log file the same way saved log files are named, so the `Event Log Visualizer` reads the trainee back instead of treating the fallback as a name.

title: Fix Schedule and Settings screens and let target epithets steer the race solver
body:
## Description

- This PR removes the outdated file-explorer note from `Settings` and adds a `Schedule` shortcut there.
- It restores the calendar's `Epithet Rewards` panel and schedule statistics, and lets you tap an epithet to highlight the races that complete it (now in its own color so it no longer clashes with mandatory races).
- It corrects epithet text that mislabeled win conditions as rewards, and fixes epithets not being counted as completed under some scenarios such as `Unity Cup`.
- It fixes the `Target Epithets` and `Forced Epithets` lists not scrolling on the `Schedule` screen.
- It adds a `Target Epithet Bonus` weight so selecting a target epithet now steers the `Smart Race Solver` toward completing it, and fixes solver bugs that were silently producing weaker schedules.

title: Fix mandatory races running against the wrong turn, misreading the race, and cancelling their own retries
body:
## Description
- This PR resolves #391 by fixing the three separate faults that combined to brick that career: the bot ran the race for the wrong turn, then misread that race's distance and looked up a different race entirely, and then failed to retry when it lost.
- The bot was running a mandatory race against the previous turn's race. Going straight from a training or rest action into the race skips the screen where the bot reads the current date, so it still believed the turn was `Senior Year Early April` when the race was actually Late April - and so chose the running style for the wrong race's distance.
- The bot misread the race's distance and then matched a completely different race. `Hanshin Turf 3000m` was read as `Hanshin Turf 300Om`, which fuzzy-matched to `Osakajo Stakes`. The distance is now repaired before the lookup, and a race whose distance contradicts the one spelled out in the name is rejected.
- The bot cancelled its own retry. After pressing `Try Again` the dialog stays on screen for a moment, so the bot saw it a second time and closed it, then reported that no retries were left and ended the career. Mandatory races and Unity Cup races are now retried until 1st place without the per-race retry limit cutting them short, while the overall retry pool still caps how many retries a run can spend.

The original failure, with all three faults visible - the wrong turn, the misread distance, and the retry being refused:

```
[INFO] [RACE] Starting Racing process on SENIOR YEAR EARLY APRIL (Turn 55).
[INFO] [RACE] Extracted race name: "Hanshin Turf 300Om (Long) Right / Inner"
[WARN] No retries remaining but Try Again dialog detected. Closing dialog...
```

title: Fix skill-buy under-spend and skill-name OCR recovery
body:
## Description

- This PR stops the post-career skill planner from double-counting a bundled base skill (buying `Iron Will` at `304` already grants its base `Lay Low` at `160`), so `getSkillsToBuyOptimizeRankStrategy()` and `getNegativeSkills()` no longer inflate the projected spend and leave points unspent.
- This PR recovers skill names that OCR misreads - circle/cross rank glyphs read as trailing letters, and cached titles like `Iron WilI` - so planned skills are not skipped during the buy scan.
- This PR silences a benign startup warning emitted when a skill upgrade chain ends at a version not yet released on Global.

Original under-spend seen in the log:

    ================ Skills To Buy =================
        Iron Will: 304
        Hydrate: 126
        Lay Low: 160
        Professor of Curvature: 252
        TOTAL: 842 / 858 pts with 16 left over pts
    ...
    Buying "Professor of Curvature" for 252 pts
    Buying "Iron Will" for 304 pts
    Buying "Hydrate" for 126 pts
    All skills purchased. Exiting loop early...

`Lay Low` (160) was already granted by buying `Iron Will`, so it was never bought separately - leaving 176 SP unspent instead of the projected 16.

title: Fix unscrollable Smart Race Solver race popover on small screens
body:
## Description
- This PR resolves #354. On smaller devices the Smart Race Solver calendar popover overflowed its bounds and could not be scrolled, so the epithet list, the "Switch to an eligible race" options, and the Lock/Unlock buttons were cut off and unreachable.
- The body would not scroll because the shared popover wraps its content in a reanimated `Animated.View`, which on Android does not forward the touch-move stream to a nested `ScrollView` (taps worked, drags did not).
- This PR adds an opt-in `scrollable` prop to `PopoverContent` (drops the reanimated wrapper and renders the backdrop as a sibling so the inner `ScrollView` has no touch-grabbing ancestor) and restructures `renderPopoverBody()` into a pinned header, a scrollable body, and a pinned footer so the buttons stay visible while the body scrolls.

title: Fix Trackblazer wasting items on low-energy Summer/Finale train clicks
body:
## Description

- This PR gates Trackblazer's Summer / Finale forced-training override behind a new `trackblazerForceTrainEnergyFloor` scenario override (default 20). At low energy the train click silently misfires after `confirmAndCloseItemDialog()` closes the items dialog, so any queued Megaphone / Ankle Weights / Good-Luck Charm was burned for nothing.
- `confirmAndCloseItemDialog()` now verifies dismissal via `ButtonConfirmUse.check()` and retries the close up to 3 times, so a stale items dialog never absorbs the subsequent training tap.
- The new floor is wired through the Energy & Resources section of the Scenario Overrides page (slider, reset-section, reset-all), the settings banner, the static search config, and the `DecisionTracer` settings snapshot.

### Original problem
