[INFO]  [TRACKBLAZER] Queuing Speed Ankle Weights for use.
[INFO]  [TRACKBLAZER] Queuing Good-Luck Charm for use.
[INFO]  [TRACKBLAZER] Closing training items dialog.
[WARN]  Training Items dialog detected. Closing it as it is not currently being handled...
[INFO]  Resting to recover energy. (Energy 0%)
```

title: Fix SRS ignoring manual race locks at runtime
body:
## Description
- This PR fixes a bug where the Smart Race Solver ignored user-locked races at runtime. The `newSolverState()` function defaulted `lockedDecisions` to `emptyMap()` and the three runtime callers (`buildCalendarSnapshotJson()`, `peekDecisionForTurn()`, `pickRace()`) never loaded locks from settings, so locked races were silently skipped even though the UI preview showed them correctly.
- Locked races are now also preserved when the schedule regenerates after a race loss.

title: Fix Trackblazer megaphone counter not decrementing on mandatory races
body:
## Description
- This PR fixes a bug where the `megaphoneTurnCounter` in Trackblazer was only decremented after trainings and voluntary races, but never after mandatory races, leaving the counter stuck higher than the buff's true remaining duration.
- The mandatory-race branch in `handleRaceEvents()` now captures the result of `super.handleRaceEvents(true)` and applies the same per-turn decrement that `executeAction()` already applies for trainings and voluntary races, so any subsequent megaphone queue decision is made against an accurate counter.

Before the fix, a Coaching Megaphone (4-turn buff) queued on Turn 73 produced only 3 decrements over 5 turn-advancing actions because the two mandatory races silently skipped the decrement:

```
01:02:44.103 [INFO] [TRACKBLAZER] Megaphone duration reduced. Turns remaining: 3.   <-- Turn 73 WIT training
(Turn 73 Finale Qualifier mandatory race ran here, no decrement logged)
01:03:43.907 [INFO] [TRACKBLAZER] Megaphone duration reduced. Turns remaining: 2.   <-- Turn 74 WIT training
(Turn 74 Finale Semi-Final mandatory race ran here, no decrement logged)
01:04:38.204 [INFO] [TRACKBLAZER] Megaphone duration reduced. Turns remaining: 1.   <-- Turn 75 POWER training
```

title: fix(sync): judge mirror files against the live row; conflict-copy banner — v2.67.0
body:
Refs #434. The reporter's follow-up says the copies are rarer since v2.51.0 but still appear, and the copy holds the **whole** older note. They also asked to be told when one appears.

## Fix — decide each file against the live row

A file Markleaf wrote carries a matching `body_sha256`. A stale but verified file is judged by its own older `updated_at`, so the v2.51.0 rule can't create that copy from a stale **file**. It could be misled by a stale **note**, though:

- `MainActivity` calls `getAllNotes()` once on resume. The pass then reads every file over the provider, which is slow on rclone crypt to pCloud.
- Meanwhile the user keeps typing in the note they came back to. Each save writes the file and confirms it.
- Against the snapshot, a version written during the pass looks like a remote edit:
  - **Conflict** when the snapshot row was itself unconfirmed: the copy holds a version older than what the note now has, which is the reported symptom.
  - **Overwrite** otherwise: a silent revert.
- Both paths write `snapshot.copy(...)` back over the newer row.

Changes:

- **Live read per file.** `MirrorImport.importChangesFrom` takes `currentNote`, and `liveNote` reads the row for each file, in both the frontmatter and sidecar passes. `currentNote` is required on the public `NoteFolderMirror.importChanges`, and all four callers pass `NoteImporter.current`.
- **Note deleted during the pass:** it was in the snapshot and is gone now, so its file is skipped instead of re-created (#148).
- **Note created during the pass:** it is matched to its file instead of being re-inserted with REPLACE.
- **Remaining window:** a small one between that read and the write. The editor's own autosave has the same read-then-write window.

One other path to a whole-older-note copy is unchanged: a note whose file predates the digest, when the first write after updating doesn't finish (limit 1 in the issue). The report alone can't distinguish the two.

## Feature — conflict-copy banner

The maintainer chose a banner over auto-opening the Conflict Center.

- `ConflictCopiesBanner` sits under the app bar (the `topBar` slot) while `observeConflictNotes()` is non-empty. It is styled like the sideload update banner. It started as a list item next to the update banner, but the emulator showed that never works; see Verification.
- Tapping it opens the new route `sync_center/conflicts`, which scrolls the Sync Center to the Conflict Center.
- New `conflict_copies_banner` plural in all 11 languages, with the plural categories each language already uses.

## Release

v2.67.0 / vc184: CHANGELOG (en, ko), 11 fastlane notes (98–294 chars), README and landing versions.

## Verification

- `ImportPassLiveRowTest` (5 tests). Each race case first runs the pass against the snapshot (old behaviour) and asserts it reproduces the copy or the overwrite, then runs it live and asserts nothing is written.
- `SyncCenterConflictLandingTest` (2) and `ConflictCopiesBannerTest` (2). Both deliver their data **after** the first frame, and each fails against the first version of its screen (checked by swapping that file back to the previous commit). The landing test also fails with `CONFLICT_CENTER_ITEM_INDEX = 0`.
- Local `testDebugUnitTest` + `lintRelease` on `eb90e451`: **1252 tests, 0 failures**, lint OK. After `902575ba` (which changes only the banner and landing), the affected test classes were re-run locally (pass); CI runs the full suite.
- `verify-release-notes.ps1`, `verify-landing-versions.ps1`, `verify-locales.ps1`: pass.
- Emulator (`markleaf-phone-api36`, debug build, two conflict rows inserted with `sqlite3` under `run-as`):
  - The first build **did not show the banner**. As a list item that appears after layout, it was scrolled out of view by first-visible-row anchoring.
  - The Sync Center **opened at the top**. Its scroll ran before Room delivered the copies and was clamped to the short list.
  - Both are fixed in `902575ba`. Now: banner "2 conflict copies…"; tap opens the Conflict Center with both copies on screen; deleting one shows "1 conflict copy…"; deleting the other removes the banner.
- No golden contains conflict copies, so no Roborazzi golden should move.

title: fix(settings): shortcut jumps move focus to the section heading (v2.66.1)
body:
## What

The section shortcuts added in v2.66.0 (#520) scrolled the page, but TalkBack focus didn't come along. On the emulator with TalkBack on, a build with the fix commented out scrolled to Privacy while the TalkBack box sat on the top bar's back button. A screen-reader user then had to swipe through the whole page to reach the section they had asked for. This was the first `## v2.66.0` item on #262.

- Each section heading gets a `FocusRequester` and `focusable()`. After `animateScrollTo` finishes, the jump calls `requestFocus()` on the heading. TalkBack follows input focus, so its box lands on the heading, and swiping right continues into that section.
- `SettingsSection` and `SyncSection` take an optional `headingFocus`. Only the eight shortcut targets pass one.
- Side effect: those headings become keyboard tab stops, which is also where a keyboard user wants to land after a jump. Nothing changes visually, so no golden moved.

Release prep for v2.66.1 (vc183) is in the same branch.

## Tests

- `SettingsSectionShortcutsTest` +2: the heading is focused after a jump, and focus follows a second jump back up. Both fail with the `requestFocus()` call commented out; all 6 pass with it.
- Local gate: `testDebugUnitTest` 1245/1245, `lintRelease` green.

## On a device

Emulator (API 36, debug build), TalkBack on. Single tap on the Privacy chip, then double tap: the TalkBack box moved to the "Privacy" heading. The same steps on the baseline build left the box on the back button. TalkBack was turned off afterwards.

Refs #262

title: fix: focus Find's search field on open; keep comparisons in section text (v2.65.1)
body:
## Why

There was no new outside activity, so the maintainer picked user-facing defects from the hardening tracker #262. Two are fixed here. The third candidate (wikilink vs local-link locked/trashed verdict order) was already fixed in `64a8987f`; only its tracker box was left open, and I'll tick it after merge.

## Change

- **Find focuses its field.** `FindBar` exists only while Find is open, so `FindBar` now holds a `FocusRequester` on the search field and requests it in `LaunchedEffect(Unit)`. That covers both the editor and Preview. The editor's own focus request only runs on load, so the two don't compete.
- **Section text keeps comparisons.** `CommonMarkPreviewAdapter.HTML_TAG_REGEX` was `<[^>]+>`, which removed any `<…>` span: "1 < 2 > 0" became "1  0", and `title="a > b"` ended the tag early and left `b">` on screen. It is now `<!--…-->`, or `</?` followed by a letter, up to the first `>` outside quotes. Entities are still decoded after the strip, as before.

## Verification

- `FindBarFocusTest` (2: with and without the Replace row) fails before the change.
- `CollapsibleSectionPreviewTest` +3: comparison and quoted `>` fail before the change; a guard checks that real tags and comments are still removed.
- `core.markdown` plus the find tests pass: 390.
- Emulator (debug build):
  - Opening Find focused the search field with the IME up, and typing at once matched 1/1.
  - In Preview, the `<details>` body read "It holds: 1 < 2 > 0 here."
- Local gate:
  - `testDebugUnitTest`: 1237 tests, 1 failure in `EditorSurvivesRotationTest.thePreviewScrollPositionSurvivesARotation`, the known Windows-only full-suite flake. That class passes 5/5 on its own.
  - `lintRelease`: 0 issues.
  - The three `verify-*` scripts pass for v2.65.1 / 181.

Release: v2.65.1 / versionCode 181.

title: fix(nav): write the dropped tablet selection on the main thread (TabletSelectionTest flake)
body:
## Why

`TabletSelectionTest` failed on CI three times in two days, each time in a different test (#262 `## v2.63.5`):
- `aNoteTrashedWhileOpenClosesThePane` on the v2.63.5 tag run (blocked the release until re-run);
- `aNoteLockedWhileOpenClosesThePaneAndStaysClosedAcrossARotation` on PR #513;
- `aNoteDeletedWhileOpenClosesThePaneAndIsNotCarriedUpright` on this PR's first run, this time as `AppNotIdleException` (Compose never idle for 60 s).

All three wait for the pane to clear after the open note is deleted, locked or trashed. Locally the same scenario never failed: 40 and 60 iterations, the slowest at 0.16 s.

## Cause

`MarkleafNavHost` drops a pane selection whose note is no longer selectable:

```kotlin
viewModel.observeNote(id).first { !isPaneSelectable(it) }
if (selectedNoteId == id) selectedNoteId = null
```

In the app this effect runs on the main thread. Under the Compose test rule, effects run on an unconfined dispatcher and resume on whatever thread Room emitted from. A temporary log showed the write happening on `arch_disk_io_3` in 2 of 4 runs, so composition state was written off the main thread. This is the same trigger as the poison flake recorded under #262 `## v2.51.0`.

## Change

The write goes through `withContext(Dispatchers.Main.immediate)`, as the carry-over effect right below it already did. In the app it is already on main, so nothing changes. In tests it is now always a main-thread write: 64 of 64 logged after the change.

## Verification

- Local: `TabletSelectionTest` 10/10. A temporary probe repeating "select, then lock immediately" passed 60/60 with every write on the main thread.
- CI: with the fix and the probe in place, `build` was green. That covers `testDebugUnitTest` twice (store and sideload variants), each running `TabletSelectionTest` and the 60-iteration probe. The probe is removed in the last commit.

## Not verified

There is no deterministic reproduction of the old failure (it is CI-only and intermittent). The case for the fix rests on the logged off-main write and the clean CI run, not on a test that fails without the change.

title: fix(preview): glide a zoomed pan in real time whatever the animation scale (v2.63.5)
body:
## Why

#500, fourth report from @kise82 on v2.63.4: unzoomed flings "have the desired smoothness"; zoomed (1.75–2.15x) they are "very quick movements that come to an instant halt". Frame logs on the emulator already showed the right speed and curve, so the difference had to be something a phone has and that emulator run didn't.

## Cause

The device's animator duration scale. Compose's list fling (`DefaultFlingBehavior`, foundation 1.7.6) runs under `DefaultScrollMotionDurationScale`, fixed at 1, so the list ignores Developer options / Accessibility "Remove animations" / battery savers. The zoomed glide was launched in the composition's scope and inherited the device's `MotionDurationScale`. animation-core's `doAnimationFrameWithScale` divides play time by it, and at 0 it plays the full duration in the first frame. At 0.5 the glide ran twice as fast; at 0 it jumped to the end in one frame.

## Change

`flingJob = scope.launch(GlideMotionDurationScale) { … }` — a private 1f `MotionDurationScale`, as the list's fling uses.

## Verification

- New `PreviewZoomGlideAnimationScaleTest` composes with `effectContext` = scale 0 and checks the glide is still moving 100 ms after release. **Unfixed: 294 px at release → 1372 px after one 16 ms frame, then still — fails.** Fixed: passes. (A first version passed on the unfixed code because the clock was stopped before the pinch's recomposition reached the handler; `waitForIdle()` before stopping it fixed that, and probes confirmed the glide path ran.)
- Emulator (`markleaf-phone-api36`, debug build with a temporary log, removed): pinch via `sendevent`, flick via `input swipe`. With `animator_duration_scale` 1.0 / 0.5 / 0 the composition scope reported `1.0 / 0.5 / 0.0`, so the setting does reach it, and the glide ran 1,343–1,368 ms in every case. Scales restored to 1.0.
- Gate: `testDebugUnitTest` 1203 tests, 0 failures; `lintRelease` 0 issues; `verify-release-notes.ps1`, `verify-landing-versions.ps1`, `verify-locales.ps1` pass for v2.63.5 / 178.

## Not verified

That this setting is what kise82's phone has; the issue reply asks.

Release: v2.63.5 / versionCode 178.

title: fix(preview): glide a zoomed pan along the line it was thrown (v2.63.4)
body:
## What

A zoomed Preview's glide now decays the throw's speed **once** and moves along the direction it was thrown, the way `android.widget.Scroller.fling` (and a zoomed page in a browser) does. It used to run `splineBasedDecay<Offset>`, which decays x and y independently.

Refs #500 (third report from @kise82). Release: v2.63.4 / versionCode 177.

## Why

The spline's distance grows roughly as v^1.74, so with independent axes the smaller component dies early:

- a mostly-upward flick with a slight sideways lean bends into a straight-up glide;
- a (2461, −7385) px/s diagonal moved 456 px sideways on the emulator, where a single decay along the direction gives ~1065 px.

When one axis reaches its edge, the other now carries the rest of the glide. A straight vertical or straight sideways glide is unchanged.

## What this does *not* claim

The report's main description — "too fast, seemingly disregards the gesture speed, then an abrupt stop" — does **not** reproduce on the emulator:

| swipe (600 px) | expected | measured | glide | duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 80 ms | 7500 px/s | 7690 | 3297 px | 1233 ms |
| 150 ms | 4000 px/s | 4011 | 1065 px | 776 ms |
| 300 ms | 2000 px/s | 1989 | 315 px | 468 ms |
| 600 ms | 1000 px/s | 997 | 95 px | 288 ms |

The 1000 px/s row matches Android's `OverScroller` spline at 420 dpi to the pixel (95.6 px, 273 ms), i.e. the same fling the unzoomed note uses. `gfxinfo` percentiles showed no glide-specific jank once repeated. The issue reply asks the reporter to compare zoomed vs unzoomed on their phone.

## Verification

- **Failing first:** new `aSlantedFlickWhileZoomed_glidesAlongTheLineItWasThrown` (4 px sideways per 64 px up at 2x, total movement must keep the 1:16 slant, 0.05–0.075) fails against the per-axis decay with slant **0.0153**, passes with the fix. All 14 `PreviewZoomGestureTest` + 10 `PreviewZoomTest` pass.
- **Emulator (`markleaf-phone-api36`, 2x, temporary per-frame log removed before commit):** (535, −4017) px/s → 143 px sideways / 1075 px up (ratio 0.133 = 535/4017); (2479, −7437) → 417 px sideways to the right edge, 3234 px up in total; pure vertical 4027 px/s → 1072 px (unchanged).
- Gates: `testDebugUnitTest` + `lintRelease` — 1202 tests, 0 failures; lint passed. (`EditorSurvivesRotationTest.aNoteReadInPreviewStaysInPreviewAfterARotation` failed once in the first full run and passed 5/5 in isolation and in the full re-run — the known local flake on this PC, unrelated to the glide.)
- `verify-release-notes.ps1`, `verify-landing-versions.ps1`, `verify-locales.ps1`: pass.
- Not verified: the feel on a real phone (no device reachable over ADB today).

title: fix(preview): measure a zoomed glide's throw the way the list does (v2.63.3)
body:
## Why

#500, second report from @kise82 (with a screen recording): after v2.63.x a flick on a zoomed-in Preview "still feels like there's no momentum", and sideways strokes "continue too rigid".

## Cause

`previewZoomGesture` fed its `VelocityTracker` by hand — `addPosition` for the down, each move (current position only) and the release. Compose 1.7.6's `addPointerInputChange` (what the list's own scroll uses; checked by disassembling `ui-release.aar`) keeps historical samples, **leaves the release position out** (as the platform does) and resets when the release comes > 40 ms after the last move. With the default `Lsq2` strategy, a stationary sample a few ms after a fast move bends the fit down, so every flick read as braking. The existing tests lifted at the instant of the last move, which hides this.

## Change

All samples (down, long-press-race moves, pan moves, release) go through `addPointerInputChange`. The glide itself (`flingZoomedPan`) is unchanged.

## Verification

- New `aFlickWhileZoomed_carriesAsFarOnScreenAsTheSameFlickAtRest`: same device-like flick (release 8 ms after the last move) unzoomed vs 2x, comparing on-screen travel. **Unfixed handler: 1496 px vs 2525 px (ratio 0.59) — fails.** Fixed: passes within 0.8–1.25.
- New `aSidewaysFlickWhileZoomed_keepsGlidingAfterTheFingerLifts` is a guard only (it also passes on the old code; the comment says so).
- `aPanThatRestsBeforeTheFingerLifts_doesNotGlide` still passes, now via the 40 ms reset.
- Emulator (`markleaf-phone-api36`, debug build with a temporary log of both trackers on the same events — removed before commit), pinch via `sendevent`, flicks via `input swipe`:

  | Flick | Expected | New | Old |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 900 px / 80 ms vertical ×3 | 11,250 px/s | 11,135–11,278 | 5,709–8,533 |
  | 500 px / 80 ms sideways ×4 | 6,250 px/s | 6,204–6,304 | 537–5,532 |
  | 900 px / 150 ms vertical ×2 | 6,000 px/s | 6,031–6,108 | 4,380–5,624 |

- Gate: `testDebugUnitTest` 1201 tests, 0 failures; `lintRelease` 0 issues; `verify-release-notes.ps1`, `verify-landing-versions.ps1`, `verify-locales.ps1` pass for v2.63.3 / 176.

## Not verified

The feel on a real phone (both devices refused wireless ADB). Sideways glides are still bounded by the magnified note's width (0.3 of the screen at 1.3x) — that is the edge, not the measurement.

Release: v2.63.3 / versionCode 176 (CHANGELOG both editions, 11 fastlane changelogs, README and landing versions).

title: fix: tablet keeps its open note; fenced # lines are not titles (v2.63.2)
body:
Two user-facing defects from the hardening tracker #262 (`## v2.63.1` and `## v2.62.0`), released as v2.63.2. Every open issue is currently waiting on its reporter or on a product decision, so nothing there was actionable in code.

## Tablet: the open note stays open

`selectedNoteId` was a plain `remember` inside the two-pane branch of the NOTES destination, so three ordinary things closed the note and left "Select a note to view":

- a rotation (activity rebuilt),
- Settings and back (the destination leaves composition),
- turning the tablet upright — most tablets are ~800 dp wide in portrait, below the 840 dp `Expanded` class, so the branch itself switches to the phone layout. The tracker entry did not name this one; it is the common case, and saving the value alone would not fix it.

Fix: the selection is `rememberSaveable` and sits outside the layout branch (the two collapse flags are saveable too). When the phone layout composes with a selection, it opens that note full-screen through `resolveOpenNoteRoute` (a note locked meanwhile goes to the passcode gate), clearing the selection in the same main-thread step as the navigation so Back lands on the list. Clearing it before the suspension cancelled the effect (it is the effect's key) — the new test caught that.

## Titles: a fenced `# comment` is not a heading

`TitleExtractor` (FIRST_HEADING) now skips lines inside fenced blocks. The fence scan moved from `MarkdownSyntaxHighlighter` into `FencedCodeBlocks` (pure, no Compose) so the editor and the title share one set of rules.

**Pure-move check (AGENTS.md):** sorted, whitespace-normalised line diff between the removed highlighter lines and the new file — the only removed lines not present are `internal fun fencedCodeRanges(...)` and its call `val fences = fencedCodeRanges(text)`, replaced by `fun ranges(...)` and `FencedCodeBlocks.ranges(text)`; the function body compared statement by statement in order: identical.

## Tests

- `TabletSelectionTest` (6) drives the real `MarkleafNavHost` with the window size class as test state: rotation (`StateRestorationTester`, clock running), Settings and back, landscape → portrait opens the editor on the right note, Back stays on the list, nothing selected stays on the list, plus a guard that the empty-pane text shows with no selection.
- `TitleExtractorTest` +5.
- Against the unfixed code, 8 of the new tests fail for the expected reasons (empty pane / no navigation / wrong title).

## On a device

Lenovo and S24 refused wireless ADB, so the emulator with `wm size 1600x2560` + `wm density 320` (landscape 1280 dp two-pane, portrait 800 dp phone layout — the boundary a real tablet crosses): select → recreate (night mode) keeps the note in the pane; rotate upright → full-screen editor on that note; Back → list, stays; back to landscape → empty pane. A shared note starting with a ```` ```bash ```` block holding `# install the tools` is listed under its real heading.

Not verified on hardware: a tablet that stays `Expanded` in portrait (covered by the rotation test).

title: fix(navigation): rotation keeps Preview for a note opened from a row (#499, v2.63.1)
body:
## What

Hotfix v2.63.1 (versionCode 174) for #499. v2.63.0 shipped a rotation fix that did not work for the most common path: a note opened by tapping a row in the list or in search still came back in **Edit** on its first rotation (and forgot its Preview position).

Found by running the v2.63.0 release APK on an emulator after tagging: list → open → Preview → rotate gave Edit in 3 of 3 cold starts and 1 of 1 warm run. An editor that had already been through one rotation kept Preview, which is what made it look fixed.

## Cause

`noteOrigin` in `MarkleafNavHost` was a plain `remember` (left unsaved on purpose in D077, because losing it only costs the container motion). But the origin also decides whether the editor is composed inside `NoteContainerTarget`, and `rememberSaveable` keys what it stores by the composition path. A note opened from a row was saved *wrapped* and rebuilt *unwrapped* after the rotation, so its mode, `<details>` toggles and scroll were looked up under a key they were never written to. An editor rebuilt unwrapped and then saved unwrapped matched itself, hence the second rotation worked.

The v2.63.0 test (`EditorSurvivesRotationTest`) hosts `EditorScreen` alone, so it could not see where the host puts it.

## Fix

- `rememberNoteOrigin()` (`rememberSaveable` + `NoteOriginSaver`: note id and source name) replaces the `remember`, so the rebuilt tree has the same shape.
- The wrapper-or-not branch moves out of the EDITOR destination into `NoteEditorDestination`, so the host and the test call the same code. Checked as a move: a normalised line comparison shows the condition, the key and the start colour lines are verbatim; the only lines that differ are the renamed `editorContent` → `content` lambda, `origin` becoming a parameter, and the `noteOrigin` declaration (the fix itself).
- D084 records the decision and reverses the "not saved on purpose" clause of D077.
- `chore(release): v2.63.1`: version bump, `CHANGELOG.md` / `CHANGELOG.ko.md`, 11 fastlane changelogs, README and landing versions (11 each).

## Verification

- **The regression test fails against the unfixed code.** `NoteOriginRestorationTest` (3) drives a real `NavHost` with the production `rememberNoteOrigin` / `NoteEditorDestination` and rebuilds it with `StateRestorationTester`. With a plain `remember` the two row tests fail (after the rebuild `origin=null` and the key hash differs) and the no-origin test passes, which is the device picture. `NoteOriginSaverTest` (5) pins the saved form.
- **A trap I fell into while writing it:** `StateRestorationTester` does nothing on a paused clock (its dispose-then-restore needs a frame between the steps). My first version used the paused clock the neighbouring transition test uses and *passed against the broken code*, because it never rotated. An instrumented run showed no composition after the "rotation". It now runs on the auto-advancing clock. Recorded in D084.
- **On a device** (emulator, API 36, debug build of this change): list → open → Preview → landscape → portrait kept Preview in 4 of 4 cold starts; the same through Search and through the new-note button; three further rotations in a row; back from a rotated editor; no crash in the log. Preview's scroll comes back at the same part of the note and returns to exactly where it was in portrait.
- `testReleaseUnitTest` / `testBenchmarkUnitTest` 976 each, 0 failures; `lintRelease` 0 errors; `verify-release-notes.ps1` and `verify-landing-versions.ps1` pass for v2.63.1 / 174.
- `testDebugUnitTest` 1183 (1175 + 8 new). **The 8 new tests pass in every run, but a full debug run on my Windows machine also loses one or two existing tests** (`EditorPreviewFindTest`, `EditorSurvivesRotationTest`; each passes alone; the assertions race the preview's first render). That is 3 of 3 runs with this change and 2 of 4 runs of the same tree *without* the two new test files, so it is the existing tests, not this change. I did not touch them; they are in the hardening tracker. If the `build` job hits one of them, a re-run is the right response.

## Not verified

- The archive and grid-tile sources (same branch as list and search).
- The tablet two-pane layout: the open note is held in a `remember` there, so a rotation drops it entirely. Not part of #499.
- Going back to an editor after its origin changed underneath it (an editor, Search, another note, back). Same mechanism, different trigger; recorded in D084 and the tracker.
- The non-English fastlane changelogs (ja, zh-CN, de, fr, es, hr, ru, vi, sk) were written by me and are not native-reviewed.

## After merge

Tag `v2.63.1` on the merge commit, GitHub only; check the Release assets once the tag run is green; post the Announcements discussion (v2.63.0 was released without one because of this defect, so this one covers both).

title: fix(editor): rotation keeps Preview; feat(preview): zoomed pan glides (v2.63.0)
body:
## What

Refs #499, refs #500. Both come from @kise82 and are in one release, v2.63.0 / versionCode 173. The issues are deliberately not auto-closed: whether the glide feels right is a device question I could not answer here.

- **#499 — rotating switched Preview back to Edit.** Rotation recreates the activity and `EditorScreen` held its mode in `remember`, so the load that follows decided it afresh from the settings. `isPreviewMode`, a new `openingModeDecided` flag and the toggled `<details>` ids are now `rememberSaveable`; the load skips the setting-driven mode and scroll once the flag is set. The preview list's own scroll was already saveable. The reverse also holds now: with "Open notes in preview" on, a note switched to Edit stays in Edit. Saved instance state rather than `NoteViewStateEntity`, because that row is only written while "Open notes at: where I left off" is selected (D083).
- **#500 — no momentum on a zoomed pan.** While zoomed, `previewZoomGesture` consumes the one-finger drag, so the list never measured a velocity. The handler now tracks velocity and carries the pan on after release (`flingZoomedPan`: one 2-D spline decay, converted the way a drag is, run inside the list's own scroll). It ends at the edge of the note and a touch stops it.
- **A #423 defect found on the way.** The long-press race read the release of a tap and left the gesture waiting, so the next touch's first event was consumed as a pan: every second tap on a link or checkbox was lost while zoomed. Probed on the unmodified handler (1 click for 2 taps); a lift now ends the gesture.
- `chore(release): v2.63.0`: version bump, `CHANGELOG.md` / `CHANGELOG.ko.md`, 11 fastlane changelogs, README and landing versions (11 each), `HISTORY.md`, `.agent/progress.md`, `.agent/decisions.md` (D083).

## Verification

- `testDebugUnitTest` 1175 and `testReleaseUnitTest` 971 — 0 failures; `verifyRoborazziDebug` (no golden changed), `assembleDebug` (`app-debug.apk`, 21.2 MB) and `lintRelease` (0 issues) pass.
- New tests: `EditorSurvivesRotationTest` (5, via `StateRestorationTester`) and five cases in `PreviewZoomGestureTest`. Each piece was checked by taking it away: the original `EditorScreen` fails 4 of 5; without `isLoaded &&`, or with the toggles in plain `remember`, the section test fails; the original gesture handler fails 4 of the 5 new cases, without the lift fix 2, without the release velocity sample the rest-then-lift case.
- Not code motion: nothing was moved between files, so the pure-motion checks do not apply.
- `pwsh` is not in this container, so `verify-release-notes.ps1` / `verify-landing-versions.ps1` were not run; I reproduced their checks by hand (11 fastlane files ≤ 500 chars, the two CHANGELOGs in sync, versions on all landing pages and READMEs) — CI will run the real ones.

## Not verified

- The feel of the glide on a device (none here; the tests inject velocity through Compose's touch pipeline).
- Whether going back from a followed link now returns to the mode and place it was left in. The saved state is per back-stack entry, so it should, but it is not tested.
- The tablet two-pane layout was not looked at.
- ja, zh-CN, de, fr, es, hr, ru, vi, sk fastlane changelogs were written by me and are not native-reviewed.

## After merge

Tag `v2.63.0` on GitHub only, check the Release assets once the tag run is green, post the Announcements discussion, then thank and close #499 / #500 per AGENTS.md step 6.

title: fix(i18n): untranslated strings, Spanish diacritics, and four resource-correctness bugs
body:
Reported: `sync_title` in `values-fr` was showing the English source ("Multi-device sync (folder mirror)") on French devices. Auditing for that pattern turned up more of it, plus a separate orthography defect in `values-es`.

## Why lint never caught this

`lintRelease` passes on the unmodified code, with `sync_title` sitting there in English. `MissingTranslation` only fires when a `<string>` is **absent**; a present-but-untranslated one is indistinguishable from a legitimately identical value (`Markleaf`, `F-Droid`, `Apache License 2.0`, URLs, `#%1$s`). That is why these reached release.

This PR does not close that gap — a regression guard (`UntranslatedStringTest`, run under `./gradlew test`) is in **#164**, opened after this one merged.

## Untranslated English

| locale | resource | was | now |
|---|---|---|---|
| fr | `sync_title` | `Multi-device sync (folder mirror)` | `Synchronisation multi-appareils (dossier miroir)` |
| fr | `sync_recommended_locations` | English prose + `/Internal storage/` | French + `/Stockage interne/` |
| fr | `sync_explainer` | `OneDrive, a NAS` | `OneDrive, un NAS` |
| fr | `locked_passcode_setting_description` | `l'app`, subjectless `Les masque` | `l'application`, `Cela les masque` |
| de | `onboarding_body_welcome` | `lokal-first` (neither language) | fully German |
| de | `privacy_data_storage_title` | `Lokal-first-Speicherung` | `Zuerst lokal gespeichert` |
| es | `application_id_format` | `Application ID %1$s` | `ID de aplicación %1$s` |
| es | `onboarding_body_welcome` | `local-first` | `con almacenamiento local primero` |
| ja | `application_id_format` | `Application ID %1$s` | `アプリケーション ID %1$s` |
| ko | `application_id_format` | `Application ID %1$s` | `애플리케이션 ID %1$s` |
| ko | `theme_description` | bare English `leaf` in Korean prose | `잎` |

Two of these — the fr `a NAS` fragment and the de/es `local-first` hybrids — are invisible to exact-string comparison, since the surrounding text *is* translated.

`application_id_format` was English in es/de/ja/ko; only fr had translated it. Translated where the adjacent `version_format` was already localised (es/ja/ko). **Left as-is in de**, where `Version` is also the German word so there is no inconsistency to resolve, and the file deliberately keeps other English loanwords.

## Spanish diacritics

`values-es` spelled the same word both ways, which is self-proving without any external dictionary:

`código`/`codigo` ×8 · `sincronización`/`sincronizacion` ×6 · `viñetas`/`vinetas` · `línea`/`linea` · `título`/`titulo` · `días`/`dias` · `aquí`/`aqui` · `rápida`/`rapida` · `aún`/`aun`

Four interrogatives were also missing the opening `¿` (`delete_forever_title`, `move_to_trash_title`, `move_to_trash_message`, `move_to_trash_editor_message`) while two others had it. **59 entries corrected.** Distinct accented word-types went from 27 to 70.

Homographs where the unaccented spelling is correct were deliberately left alone: comparative `como` ×8 (*"Guardar **como** archivo .md"*), possessive `tu` ×6, demonstrative `esta` ×5, conditional `Si` ×1, and `solo` per the 2010 RAE rule.

## `remove_from_locked` mistranslation (ja/ko)

Pulled in from #161 on request; everything else there stays out of this PR.

*Remove from Locked* takes a single note **out** of the Locked space and returns it to the note list (`LockedNotesScreen.kt:343`, `removeLock()`, which also restores the note's sync mirror file). Both ja and ko rendered it as *unlock* — a different action.

In Korean it was worse than a mistranslation: `remove_from_locked` and `locked_unlock_button` were the **byte-identical** string `잠금 해제`, so the per-note menu item and the passcode-entry button showed the same label for unrelated actions.

| | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| ja | `ロックを解除` | `ロックから戻す` |
| ko | `잠금 해제` | `잠금에서 제거` |

Both now pair with `move_to_locked` (`ロックに移動` / `잠금으로 이동`) and match how the app already describes this operation in `locked_passcode_removed_done` (`ノート一覧に戻しました` / `노트 목록으로 되돌렸습니다`). de, fr and es already had it right (`Aus Gesperrt entfernen`, `Retirer de Verrouillées`, `Quitar de Bloqueadas`), which is what established the intended meaning. The two labels are now distinct in all six locales.

## Korean object particle broken by a placeholder (ko)

Also pulled in from #161 on request.

Korean selects the object particle by whether the preceding noun ends in a consonant: `을` after a 받침, `를` otherwise. `move_to_trash_message` hardcoded `를` directly after the note-title placeholder:

| title | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `회의록` (consonant-final) | `"회의록"를 휴지통으로…` ✗ should be `을` | `"회의록" 노트를 휴지통으로…` ✓ |
| `메모` (vowel-final) | `"메모"를 휴지통으로…` ✓ | `"메모" 노트를 휴지통으로…` ✓ |

Android cannot select a particle at format time, so it has to sit on a fixed noun. Putting it on `노트` also makes the string parallel to its own sibling `move_to_trash_editor_message`, which already reads `이 노트를 휴지통으로 옮길까요?`.

Every ko string was scanned for a variable particle (`을/를`, `이/가`, `은/는`, `과/와`, `으로/로`, …) adjacent to a placeholder: **11 placeholders are followed by Hangul and this was the only breaking one.** The other 10 are safe because the particle attaches to a fixed counter noun (`%1$d개를`, `%1$d단어`, `%1$s 후에`) rather than to the substituted value. The scan reports 0 after the change.

## Quotes silently stripped at build time (incl. the English source)

Also pulled in from #161 on request. **This one changes `values/strings.xml`.**

Android treats a bare `"` in a string resource as a whitespace-preservation delimiter and removes it from the compiled string; a literal quote must be written `\"`. Confirmed empirically with `aapt2 36.1.0` rather than from documentation — compiling a probe resource gave:

| source | compiled output |
|---|---|
| `Tap "Sync now" to pull changes.` | `Tap Sync now to pull changes.` ← quotes gone |
| `Tap \"Sync now\" to pull changes.` | `Tap "Sync now" to pull changes.` ✅ |

A scan of all six resource files found exactly 4 affected strings (8 bare quotes):

| file | resource | quoted text |
|---|---|---|
| `values/` | `sync_behavior_summary` | `"Sync now"` |
| `values-es/` | `sync_behavior_summary` | `"Sincronizar ahora"` |
| `values-ko/` | `sync_behavior_summary` | `"지금 동기화"` |
| `values-ko/` | `archive_empty_hint` | `"보관"` |

**The English source carried the bug**, which is how es and ko inherited the structure. fr already escaped correctly (`\"Synchroniser maintenant\"`), de used `„…"` and ja used `「…」`, so those three were never affected.

After the fix the real resource files were re-compiled with aapt2 and all four now emit their quotes. Bare-quote scan: 8 → 0.

Because this touches the default resource, regression surface was checked first: no test references either string, and none of the 42 Roborazzi snapshots covers the Sync Center or Archive empty state (they are all editor/markdown surfaces), so no snapshot re-record is needed. `:app:testDebugUnitTest` passes.

## `archive_empty_hint` named a menu entry that doesn't exist

Last item pulled in from #161. **This one changes Kotlin**, not just resources.

`archive_empty_hint` tells the user to long-press a note and choose a menu entry, but `R.string.archive` served both the Archive *destination* and the per-note archive *action*. English gets away with it because "Archive" is both noun and verb; other locales must pick one, so the hint pointed at a label that isn't on screen:

| locale | hint told the user to choose | menu actually showed |
|---|---|---|
| fr | `Archiver` | `Archives` |
| es | `Archivar` | `Archivo` |
| de | `„Archivieren"` | `Archiv` |
| ko | `"보관"` | `보관함` |

**The translations were already correct** — every locale's hint used the verb. Only the resource structure was wrong, so adding `archive_action` makes all six hints true *without editing a single hint string*; each locale's verb was taken from the wording its own hint already used.

What each call site actually does was checked rather than assumed:

| call site | behaviour | resource |
|---|---|---|
| `ArchiveScreen.kt:71` | screen title | `archive` (noun) |
| `NotesListScreen.kt:251` | `navController.navigate(NavRoutes.ARCHIVE)` — opens the Archive screen | `archive` (noun) |
| `NotesListScreen.kt:579` | `onArchive()` — archives this note | **`archive_action`** (verb) |

Only `:579` changed. `:251` is navigation, so the noun is right there and fr/de/ko keep showing `Archives`/`Archiv`/`보관함` for it — changing both would have introduced a new bug. `unarchive` needed no change: single call site, and every locale already renders it as a verb. `values/strings.xml` carries a comment explaining the split so it doesn't get merged back.

## Deliberately not changed

- **ja/ko `<plurals>` keep only `quantity="other"`.** CLDR defines no plural distinction for either language; all 5 plurals are consistently `other`-only in both files. Adding `one` would trip lint's `UnusedQuantity`. An initial mechanical pass flagged these as "5 missing entries" — they are not.
- **de keeps `Tags`, `Checkbox`, `App`, `Passcode`.** Established German loanwords, already morphologically integrated elsewhere in the file ("Checkboxen", "Noch keine Tags").

## Verification

- All six resource files parse.
- The es diff is provably **59 diacritic-only entries + exactly 2 intended semantic changes**, established by comparing both sides with accents stripped — so no meaning drifted while touching 61 strings.
- `./gradlew :app:lintRelease` → `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, identical to the pre-change baseline captured before any edit.

This PR fixes the four **structural** user-visible bugs from #161 (broken particle, stripped quotes, wrong action label, missing menu label). Three wording-accuracy bugs remain open there (fr `privacy_data_storage_desc`, ko `editor_empty_hint`, de `expanded`/`collapsed`), along with terminology drift. The CI guard moved to #164, which was opened after this PR merged.

## Verification summary

| check | result |
|---|---|
| all six resource files parse | ✅ |
| es diff is 59 diacritic-only + exactly 2 intended semantic changes | ✅ proved by accent-stripped comparison |
| `remove_from_locked` vs `locked_unlock_button` distinct in all 6 locales | ✅ |
| ko variable-particle scan after a placeholder | ✅ 1 → 0 |
| bare-quote scan across all 6 files | ✅ 8 → 0 |
| aapt2 compile of real resources: quotes survive | ✅ |
| every locale's `archive_empty_hint` contains its own `archive_action` | ✅ 6/6 |
| `./gradlew :app:lintRelease` | ✅ matches pre-change baseline |
| `./gradlew test` (all 3 unit-test variants) | ✅ |

title: fix(i18n): restore three claims that translation had changed
body:
The last three verified user-visible bugs from #161. Unlike the four fixed in #160, these are not structural — each string is wired correctly and simply **says something different from the English it was translated from**, which is why they were held back for a wording decision rather than bundled in.

## 1. fr `privacy_data_storage_desc` — a privacy guarantee pointing the wrong way

EN says *"No cloud servers, no data **uploads**."* French rendered it `aucun **téléchargement** de données`, and in French `téléchargement` is normally read as **download**. The guarantee being made is that nothing *leaves* the device; as translated it reads as a claim about nothing *arriving*.

French was the only locale to lose the direction:

| locale | value | direction |
|---|---|---|
| de | `keine Daten-Uploads` | up ✅ |
| es | `sin subidas de datos` | up ✅ |
| ja | `アップロードもありません` | up ✅ |
| ko | `데이터 업로드 없음` | up ✅ |
| **fr** | `aucun téléchargement de données` | **down** ❌ |

→ `aucun envoi de données` — unambiguous about direction, and plainer French than `téléversement`.

## 2. ko `editor_empty_hint` — dropped the local-first claim

EN: *"Markleaf saves **locally** as you write."* → ko: `작성하는 동안 **자동으로** 저장됩니다` (*saves automatically*). That is a weaker and different promise, and local-first is the app's core positioning — stated correctly elsewhere in the same file as `로컬 우선 저장`. Every other locale kept it: `localement`, `lokal`, `localmente`, `端末内へ`.

→ insert `기기에`: `작성하는 동안 기기에 자동으로 저장됩니다`. Minimal — it restores what was lost without discarding the auto-save nuance, which the Japanese translation also carries (`端末内へ自動保存`).

## 3. de `expanded` / `collapsed` — misleading as TalkBack state

These are Compose `stateDescription` values (`EditorFormattingControls.kt:175`, `:239`), so a screen reader announces them as the control's state. `Erweitert` reads as *advanced* and `Reduziert` as *reduced* or *discounted* — neither describes a disclosure state.

The same file already uses the `einklappen`/`ausklappen` stem for the corresponding verbs (`collapse_note_list` = `Notizliste einklappen`, `expand_note_list` = `Notizliste ausklappen`), so the participles were simply off-stem:

| | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| `expanded` | `Erweitert` | `Ausgeklappt` |
| `collapsed` | `Reduziert` | `Eingeklappt` |

## Notes

No interaction with the guard in #164 — none of these keys is allowlisted, and every change moves the value *further* from English, so neither `localeStringsAreNotStillEnglish` nor `allowlistEntriesAreStillNeeded` is affected.

With this merged, all seven verified user-visible bugs in #161 are closed; what remains there is terminology and style drift only.

**Verified:** all six resource files parse; `./gradlew test` and `./gradlew :app:lintRelease` both `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`.

title: fix(scripts): make verify-mirror gate on actual mirror divergence
body:
## 문제

`scripts/verify-mirror.ps1`은 런북에서 "두 원격의 ref 일치를 판정하는 최종 게이트"로
문서화되어 있지만, 종료 코드가 그 판정을 전혀 반영하지 않았다.

1. **잡아야 할 실패를 놓친다.** `exit 2`는 로컬 vs GitLab 결과(`$d`)만 보고 결정됐다.
   GitHub vs GitLab 결과(`$d2`)는 출력만 하고 버려서, GitHub와 GitLab의 `main`이
   갈라져도 로컬이 GitLab과 맞기만 하면 `0`으로 통과했다.
2. **정상 상태에서 항상 운다.** 두 비교 모두 모든 head를 대상으로 했다. 기능 브랜치는
   의도적으로 미러하지 않으므로(런북 "동기화 범위" — `main` + 릴리스 태그만),
   로컬 브랜치가 있는 작업 사본은 언제나 `2`로 실패했다.

2026-07-20 실측: 로컬 vs GitLab 차이 8건이 전부 미러 대상이 아닌 기능 브랜치였고,
`main`과 태그 94개는 양쪽 원격에서 완전히 일치했다.

## 변경

- 두 비교의 범위를 문서화된 미러 표면(`refs/heads/main` + `refs/tags/v*`)으로 좁혔다.
  **양쪽 다 좁히는 것이 핵심이다** — 로컬 비교만 좁혔다면 새 종료 코드가 GitHub의
  열린 PR 브랜치(현재 4개)에서 바로 오탐을 낸다.
- 종료 코드가 미러 판정을 반영하게 했고, 실패 종류를 구분한다:

  | 코드 | 의미 |
  |---|---|
  | 0 | 요청한 검사 모두 통과 |
  | 1 | GitLab ref를 읽지 못함 |
  | 2 | 로컬이 GitLab과 불일치 (미러 자체는 정상) |
  | 3 | **GitHub와 GitLab의 미러 ref가 갈라짐** |
  | 4 | `-IncludeGitHub`를 줬으나 GitHub 접근 불가 — 미러 미판정 |

  둘 이상이면 `3 > 4 > 2` 순으로 심각한 쪽을 반환한다.
- `docs/mirror-runbook.md`의 "동기화 범위"·"백업 검증"에 비교 범위와 종료 코드 표를 추가.

### 리뷰 포인트 — 명시 요청 범위를 넘는 변경 1건

종료 코드 `4`는 기존의 조용한 건너뛰기를 대체한다. 이전에는 `-IncludeGitHub`를 줬는데
GitHub가 flagged/접근 불가면 경고만 찍고 `0`으로 통과했다 — 요청한 검사가 실행되지
않았는데 초록불이 나오는, 1번과 같은 종류의 결함이다. 검사 없이 통과시키지 않도록
별도 코드로 분리했다. GitHub 장애 중 통과가 필요하면 호출부에서 `4`를 예외 처리하면
된다. **기본 동작(스위치 없음)은 그대로 GitHub를 건드리지 않는다.**

## 검증

실제 원격 + 일회용 로컬 원격으로 9개 경로 전부 실측:

| 시나리오 | 기대 | 실측 |
|---|---|---|
| 실제 원격 (`main` + 태그 94개 양쪽 일치) | 0 | 0 |
| 범위 밖 브랜치가 한쪽에만 존재 | 0 | 0 |
| `main` 갈라짐 | 3 | 3 |
| 릴리스 태그 누락 | 3 | 3 |
| GitHub 접근 불가 | 4 | 4 |
| 로컬만 뒤처짐 | 2 | 2 |
| 로컬 뒤처짐 + 미러 갈라짐 | 3 | 3 |
| 로컬 뒤처짐 + GitHub 불가 | 4 | 4 |
| GitLab 접근 불가 | 1 | 1 |

변경 전에는 이 저장소에서 `-IncludeGitHub` 실행이 `2`로 실패하면서 "3 건의 GitHub vs
GitLab 차이"까지 함께 출력했다. 변경 후:

```
미러 범위: refs/heads/main + refs/tags/v*  (범위 내/전체)
  로컬 95/105  |  GitLab 95/96
OK: GitLab이 로컬과 일치합니다 (95 refs).
  GitHub 95/99
OK: GitHub가 GitLab과 일치합니다 (95 refs).
exit=0
```

태그 비교는 annotated 태그의 tag object SHA 기준으로 양쪽을 대조하므로, 같은 이름의
태그가 다른 객체를 가리키는 경우(F-Droid 픽업에 영향)도 `3`으로 잡힌다 — 검증 중
실측 확인했다.

title: fix(landing): stop multilingual layouts from overflowing
body:
Several language versions of the landing page overflowed their containers. Measuring the pages in a browser turned up three shared root causes plus one on the privacy pages — none of them language-specific bugs, all of them layout rules that only held for the copy they were written against. ## What was broken Measured with a real browser across **6 languages × 9 viewport widths**: | Root cause | Worst measurement | |---|---| | `word-break: keep-all` applied to every language | ja: **207px** horizontal page scroll at 375px, **262px** at 320px | | `.no-break { white-space: nowrap }` | hero h1 past its column — es **211px**, de **95px**, en **80px** (all 6 affected) | | Header nav could not wrap | fr brand squeezed **36px** at 900px; fr/de nav links outside the viewport at 320–375px | | Long German compound in privacy headings | `privacy.de.html` h1 over by **77px** at 320px | ### 1. `keep-all` was disabling Japanese line breaking entirely `keep-all` forbids breaks between CJK characters. Korean puts spaces between words, so it still wraps at those spaces — that is the rule's intended use. Japanese and Chinese have no such spaces, so an entire sentence became one unbreakable run. Now scoped to `:lang(ko)`; every other language falls back to normal line-breaking. ### 2. `.no-break` overflowed in **all six** languages, not just a few The `
` already starts that phrase on its own line, and `h1/h2/h3` already carry `text-wrap: balance`, so the `nowrap` contributed nothing but overflow risk. Removed. The German `h3` was the extreme case — it wrapped the *entire* remaining clause (35 chars at up to 2.5rem) where the other languages wrapped only a short fragment. The `` inside the hero `h1` is kept deliberately: `h1 span { color: var(--color-primary) }` gives the second line its accent green (`#2E7D32` against the h1's `#00390A`). Only the class is dropped, so the two-tone title survives. ### 3. Header could not wrap `flex-wrap` on the nav rows and `flex-shrink: 0` on the brand, so long labels (`Fonctionnalités`, `Confidentialité`, `Datenschutz`) wrap instead of crushing the logo or leaving the viewport. ## Verification Re-ran the same measurement harness over **12 pages × 9 widths = 108 combinations**: - Element overflow: **0** across all 108 combinations - Horizontal page scroll: **0** at a true 320px viewport in all six languages - `word-break` computed value: `keep-all` for ko, `normal` for en/ja/de/es/fr - Wrapping quality re-checked at 390px — ja h3 2 lines, ko h1 3 lines (still breaking at word boundaries), de h3 3 lines, es h1 4 lines, every line ending inside its box - Hero accent color re-measured in all 6: h1 `rgb(0,57,10)`, span `rgb(46,125,50)` No CHANGELOG entry: this is website-only with no app impact, matching how previous `docs:`-scoped landing changes were handled. ## Follow-ups (not included) - **#187 — guard this in CI.** Nothing currently verifies that the rendered pages fit their containers, which is why these three bugs survived since the pages were written. Filed with the measurement approach and two implementation gotchas (skip deliberate scrollers, correct for scrollbar width). - `:lang(ja) :is(h1,h2,h3) { word-break: auto-phrase }` would break Japanese headings at phrase boundaries rather than anywhere. Chrome 119+ only, degrades cleanly — left out as it is a readability improvement, not part of this fix.

title: fix(ime): allow consonant input after a standalone hangul medial
body:
In the current version, if a consonant follows a standalone medial (jungseong), `HangulComposer` attempts to combine it as a final consonant (jongseong) and fails.

I fixed the code so that if a consonant follows a standalone medial (jungseong), the compose for that medial is finalized, and the consonant is treated as a initial consonant (choseong).

For example, currently, typing `ㅠㅠㅠㅋ` results in `ㅠㅠㅠ` (the `ㅋ` is omitted). Once the patch is applied, `ㅠㅠㅠㅋ` will be entered correctly.
