title: Fix unreliable Cast device discovery
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of the Cast overhaul (see the [root-cause analysis](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/d862e987-57f1-4c1a-9a27-cc5adae02d44)): makes device discovery actually work. The handoff hang (receiver auth, session brokering, chapter mapping) is Phase 2.

### Discovery was broken by design
- **Wrong selector**: `MediaRouterCastController` subscribed with generic `MediaControlIntent` categories that no Cast route matches — devices only leaked in via the system output-switcher provider, which is why they appeared intermittently. Discovery now uses `CastContext.getMergedSelector()` (the SDK's source of truth), with a fallback selector for the media3 default receiver.
- **Lifecycle inversion**: the `AppScope` singleton controller was driven by `MainActivity`, and recreation order (`new.onStart` → `old.onStop` → `old.onDestroy`) meant every rotation/config change unregistered the freshly-registered MediaRouter callback and hard-reset state to `Unavailable`, hiding the cast button until process restart. The controller (and `MediaControllerConnector`, which had the same inversion) now follows `ProcessLifecycleOwner`, wired through the existing `AppInitializer` startup sequence instead of construction-time side effects, using the injected app-scoped `CoroutineScope`.
- **Scan intensity**: passive `CALLBACK_FLAG_REQUEST_DISCOVERY` while foregrounded; `CALLBACK_FLAG_PERFORM_ACTIVE_SCAN` only while the device picker is open, re-registered inside MediaRouter's 30-second active-scan suppression window.
- **Blocking init**: the deprecated synchronous `CastContext.getSharedInstance` (documented ANR source) is replaced with the async Task API. Only `ModuleUnavailableException` locks cast out for the session; transient failures (Play services mid-update) retry.

### Honest state & device list
- `CastState` now derives only from `CastStateListener` — no more fabricating `Connected` from any non-default route selection.
- The connected device stays in the list (matched by Cast device id across the session-scoped duplicate route) instead of being filtered out; routes dedupe by device id.
- `connect()` re-finds the live route by id, since MediaRouter silently ignores stale `RouteInfo` instances.

### Android 16 local network permission (opt-in, never auto-prompted)
Cast discovery is LAN-bound regardless of where the ABS server lives, but the permission is only requested automatically for private server URLs. The device picker now shows an opt-in row ("Allow local network access") when the permission may be needed. On grant, discovery is fully restarted — callback dropped, receiver app id cycled — so the cast module recreates the mDNS sockets it built while access was denied (a runtime grant doesn't repair sockets whose multicast joins already failed).

### Misc
- `CastPlayer.Builder` gets `applicationContext` so the playback service instance no longer leaks into a process-wide GMS static.

## Testing
- `./gradlew test` passes; `alphaDebug`, `fossDebug`, and desktop compile
- ktlint clean

Most changes are `androidMain` platform code with no host-test coverage, so this will likely need the `skip-coverage` label.

title: Fix changelog.json intermittently missing from release builds
body:
## Problem
On some **cold** builds the APK shipped without `assets/composeResources/…whats_new.impl…/files/changelog.json`, leaving the What's New screen empty. Found while validating F-Droid reproducibility (1 of 4 cold builds missed it).

## Root cause
`ChangelogConventionPlugin` registered `build/generated/composeResources` as a Compose resource directory using a **plain** `layout.buildDirectory.dir(...)` provider — which carries **no task dependency** on `generateChangelog`. It compensated with a `tasks.matching { name.startsWith(...) }.dependsOn(generateChangelog)`, but that name match didn't cover the Android asset-packaging consumer. So the asset merge could race ahead of `generateChangelog` and package an empty resource dir.

## Fix
Derive the custom-directory provider from the task provider itself:
```kotlin
directoryProvider = generateChangelog.map { generatedResources.get() }
```
Now the dependency is carried implicitly to **every** consumer (including Android asset packaging), and the brittle task-name match is removed.

## Validation
- build-logic compiles + tests pass
- `changelog.json` present across **5/5** cold `assembleFossRelease` builds (was intermittent before)

Split out from the FOSS-reproducibility work (#978); independent of it.

title: Fix misleading auth error when account has no library access
body:
## Summary

Fixes #916

Logging into a server where the account has no accessible libraries returned a 200 whose `userDefaultLibraryId` is `null`. Campfire's `LoginResponse` declared the field non-nullable, so deserialization threw and the failure surfaced as *"The provided username and password combination is incorrect"* — a misleading message given the credentials were fine.

## Changes

- `LoginResponse.userDefaultLibraryId` is now nullable so the response parses
- `DefaultAuthRepository` rejects such logins with a typed `AuthException.NoAccessibleLibraries` **before** anything is persisted (the `user` table's `selectedLibraryId` is NOT NULL), on both the password and OIDC paths
- The login screen now shows an accurate message telling the user to ask their server admin for library access
- Auth failures are typed end-to-end via a new sealed `AuthException` in `features/auth/api`: HTTP 401 → `InvalidCredentials`, IO failures → `Network`, everything else (including serialization errors) → `UnexpectedResponse` with its own user-facing message — so future server schema drift can never masquerade as bad credentials
- Removed the unused `CampfireDatabase` constructor dependency from `DefaultAuthRepository` and consolidated the duplicated login/OAuth result handling
- Added `DefaultAuthRepositoryTest` (8 tests) covering the no-libraries case on both auth paths, error translation, and a regression test decoding a real-shaped `/login` payload with `"userDefaultLibraryId": null`

title: Fix app freeze when connecting to Android Auto
body:
## Summary

Fixes #928 — the entire app froze (on both the phone and the car screen) for as long as an Android Auto session was connected, in the alpha builds only.

## Root cause

The Media3 1.11.0 upgrade (#925) introduced a main-thread deadlock in the legacy browser path Android Auto connects through:

1. The framework invokes `MediaLibraryServiceLegacyStub.onGetRoot` on the **main thread**.
2. The 1.11.0 stub calls our `onGetLibraryRoot` — which returned a coroutine-backed future completing on `Dispatchers.IO` — then blocks the main thread on a `ConditionVariable` with no timeout (`MediaLibraryServiceLegacyStub.java:98`).
3. The future's completion callback is registered with an executor that **posts back to the main thread**, which is blocked. The post never runs, the condition variable never opens → permanent deadlock.

Media3 1.10.1 (stable builds) used `future.get()` instead, which is woken directly by the completing thread — that's why only the alpha freezes. Crashlytics confirms: the matching ANR (`Object.wait` via `ConditionVariable.block` at `onGetRoot:98`) first appeared the day #925 merged, with 31 events from the reporter's Galaxy S24 Ultra.

## Fix

Return an **already-completed future** from `onGetLibraryRoot`. When the future is already done, the stub's callback executes inline on the main thread *before* the blocking wait, so no deadlock — on any Media3 version. The library root is a static `MediaItem`, so nothing needed to suspend there anyway.

- `MediaSessionCallback` overrides `onGetLibraryRoot` directly with `Futures.immediateFuture`, keeping the same error-fallback behavior.
- `SuspendingMediaLibrarySessionCallback` no longer offers a suspend adapter for `onGetLibraryRoot`, with a comment explaining why that method must never return an incomplete future.

The other legacy-stub paths (`onLoadChildren`, `onSearch`, …) don't block the main thread, and `onConnect` is synchronous in Media3, so this was the only deadlock site. This looks like an upstream Media3 1.11.0 regression worth filing at androidx/media.

## Testing

- `:infra:audioplayer:impl:compileAndroidMain` builds, ktlint clean.
- Needs verification against a real head unit or the Android Auto Desktop Head Unit before release.

title: Fix socket crash on large or malformed realtime sync payloads
body:
## Summary

Resolves #906 

Fixes Crashlytics issue [`4350da0dd8d479a67b4004bddebb06da`](https://console.firebase.google.com/v1/appid/project/campfire-a9687/crashlytics/app/1:524630200499:android:1b5178780e730a271260c6/issues/4350da0dd8d479a67b4004bddebb06da) (`InvalidSocketIOPacketException`, first seen 0.13.0-beta, still crashing in 1.0.0-rc2) by vendoring patched copies of the two socket libraries under `thirdparty/`, replacing the published artifacts.

## Root cause

Two stacked library bugs, both fatal because they escape unhandled coroutine scopes:

1. **socketio-kotlin (all published versions)** — the packet-parsing regex crashes on real Audiobookshelf payloads. `< 2.7.0` uses `.*`, which rejects the Unicode line terminators (U+2028/U+2029/U+0085) ABS emits verbatim in descriptions; `2.7.0–2.8.0` "fixed" that with `(.|[^.])*`, whose per-character alternation backtracking fails on large (~70KB+) `user_updated`/`item_updated` packets — `StackOverflowError` on the JVM, and a silent match failure on Android's ICU regex engine that the library reports as an invalid packet and throws.
2. **kmp-socketio 1.4.4** — `WebSocket.onWsText` only catches `InvalidEngineIOPacketException`, so the exception from (1) escaped the library's internal `CoroutineScope`s, which have no exception handler: the app crashed, and the scope's implicit job was cancelled, silently killing the socket.

## Fix

- **`:thirdparty:socketio-kotlin`** (2.8.0, MIT) — payload regex patched to `[\s\S]*`: matches any character (including line terminators) with zero backtracking; verified against 5MB packets.
- **`:thirdparty:kmp-socketio`** (v1.4.4, MIT) — `onWsText` catches all decode exceptions into the existing transport error path (mirroring upstream's own `PollingXHR`), and the internal scopes are supervised (`SupervisorJob` + logging `CoroutineExceptionHandler`) so future uncaught exceptions degrade to logged errors instead of crashes. Patches are marked `CAMPFIRE PATCH` and listed in the module README; everything else is byte-identical to upstream for easy re-syncs.

Bad packets now surface through the existing `EVENT_CONNECT_ERROR`/error path that `DefaultSocketManager` already handles (state → `Failed`, retryable).

## Tests

- `SocketIOLineTerminatorTest` — line-terminator payloads plus a 200KB-payload regression test (fails with `StackOverflowError` against the old regex).
- `CampfirePatchesTest` — a supervised scope survives a child failure and keeps accepting work; a malformed frame produces exactly one transport error event instead of an escaping exception. Green on JVM and iosSimulatorArm64.

Verified: `jvmTest` for all three modules, `iosSimulatorArm64Test`, iOS test-binary link, `assembleAlphaRelease`, ktlint, regenerated `MODULARIZATION.md`.

`skip-coverage`: the bulk of the diff is vendored upstream library code; the patched lines themselves are covered by the tests above.

title: Support Gradle Isolated Projects + fix custom ModuleType plugin snapshots
body:
## Summary

Builds on [@findyourexit](https://github.com/findyourexit)'s Isolated Projects / Configuration Cache work ([#71](https://github.com/iurysza/module-graph/pull/71)) and fixes a regression in how plugin ids are snapshotted for `ModuleType` resolution.

### Isolated Projects (from #71)

- Per-project `ProjectInfo` snapshots + `ModuleGraphRegistry` build service
- Settings plugin (`dev.iurysouza.modulegraph.settings`) for multi-project aggregation
- Graph assembly at task execution time (CC-friendly)
- Gradle wrapper bump to 8.11.1, README + sample migration

**Breaking:** multi-project builds that relied on `allprojects` need the settings plugin for a full graph.

### Custom ModuleType fix

`collectProjectInfo()` only probed default module-type plugin ids (`appliedModuleTypePluginIds(emptyList())`), so custom `ModuleType`s keyed on a plugin id never appeared in the snapshot.

Now we snapshot applied plugin ids via the plugin manager (with a safe fallback), so custom types keep resolving after the IP move. Added unit coverage.

- [ ] CI green (Pre Merge Checks + wrapper validation)
- [ ] Spot-check sample with Isolated Projects + Configuration Cache if you have a minute

Keep the current document's paint history until navigation or close. A replacement surface still needs a new composite before releasing the handoff. title: fix(gecko): Guard content presentation across surface recreation
body:

title: fix(browser): improve payment checkout support
body:
## Why

Payment checkouts can open a new window and expect it to stay connected to the opener. Candy previously blocked Gecko's native new-session path and opened the URL itself, which could break popup-based payment flows such as PayPal. System WebView also left the Payment Request API disabled, preventing compatible Google Pay flows from discovering an Android payment app.

## What changed

- Let user-initiated HTTP(S) and `about:blank` Gecko popups use Gecko's prepared child session, preserving opener relationships and navigation state.
- Give an initially blank checkout popup 30 seconds to navigate while keeping the existing 5-second timeout for other pending popups.
- Enable Payment Request on compatible System WebViews, advertise the supported user agent token, and declare the payment intent queries required for Android app discovery.
- Add focused controller, rules, and Android WebView tests; update the browsing engine documentation.

## Verification

- `./gradlew testFullDebugUnitTest testFossDebugUnitTest --max-workers=1`
- Focused `connectedFullDebugAndroidTest` runs for `BrowserControllerGeckoViewBindingInstrumentedTest#userOpenedWebPopupAllowsGeckoNewSession` and `SystemWebViewBrowserEngineInstrumentedTest#paymentRequestIsEnabledWhenSystemWebViewSupportsIt` on a dedicated API 37 emulator.
- `./gradlew lintFullDebug lintFossDebug assembleFullDebug assembleFossDebug assembleSystemwebviewDebug --max-workers=1 --console=plain`
- `git diff --check`

## Remaining limits

- Gecko's native Android Google Pay support remains an upstream GeckoView issue. This change improves popup checkouts on Gecko and enables Payment Request in the System WebView flavor.
- No real merchant checkout or payment was performed. A payment account, merchant integration, and Google Pay publication approval are needed for that end-to-end check.

Refs #194

title: fix(release): Make F-Droid signatures reproducible
body:
## Context

F-Droid builds the FOSS flavor independently and uses `apksigcopier` to transfer the upstream signature. The reference APKs published by PR #34 contained a legacy v1/JAR signature; copying that signature produced an APK Signature Scheme v3 digest mismatch even though the unsigned APK payload was byte-identical.

## Change

Disable v1/JAR signing explicitly and enable the modern APK signature schemes in the isolated reference-signing job. Document the compatibility requirement for future releases.

## Evidence

The same F-Droid-built v0.31 unsigned APK fails `apksigcopier compare` when signed with v1 enabled and passes when signed with these flags. Workflow YAML parsing and actionlint also pass.

Refs #34

title: (fix): Insights events without queryID are not sent
body:
| Q                 | A
| ----------------- | ----------
| Bug fix?          | yes
| New feature?      | no
| BC breaks?        | no
| Related Issue     | Fixes #439
| Need Doc update   | no

## Describe your change

Since 4.0.0, `clickedObjectIDs()` and `convertedObjectIDs()` (the variants **without** a `queryID`) were never mapped to an Insights API event, so `InsightsHttpRepository.send()` bailed out before making any request. This PR fixes the mapping and hardens the surrounding code so the same class of bug can't silently drop events again.

Supersedes #440 (thanks @sroebert for the report and the initial fix), which covered the two missing `when` branches but not the cases below.

### Mapping (`EventsItems.kt`)
- Plain click → `ClickedObjectIDs`, plain conversion → `ConvertedObjectIDs`.
- A click with a `queryID` but **no positions** can't be expressed as an after-search event by the API; it is now sent as a plain click instead of being dropped.

### Reverse mapping (`InsightsEventsMapper.eventsItemToDO`)
- Rewritten as a single `when` covering all 12 Insights event shapes (previously `ClickedObjectIDs`/`ConvertedObjectIDs` were missing and the five parallel `when` blocks had to be kept in sync by hand).
- Returns `null` for unknown shapes instead of throwing `IllegalStateException` from the builder.

### Queue semantics (`InsightsHttpRepository` / `InsightsEventUploader`)
- An event that can't be mapped used to be reported with the same code as a network error (`-1`), so it was kept in the local queue and retried on **every** flush until the 4‑day expiry. It is now reported as `EventResponse.CODE_UNMAPPABLE` and dropped with an explicit log, since retrying a deterministic mapping failure can never succeed. Network errors (`CODE_EXCEPTION`) are still retried.

### Tests (`InsightsTest`)
- Send + mapping tests for click/conversion without `queryID`.
- Table test round‑tripping **all 12** event shapes through `doToEventsItem` → `eventsItemToDO`, asserting the concrete API type and that identifying fields survive.
- Every public tracking method on `HitsAfterSearchTrackable`/`FilterTrackable` produces a sendable event.
- End‑to‑end: `clickedObjectIDs`/`convertedObjectIDs` tracked through `InsightsController` are uploaded; the captured request bodies contain `objectIDs`/`index`/`userToken` and no `queryID`.
- Unmappable events are dropped from the queue; failed requests are kept for retry.
- Verified the new tests fail on `master` (9 failures) and pass with the fix.

## What problem is this fixing?

Customer report (#439): `convertedObjectIDs(eventName, objectIDs)` and `clickedObjectIDs(eventName, objectIDs)` stopped producing any HTTP request after upgrading from 3.3.3 to 4.x; Logcat shows "Failed to map event for Insights." This affects every 4.x release (4.0.0 → 4.1.0) and impacts ranking for customers who track events outside of a search context.

CHANGELOG entry to be added in the release bump PR, as per the repo convention.

title: Reader fixes, page-slider toggle, and dependency updates
body:
## Summary

Bundles the reader fixes and improvements on `feature` since the last merge, plus a dependency refresh.

### Fixes
- **Open PDFs whose path contains an apostrophe (#57).** `openUrl()` built its JS argument as a hand-written single-quoted object literal; `Uri.encode()` leaves `'` unescaped, so a file like `John's report.pdf` broke the JS string and the document hung on the loading spinner. Now built with `JSONObject`. — Closes #57
- **In-PDF search arrow navigation now traverses every match** across all pages (was non-deterministic, covering only a few pages), and the active match is centered in the viewport.

### Features
- **"Page Slider on Scroll" toggle (#54).** When the toolbar is hidden, scrolling used to always reveal the vertical page slider on the right edge, which several users found distracting. Added a toggle in the View Mode sheet that gates this scroll-triggered slider; **off by default**. Toolbar-visible behaviour is unchanged. — Fixes #54

### Chore

TTML 的父行缺少 begin/end 或范围未覆盖词时间时，原解析器会跳过歌词行或丢弃整行逐字时序。现在从有效且有实际时长的词推导缺失边界，并按需扩展父行范围；主歌词及背景歌词均支持，词的绝对播放时间保持不变。

零时长词不参与范围推导。修复《APT.》2:33 的末词 `the` 被标为 `0 → 0` 时，整句及背景歌词被错误排到歌曲开头的问题。无效、逆序或范围外的占位仍保留整句文字并安全退回逐行歌词，翻译和罗马音不参与时间推导。

验证：Android Debug 构建、桌面端编译和 446 项单元测试通过（app 200 / shared 246）。新增 8 项回归测试，覆盖缺失单侧/双侧行时间、范围扩展、背景和声、零时长占位、真实 0 秒起唱，以及时间轴处理后词时间不变。基于最新 upstream/main（efc2435），仅修改解析器及测试两个文件。

body:
## 问题
歌单页"推荐歌曲"板块里点击一首推荐歌曲,播放的却是歌单第一首。

原因:推荐歌曲的点击与歌单内歌曲共用 `onPlaySong`,最终走 `playSongInList(track, 歌单tracks)`。推荐歌曲不在歌单的 `tracks` 里,`indexOfFirst` 返回 -1,又被 `coerceAtLeast(0)` 改成 0,于是播放了下标 0 的歌单第一首。该问题在 #23 之前就存在。

title: fix(player): 蓝牙耳机断开/耳机拔出时自动暂停，避免外放
body:
## 问题
蓝牙耳机放回耳机盒关盖后，音乐没有暂停，而是切到扬声器继续外放。

## 原因
ExoPlayer 默认 `handleAudioBecomingNoisy = false`，不响应系统的 `ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` 广播。项目中 `ExternalInterruptionResumeController` 虽监听了该广播，但只用于取消"外部打断后自动恢复"的等待，并不会暂停播放。

## 修改
`MelodiaPlaybackService` 中交叉淡化用的两台 ExoPlayer 均开启 `setHandleAudioBecomingNoisy(true)`。

## 影响分析
- 交叉淡化期间断开：当前播放器暂停后，`CrossfadePlayer.InternalListener.onPlayWhenReadyChanged` 会接管缓冲中的新歌并保持暂停、停掉淡出方。
- 暂停原因为 `PLAY_WHEN_READY_CHANGE_REASON_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY`，走 `onUserOrSystemPause()`，不会被"外部打断自动恢复"重新拉起。
- `PlayerManager` 通过监听同步 UI / 通知栏状态，无需改动。

title: fix(player): 暂停较久后续播链接过期时换新链接原地续播，不再跳到下一首
body:
## 问题

用户反馈：暂停一段时间后回来点播放，无法继续播放暂停前的歌曲，会直接跳到下一首。

## 根因

- 网易云播放链接带时效签名，暂停较久后链接已过期（或空闲连接被服务端断开）。
- 恢复播放时 ExoPlayer 需以旧链接继续缓冲，请求返回 403 / 连接失败，触发 IO 类 `onPlayerError`。
- `PlayerManager.onPlayerError` 原逻辑不区分错误类型，一律提示“已自动跳过”并切下一首。
- 附带问题：`CacheDataSource` 默认以完整 URL 作缓存 key，每次换新链接都无法命中已缓存的数据。

## 修改

- **`PlayerManager`**：`onPlayerError` 遇到 IO 类错误（2000–2999）时，先重新获取播放链接、从出错位置原地续播当前曲目；同一首仅尝试一次，真正播起来后才重置，仍失败再走原跳过逻辑。
- **`PlayerManager` / `MediaControllerHolder`**：`fetchUrlAndPlay` / `playItem` 新增 `playWhenReady` 参数，恢复时保持原播放/暂停状态，暂停中出错不会擅自起播。
- **`QueueItem`**：网络流 `MediaItem` 使用 `songId/文件名` 作为稳定的 `customCacheKey`，换新链接后仍能命中已缓存数据；本地 Uri 保持默认 key。

## 测试建议

1. 播放一首在线歌曲，暂停 20 分钟以上后点播放，应从原位置继续播放当前歌曲。
2. 日志中应出现“播放链接疑似失效，换新链接原地续播”。
3. 真正不可播放的歌曲仍会在一次恢复尝试失败后自动跳过。

## Summary

In a paginated book, dragging a selection handle near the top of a page could make the page slide sideways. The highlighted words then flashed between different spots, so the selection was hard to finish. The web view tried to scroll the page to follow the finger while the reader blocked that scroll, and the two kept undoing each other.

- Hold the page in place horizontally while text is selected in paginated, horizontal-text books.

title: fix: Match book dark mode to the reading theme
body:
## Summary

Fixes #256

Standard Ebooks turns its black title and logo drawings white when a book says the screen is dark. Liseur's pages took that answer from the phone's dark mode, not from the page the reader picked. With the phone dark and a Light page, the title page came out blank. With the phone light and a Dark page, the drawings stayed black on dark grey. The app's own Light and Dark setting changed nothing.

Book pages now report whether the reading page is light or dark, and sepia counts as light.

## Changes

- The reader sets the page's colour scheme from the reading theme when a book opens and whenever the theme moves between light and dark.
- Pages already on screen repaint in place after a theme change. The book does not reload and the position stays put.
- Switching the phone's dark mode in the middle of a book no longer overrides the reading theme.
- Android 9 and older behave as before, because the system has no attribute to carry this.

The system WebView answers `prefers-color-scheme` from `android:isLightTheme` on the theme of the activity that created it, and `Theme.Liseur` only set that through `values-night`:

```kotlin
// ReaderActivity
LaunchedEffect(readingPage?.isDarkPage) { readingPage?.let(::showPagesAs) }

// PageColorScheme.kt
theme.applyStyle(pageColorSchemeStyle(page), true) // android:isLightTheme, API 29+
window.decorView.forEachWebView { it.dispatchConfigurationChanged(resources.configuration) }
```

## Testing

- [x] `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`
- [x] `./gradlew lintDebug`
- [x] `./gradlew assembleDebug`
- [x] Manually tested on API 36 and API 26 emulators

title: fix: Count other devices' reading on the stats widget
body:
## Summary

Fixes #253

The home-screen stats widget counted only the reading done on the phone it sits on. If you also read on an e-ink tablet or in the liseur-sync web reader, the widget showed a fraction of your week. In one real week the stats screen said 12h21 and the widget on the same phone said about 4h20.

The widget still never contacts the server. When the stats screen gets a complete liseur-sync snapshot and checks it against this phone's sittings, it now saves the reading that happened on other devices. The widget adds that to the phone's own figures when it draws.

## Changes

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S[Stats screen] -->|proven snapshot| R[Residual: server minus this phone's sittings]
  R --> D[(remote_stats_day)]
  R --> W[(remote_stats_window)]
  L[(reading_sessions)] --> P[periodStats]
  D --> P
  W --> P
  P --> G[Widget]
```

- Two new Room tables (database version 61). `remote_stats_day` keeps other devices' minutes for each day. `remote_stats_window` keeps this week's and this month's sittings, the books read elsewhere and the combined streak.
- The saved figures exclude this phone's sittings, so a sitting read here after the snapshot is counted once, whether or not it has been uploaded yet.
- Minutes and bars include other devices on all three widgets (today, week, month). Sittings and books for the week and month use the saved window when it covers the same period. The Today widget keeps this phone's sittings and books, because the server has no per-day sitting count.
- The saved rows apply only to the current liseur-sync account and only when the phone's timezone matches the account's. A save that arrives after a disconnect or re-pair is dropped.
- Each visit to the stats screen saves both this week and this month, whichever one is on screen, so the week and month widgets stay in step. It also saves the last seven days when neither span reaches back that far, for the Today widget's bars. The widgets catch up with other devices on the next visit. Nothing new runs in the background.
- Re-pairing moves the rows to the new account key, and disconnecting removes them.
- The code that works out the other devices' share moved out of the stats screen into `snapshotResidual`, so the screen and the widget use the same arithmetic.

title: fix: Prevent page turning gestures while text selection is active
body:
Prevent page turning gestures while text selection is active.

Fixes #206

## Summary

Dragging a selection handle sideways on a paginated book was contested by
the reader's own page turn drag. The pointer loop in `ReaderScreen` sees
touches before the web view does and consumes the ones it claims, so a
handle drag that read as a sideways swipe was taken away from the web view
and turned a page instead of moving the handle.

The settled selection that drives the action bar deliberately waits for the
web view's reports to quiet down, so it is too slow to arbitrate a gesture
that is already under way. This adds a second piece of state that follows
the raw selection events with no delay, and refuses the page turn claim
while a selection is live.

## Changes

- Track `selectionActive` from `SelectionEvent.CHANGED` and
  `SelectionEvent.CLEARED` directly, ahead of the settling window.
- Add it to `PageTurnDrag`'s `canTurn`, so a sideways drag stays with the
  web view while text is selected.
- Reset it whenever the selection effect restarts. The event flow does not
  replay, so a navigator swap from rotation or a column, scrolling, or font
  change could otherwise leave the flag standing from the page that was
  left and hold drag turns off on the new one.
- Cover the gating in `PageTurnDragTest`.

## Scope

This covers the part of #206 that was Liseur's own. With "Read by
scrolling" enabled the page turn drag never claims anything in the first
place: `canTurn` is already false for a scrolled book, and under the Slide
page turn style the gesture is handed to Readium before `canTurn` is
consulted. Tracing a one-finger handle drag through the pointer loop in
that mode, nothing of ours consumes it. Whatever resistance remains there
sits in `R2WebView`'s native gesture code and Chromium's handle handling,
which an app hosting a web view has no say over.

title: fix: Let the book loading spinner keep your accent colour
body:
## Summary

A reader whose Material You accent is aquamarine saw a golden loading
indicator when opening a book, while the rest of the app stayed aquamarine.
Fixes #221.

Since v0.17.0 ([#214], [ADR 0031]) the reader wears a Material theme built
from the reading page, so `primary` inside it is Liseur's `Leather` brown
rather than the app's accent. `BusyIndicator()` draws in `primary`, so the
spinner went brown.

A spinner is not reading chrome. It shows before there is a book to read, on
a screen with no page on it. ADR 0031 stays as it is for everything that
really is chrome over a page; this adds one bounded exception for the loading
indicator.

## Changes

- `loadingAccentOn()` in `ReadingColorScheme.kt` returns the app's accent
  when it holds 3:1 against the page background, and the reading scheme's
  `primary` when it does not. 3:1 rather than 4.5:1 because an indicator
  carries no glyphs (WCAG 1.4.11).
- `appAccent()` in `Theme.kt` exposes what the app itself would draw in,
  asked for at the page's lightness so a dark page gets the dark scheme's
  tone.
- `usesWallpaperColours()` splits the wallpaper gate out of the private
  `schemeFor()` so it can be tested without a `Context`.
- `ReaderLoadingScreen` takes the colour; `ReaderActivity` computes it once
  and hands it to both call sites.
- `ReaderErrorScreen` is untouched. Its red is semantic.

With wallpaper colour off, below API 31, or under e-ink, the app's accent at
the page's lightness is the reading scheme's `primary`, so the result is
bit-identical to before. That is the whole safety argument, and it is what
`wallpaper colour off changes nothing at all` asserts, walking the real path
through `eInkPalette()` and the API gate.

## Testing

| wallpaper accent on, black page | `#FFAEE3` |

| e-ink | `#000000`, unchanged |

title: fix: never date a setting later than now
body:
## Summary

Two follow-ups on settings sync (#227), from review comments that landed
while that pull request was being merged.

A phone whose date is wrong records the time a setting changed as a time
in the future, and putting the clock right afterwards does not put the
stamp right. The server turns away a whole batch of settings if any one
of them is dated more than a day ahead, and that batch is rebuilt from
stored state on every pass — so a single leftover stamp quietly stops
every *other* setting from syncing, permanently, until the reader
happens to change that exact setting again. Outgoing times are now
capped at the present. Nothing worth keeping is lost: a change that has
not happened yet is a wrong answer however it is compared, and now is
the nearest right one.

The second is smaller. The auto-scroll pace slider lands on whole
notches and the setter snaps to one, but the sync adapter accepted any
number between the two ends. A pace arriving from a device with a finer
slider would be stored rounded while being recorded as agreed at its
original value, and this device would then push its own rounding back
over the pace that was actually chosen. It is refused now, the way the
typography sliders already refuse one.

## Changes

- Cap an outgoing `updated_at` at the current time.
- Refuse an auto-scroll pace that is not on a notch.
- Two tests, each checked against the unfixed code.
- The rule written down in `AGENTS.md` and ADR-0034.

title: fix: move the bar icons with the page a sheet is on
body:
## Summary

Changing the reading theme from the typography sheet repainted the page
and the sheet but left the status bar's clock and icons in the colour
they already were. Picking a black page while the sheet was open drew a
black clock on a black bar, where it simply vanished.

A bottom sheet is a window of its own, and Material points that window's
icons at the sheet's paper exactly once, when the window is built:
`updateParameters` takes a new colour and never says it again. It went
unnoticed until 0.17.0 made the reader's sheets take the page's colours,
because until then a sheet's paper never moved while a book was open.

`SystemBarIcons` now speaks for the window it is actually composed in,
resolved through `DialogWindowProvider`, and `LiseurModalBottomSheet`
says which way round it wants the icons whenever its paper changes —
once, for every sheet in the app.

Fixes #225

## Changes

- `SystemBarIcons` resolves its own window instead of always reaching for
  the activity's.
- `LiseurModalBottomSheet` applies it from inside the sheet, keyed on the
  sheet's paper.
- `isDarkSurface()` shares Material's own threshold, with a test pinning
  the invariant: a sheet's paper is dark exactly when the page is, so
  opening or dismissing a sheet can never flip the bars on its own.
- ADR 0031 and `AGENTS.md` updated to say which window the icons belong
  to.

Plain `Dialog`s never touch the bar appearance, so nothing else needed
the same treatment.

title: fix: turn every page the same way
body:
## Summary

Fixes #201.

Two faults were reported as one, and they share a cause: the same page turn
could happen in two different ways.

The reading menu changed the turn. Under the lift, `PageTurner` photographs
the page so it can fly the old one off, and it cannot take that photograph
while the chrome is drawn over the publication view. It fell through to
`navigate(..., animated = true)`, which is Readium's native slide. So the
same volume key turned the page one way with the menu closed and another
way with it open, and the footer's page number lagged, because Readium
publishes its locator when its scroller stops while the lift publishes it
at the jump.

The app also never read `Settings.Global.ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE` or
`TRANSITION_ANIMATION_SCALE`. Compose's default `MotionDurationScale`
already collapses Compose tweens, which is exactly why the menu-open slide
stood out: it is not a Compose tween. Neither is the `behavior: smooth`
scroll in `scrollScreenful`, nor the endpaper's arrival.

## Changes

- The lift's fallback jumps instead of sliding. A turn it cannot draw still
  has to happen, and where the lift ends up is the next page, now. Borrowing
  another style's motion for it is what made the two turns disagree.
- A system with animations removed resolves the turn style to `NONE`. That
  decision goes in the one place the e-paper overrule already lives, the
  `turnStyle` lambda in `ReaderScreen`, so the tap, the volume key, the drag
  claim, the smooth scroll and the endpaper all read one answer.
- `ui/SystemMotion.kt` holds the new fact, shaped after `ui/EInk.kt`: a pure
  `motionRemoved(animatorScale)`, a `ContentResolver` reader, and
  `rememberMotionRemoved()` that watches the setting and re-reads on resume,
  so toggling it reaches an open book without a restart. The scale read is
  `ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE`, alone, because it is the one Compose's own
  `MotionDurationScale` obeys: ask Compose's question and the page a tap
  turns and the spring that settles a released curl can never disagree.
- `pageTurnStyleOnScreen(chosen, eInk, motionRemoved)` in `ReaderPrefs.kt`
  keeps the two overrules named apart. They collapse to the same value but
  are not the same fact, and the curl still answers to e-paper alone.

The finger-tracked curl is kept. It follows the thumb rather than playing
something at the reader, and its release is a Compose animation the platform
scale already collapses. No new setting: the system's answer wins, which is
the accessibility position.

## Testing

- [x] `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`
- [x] `./gradlew lintDebug`
- [x] `./gradlew assembleDebug`
- [x] Manually tested on a device or emulator, if applicable

## Screenshots or recordings

with the volume key. Left is `main`, right is this branch.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9826e6e7-b478-4b1e-913d-2df1fdacbe50

One frame from partway through the turn: the old build is still sliding, the

![before and after, mid-turn](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3a9c3fd-c35e-45dd-a1ad-872d12df37fe)

Three turns each:

| Menu closed | 18-23 updates over 350-510ms | 18-23 updates over 350-570ms |
| Menu open | 11-20 updates over 350-420ms | 2 updates over ~90ms |

Menu closed is the lift, and it is unchanged, which is the point. Menu open

The animations-removed half is covered by the unit tests rather than by

title: fix: tell a bookmarked page by its locator, not its page number
body:
## Summary

#202 and #194 are the same defect. Writing a bookmark and testing whether the
current page already has one used two different measurements of the page.

`annotation()` stored `locator.locations.position`, Readium's raw integer
position. `isHere()` compared that against `_progress.value?.position`, which
comes from `BookPositions.resolve(locator).position`: a fractional coordinate
interpolated between the synthetic locators and then rounded. Both symptoms
follow from the mismatch.

When the two numbers disagree, the bookmark just written does not match the
page it was written on. The ribbon stays retracted, `bookmarkForCurrentPage()`
returns null, and the next tap writes a second row instead of removing the
first, which is #194's pile of duplicates and the "button does nothing" half
of #202. When they agree too loosely, one integer position spans several
screens, so the ribbon keeps showing on pages the reader has already turned
past, which is the rest of #202. The existing epsilon fallback rescued
neither, since it only ran when one of the two positions was null.

A bookmark now marks the screen it was made on, and the locator it already
stores names that screen. `samePage()` compares the `href`, then lets the
exact viewport anchor decide when both sides carry one, then integer positions
that contradict each other, then within-resource progression. The stored
`position` stops deciding anything and goes back to being the page number the
bookmarks list prints, written from `BookPositions.resolve()` so it matches
what the reader saw in the footer.

Scroll mode gets its own answer. There the anchor and the progression both
move with every line, so the strict test would retract the ribbon at the first
nudge; `sameScreenful()` falls back to comparing resolved positions, which is
roughly a screenful and what the footer counts.

Known cost: a bookmark made at one font size will not light the ribbon after a
typography change, because the page it named has moved. It still lists and
still jumps correctly. Loosening the test to survive that is what made the
ribbon unreliable in the first place.

Refs #202, refs #194.

## Changes

- New `reader/progress/ReadingPlace.kt` holds the pure page-identity rule.
  `Locator.sameReadingPositionAs()`, used by the catch-up guards, now calls it,
  so the guards and the ribbon cannot drift apart.
- `ExactLocatorAnchor.anchorIn()` reads the viewport anchor without serialising
  the locator to JSON, since the ribbon asks on every page turn.
- `bookmarked` combines the annotations with an explicit current-place flow
  rather than triggering off `_progress` while reading a plain `lastLocator`
  var, which was only correct because of assignment order.
- `annotation()` takes `position` and `chapter` from `BookPositions.resolve()`.
- Bookmark rows written before this recompute their page number on book open.
  `AnnotationWire` never sends `position` and the acknowledged fingerprint does
  not cover it, so the repair does not restamp `updated_at` or look like an
  edit to a sync peer.
- Unit tests for the page-identity rule.

## Testing

- [x] `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`
- [x] `./gradlew lintDebug`
- [x] `./gradlew assembleDebug`
- [x] Manually tested on a device or emulator, if applicable

On an emulator with "Remove animations" on, which both reporters had:

- One tap bookmarks, the ribbon fills, a second tap removes it. Five taps in a
  row leave exactly one row or none, never a duplicate.
- Bookmarking twelve successive screens of Moby-Dick produced twelve rows, two
  pairs of which share a footer page number. That is the second-screenful case
  #194 described, and the old integer-position test could not tell those two
  screens apart.
- Removing the bookmark on the second screenful of page 32 removed that one and
  left the first screenful's alone.
- Turning one page retracts the ribbon; turning back restores it.
- Scroll mode adds, removes and retracts correctly.
- Corrupting a stored `position` and reopening the book repaired it, with
  `updated_at` unchanged.

## Screenshots or recordings

The ribbon on the bookmarked page, and one page on with it gone.

![Bookmark ribbon before and after turning a page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2de71005-cf7d-4b0f-bb80-d56cdfc06fa6)

title: fix: keep the library's bar icons on the theme in force
body: ## Summary Switching the app theme in Settings left the status and navigation bar icons the colour they were when the app started. Going from Light to Dark put black icons on a black bar, where they simply were not there any more — and stayed that way until something happened to recreate the activity. `enableEdgeToEdge()` picks the icon colour once, in `onCreate`, from the configuration the app happened to open in. Liseur's theme is an in-app setting rather than a system one, so nothing ever asks again. > [!NOTE] > **Stacked on #214**, which is where `SystemBarIcons` comes from. Please merge > that one first; this branch is based on it, so the diff below is only the > three files this change actually touches. #214 gave the reader an effect that answers this question whenever the answer moves, because its page can disagree with the app theme. It turns out the library needed the same thing for a different reason, so it is now shared: moved from `reader/ReaderScreen.kt` to `ui/theme/SystemBarIcons.kt` and called from both activities. **The effect's body is unchanged**, so the reader keeps behaving exactly as it did. Worth noting the two directions were not symmetric, which is probably why this survived: going Dark to Light came out fine on its own, and only Light to Dark lost the icons. ## Changes - New `ui/theme/SystemBarIcons.kt`, moved verbatim out of `ReaderScreen.kt`, with its KDoc rewritten to cover both callers rather than just the reader's. - `MainActivity` calls it, keyed on `themeMode.isDark()`. - `ReaderActivity` imports it from its new home; no behaviour change. ## Testing - [x] `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` - [x] `./gradlew lintDebug` (0 errors) - [x] `./gradlew assembleDebug` - [x] Manually tested on an emulator (`liseur_phone_api36`, API 36) Reproduced the bug on a build of the parent commit, then confirmed the same steps on this one. Also checked Dark back to Light, and that entering and leaving the reader still hands the bars back to the library. ## Screenshots or recordings The same moment in both: Settings, immediately after tapping **Dark** while the app was Light. Before, the clock and the wifi, signal and battery icons are gone. | Before | After | |---|---| | | | ## Checklist - [x] I have kept this change focused and documented any user-facing behaviour. - [x] I have added or updated tests where needed. - [x] I have checked that dependencies remain FOSS and available from allowed repositories. - [x] I have not included private data, credentials, copyrighted book files, or generated build artifacts.

title: fix: 修复平板横屏专辑详情下载/保存按钮消失
body:
平板横屏进入专辑详情时，“打开网页”控件内部的填充布局会占满操作栏，导致带权重的下载/保存按钮组被挤成零宽。将横屏网页入口约束为原定的 104.dp，恢复按钮组显示和点击，保留现有主题、动画及竖屏布局。

共享 header 的渐变模糊遮罩改用现有主题色混合值，保留原有渐变范围、透明度曲线、布局和模糊效果。

title: fix: 修复任务卡片暂停继续、翻译暂停闪退及下载删除
body:
任务管理中的卡片暂停/继续会被等待入库的文件状态误导；暂停翻译时，取消协程后仍在执行的 JNI 推理可能访问已释放的模型并导致闪退；暂停下载文件后删除又会被整专辑互斥检查误拦截。

- 区分实际下载与等待入库状态，在事务中暂停任务文件，并按顺序恢复后统一调度。
- 保留取消中但尚未完成的推理任务，等待其完全退出后再释放模型，修复实机日志中的 destroyed mutex 崩溃。
- 按目标文件协调删除，先停止目标下载并等待写入退出；删除整任务时排除自身任务状态，保留同路径写入、字幕引用与入库互斥保护。

验证：44 项 Release 单元/交互回归测试通过，使用 `gradlew-local.bat :app:installRelease` 安装到实机，验证卡片暂停/继续、翻译暂停、暂停文件删除及暂停整任务删除。临时下载已清理，原有下载数据保留。文件操作与释放模型在后台执行，保留原有界面样式及反馈。

title: fix: 完善批量字幕翻译的不可用提示与配置说明
body:
批量字幕翻译在没有可处理的本地音频时原本直接置灰，点击没有反馈。现在批量和多选入口保留灰色样式，点击后会提示音频未下载、格式不支持、未选择音频或本地音轨未索引等具体原因；缺少字幕模型和设备不支持时继续直接提示，API 配置仍由任务校验反馈。

翻译配置页的「字幕翻译」标题旁新增无底色信息图标，点击气泡可查看本地 MP3/WAV、已下载并选用的字幕模型和 DeepSeek API Key 等条件，以及手动开始批量翻译的方法。说明明确保存 API Key 不会自动创建任务，原有设置入口摘要保留。目录检查及任务入队中的 IO 放在后台执行。

验证：
- 44 项 Release 单元及 Compose 回归测试通过，覆盖不可用批量／多选入口、正常点击流程、提示分类和按需展开的配置说明。

关联 #325。

title: fix: 修复本地文件删除后启动反复闪退
body:
本地音频在应用外删除后，数据库记录和持久化播放队列仍可能存在，启动时会反复恢复失效来源。恢复队列时在 IO 线程检查文件及 SAF 文档，在播放器 prepare 前持久化清理结果；队列全部失效时清空播放状态。

过滤曲目后按原队列位置恢复当前曲目及进度；当前曲目已删除时选择后续有效曲目并从头开始。保留权限或提供者暂时不可用的 SAF 来源，复用现有文档失效判断，不删除本地库数据库记录。

title: fix: 修复作品元数据图标对齐和详情转场顶栏遮罩跳变
body:
修复在线搜索、本地库、热门收听中作品条目的图标对齐，以及进入、退出专辑详情页时 header 渐变遮罩突然消失和恢复的问题。

## 改动

- 社团、CV、tags 图标按文字的实际测量中心对齐，支持字体缩放；网格换行时保持与首行对齐，保留现有尺寸、颜色和间距。
- 移除详情转场期间主页面内容的动态层级提升，使 header 遮罩随详情页滑动自然被覆盖和露出，保持原有模糊、转场时长和裁剪效果。
- 转场基准按屏幕短边识别作品卡片，兼容横屏四列布局。

## 验证

- `AlbumItemLayoutTest` 的 2 项 Debug 单元测试和 `HeaderBlurLayoutTest` 的 1 项 Debug 单元测试通过。
- `.\gradlew-local.bat :app:installRelease` 执行成功，Release 已安装到实机。
- 实机复核 1.3 倍字体下的列表、网格首行对齐，并录屏检查列表内容位于 header 后方时进入、退出详情页的遮罩连续性。本地库为空，其条目使用同一共用组件。
- 热门收听转场基准完成 5 轮，Gfx P99 中位数为 34 ms，尚未达到 8.3 ms 目标。在线搜索基准在准备阶段切页超时，单独重试后仍未完成，不能据此宣称 120 Hz 性能达标。

title: fix: 删除专辑或音频时同步清理分组、列表和收藏
body:
删除已加入分组的专辑后，分组可能显示“共 0 张专辑 242 首”，列表和“我的收藏”也会保留已删除作品的音频。本次修复让本地及在线专辑、音频在删除时同步移除这些关联。

- 统一删除事务，按数据库编号、媒体路径及播放 URI 清理关联，并覆盖下载删除、文件消失等入口。
- 分组统计和封面只使用有效音频；数据库升级至 33，清理可确认的历史残留，保留独立在线列表项及重新导入的有效内容。
- 保留重扫、合并和在线音频转下载时仍然有效的列表关联；按批次处理大量音频，避免 SQLite 参数数量限制。

验证：29 项 Release 单元回归测试通过，覆盖删除、收藏、分组统计、迁移、回滚、批量数据、重扫及下载合并。已通过 .\gradlew-local.bat :app:installRelease 安装到连接设备，确认冷启动正常。git diff --check 通过。

性能：清理在数据库事务内批量完成，不新增页面收集器或逐帧工作。未运行现有 Macrobenchmark，因为其脚本会清空设备应用数据；未验证 120 Hz 下的 P99 帧时间目标。

title: fix: 开启悬浮歌词时直接申请悬浮窗权限
body:
开启悬浮歌词时，缺少悬浮窗权限会立即跳转系统授权页面。返回后重新检查权限，授权成功才开启；未授权则保持关闭。移除原先隐藏在页面底部的授权按钮，并在回到歌词设置页时刷新权限状态。

验证：
- 基于最新 `release/v1.2.4` 执行 `.\gradlew-local.bat :app:installRelease`，Release 构建、安装及真机启动通过。
- Android 16 真机验证未授权时立即跳转、未授权返回保持关闭、授权后返回自动开启、已有权限直接切换，以及权限撤销后返回刷新状态。
- `git diff --check` 通过，提交仅包含歌词设置页修改。

title: fix: 修复收藏和我的列表中在线字幕重启后丢失
body:
从在线搜索、热门收听等在线专辑详情页直接添加音频到「我的收藏」或「我的列表」后，原先没有保存字幕来源，重启应用后再次播放会丢失字幕。本次将字幕地址、语言和格式随列表项持久化，并在从列表恢复播放项时完整传递。

- 数据库升级到 32，新增无损迁移，保留已有收藏和列表数据。
- 收藏列表读取持久化字幕来源，保留字幕标识；保存时兼容仅有内存字幕来源的在线音频。
- 重新添加已有音频可补齐字幕来源，不重复添加、不改变排序；空来源不会覆盖已有来源。
- 共用字幕来源编解码，保持播放队列与列表的格式一致。

验证：
- Release 单元测试 15 项通过：PlaylistSubtitlePersistenceTest（4）、PlaylistRepositoryOrderTest（3）、AppDatabaseMigrationsTest（8）。覆盖关闭并重开数据库、清空内存缓存后恢复并加载字幕、多语言来源、列表保存、旧记录补齐和排序。
- 已执行 `.\gradlew-local.bat :app:installRelease`，成功安装到连接的 23078RKD5C 手机，冷启动正常，未发现本次启动的崩溃或 SQLite 错误。
- `git diff --check` 通过，构建缓存已清理。

旧版本已丢失字幕来源的条目需从在线详情页重新添加一次以补齐来源。

title: fix(player): show cover layout hint only once
body:
## Summary

title: Fix background playback crash during track transitions
body:
## Summary
- Let Media3 determine whether the playback service stays in the foreground when refreshing its notification.
- Handle Android's foreground-service start rejection in the asynchronous artwork notification callback so it cannot terminate the playback process.

## Cause
ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException from LyricMediaNotificationProvider.requestArtworkLoad. PlaybackService manually called onUpdateNotification(session, false); Media3 1.8.0 uses that flag to leave foreground service state. A later artwork callback could then attempt to re-enter the foreground while the app was in the background.

## Verification
- Release build: :app:assembleRelease succeeded.
- Release APK installed on the connected device with adb install -r; app launch succeeded.
- Background playback through an automatic end-of-track transition has not yet been reproduced on the device.

title: fix: 更新内置 DeepSeek 模型名称为 deepseek-flash
body:
按照 [DeepSeek 官方文档](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/)，将内置模型 ID 从 `deepseek-v4-flash` 更新为 `deepseek-flash`。设置页模型展示、标题翻译、字幕翻译和字幕润色请求共用该常量，因此会同步使用新名称。

验证（2026-09-22）：

- 翻译客户端 Release 单元测试 32 项全部通过。

title: fix: 修复平板忽略系统屏幕旋转锁定
body:
平板普通页面和普通播放页原先使用 `SCREEN_ORIENTATION_SENSOR`，会绕过系统旋转锁，导致锁定竖屏后仍随重力转为横屏，退出 App 又恢复系统锁定方向。改用 `SCREEN_ORIENTATION_USER`，让平板遵守系统的方向锁定和自动旋转设置。

保留手机原有方向策略，以及用户手动进入视频全屏时的横屏行为。更新现有方向策略测试，并补充普通播放器和全屏状态残留时的平板回归用例。本次改动不增加传感器监听、轮询、主线程 IO 或额外 Compose 状态。

验证结果：

- `:app:testReleaseUnitTest --tests com.asmr.player.MainNavigationSupportTest`：25 项测试全部通过。
- Release APK 已完成编译、R8 优化和打包，并成功安装、启动于 `Pixel_Tablet_API_34`（Android 14）模拟器。
- 通过模拟重力传感器进行 30 个设备检查点验证，全部通过：竖屏/横屏锁定、四个重力方向、冷启动、退出再进入、前台开关自动旋转，以及普通播放器的方向切换与退出。
- 验证期间关闭模拟器额外的 `fixed-to-user-rotation` 强制设置，确认应用实际请求 `SCREEN_ORIENTATION_USER`；结束后恢复原系统设置。
- `git diff --check` 通过。OriginOS 5 HD 真机尚未验证。

Fix ShellChromeScrollTest on main: read FAB expansion from its shape
body:
`ShellChromeScrollTest.scrollingDownHidesChromeAndScrollingUpBringsItBack` failed in the emulator job on `main` after #570 ([run 37203508059](https://github.com/sreichholf/dreamDroid/actions/runs/37203508059)). It failed at the first assertion, "FAB label shown", before any scroll.

## Cause
The test looked up the FAB label by text. Material 3's `ExtendedFloatingActionButton` wraps the label row in `clearAndSetSemantics {}` (checked in the material3 1.4.0 bytecode, `ExtendedFloatingActionButton$3$1$1`), so the label never appears in the semantics tree. The lookup could never match:
- The "label shown" checks always failed.
- The "label hidden" check in `resumeBringsBackBottomChromeOnly` always passed, so it proved nothing.

The other six tests in the class, which check bar positions, passed on the emulator.

## Fix
- Read the FAB's expansion from its shape. A collapsed FAB is square (56×56dp); the label makes an expanded one wider than tall.
- Only the test changes.

The other two entries in the report, the `Upgrade115Test` cases, are scenario-gated `assumeTrue` skips that predate this change. Earlier `main` runs were green with them.

title: Fix SleepTimerCountdownTest on main: show the countdown in keyboard mode
body:
Main has been red since #564 (sleep timer). The instrumented job fails on `SleepTimerCountdownTest.countdownShowsSecondsLeftAndExtendIsFocused`: "+15 min." is never focused.

## Cause

`SleepTimerCountdown` requests focus on the extend button so a remote's OK extends the timer. Instrumented tests run in touch mode, where a clickable `TextButton` is not focusable, so `requestFocus()` does nothing. The emulator job does not run on PRs, so the test first ran after the merge ([run 37005575913](https://github.com/sreichholf/dreamDroid/actions/runs/37005575913)).

The two `Upgrade115Test` entries in the same report are assumption skips; they appear in green runs too.

## Change

Test only. The product behavior is right: a TV driven by a remote is not in touch mode. The test now calls `LocalInputModeManager.current.requestInputMode(InputMode.Keyboard)`, checks that the input mode is `Keyboard`, and only then shows the countdown, as a remote would. It does not assert the request's return value: that reports whether the root view took focus, which it cannot while nothing focusable is composed.

## Verification

- `./gradlew -Pci spotlessCheck :app:testGoogleDebugUnitTest :app:compileGoogleDebugAndroidTestKotlin :app:lintGoogleDebug` passes locally.

title: Keep libVLC calls off the main thread (fixes player ANR on zap)
body:
## Problem

Zapping in the player sometimes showed "dreamDroid isn't responding". The dialog came back after every "Wait" while the stream kept playing.

The ANR trace (`Input dispatching timed out … VideoActivity … Waited 5001ms for MotionEvent`) shows the main thread blocked inside the zap-list tap:

```
PhoneZapList click → zapToService → streamCurrent → (state collected inline)
→ onSessionChanged → playZappedService → VideoActivity.handleIntent
→ VLCPlayer.playUri → MediaPlayer.setMedia → libvlc_media_player_set_media
→ input_Close → vlc_join
```

`setMedia` joins the previous stream's threads. One of them was stuck in `vlc_http_file_read` / `vlc_tls_Read`, so the tap waited until the old HTTP read returned. That is quick most of the time and occasionally much longer, which is why the bug looked random.

## Change

Modelled on VLC for Android's `PlayerController` (3.5.x, libVLC 3):

- **`PlayerCommandQueue`**: runs blocking libVLC calls one at a time, in posting order, on a background coroutine. Calls that take 5 s or more are logged. A failing call (including an `Error`) doesn't stop the queue.
- **`VLCPlayer`**: now a Hilt `@Singleton` instead of a static object.
  - **Starting a stream follows VLC's `startPlayback`.** Remove the event listener, run `setMedia` on the queue and wait for it, then attach the listener and call `play()` on the main thread. A failing `setMedia` is logged instead of crashing.
  - **Stream generation.** A counter skips the pending `play()` if a newer zap, detach or release happened while `setMedia` ran. It also drops events from an older stream.
  - **Main-thread calls, as in VLC:** play/pause and the track getters (counts, lists for the dialogs). They are skipped while `setMedia` is still closing the previous stream, when libVLC holds the lock they would wait for.
  - **Queued:** `stop`, `release`, seek and rate, track selection, and scale and aspect.
  - The overlay reads seekable, length, time, position and track counts from a `StateFlow<PlayerState>` fed by libVLC's events.
  - `setVideoTrackEnabled` is no longer called by the app. Like VLC for Android, it is left to libVLC's own surface callback. Queued, it selected the video track while a new stream was starting, and video sometimes stayed frozen while audio played.
- **`VideoActivity` / `VideoOverlayController`**: use the injected player.
  - The empty vout callback is gone.
  - The `getVideoWidth/Height` fallback is gone. The size comes from `onNewVideoLayout`, which now also updates the picture-in-picture params.
- **libVLC 3.7.5 → 3.7.7**. Its Java classes are byte-identical to 3.7.5.
- **Changelog**: added a line for the fix and the libVLC bump.

## Compared with VLC for Android

- **Same:** `setMedia` and `release` off main; `play()`, pause and track getters on main; views detached on main before release; progress and seekable state from events; no `setVideoTrackEnabled` on a normal start.
- **Stricter:** VLC calls `stop()` on the main thread; here it is queued. The main-thread calls are skipped while a stream is switching.
- **Known remaining wait (VLC has it too):** detaching the views while a stream is still closing makes libVLC disable the video track on the main thread. Leaving the player in the middle of a stuck zap can still be slow.
- **Not done here:**
  - A foreground `PlaybackService` with a `MediaSession`.
  - Checking whether the stream is pausable before pausing.
  - A Hilt-provided `LibVLC` in place of the `VLCInstance` object.
  - A user-visible message when a stream fails to start (it is only logged).

## Testing

- `./gradlew -Pci spotlessCheck :app:testGoogleDebugUnitTest :app:compileGoogleDebugAndroidTestKotlin :app:lintGoogleDebug` passes, and CI "Unit tests + assemble" is green.
- New JVM tests in `PlayerCommandQueueTest`: posting returns while a call blocks; later calls run after it, in order; `call` returns the result; an exception or `Error` doesn't stop the queue.
- Tested on a phone by the author (zapping, starting the player). Possible decoding issues are tracked separately. The `workflow_dispatch` emulator job has not run.

title: Fix the AutoTimer instrumented test failures on main
body:
The instrumented job on `main` has failed since the AutoTimer merge (#556; its own run was cancelled, so #557, #559 and #558 inherited it). Three tests failed:

**AutoTimer rows.** `AutoTimerPreviewScreen` and `AutoTimerTargetPickScreen` put the row's click/toggle and state description on `ListRowSurface`. **Record series.** The test called `performScrollTo()` on "Record series", but the action panel is pinned outside the scrolling body, so there is no scroll parent. It now asserts the button is displayed and clicks it, like the existing Set Timer check.

Spotless, androidTest compile and lint pass locally. The emulator job is running via `workflow_dispatch` on this branch.

title: Fix the release startup crash and the empty TV & Movies bar
body:
Two fixes found while testing a signed release build.

## Release build crashes at startup

R8 removed the no-arg constructor of WorkManager's `WorkDatabase_Impl`. Room creates that class by reflection, so `androidx.startup`'s `WorkManagerInitializer` threw `NoSuchMethodException` and the app died on launch. `proguard-rules.pro` now keeps the no-arg constructor of every `RoomDatabase` subclass. Confirmed working on a device with a signed release APK.

## Empty grey bar at the bottom of the TV & Movies hub

A hub publishes its bottom bar to the shell's `ShellDestinationBarController`. `PhoneNavigator`'s destination listener set the controller to `Hidden` for every route that is not a hub, dialog destinations included (Changelog, About, Power, Send message, Sleep timer). A dialog floats over the hub, which stays composed. So the hub never published its bar again, and once the dialog closed the hub's bottom spacer showed as an empty grey band. The first start after the setup assistant opens the changelog, so every fresh install ran into this.

- A floating destination (`FloatingWindow`) no longer hides the bar, and no longer changes the NavHost viewport padding (`PhoneNavHost` now looks at the top non-floating entry).
- `RegisterShellDestinationBar` publishes again whenever its back stack entry resumes. This covers any other path that leaves the bar hidden while the hub stays on screen, such as the user's reports of an empty bar after returning to the app.

## Tests

- JVM: `ShellDestinationBarRouteTest.dialogOverHubLeavesPublishedChrome`.
- Instrumented: `ShellDestinationBarHostTest.resumeRepublishesAfterShellHidBar`. It compiles; the emulator job does not run on PRs.
- `-Pci spotlessCheck :app:testGoogleDebugUnitTest :app:compileGoogleDebugAndroidTestKotlin :app:lintGoogleDebug` passes locally.

title: Hilt follow-ups: fix what the post-migration audit found
body:
An audit of `main` after PR 15 found the End state in `docs/hilt-migration.md` holds, but some ViewModel shape, UiText, saved-state, and settings rules from `AGENTS.md` were not met. This PR fixes all of it, one commit per finding, plus follow-ups from a review and from the emulator run.

## Changes

- **`PhoneNavHostState` no longer holds UI objects.** It was a `@HiltViewModel` holding the `NavHostController`, the activity, a `Handler`, and result listeners, with no UiState. New `PhoneNavigator` (plain class, created by `MainActivity`) implements `PhoneNavHandle` and owns those. The ViewModel keeps only state that outlives the activity (saved start route and request codes, queued navigations, a held activity result), takes only `SavedStateHandle`, and exposes `StateFlow<PhoneNavUiState>`, which replaces four separate flows on `PhoneNavHandle`.
- **`TvShellViewModel` owns the TV ProfileCheck gate** as `StateFlow<TvShellUiState>`. `TvSessionGate` carries `UiText`. `TvHubViewModel` drops the cache flag and receiver label it only kept for the gate.
- **Profile check reports its failure as `UiText`.** `CheckProfile` no longer takes a `Context`. The unread `ProfileCheckEntry` list, the write-only `CURRENT_VERSION`, and the now unused `R.string.host` go.
- **Send-message and sleep-timer forms live in ViewModels** (`SavedTextField` / `SavedStateHandle`). Rotation no longer loses the input.
- **TV timer editor keeps its edits across process death.** `TvTimerEditViewModel` and `TvTimerHostViewModel` take a `SavedStateHandle`.
- **Settings through `SettingsRepository`.** Instant zap, picons, and MultiEPG text size come from ViewModels instead of `SharedPreferences` in composables. `MainActivity` and `RoomProfileStore` use injected settings. The picon and online-picon preferences default to `@bool/is_television`, and every reader falls back to off, so the screens and `SettingsRepository` agree on TV.
- **Picons follow the current profile's trust-all setting.** The picon loader picks its OkHttp client per call instead of once at startup. This bug predates the migration.
- **Dead code:** `userMessage(context)`, `mutationResultText`, `MainActivity.onTitleChanged`, the unregistered listener in `BaseActivity`, and unused `StartScreen` overloads. The profile-check gate now reports its own title.
- **Test stability:**
  - Waits on MockWebServer and OkHttp threads under `runTest` used `withTimeout`, which counts virtual time, so the bound could fire at once. They now use `withRealTimeout`, which counts wall-clock time. Under load this failed 1 in 4 full runs.
  - `TvShellViewModelTest` waits for the failed gate itself.
  - The MultiEPG picon screen tests pass `piconsEnabled`.
- **Docs:** fixed the widget-provider line in `hilt-migration.md` and added an "After the wave" section.

## Behaviour to check

- The preference defaults are now written at app start, because `RoomProfileStore` injects `SharedPreferences`.
- After process death, the TV Timers header reopens the editor. The hub overlay and MultiEPG editors still don't, because those hosts don't save which timer is open.

## Verification

- PR CI ("Unit tests + assemble") is green on `2829c70b`.
- Run locally 7 times under load, all passing: `./gradlew -Pci spotlessCheck :app:testGoogleDebugUnitTest :app:compileGoogleDebugAndroidTestKotlin :app:lintGoogleDebug` (886 JVM tests).
- Emulator runs, started with `workflow_dispatch`:
  - The instrumented suite is green on `b08bde81`, run [36572266004](https://github.com/sreichholf/dreamDroid/actions/runs/36572266004). The first run caught the MultiEPG picon tests, fixed in `b08bde81`. The only later commit changes a JVM test.
  - The upgrade from 1.15 to 2.0 on an emulator is green on `2829c70b`, run [36574072752](https://github.com/sreichholf/dreamDroid/actions/runs/36574072752).
- New JVM tests: `PhoneNavHostStateTest`, `PhoneNavigatorTest`, `SendMessageViewModelTest`, `SleepTimerViewModelTest`, `PiconCallsTest`, `SimpleResultUserMessageTest`, plus new cases in the shell, TV shell, TV timer, MultiEPG, EPG, and hub list tests.
- A review by a separate agent found nothing blocking; its minor points are addressed in `077cbe78`.
- Not run: a `googleRelease` (R8) smoke on a device.

title: Fix review findings from Hilt PRs 12 and 13
body:
Follow-up to the review of the merged Hilt PRs 12 (TV shell and hub) and 13 (share and player).

## Fixes

**TV shell (`TvShellViewModel`, PR 12)**
- A check that reuses cached device info no longer calls `beginChecking()`. The old activity code applied that result synchronously. Now, starting again after an edit that kept the connection settings (same id, new instance) no longer flashes Checking on the status chip.
- The result is applied with the cache of the profile that was checked, not whatever is current at the time.

**Share (`ShareViewModel`, PR 13)**
- A failed send whose error has no text (an HTTP status without a message, or a cancelled request) reported "Sent as …". This predates PR 13. It now shows the receiver's text, or the generic error.
- youtu.be links are parsed with OkHttp's `HttpUrl` instead of `java.net.URI`. `URI` throws on unescaped characters, and such links were then sent as plain `4097` streams instead of `yt://` refs.

## Test races

While I ran the PR check, two existing JVM tests failed intermittently. Both are fixed in their own commit:
- `MultiEpgViewModelTest.refreshRefetchesAFreshWindow`: `uiState` is `combine(...).stateIn`, so it can still show the idle state from before `refresh()`. The test now also waits for the new `/web/epgmulti` request.
- `HubViewModelTest.loadsTheBouquetsAndSelectsTheProfileDefault`: `update()` publishes the state and then writes the `SavedStateHandle`, on the load's thread. The test now waits for the save.

## Checks
- The three new tests (`TvShellViewModelTest`, and two in `ShareViewModelTest`) fail without the fixes.
- `./gradlew -Pci spotlessCheck :app:testGoogleDebugUnitTest :app:compileGoogleDebugAndroidTestKotlin :app:lintGoogleDebug` passes, and the unit tests passed again with `--rerun`.

Two other points from the review need no change:
- The identity comparison on `Profile` in `TvShellViewModel` matches the old `==`, because `Profile` has no `equals`.
- The player's zap job outlives an overlay detach. That keeps the stream across a rotation, and I'd call it an improvement.

title: Fix all lint errors and fail CI on new ones
body:
Lint reported 58 errors, but `abortOnError false` and no CI step meant nothing ever failed on them. That's how the API 33 `URLEncoder` call behind #502 shipped. This PR fixes all 58, puts `abortOnError` back to its default and adds a `Lint googleDebug` step to CI. The lint HTML report is uploaded with the unit test reports. The 178 warnings are still reported but don't fail anything.

## Behaviour fixes

- **Navigation dialogs** (power, send message, sleep timer) and profile check now get the activity through `LocalActivity`. Casting `LocalContext` can fail inside a Navigation `dialog`, where the context is the dialog's, not `MainActivity`.
- **PiconSyncWorker** checks `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` before posting its completion notification. It needs that permission on Android 13+.
- **VideoActivity.onUserLeaveHint** now calls `super`.
- **The session reachability probe** is launched once from `onCreate`, on both the phone and TV `MainActivity`. It is no longer started from the shell start, which `onStart` can reach. It idles while setup is showing.
- **Manifest:** `application/x-mpegURL` is now lower-case, which a MIME type needs in order to match. The `SEND` filter no longer has `host="youtu.be"`. Without a scheme the host had no effect, so every `text/*` share already reached the filter, as it still does.

## Correctness without visible change

- **Compose destinations** (13 files) read strings through `stringResource` or `LocalResources` instead of `LocalContext.current.getString`. The EPG label locale comes from `LocalLocale`. Effect keys are unchanged.
- **Activity transitions** move from `res/animator` to `res/anim`. They are view animations, and `overrideActivityTransition` takes `@AnimRes`.
- **Removed or tidied:**
  - The unused View drawer header layout (`navigation_header.xml`) is deleted.
  - The widget label's `layout_gravity` now matches its `textAlignment`. It had no effect on a full-width view.
  - Three `lint.xml` entries for issue IDs lint no longer knows are removed.

## Verification

- `:app:lintGoogleDebug`: 0 errors, and the task passes. It failed before these fixes, which shows the gate works.
- `spotlessCheck`, `:app:testGoogleDebugUnitTest`, `:app:compileGoogleDebugAndroidTestKotlin`: pass.
- Full instrumented suite on an API 30 emulator, the same level as CI: 575 tests, all passing.

title: Fix the share crash below Android 13
body:
The CI emulator job on `main` (API 30) failed `ShareActivityRetentionTest` after #500:

```
java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: No static method encode(Ljava/lang/String;Ljava/nio/charset/Charset;)Ljava/lang/String; in class Ljava/net/URLEncoder
```

`URLEncoder.encode(String, Charset)` exists only on API 33+, and minSdk is 26. Sharing a URL to dreamDroid crashed on every device older than Android 13. The call predates #500: the old `ShareActivity` had it too, but nothing tested share on an older API. The share code now uses the `encode(String, String)` overload, which exists on every API level.

Lint never flagged this because `app/lint.xml` set `NewApi` to `ignore`. It is set to `error` again. The only other hit was `android:windowLightNavigationBar` (API 27) in `themes.xml`. That one is harmless, since API 26 ignores unknown theme attributes, so it's marked `tools:targetApi="27"`. CI doesn't run lint, so this shows up in local lint reports but does not gate PRs.

Also fixes the spotless comment in the CI workflow, which was out of date after #501.

## Verification

- API 30 emulator, `main`: `ShareActivityRetentionTest` fails with the `NoSuchMethodError` above (reproduced locally).
- API 30 emulator, this branch: `ShareActivityRetentionTest` and `ShareProfilesScreenTest` pass (4 tests).
- `:app:lintGoogleDebug`: 0 `NewApi` issues.
- `spotlessCheck`: pass.

title: Fix backup import crash after choosing a file
body: Fixes #159. Choosing a backup file crashed instead of showing the import error. Storage Access Framework `*/*` can return a null stream (`InputStreamReader` then throws `NullPointerException`, which is not an `IOException`). Gson syntax errors and a setting value that does not match its type were also uncaught, and a bad document could delete profiles before the failure. A null stream is now an `IOException`, and the existing `backup_import_error` toast is shown. `parseBackupImport` rejects malformed JSON, a null document, and a mistyped setting before any profile is deleted or any preference is written. title: Fix session, poll, and overlay lifecycle leaks
body: ## Summary Extensive lifecycle audit of the phone/TV rewrite (Activities, Compose destinations, leftover video overlay). This PR fixes the confirmed issues; remaining findings that are design choices or process-death UX gaps are listed below and left alone. An independent verification pass confirmed the original fixes and two leftover gaps, which are now included: - Profile-check results are applied **before** any pause/helper gate, so Checking cannot stick if the drawer helper is recreated between `onPause` and `RESUMED`. - TV MultiEPG event-detail set-timer jobs are cancelled when the sheet leaves composition. ### Fixed - **Profile check stuck on Checking** — phone `MainActivity.onProfileChecked` dropped the HTTP result while paused or when `NavigationHelper` was recreated. The session is now applied first; UI navigation still waits until `RESUMED`. The static `ProfileChangedListener` is cleared in `onDestroy` (TV already did this). - **Signal meter kept polling after leave** — a finished load could call `reload()` after `DisposableEffect` dispose, and the acoustic `Handler` could re-post itself. `SignalPollGate` invalidates in-flight generations on stop. - **EPG “set timer” outlived the destination** — `launchSimpleResultLoad` uses the activity `lifecycleScope`. `EpgEventDialogSession.dismissProgress()` now cancels that job (same pattern as timer edit). MultiEPG, Current Service, and TV MultiEPG detail do the same on leave. - **Video overlay** — gesture brightness is restored on pause; `tvZapListBound` is cleared in `onDestroyView` so a retained fragment rebinds the TV zap list after view teardown. ### Reviewed, not changed - VLC attach/release is paired in `VideoActivity.onStart` / `onStop`. Playback through `onPause` is intentional for PiP. - Hub / bouquet / timer destinations already cancel `loadJob` / `mutateJob` in `DisposableEffect`. - Session reachability probe already uses `repeatOnLifecycle(RESUMED)`. - MultiEPG / TV selection not using `rememberSaveable` is a process-death UX gap, not a leak. - `PiconSyncService` is still a background `IntentService` without FGS — reliability under OS limits, out of scope here. - Overlay `retainInstance = true` stays; the overlay shell rewrite is listed under **Still to do**. - TV hub `setTimerFromEvent` is toast-only (no progress blocker); a late toast after leave is accepted. ## Test plan - `./gradlew :app:testGoogleDebugUnitTest` including new `SignalPollGateTest` and `EpgEventDialogSessionTest` - Instrumented: `SignalScreenTest`, EPG/profile-check hosts, `TvMultiEpgScreenTest` via `bash .cursor/cloud/connected-test.sh`

title: Fix watch and listening history no longer reaching YouTube
body:
## What broke
YouTube's WEB and WEB_REMIX `/player` now answer **every** video with `UNPLAYABLE` / "Video unavailable" (errorScreen subreason "The page needs to be reloaded") unless the request carries `playbackContext.contentPlaybackContext.signatureTimestamp`. Neither history report got `playbackTracking`, so nothing reached YouTube or YouTube Music history. Playback kept working because it resolves through visionOS. Bug report line:

```
W/YouTubeRepo: Video history: no tracking URLs for cGePtANhXko (playback=false watchtime=false status=UNPLAYABLE reason=Video unavailable)
```

Probed 2 October 2026 (signed in, `logged_in=1`). Bumping the client version made no difference; only the timestamp did:

| `/player` | no sts | live sts 20725 | date estimate 20714 |
|---|---|---|---|
| WEB (video history) | UNPLAYABLE, no tracking | OK, tracking | OK, tracking |
| WEB_REMIX (music history) | UNPLAYABLE, no tracking | OK, tracking | OK, tracking |

End to end with the fix's exact regexes: `iframe_api` -> player `8ab5c328` -> `base.js` -> sts 20725 -> signed WEB `/player` -> `videostatsPlaybackUrl` ping HTTP 204 -> the video was at the top of `FEhistory`.

## Fix: `PlayerSignatureTimestamp`
The value is the player build day since the epoch (20725 = 28 Sep 2026). YouTube accepts about seven months of them (bisected: 20515 and up; even 99999 passed). Resolution is layered so history survives a break in any one source:
1. **Live read**: `iframe_api` (1 KB) names the player, and `base.js` holds `signatureTimestamp:<n>`. The player id is rechecked at most daily, and `base.js` (about 3 MB) is downloaded only when the id changes. Persisted in SharedPreferences, so every repository instance shares it without adding process-wide repository state. A failed read backs off for an hour.
2. **Date estimate**: today minus 14 days, never below a stored live value. Used when there is no live read, or the live read is more than 14 days old. Needs no network.
3. **Self-heal**: a `/player` without tracking forces a fresh read (rate-limited to once every 10 min) and retries once, only if the value changed. A video that really is unavailable costs no second `/player`.

## Not done locally
Not compiled, as requested; CI's `build.yml` is the first compile. Not tried on a device.

## For testers
- Signed in, watch a video for a few seconds: it should appear at the top of YouTube history right away.
- Play a song: it should appear in YouTube Music history.
- Logcat should show `Player signatureTimestamp <n> from player <id>` once, and no `no tracking URLs` lines.
