title: Fix live playback stalling at the live edge
body:
Two defects, both only visible at the live edge of a broadcast. Reported as "live is bugged out, it works if I go behind the live mark but it doesn't work LIVE LIVE".

## Live streams stalled shortly after opening

Every network fetch the video player makes runs through the playback cache, and the adaptive branch of `loadQuality` hands the player a bare `MediaItem` with no cache key — so HLS manifests and media playlists were stored under an opaque URL key like ordinary media bytes.

A media playlist is re-requested from the *same* URL every target duration, and that reload is the only way the player hears that a broadcast has produced new segments. Media3 asks for it with a plain cacheable DataSpec (`FLAG_ALLOW_GZIP`, no key) and `CacheDataSource` resolves the unset length out of the stored content metadata, so the first copy was served straight back off disk and the segment list froze at whatever the opening fetch held.

That is exactly the reported asymmetry: the stream played out the handful of segments it opened with and stalled, while seeking back into the DVR window kept working, because those segments were already listed in the frozen copy. Turning video caching off was no escape either, since that switch selects a read-only cache which still *reads* what is stored.

`isUncacheablePlaybackUrl` routes the whole adaptive pipeline past both cache sources to the direct one. Live segments are excluded alongside the playlists on purpose: the video cache has no byte ceiling, and an hour of a broadcast is an hour of media nobody replays. It is one predicate shared with `ChunkedStreamDataSource.shouldChunk`, which was already asking the same question about the same URL shapes.

## A live stream always read −0:15 and never said LIVE

A live HLS player is never at the end of its playlist. With no `EXT-X-START` and no `HOLD-BACK` in the manifest — which is what YouTube sends — Media3 deliberately holds three target-durations back from the playlist end, so with roughly five-second segments a stream sitting exactly where its own manifest asks it to sit is 15-16s short of the window end. The readout measured from that end against a flat ten-second tolerance, so the chip could never reach its live state.

That offset is the live edge rather than slack to forgive with a bigger tolerance, so it is now read off `Timeline.Window.liveConfiguration` on every timeline change — a playlist reload republishes the timeline, so a broadcast that changes its hold-back mid-stream is followed rather than pinned at its opening value — and the offset is measured from there. The number now means how far the viewer scrubbed back, instead of that plus a constant. A source declaring no target keeps the old window-end measurement.

## Verification

Both behaviours were settled against the Media3 1.11 bytecode rather than from recall: `DefaultHlsPlaylistTracker$MediaPlaylistBundle.loadPlaylistImmediately` builds its reload spec with `setFlags(1)` and no key, `CacheDataSource.open` resolves an unset length through `ContentMetadata.getContentLength`, and `HlsMediaSource.getTargetLiveOffsetUs` falls through to `3 * targetDurationUs` and publishes it via `SinglePeriodTimeline`.

`compileDebugKotlin` and the full JVM suite pass, with ten new cases across `VideoPlaybackCacheTest` and `LiveWindowOffsetTest`.

Exercised on a Pixel 9 Pro API 37 emulator: a live stream ran for 26 minutes with the playlist tracker still loading and no `PlaylistStuckException`, `ExoPlaybackException` or source error. The only warnings were 26 `PesReader` resync lines in the first fifteen seconds, which is the MPEG-TS parser joining mid-segment, and they stop once it settles.

## Worth a look on real hardware

- A long broadcast left at the live edge, and the jump-to-live control after a scrub back.
- A quality change mid-broadcast — it is a track-selector cap rather than a re-prepare, so it should be untouched, but it is the adjacent path.
- A vertical live stream, whose chip sits in a tonal container rather than on the video.
- One ordinary VOD, confirming cached replay and scrubbing are unchanged. That is the regression risk here, since this widens what bypasses the cache.

title: Fix AutoMix restarts and improve adaptive transitions
body:
## What this changes

Fixes music restarting from zero during stream recovery and makes AutoMix base its transitions on reliable audio measurements. It also fixes two silence-analysis paths that could cut tracks short: a failed probe returned the full sixty-second skip allowance, and a quiet final half-second incorrectly authorized skipping audio earlier in the tail.

AutoMix now separates tempo confidence from bar-accent confidence, uses individual beat alignment when downbeats are uncertain, limits incompatible tempos to a brief unprocessed overlap, and recognizes relative major/minor keys. Identifiable numbered album sequences remain intact, and short tracks limit their own overlap. Audio-profile version 7 discards the old measurements and requires complete head/tail decodes.

## Why

Changing the current Media3 source can reset its position. Recovery previously replaced the source and called `play()` without restoring that position; a late prefetch could also replace a song after it became current. The shared replacement helper now preserves the current index, position and playback intent at apply time, and placeholder resolution avoids duplicate replacements.

The two-player engine now validates its incoming target throughout the fade, aborts on excessive clock drift, cancels stale transitions on seeks and playback-order changes, and restores the active player if session handoff fails. A failed automatic pair falls back to ordinary advancement instead of reopening the standby every monitor tick.

Apple Music's documented restraint for incompatible songs and album playback informed the behavior: https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105067. This improves Koda's existing local DSP approach; it does not reproduce Apple's proprietary model.

## States handled

- Loading and incomplete analysis: bounded, cancellation-aware profiling; uncertain tracks use a clean short fade. A signed stream's length permits analysis before prefetch has completed caching it.
- Errors, stalls and offline playback: retain position and pause intent during recovery; abandon an unready or drifting standby while retaining the outgoing player. Metered analysis still requires fully cached audio.
- Queue edits, seeks, repeats and mode changes: discard stale transitions, avoid mixing a track into itself, and preserve exact queue occurrences.
- Short tracks, natural fades and albums: bound the overlap, avoid additional tempo/filter effects on brief fades, and preserve known consecutive album tracks when unshuffled.
- Signed out: no new account, API or authentication dependency.

## Validation

- `./gradlew compileDebugKotlin testDebugUnitTest --console=plain` passed: **189 tests, zero failures or errors**.
- Added 38 tests covering source replacement, silence probes, synthetic rhythm envelopes, transition planning and simulated two-player handoffs.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- No UI changes. No local APK packaging or device/emulator run.
- The original user reports had no logs, so their exact runtime trigger has not been reproduced. Real-song listening and Android audio-sink timing remain to be checked on a device.

## Deliberately not done

No new settings, queue reordering, vocal/stem separation, learned model or claim of Apple Music parity. Sparse silence probes remain an approximation between samples; the scanner now retains the unmeasured gap beside an audible sample.

## Checklist

- [x] Kotlin compile and full JVM test suite pass
- [x] Roadmap and operating notes updated with the final behavior
- [x] No cookies, stream URLs, probe output or private data committed
- [ ] APK build through CI (not awaited)
- [ ] Device listening: mixed-tempo playlists, quiet endings, numbered albums, seek/pause during a transition, and streaming recovery

title: Fix video scrub latency and the 100-song playlist cap
body:
## What this changes

Two independent fixes, both cases of a symptom being blamed on the wrong layer.

1. Scrubbing a video now starts playing almost immediately instead of sitting on a loading spinner, and video playback reuses bytes it has already fetched.
2. Playlists with more than 100 songs load in full instead of stopping at exactly 100.

Fixes #218

## Why

### Video scrubbing

The first commit wrote progressive VOD through the shared `SimpleCache`, on the theory that seeks were slow because video bypassed the disk cache. Testing that build showed the symptom unchanged: scrubbing into the seek bar's own buffered segment still stalled.

The pale seek-bar segment is `player.bufferedPosition` — ExoPlayer's in-memory sample queue — so a scrub landing inside it was stalling on data the player already held, and no caching change could have fixed that. Two defaults caused it, both paid whether the bytes come from RAM, disk, or the network:

- **`bufferForPlaybackAfterRebufferMs` was 2.5s.** A seek out of the buffered region counts as a rebuffer, so the first frame was withheld until 2.5s of media had been queued. A guaranteed stall on every such seek.
- **Seeking was exact.** There was no `SeekParameters` call anywhere in the codebase, so ExoPlayer decoded from the sync sample before the target and discarded every frame up to it — hundreds on a 1080p60 multi-second GOP. This is also the largest single cost on an uncached seek.

The resume threshold is now 800ms. Scrub-bar drags and the 10s steps resolve to the nearest keyframe; chapter starts, comment timestamps, SponsorBlock skips and every session or quality-switch restore stay exact. The back buffer is 45s rather than a 15s window narrower than a single drag, and the allocator ceiling is 96MB so a split pair's video and audio plus that back buffer fit without starving the forward runway.

### Playlist paging

The continuation token was never the problem — page one hands one over correctly. The reply arrives under `onResponseReceivedActions.appendContinuationItemsAction.continuationItems`, while every container the music parser knew was the older `continuationContents.<x>Continuation`. Every page after the first parsed to zero songs, and with no shelf left to scope to the token lookup returned null, so the walk stopped **reporting success** — no fallback ran, nothing was logged.

Verified by probing a live 982-track playlist: the corrected walk reaches 972 songs across 10 pages and terminates cleanly (the gap is deleted/private entries). Before: 100.

The shelf scoping is kept deliberately. The same response carries a `sectionListRenderer` continuation whose reply is a `musicCarouselShelfRenderer` of related playlists rather than tracks, so a generic search over the whole response follows the wrong chain.

Two adjacent faults went with it: `fetchContinuation` refused to run without cookies, capping public playlists signed out for a second and independent reason, and the signed-out branch only ever parsed page one. Liked Songs shares the parser and stops burning up to 499 empty continuation requests per load.

## States handled

- **Loading:** video first-frame threshold unchanged (1s), so opening a video is unaffected.
- **Signed out:** playlists now page to their end anonymously — previously capped at 100 for two separate reasons. Public browse and its continuations both answer with no session.
- **Error / offline:** unchanged; an incomplete playlist walk still returns partial rows and logs the degradation rather than claiming the page boundary is the real end.
- **Long video:** the disk cache is a 512MB shared LRU and 1080p runs ~30MB/min, so a video past roughly 17 minutes evicts its own earliest bytes. Called out below.
- **Cast:** `seekPlayerTo` only sets seek parameters on `ExoPlayer`; a `CastPlayer` is driven by the receiver and seeks unchanged.
- **Live:** unaffected — live plays through the HLS manifest, not the progressive path.
- **Duplicate rows:** playlist order and duplicates preserved; the same video id can legitimately appear twice.

## Deliberately not done

- **HTTP/2 for stream fetches.** `ChunkedStreamDataSource` is on `DefaultHttpDataSource` (HTTP/1.1, one request in flight per connection) and a split pair issues two requests per seek. `media3-datasource-okhttp` over the OkHttp already in the build would multiplex both on one pooled connection — the main remaining win for uncached seeks, and its own change since it touches the per-URL User-Agent invariant.
- **Disk cache eviction policy.** The self-eviction above wants a per-video reservation, not a bigger number.
- **Liked Songs verification.** It shares the fixed parser, but that `FEmusic_liked_videos` continuations use this same shape is inferred from the code, not probed — that needs a signed-in session.

## Screenshots or recording

No visual change in either fix. The video difference is latency; the playlist difference is row count past 100.

## Checklist

- [x] Builds with `./gradlew assembleDebug`
- [x] Run on a device or emulator, not just compiled
- [x] No hardcoded colors; everything resolves through `ColorScheme`
- [x] Material 3 Expressive components used before standard M3, springs for touch-driven motion
- [x] The signed-out path still works

### If this touches one of these areas

- [ ] **New setting** — none added. `sp_cache_music` was retitled "Cache Playback" in place and its existing `buildSettingsSearchIndex` entry updated.
- [ ] **New player style** — not applicable.
- [x] **InnerTube parser change** probed against a live response, not written from memory, with the month and year noted — `continuationItemsOrNull` in `data/InnerTubeContinuations.kt`, verified August 2026 against a 982-track playlist, with a JVM test over the container shapes.
- [x] No cookie dumps, response JSON, or `.probe/` contents committed

---

Notes for review:

`main` is merged in, so this carries SponsorBlock (#231) and the Up Next metadata fix (#232). The merge surfaced a genuine interaction: seek parameters are sticky player state, so the scrub bar's switch to `CLOSEST_SYNC` persisted into SponsorBlock's skip and undo paths, where a keyframe-snapped skip could land back inside the segment it just left and re-trigger. Both now route through `seekPlayerTo` with precise seeking.

Device testing confirmed the scrubbing fix on the pre-merge build. The playlist fix is verified by live probe and unit tests but has not been on a device.

The CodeQL alert on `DownloadNotificationHelper.kt` looks like a false positive: all three `PendingIntent`s in that file wrap an explicit `Intent(context, MainActivity::class.java)` with `FLAG_IMMUTABLE`, and the only implicit Intent in the file opens system notification settings via `startActivity` and never touches a `PendingIntent`.

title: fix: feeds that scroll under the status bar instead of stopping at it
body:
Reported as "the app is not edge to edge, the status bar stands out like a native title bar".

## What was actually wrong

The window was edge to edge the whole time: `enableEdgeToEdge()` is called, both bars are transparent, the icon appearance is set. The bug sat a layer down, in one line copied into every scrolling surface:

```kotlin
LazyColumn(
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize()
        .background(backgroundColor)
        .windowInsetsPadding(WindowInsets.statusBars),   // shrinks the viewport
    contentPadding = PaddingValues(bottom = ...)
)
```

Padding a scroll container shrinks its **viewport**, so content is clipped at the status bar and can never pass beneath it, leaving a flat band that reads as a system title bar. The same inset in `contentPadding` spaces the first item without shrinking anything.

The bottom of those very screens already did it correctly (`navBarInset` went into `contentPadding`, so content scrolls under the floating toolbar), which is why only the top ever looked wrong.

This matches Android's own guidance verbatim — *"Apply inset padding to the `contentPadding` parameter of scrollable components. DO NOT apply it as a `Modifier.padding()` to the list's parent container, as this clips the content and prevents it from scrolling behind the system bars."*

## The change

One value, seven consumers. `HomeScreen`'s `listBottomPadding` becomes `listContentPadding` and now carries the status bar inset as well, so every tab surface gets it from a single place and a new screen inherits it:

| Surface | Change |
| --- | --- |
| Music home, Spotlight, Video home | drop the clipping modifier, pass `contentPadding` through |
| Subscriptions (feed, channel drill-in, channel list) | same, three lists |
| Video library, Video history | same; history keeps the embedded case unpadded, since `SubPageTopBar` already sits in that area |

Screens with a **fixed header** — Library, Search, Settings, Stats, listening history, artist, album — are deliberately untouched. The status bar area there holds a real header rather than a band, so moving the inset would change nothing visible.

## Two things that travelled with it

- **Navigation bar scrim.** `enableEdgeToEdge` leaves contrast enforcement *on* for the navigation bar, which paints a translucent system band under the floating toolbar and mini player on three-button navigation. Now off for both bars in `Theme.kt`. API 30-34 only; the system owns this from 35.
- **Portrait watch page.** Its column took `systemBars` on both edges, which also clipped the info list at the navigation bar. Now top-only, with the nav bar inset moved into `VideoInfoSection`'s scrolling padding, so related videos pass under the bar. The video itself still sits below the status bar on black, the way YouTube's portrait watch page does — taking it higher would crop a 16:9 frame and put the clock over the picture.

`Theme.kt` keeps its manual `isAppearanceLight*` calls against the usual advice to let `enableEdgeToEdge` own them, and now says why: that helper decides from the system `uiMode`, while Koda's theme mode is its own setting, so forcing dark in-app on a light system would otherwise give dark icons on a dark bar.

## Deliberately not done

No status bar scrim. Google's guidance suggests a `StatusBarProtection` gradient for content passing under the clock; the plain treatment was chosen instead, so artwork now scrolls behind the status bar on the home feeds. Easy to add later if it reads badly on a busy shelf.

## Testing

Not built locally — the build is the owner's call in this repo, and CI covers it. Worth eyes on the music home, video home and the watch page, since the visible change is content passing under the status bar on scroll.

title: Fix music playback before 4.5
body:
## What this changes

- Removes the one-shot music playback error state and the random Toast shown for recoverable Media3 errors.
- Resolves music through NewPipe 0.26.5 first, matching the maintained client path already adopted by video playback.
- Keeps direct InnerTube as a last-resort fallback instead of accepting its long-media progressive URLs first.
- Rejects generated NewPipe stream content where Media3 requires a real URL.
- Limits visitorData reminting to 403s from direct InnerTube streams; NewPipe failures now get a fresh extraction without clearing the whole queue identity.

## Why

The latest video fix moved VOD playback to NewPipe first because direct ANDROID_VR URLs can begin normally and then hit a progressive byte ceiling on long media. Music still preferred that old direct path, so long songs carried the same risk. Music errors were also surfaced immediately as Toasts even though MusicService retries or skips them itself, producing noisy messages during otherwise recoverable playback.

## Testing

Not run at the maintainer request. The GitHub Actions APK will be tested manually before release.

title: Fix YouTube Music playback stuck on loading
body:
YouTube broke ANDROID_MUSIC v7.20.51 and rolled out PO Token
enforcement for WEB/ANDROID/IOS/MWEB clients in early 2026, causing
stream URL resolution to silently return null or hang. NewPipe's HTML
parsing also fails on the current player JS ("Page needs to be
reloaded").

- Switch stream resolution primary path to InnerTube ANDROID_VR
  (v1.65.10), which does not require a PO Token and returns
  unobfuscated audio URLs.
- Add IOS (v21.02.3) as secondary InnerTube fallback.
- Keep NewPipe as a final fallback for cookie/region cases.
- Bump WEB_REMIX (1.20260114.03.00) and WEB (2.20260114.08.00)
  clientVersion across browse, continuation and reportPlayback paths
  so YouTube does not reject them as outdated.
- Centralize client versions in companion-object constants so the
  next bump only touches one place.

title: Fix playback progress monitoring and service lifecycle issues
body:
## Summary
This PR addresses critical issues with the music service's playback progress monitoring and lifecycle management, particularly around the Android 16 Live Update feature and proper cleanup when the app is dismissed from recents.

## Key Changes

**MusicService.kt:**
- Added `onTaskRemoved()` override to properly pause playback and stop the service when the user swipes the app from recents, preventing foreground notification from getting stuck
- Added `progressJob` field to track the active progress monitoring coroutine
- Refactored progress monitoring to use a single-flight pattern: only one progress monitor coroutine runs at a time, preventing multiple concurrent loops from fighting over crossfade volume and spamming Live Update notifications
- Moved progress monitoring trigger from `onPlaybackStateChanged()` (which fires multiple times per song) to `onIsPlayingChanged()` for cleaner lifecycle management
- Enhanced `onPlaybackStateChanged()` to properly dismiss the Live Update when playback ends or returns to idle state
- Added proper cleanup of `progressJob` in `onDestroy()`
- Wrapped `monitorProgress()` coroutine in try-finally block to ensure Live Update is hidden when the loop exits
- Added clarifying comments to `onGetSession()` explaining null handling during teardown

**PlayerViewModel.kt:**
- Enhanced `controller` property getter with exception handling for cases where the MediaController future completes exceptionally (e.g., during service teardown races)
- Implemented connection retry logic with exponential backoff (up to 3 attempts with 300ms delays) to gracefully handle "Session not found" errors that occur when the service is being torn down
- Improved error logging and state management around controller initialization

## Notable Implementation Details

- The single-flight progress monitoring pattern prevents the N concurrent loops issue that was causing crossfade volume conflicts and Live Update spam
- Service teardown is now properly handled both when the user swipes the app away and when the controller fails to connect during a race condition
- Live Update notifications are now guaranteed to be dismissed when playback stops, preventing them from lingering on the lock screen
- Connection retry logic ensures the UI recovers cleanly when the service is briefly unavailable during app lifecycle transitions

title: Fix visitorData bot-check handling and stream URL caching
body:
## Summary

Fixes critical playback failures caused by YouTube's bot-check flagging stale `visitorData` tokens mid-TTL, and improves stream URL caching to handle expiry. Without these fixes, users experience "music played fine, then nothing plays anymore" after hours of uptime.

## Key Changes

**YouTubeRepository (`data/YouTubeRepository.kt`)**
- **Removed hardcoded fallback `visitorData`**: The `DEFAULT_VISITOR_DATA` constant was a shared token that YouTube's bot check explicitly rejects. Replaced with per-install persistence + empty string fallback.
- **Added `visitorData` persistence**: New `SharedPreferences`-backed `loadPersistedVisitorData()` / `persistVisitorData()` / `clearPersistedVisitorData()` methods store the last successfully minted token per install, so cold starts on flaky networks still have a usable, install-unique token.
- **Implemented mid-TTL remint on bot-check flag**: New `remintVisitorData(flagged)` method detects when YouTube rejects the current token (LOGIN_REQUIRED playability status or 200/OK with missing streamingData) and immediately mints a fresh one, then retries the resolution. Without this, a flagged token poisons all resolutions for hours until TTL expiry.
- **Refactored stream resolution flow**:
  - Extracted `resolvePlayerStreamingData()`: Wraps the two-client chain with one-shot remint + retry logic.
  - Extracted `runPlayerClientChain()`: Encapsulates ANDROID_VR → IOS fallback with a new `PlayerResponse` class that carries both streamingData and a `visitorDataSuspect` flag.
  - Renamed `fetchPlayerStreamingData()` → `fetchPlayerResponse()`: Now returns `PlayerResponse` instead of nullable streamingData, allowing callers to distinguish "no data" from "bot check flagged this token".
  - Extracted `pickAudioStreamUrl()`: Separated URL selection logic from the /player call, making the flow clearer.
- **Fixed bootstrap fetch timeout**: Changed `fetchVisitorData()` to use the general 30s `okHttpClient` instead of `streamResolveClient`'s 8s timeout, which was killing downloads on slow connections and leaving users without a usable token.
- **Allowed empty `visitorData` in requests**: Modified `/player` call construction to omit `visitorData` and `X-Goog-Visitor-Id` header when the token is blank, instead of sending an empty string (which YouTube may reject).
- **Unified quality listing**: `getVideoQualitiesFromInnerTube()` now uses `resolvePlayerStreamingData()` instead of duplicating the client chain, so quality fetches also benefit from bot-check remint.

**MusicService (`service/MusicService.kt`)**
- **Implemented stream URL expiry tracking**: Replaced simple string cache with `CachedUri(uri, expiresAtMs)` class. Googlevideo URLs carry an `expire` query param (epoch seconds, ~6h out); cache entries are dropped instead of replayed when expired, preventing 403 errors from stale URLs.
- **Separated retry tracking**: Moved per-song retry counts from the URI cache (where they were stored as `"retry_count_$videoId"` strings) to a dedicated `retryCounts` map. Retry budget is now reset when a song successfully starts playback, so one bad stretch months ago can't permanently blacklist a song.
- **Added `streamUrlExpiryMs()` helper**: Parses the `expire` param with a 5-minute safety margin; falls back to a conservative 4-hour TTL when the param is missing or unreadable.

**PlayerViewModel (`ui/player/PlayerViewModel.kt`)**
- **Added playback error surface**: New `_playbackError` StateFlow and `clearPlaybackError()` method expose resolution/network failures to the UI. Before this, failed resolutions were silent and the player sat on the buffering spinner indefinitely.
- **Moved buffering watchdog to init**: Extracted the 30-second stuck-spinner timeout into a dedicated `start

title: Fix playlist playback repeating after 50 videos
body:
For #767, this PR fixes playlist playback looping back to previously played videos after the initial batch.

The issue was in the playlist prefetch logic in `PlaylistPlaybackPage`. When the player approached the end of the loaded items and triggered a prefetch, the code used `currentIndex` (the current playback position) as the starting point for fetching new items, instead of `count` (the current playlist size). This meant:

1. Items already in the playlist were being re-fetched from the pager and appended as duplicates
2. The upper bound `currentIndex + PLAYLIST_PREFETCH` didn't extend far enough past the existing playlist, so new items beyond the initial batch were never loaded

The fix changes both the range start and upper bound to use `count`, so new items are always fetched starting from where the playlist currently ends rather than from the current playback position.

I tested locally and this does solve my issue!

title: Fix crash in forced transcoding when building playlists
body:
I've been experiencing frequent crashing after upgrading to 0.8.1. Turns out it was related to the recent forced transcoding changes in [`4ea91f16`](https://github.com/damontecres/StashAppAndroidTV/commit/4ea91f16b687215493bfd6016301574f3c92cdb2).

The rewrite of `checkIfAlwaysTranscode` changed [this line](https://github.com/damontecres/StashAppAndroidTV/commit/4ea91f16b687215493bfd6016301574f3c92cdb2#diff-a8330e6b2806eeffe85cb59f922836a975b2ec706beeda66669e1fab63541f88L250) to return `streams[streamKey]` (a URL) instead of `streamKey` (a map key like `"HLS Full HD (1080p)"`). That URL then gets passed as a `streamLabel` into `buildMediaItem`, which tries to use it as a key to look up the actual URL and fails.

The fix is just changing `return streams[streamKey]` to `return streamKey`.

title: Fix issue with the transcode resolution list
body:
This PR fixes a bug that I was experiencing. I noticed that the transcode resolution settings weren't working. In fact, upon further investigation, I found that they were perfectly swapped. If I picked 2160p, I'd get limited to 240p transcoding. If I picked 1080p, I'd get 480p, and so on. And if I picked 240p, the app would crash.

I believe this is caused by the fact that the proto enum values are in the reverse order compared to the transcode options array.

And in addition, you can see that the proto enum values jump from 4 to 6, which would explain why choosing 240p caused the app to crash (because index 6 doesn't exist in the options array).

See this:

https://github.com/damontecres/StashAppAndroidTV/blob/94e6bb7341cd89ab40ab195e9e27aa5ec4d0a70b/app/src/main/proto/preferences.proto#L88-L95

...compared to here...

https://github.com/damontecres/StashAppAndroidTV/blob/94e6bb7341cd89ab40ab195e9e27aa5ec4d0a70b/app/src/main/res/values/arrays.xml#L192-L199

Reversing the order of the proto enum should solve the issue.

**Disclaimer:** I haven't actually built/tested this locally, I don't know if this would break some other parts of the app, I'm not sure if I'm supposed to auto-generate some files from the .proto, etc. But this is what I believe will fix the issue.

A user reported this on discord. If activity tracking is enabled, when playing a playlist of scenes, as you moved to the next scene, the activity tracker would report activity for the previous scenes when it should have stopped.

The actual issue was that `trackActivityListener` was not stored in a `mutableStateOf`, so re-compositions destroyed the reference. Then when going to teh next scene, the code to cancel tracking for the previous scene thought there was no `trackActivityListener` since the reference was lost.

This PR moves the `trackActivityListener` into the view model which more accurately follows the lifecycle of the entire playlist and movement between scenes.

title: Add android_simulate_process_death and fix the Process Death action
body:
Closes #135.

## What
- **`android_simulate_process_death`**, a SAFE_ACTION tool. Args: `packageName`, `relaunch` (default `true`), `deviceSerial`. It sends the app to the background, kills the process, relaunches it from the launcher so Android restores the task from saved state, and reports the old and new pid.
- **Shared code:** `AppOperations.simulateProcessDeath` backs both the MCP tool and the tool window's **Process Death** action (`ProcessDeathCommand`). A parity test checks both send the same device commands.
- **Skill:** playbook 4 now uses the new tool instead of a confirmed `am kill` through `android_run_adb_command`.

## Bugs fixed in the existing Process Death action (found while testing on the API 34 emulator)
1. **Home was never pressed.** `isAppInForeground` parsed `dumpsys activity recents` and returned `standard` on API 34, so a foreground app stayed on screen and `am kill` could not kill it. It's replaced with a check of the resumed activity, and the broken helper is deleted.
2. **The kill was never verified.** It ran one `am kill` after a fixed 2.5 s, and `am kill` exits 0 whether or not it killed anything. It now retries until the pid is gone (8 s / 16-try cap) and fails if the process won't die.
3. **The relaunch lost the screen.** `am start -n` pushed a fresh `MainActivity` on top of the task. It now uses the launcher intent (`-a MAIN -c LAUNCHER`), so the killed screen comes back from saved state.

## Testing
- `./gradlew test detekt` passes.
- New tests: `SimulateProcessDeathTest` (success, already in the background, won't die, not running, not installed, `relaunch=false`, the tool's result and error text), the parity case, and `ActivityParserTest.parseResumedPackage`.
- **On device** (emulator, API 34, sample app → *Process death*, Count ×3):
  - before: `pid 24753 | plain 3 | ViewModel 3 | savedInstanceState 3`
  - tool: `Killed … (pid 24753 is gone). Relaunched … as pid 25006.` Took 4 `am kill` tries, 7.4 s in total.
  - after: `ProcessDeathActivity` on top, `pid 25006 | restored state: true | plain 0 | ViewModel 0 | savedInstanceState 3`

## Note
Killing a just-backgrounded app took 3–4 tries (≈2–6 s) on this emulator. The 8 s budget keeps the whole call under the 15 s HTTP cap.

title: Fix the master build, and drop the IDE the Marketplace verifier calls Critical
body:
`master` has not compiled since #75 was merged on 6 September. That PR landed with
**`Build: FAILURE` and `Plugin Verifier: FAILURE`** — both required checks were red at merge.

This restores the build and removes the IDE the Marketplace verifier reports as Critical.

## Three failures, each hiding the next

A failing `compileKotlin` stops the `test` task before it starts, so only the first was visible.

**1. It did not compile.** `declaredAttachMethods()` walked the class hierarchy with
`var current = androidDebugger.javaClass`, which Kotlin infers as `Class<AndroidDebugger<*>>`,
while `getSuperclass()` is declared `Class<? super T>` — the reassignment could never
typecheck. `declaredMethodsFor()`, thirty lines below, already had this right as `Class<*>?`.

**2. A test that could never have passed.** `private createState methods are still discovered`
handed a `PrivateFakeDebugger` to `FakeDebugSessionStarter`, whose method declares
`debugger: FakeDebugger`. `matchesAttachSignature` rejects an argument that is not an instance
of the declared parameter type — correctly, since the real starter's parameter is the real
debugger type — so the call never matched and `attach()` returned false.

The production code was right; the fixture was wrong. It now has its own starter, and the test
asserts the state object *reached* it, which is what proves the private factory was invoked
rather than merely that a signature matched.

**3. Three Detekt violations** from the same change: a wrapped `->` body, and fixture
parameters that are unused because being unused is the point — suppressed where they are
declared, with the reason stated.

## Compatibility: `sinceBuild` 231 → 232

The Marketplace verifier reports **IntelliJ IDEA 2023.1.7 as Critical**. The Android plugin
bundled with IDEA 2023.1 has no `com.android.tools.idea.execution`, which
`Restart App With Debugger` links against — and `verifier-ignored-problems.txt` told *our*
verifier to ignore exactly that message. CI and the Marketplace ran the same tool and
disagreed because one of them had been told to look away.

2023.1 is the only build missing the package, so the floor moves rather than the suppression
growing. **`verifier-ignored-problems.txt` is deleted**, and the result is verified rather
than assumed:

| Target | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `AI-232.10300.40` (Iguana, new floor) | Compatible — 2 deprecated API usages |
| `AI-242.23339.11` | Compatible — 2 |
| `AI-251.25410.109` (compile target) | Compatible — 3 |
| `IC-232.10335.12` (new IDEA floor) | Compatible — 2 |
| `IC-251.23774.435` | Compatible — 3 |

Nothing suppressed, on any of them. Run locally with `./gradlew verifyPlugin`.

## ⚠️ This drops Android Studio Hedgehog

Hedgehog is `AI-231`, so raising the floor to 232 drops it along with IDEA 2023.1. `README.md`
and `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md` now say **Android Studio 2023.2 (Iguana) and later**. If that is
too aggressive, the alternative is making the `AndroidDebugger` reference fully reflective so
no build links against the missing package — more work, and it keeps one more IDE generation.

## Not addressed here: the 2026.3 EAP Critical

The same Marketplace report flags `IU-263.4732.28` with *"1 missing mandatory dependency"*,
while `IU-263.3889.65` a week earlier was Compatible. Nothing in the plugin changed between
them. Android support is not bundled with IntelliJ IDEA — it is a Marketplace plugin — so the
verifier running against a bare IDE cannot resolve `org.jetbrains.android`, which is also why
the report hedges the other four as *"may be caused by absence of dependency in the target
IDE"*. That dependency is correct and cannot be dropped; every Android API comes from it.

Capping `untilBuild` to silence the row is specifically **not** proposed — that is the bug
that made the Marketplace serve 1.0.2 for four years, and `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md` records it.

## Build memory (found by CI on this PR)

The first CI run failed the Plugin Verifier job with *"Gradle build daemon has been stopped:
since the JVM garbage collector is thrashing"* during `compileJava`, before any verification
started. `gradle.properties` set no `org.gradle.jvmargs`, so the daemon ran on Gradle's
defaults of 512 MiB heap and 384 MiB metaspace.

The same shortage had already shown up locally as the Kotlin daemon's *"Not enough memory to
run compilation"*, which I initially put down to a loaded machine — wrong: it is the project,
and a clean runner reproduces it. The Kotlin compile daemon is a separate process and does not
inherit `org.gradle.jvmargs`, so it is sized on its own line.

(The `Build` job on that same run failed separately with `read ECONNRESET` while `Setup Java`
downloaded the JDK — unrelated infrastructure, cleared by the re-run.)

## Verification

`./gradlew clean buildPlugin test detekt verifyPlugin` and
`scripts/verify-marketplace-descriptor.sh` all pass locally. The built descriptor reports
`since-build = 232`, no `until-build`.

title: MCP: debug context, file transfer, screen recording, and two defect fixes
body:
Four commits toward the 5.0 release: two new tool groups, one triage bundle, and two defect
fixes in the MCP layer.

## What's here

**`23fa1a2` — `android_get_debug_context`**
One call returning activity, UI semantics, logcat and a screenshot describing the same moment,
instead of the four round trips an agent has to know to make.

**`b6ed821` — file transfer and screen recording**
`PushFileTool`, `PullFileTool`, `StartScreenRecordTool`, `StopScreenRecordTool`. Both go through
`executeShellCommand` rather than the obvious ddmlib APIs, which Android Studio ships as stubs —
the same failure that broke `android_take_screenshot`. Device paths are restricted to `/sdcard`,
`/storage` and `/data/local/tmp`, and the local destination of a pull is deliberately *not* a
parameter, so nothing holding the MCP token can choose where a file lands.

**`a541b9f` — two defects: project resolution, and start/stop on the EDT**

*Every project-dependent tool failed whenever two projects were open.* The tool context resolved
the project with `openProjects.singleOrNull { !it.isDisposed }`, so a second open project turned
`android_get_current_activity`, `android_get_activity_stack`, `android_get_current_fragments`
and the default logcat package filter into "No project is open" — wrong, and unactionable.

Resolution now follows the rule `requireDevice` already uses: the selected project, or the only
one open, and otherwise **refuse to guess** and name the candidates. Falling back to the focused
window was rejected deliberately — it is wrong exactly when it matters most, with an agent
working while the developer looks at something else. `ProjectResolution` is generic and free of
IntelliJ types so the rule is unit tested directly, and `android_select_project` exists so the
ambiguity error names a fix the agent can actually perform.

*Starting and stopping the MCP server ran on the EDT.* Starting binds two sockets and writes the
stdio endpoint descriptor; stopping waits for live stdio sessions to end. Stopping from the MCP
panel with a client attached froze the tool window until that wait expired. Both transitions now
run on a pooled thread, the panel shows the transition and disables its controls, and Restart
chains stop → start. The menu actions had the same defect. `start()` is also idempotent now —
called twice it used to replace the HTTP server and strand the previous bridge's threads.

**`e719fc9` — plan checklist update**

**`3515cac` — the two test guards the commits above refer to**
`StubbedIDeviceApiTest` scans compiled bytecode for calls to the nineteen `IDevice` methods
Android Studio leaves unimplemented — it reads bytecode rather than source because Kotlin's
property syntax hides the call (`device.screenshot` is `getScreenshot()`). `McpSmokeTest` calls
every read-only tool against a real device through a running server; its live checks are opt-in
via `SPOCK_MCP_URL` / `SPOCK_MCP_TOKEN`, but its coverage assertion always runs.

**`8a28765` / `b6cb6fb` — README tool count, and a guard against it drifting again**
The README said 36 against a registry of 42, in two places — one of them inside the
`<!-- Plugin description -->` block that `buildPlugin` extracts into the Marketplace listing, so
the stale number was on the public plugin page. `ReadmeToolCountTest` now fails the build when
the count is wrong *or* when the wording changes such that no count is found, so rewording
cannot silently disable the check. Both failure modes were verified by breaking the README.

**`a9c2963` — probe tables fixed, and the CHANGELOG filled in**
`McpSmokeTest.PROBES` was a map keyed by tool name, so probing one tool two ways silently
dropped the first entry; both tables are lists of pairs now. The `[Unreleased]` section gained
entries for the debug context, file transfer and screen recording tools, which CI reads to
populate the GitHub Release and Marketplace change notes.

## Verification

- `./gradlew test detekt` is green at **each** commit, checked in a separate worktree so a
  bisect does not land on a red intermediate.
- New coverage: `ProjectResolutionTest` (10 cases), `SelectProjectToolTest`, `FileToolsTest`,
  `ScreenRecordToolsTest`.
- No new platform APIs beyond ones already used elsewhere in the plugin, so `sinceBuild=231` is
  unaffected. `verifyPlugin` has not been run locally — CI covers it.

**`4412544` — `docs/MCP.md` brought back in line with the code**
Its "Not yet implemented" list named three features that ship (screen recording, file push/pull,
the activity panel); the safety table named `android_get_ui_hierarchy`, which has never existed,
and omitted `android_uninstall_app` from the destructive row. The table is now generated from
`ToolRegistry`, all six new tools are documented, and every one of the 42 registered tool names
appears in the file.

## Known gaps, called out rather than left to be found

- **No per-tool allow-list.** A developer cannot expose the read-only tools and nothing else;
  the per-call confirmation on destructive tools is the only boundary. Recorded in `docs/MCP.md`.
- **`prompts/list` returns an empty array.** The debugging workflows in `docs/MCP.md` are prose
  an agent cannot call.

title: Fix android_take_screenshot, which never worked inside Android Studio
body:
## The bug

`android_take_screenshot` called `IDevice.getScreenshot()`. Android Studio ships that as a stub which fails with `This method is not used in Android Studio`, so **every call returned that sentence as an error result instead of an image**:

```json
{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"This method is not used in Android Studio"}],"isError":true}
```

It presumably passed against stock ddmlib, where the method is real. The IDE is the one environment the tool actually runs in.

Found while capturing a screenshot through the running MCP server — the tool failed and `adb exec-out screencap -p` had to be used instead.

## The fix

Capture goes through `screencap -p` on the shell, like every other tool in the plugin, so it depends only on what the device provides.

The bytes come back **base64 encoded**. ddmlib's shell channel hands its output to `IShellOutputReceiver` as text and `ShellOutputReceiver` does `String(bytes)` on it, which corrupts a PNG in transit; encoding on the device keeps the payload ASCII for the whole trip. That output is deliberately **not truncated** — half a PNG is not a smaller PNG.

Two failures used to be indistinguishable from a corrupt image, and both now say what happened:

- a command that fails prints diagnostics to the same stream in plain text, so undecodable output is reported **with the device's own words attached**
- output that decodes but has no PNG signature is reported as a likely **`FLAG_SECURE`** screen, rather than returned as a broken image

New `McpShell.runBinary()` carries the transport, so the next tool that needs bytes off a device does not reinvent it.

## Verification

Run in a sandbox IDE (`./gradlew runIde`) against a live emulator — the environment where the stub actually bites:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `android_take_screenshot` | `isError: true`, stub message | valid PNG, 1080×2220, 47,344 bytes, magic `89504e47` |

Two captures taken minutes apart showed different device clocks, confirming a live capture rather than a cached artifact. Regression-checked on the same rebuilt server: 36 tools still registered, `android_list_devices` and `android_get_current_activity` correct, screenshot works with an explicit `deviceSerial`, and a bad serial still yields a clean `isError` naming the connected devices.

`./gradlew test` green (3 new tests, executed and passing), `./gradlew detekt` clean.

## Tests

`TakeScreenshotToolTest` pins the behaviour that broke:

- round-trips a PNG through a **76-column-wrapped** reply, matching how the device really wraps base64
- asserts the command is `screencap -p | base64`, so a future change back to `getScreenshot()` fails here
- surfaces a shell error verbatim
- rejects non-PNG bytes

title: UI fixes, MCP Server panel, and Keymap-native actions
body:
> Split out of #58. That PR was merged before this commit was pushed, so this work needs its own PR. 31 files, +1,682 / −157.

## 1. UI fixes — from the reported screenshot

All four confirmed in code before changing anything:

| Screenshot showed | Actual cause |
|---|---|
| Preset reads `CURRENT_APP` | Both combos had **no renderer** → `toString()` on the enum. A `label` field existed on both enums and was never used |
| Filter row sliced in half | Toolbar + filters + status shared **one `BorderLayout` row**; the taller filter panel was clipped |
| `35 shown of 20000` truncated | Status was in `BorderLayout.EAST`, squeezed by the centre |
| Ragged log columns | Renderer used the list's **proportional** font |

Fixed: human labels; an actions row + a **wrapping** filter row + a status bar of its own; monospace rows so timestamp/PID/level line up.

`WrapLayout` makes controls reflow in a narrow docked tool window — plain `FlowLayout` reports a single row's height, so it gets clipped rather than wrapping. A tool window is often docked at ~300px, so anything that cannot reflow is unusable there.

The Command Center now flags a destructive command **as you type it**, not only in a dialog after Run — a dialog is easy to dismiss on autopilot.

## 2. MCP Server panel

A tool window tab, not a buried setting.

- **Status** — running/stopped, transport, tool count; Start / Stop / Restart / Copy Config / Settings
- **Live activity monitor** — every call with a safety marker (`✓` read-only, `⚡` action, `⚠` destructive), outcome, duration
- **Request details** — arguments, result, client, target device, and for destructive calls whether you **approved or denied** it; copy request/response
- **History** — searchable across tool name/arguments/result, filterable by tool and outcome, **bounded**, size configurable in Settings

### Two places I did not follow the mockup, deliberately

- The mockup says `Transport: stdio`. Ours is **HTTP on loopback** — the panel says that.
- **No `● Cursor / ○ Codex` presence list.** Plain HTTP POST is stateless; there is no connection to be "online" on. The panel names a client only once it sends `clientInfo` at `initialize`, and otherwise says so in words. That is the brief's own "do not fake it" rule.

Also adds `android_uninstall_app`, which the safety mockup listed but did not exist.

## 3. Actions + Keymap

Every major operation is an `AnAction` in one group → Find Action and `Settings → Keymap → Spock ADB`. **No custom shortcut engine.**

**No default shortcuts ship.** A binding free in one keymap is taken in another, and silently claiming a combination the developer already uses is worse than shipping none. A test fails if one creeps in.

Actions are **context-aware and explain themselves**: `update()` runs on `ActionUpdateThread.BGT` and sets a disabled reason ("no Android device connected"), reading a **cached** device list so it never triggers an ADB round trip.

Existing action IDs are unchanged — renaming one would drop any shortcut a user had already assigned.

`Settings → Tools → Spock ADB` shows currently-bound shortcuts read live from `KeymapManager`, with an "Edit in Keymap" button. Keymap remains the single source of truth.

## Bug found while wiring this up

`observeDevices` supported only **one** observer, so the project service subscribing would have silently replaced the tool window's subscription. Now multi-observer.

## Verification

**134 tests**, all green. `test`, `detekt`, `buildPlugin`, `verifyPlugin` pass — all five IDE targets **Compatible**.

title: UI fixes, MCP Server panel, and Keymap-native actions
body:
The tool window is now three tabs — **Devices**, **Logcat**, **Commands** — sharing the device selected in Devices, so there is one answer to "which device is this acting on" across the whole window.

## Cancellation had to come first

Neither feature was possible before. `ShellOutputReceiver` hard-coded `isCancelled()` to `false`, and ddmlib polls that between chunks — so **no long-running command could ever be interrupted**. This was flagged in the audit as the thing blocking progress, cancellation *and* the coroutine migration.

`CancellableShellReceiver` streams output line by line and honours cancellation. That is what makes a live logcat tail and a Cancel button that actually stops a command possible.

## Logcat

Android Studio already has a capable Logcat window, so this one earns its place by being **pre-scoped** rather than being another general-purpose log viewer: it defaults to the open project's application ID and offers presets for the failures developers actually go looking for.

- **Presets:** Current app, Errors only, Crashes, ANRs, Network
- **Filtering by process ID**, not by matching the package name against message text — text matching both misses lines and returns unrelated ones
- Level, tag, plain-text and regex search. An invalid regex **matches nothing and says so**, rather than silently showing the unfiltered log and looking like the filter was ignored
- Crash and ANR highlighting, pause/resume, clear (view + device buffer), copy, export, auto-scroll

Two things worth reviewing:

- Entries arrive on an ADB reader thread far faster than Swing repaints, so they queue and drain on the EDT on a 100 ms timer. Appending per line floods the event queue on a busy device.
- The buffer is a **bounded ring**. A busy device produces thousands of lines a minute; keeping them all grows the heap for a panel that only shows a screenful.

## Command Center

Run any shell command with a real timeout and a working Cancel. History that **de-duplicates and reorders** instead of piling up, favourites that survive clearing history, searchable output, copy command / copy output / clear.

Destructive commands are confirmed before running and catastrophic ones refused outright. `DangerousCommands` is **shared with the MCP `android_run_adb_command` tool**, so a command needing confirmation for an AI agent needs it in the UI too — two lists would drift, and the one that drifted would be the one letting something through.

## Compatibility — a third `NoSuchMethodError` caught

`FileSaverDescriptor(String, String)` reads better and the vararg form is deprecated on 2025.1 — but the two-argument constructor **does not exist before it**:

```
Method LogcatPanel.export() contains an *invokespecial* instruction referencing an
unresolved constructor FileSaverDescriptor.<init>(String, String).
This can lead to NoSuchMethodError exception at runtime.
```

Caught on AI-231, AI-242 and IC-231. The deprecated-but-present overload is used instead: **a deprecation warning on the newest platform beats a crash on the oldest.** Recorded in `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md` as the third instance of this failure mode (after compatibility bridges and an inlined platform helper).

## Docs

README now documents the MCP server, Logcat and the Command Center, and links the docs. The Marketplace description mentions MCP and IntelliJ IDEA support — **MCP shipped in 4.0.0 with no README mention at all**, which was an oversight.

## Verification

**117 tests**, all green (up from 81). `test`, `detekt`, `buildPlugin`, `verifyPlugin` all pass — all five IDE targets **Compatible**.

Tests cover the parts that are pure: the `threadtime` parser (including `F`→ASSERT and logcat banners), filter and preset matching, the bounded buffer, history de-duplication and eviction, and dangerous-command classification.

title: Fix shell injection and add confirmations for destructive actions
body:
> Stacked on #52.

## Shell injection via the device

ADB commands are built by string interpolation and handed to `IDevice.executeShellCommand`, which runs them through the **device's shell**. The two fields the user types into were interpolated inside hand-written quotes:

```kotlin
"input text '$p'"
"am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d \"$p\""
```

A value containing the matching quote character closes it early, and everything after is parsed as shell. So this deep link:

```
a'; rm -rf /sdcard; echo 'b
```

…runs as three commands on the connected device. Pasting a crafted deep link — the exact thing this feature exists for, with URIs from bug reports and test links — was enough.

**Fix:** `ShellQuote.quote` wraps values in single quotes and emits embedded single quotes as `'\''`, so no expansion survives. Applied at **every** interpolation site: the two user-typed fields, plus package names, activity components, permission names and animation scale values.

`ShellQuote.requireValidComponent` is a separate, deliberately loose sanity check that turns malformed device output into a clear message. It is explicitly *not* the security boundary — quoting is — so it permits `$`, which inner-class activity components legitimately contain.

## Confirmations for destructive actions

Uninstall, Clear App Data, Clear App Data & Restart and Revoke All Permissions were **single clicks with no confirmation**, sitting in the same panel as read-only actions like *Current Activity*.

Each now asks first, and the prompt **names the target device** (model + serial) — with several devices attached it was previously not visible which one a click would hit.

## Tests

13 tests covering the quoting rules, including the injection payloads above.

## Verification

`test`, `detekt`, `buildPlugin`, `verifyPlugin` green — all five IDE targets **Compatible**.

title: Fix EDT freezes, threading violations, crashes and leaks
body:
> Stacked on #51 (which is stacked on #50). Review those first.

Ten defects, all reachable through normal use.

## Threading

- **EDT freeze.** `AndroidSdkUtils.getDebugBridge()` blocks while ADB starts, and was called on the EDT twice over — once opening the tool window, once inside *every* menu action. Now resolved lazily on a pooled thread.
- **Swing from a ddmlib thread.** Device connect/disconnect callbacks mutated the combo box model directly. Device lists are now read off the EDT and delivered on it.
- The permission dialog was opened from a pooled thread. Moving that callback to the EDT exposed a second problem: `grantOrRevokeAllPermissions` shared it, so it would have issued one `pm grant` per permission **on the UI thread**. It now runs entirely in the background.

## Crashes

- **`ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`.** The device combo box did `devices[selectedIndex]`; `selectedIndex` is `-1` once the model empties after the last device disconnects. It also ignored the event type, running the handler twice per selection.
- **Tool window would not open.** A persisted setting naming a renamed/removed action made `SpockAction.valueOf` throw *from the constructor*. Unknown entries are now ignored.
- **Permanent hang.** `ProcessDeathCommand` passed timeout `0` to `executeShellCommand` — in ddmlib that means *wait forever*, so an unresponsive device pinned a pooled thread for the life of the IDE.

## Leaks and lifetime

- `project.messageBus.connect()` had no parent `Disposable`; the listener was never released.
- Every menu action constructed its **own** `AdbControllerImp`, each registering another global ADB device-change listener, then disposed it immediately after kicking off async work — cancelling that work before it ran. A single project-scoped `SpockAdbService` now owns the controller. This is also the reusable ADB service layer the later work builds on.

## Error handling

- Exceptions were swallowed and shown as `e.message ?: "not found"` — a null-message exception surfaced to the user as the words *"not found"*, with no stack trace recorded anywhere. Failures now go to `idea.log` too.
- `connectDeviceOverIp` reported `"connected to $ip"` while its command was an empty stub that did nothing. It now fails honestly.

## Compatibility regression caught by the verifier

Introducing the service surfaced a second instance of the trap from #51 — this time via **inlining**:

```
Method SpockAdbService.Companion.getInstance(Project) contains an *invokestatic*
instruction referencing an unresolved method ServicesKt.serviceNotFoundError(...).
This can lead to NoSuchMethodError exception at runtime.
```

`project.service<T>()` is `inline`, so it copies a call to an API that doesn't exist before 2023.3 into our bytecode. Both services now use the non-inline `getService`. Documented in `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md`.

## Verification

`test`, `detekt`, `buildPlugin`, `verifyPlugin` all green — all five IDE targets **Compatible**. New tests for `ShellOutputReceiver` chunking/newline handling and the device state enums.

title: Support IntelliJ IDEA and fix NoSuchMethodError on older Android Studio
body:
> Stacked on #50. Review that first; this PR's diff is only the compatibility work.

Two compatibility claims in the descriptor were wrong. Both are now **verified by Plugin Verifier** rather than assumed.

## 1. The plugin was needlessly Android Studio only

This is the cause of the Marketplace showing 3.0.0 as **"Non compatible"** with IntelliJ IDEA:

```xml
<depends>com.intellij.modules.androidstudio</depends>
```

It is a hard gate — IDEA refuses to install the plugin regardless of whether the code would run. And it bought nothing. Every Android API used here (ddmlib, `AndroidFacet`, `AndroidModel`, `AndroidSdkUtils`, the execution tooling) ships inside `plugins/android/lib/*.jar` — the `org.jetbrains.android` plugin the descriptor **already** depends on — not the Android Studio platform.

Removed it, and added the two dependencies that were genuinely missing: `com.intellij.modules.platform`, and `com.intellij.modules.java` for the Java PSI used to navigate to sources. The verifier reported the undeclared Java usage as a compatibility problem on *every* target.

## 2. `sinceBuild=231` did not actually work on 231

`sinceBuild` was `231` while compiling against platform `251`. The verifier found two `NoSuchMethodError` risks:

```
Method spock.AdbDrawerViewer.manage(...) contains an *invokespecial* instruction
referencing an unresolved method ToolWindowFactory.manage(...).
This can lead to NoSuchMethodError exception at runtime.

Method spock.AdbDrawerViewer.isApplicableAsync(...) ... unresolved ...
```

`ToolWindowFactory` is a Kotlin interface with default methods, and Kotlin emits *compatibility bridge* overrides that `invokespecial` into every default method the interface had **at compile time**.

`AdbDrawerViewer` is the tool window factory — **the plugin's entry point** — so this was not a corner case: the tool window would fail to open on Android Studio 2023.1 through 2024.x. Fixed with one flag, `-Xjvm-default=all`.

## Verification

Restored `verifyPlugin` and added a CI job. All five targets now report **Compatible**:

| IDE | Version | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Android Studio | 2023.1.1.28 | 3 problems (2× NoSuchMethodError) | ✅ Compatible |
| Android Studio | 2024.2.1.12 | — | ✅ Compatible |
| Android Studio | 2025.1.1.14 | 1 problem | ✅ Compatible |
| IntelliJ IDEA | 2023.1.5 | blocked by descriptor | ✅ Compatible |
| IntelliJ IDEA | 2025.1 | blocked by descriptor | ✅ Compatible |

`failureLevel` includes `COMPATIBILITY_PROBLEMS`, so regressions break the build.

`Restart App With Debugger` needs the Android Studio execution stack, absent in IDEA 2023.1. Rather than gate the whole plugin on one action, `DebuggerSupport` feature-detects the class **before** `Debugger` is loaded; the action is hidden where unavailable instead of failing with `NoClassDefFoundError`. The corresponding verifier finding is listed in `verifier-ignored-problems.txt` with its justification.

## Also fixed

- **Wrong module in multi-module projects.** Application ID resolution used an arbitrary `AndroidFacet`, so it could resolve a library module or none at all. Now prefers application modules and reads through the stable `AndroidModel` interface instead of the Gradle-specific `GradleAndroidModel`.
- **Misleading error.** An unresolvable application ID was passed through `.toString()`, producing the literal string `"null"` and the error `Application null not installed`.
- Dropped the deprecated `ToolWindowManagerListener.stateChanged()` override and `AndroidVersion.getApiLevel()` call.

`docs/COMPATIBILITY.md` records the supported range, the matrix, and how to change it safely.

title: Fix broken test source set, add parser tests and static analysis
body:
## Why

The test source set has **never compiled**. JUnit was never declared on the test classpath, and CI only ran `buildPlugin`, so `./gradlew test` failing was invisible:

```
e: GetFragmentsCommandTest.kt:3:12 Unresolved reference 'junit'.
> Execution failed for task ':compileTestKotlin'.
```

`./gradlew detekt` is documented in the developer guide, but the detekt plugin was never applied either — the task does not exist.

## What changed

**Build**
- JUnit 5 on the test classpath, `useJUnitPlatform()`
- detekt applied, with a baseline capturing the existing **178** findings so new code cannot add to the debt while the existing debt is paid down separately
- CI runs `test` and `detekt` on every push and PR, and uploads the reports

**Testability**
- ADB output parsing extracted from the command classes into pure functions under `spock.adb.parser`. The commands keep their behaviour and just delegate, but the parsing rules can now be exercised without a connected device.
- **21 tests** covering the activity, back stack, application back stack and fragment `dumpsys` formats — including Android 13's `topResumedActivity` and the Navigation-component fragment layout.

## Bugs found while adding coverage

- **API level detection was wrong.** `getApiVersion()` read `ro.build.version.release`, the *marketing* version string. Values like `"8.1.0"` fail `toIntOrNull()` and were treated as unknown, which routed modern devices down the **pre-Honeycomb** back stack parser. Replaced with `apiLevel()`, reading `ro.build.version.sdk`.
- **Crash.** `GetApplicationBackStackCommand` called `tasks.last()` without checking the list was non-empty, throwing `NoSuchElementException` when a fragment line arrived before any activity line. Covered by a regression test.

## Verification

`./gradlew test detekt buildPlugin` — all green, 21 tests passing.

body:
#b44a42 introduced ToolWindowManagerListener to update the developer options settings whenever the plugin becomes visible (this tried to keep the plugin updated since we don't have a callback for when that settings change).
Although the current stable Android Studio version is based on idea version 193, the ToolWindowManagerListener lacks the "toolWindowShown" method (available in Android Studio version 4.2).

This commit uses a deprecated method to achieve the same result. When AS is updated, the not deprecated method will be used.

title: fix(android): preserve background chat alerts and unread state
body: ## Summary Background chat alerts could stay disabled after notification permission was granted, and replies from conversations left running had no completion alert. Alerts now retain the owning connection, profile, and conversation. Off-screen completed replies also keep unread markers, and chat progress stays above the composer. ## Changes - Refresh permission-based alert defaults on resume, observe alert settings outside UI recomposition, and initialize topology before eager profile collectors can rebuild clients. - Preserve notification ownership across session/profile switches, reject failed/interrupted detached completion, and retain background protection through local notification preparation. - Restore the exact conversation on notification taps, preserve sibling alerts, and keep an already-running newer turn intact. - Add bounded unread receipts, conversation/profile badges, official profile names and cached avatars, and generic public notification copy. - Add focused CI coverage, translated labels, documentation, and synthetic rendered evidence. ## Verification - Sideload debug assembly passed. Local focused JVM/rendered verification passed 185 unique tests, including notification/permission/ownership, unread persistence, avatar isolation, scroll anchoring, and profile switching. - `python -W error::ResourceWarning -m unittest discover -s test-fixtures/vanilla-gateway/tests` — 37 passed. - `python -m unittest scripts.tests.android_prepush_test` — 4 passed. - `python scripts/check-android-locales.py` — 12 catalogs passed; collection API and Play capability checks passed. - `scripts/check-gateway-scenario-conformance.py` passed for `clarify_batch.json` and `notification_terminal_outcomes.json` against clean vanilla upstream `bed0d535556b5b0a2bdd6fd3a74162ad5f860ca1`. - Final-head [required checks](https://github.com/Codename-11/hermes-relay/actions/runs/37065915769) passed for `bdfc41e031ff63f31621b6794c15832e9182218d`: Android lint, both debug builds, focused tests, and the upstream route contract. - `:app:standardPhoneApi36SideloadDebugAndroidTest -Pandroid.testInstrumentationRunnerArguments.class=com.hermesandroid.relay.viewmodel.GatewayForegroundRecoveryInstrumentedTest` — 8 passed on Standard Phone API 36, with no failures or skips. - The eager-constructor regression and all four Chat progress renders passed locally after the initialization-order correction. - An earlier test APK was installed and version-checked on Android API 36. The final constructor correction has not been installed on that phone; functional physical-device verification remains outstanding. ## Screenshots Production Compose surfaces with synthetic data, rendered in Robolectric API 34: Chat at 360 × 800 dp; drawer/profile shelf at 320 × 700 dp and 1.3 font scale. title: fix(android): disclose and preserve Standard Voice fallback
body:
## Summary

Standard Voice in #639 reached legacy TTS after the configured streaming provider rejected access. Android only logged that failure, and chunks already queued could still retry streaming while a short buffered tail could be discarded. Show one warning, preserve pending speech in order, and expose useful playback timing.

title: fix(android): restore upstream Gateway interactive requests

## Summary

Restores native Clarify, approval, sudo and secret cards against current unmodified Hermes. Android previously dropped the JSON-RPC request frames that replaced the notification-era ask protocol. Refs #631.

## Changes

- Advertise `server_requests` after each connection becomes ready; preserve typed request IDs and ordinary RPC correlation.
- Answer native requests on their owning socket. Restore open requests and accepted Clarify locks, fence stale snapshots and cancellations, and reconcile answers from another client through the read-only replay RPC.
- Keep existing approval scope, supervised mode and masked secret/sudo controls. Add Clarify Skip and let upstream own native ask deadlines.
- Keep legacy fixtures separate; add current protocol fixtures, upstream source/runtime conformance, wire tests and API 36 coverage.

| Methods | Android behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `clarify` | Single-answer response or exact per-question `clarify.lock`; partial progress and skip |
| `approval` | Advertised, permitted choices via `{choice}` |
| `sudo`, `secret` | Existing masked cards via `{value}`; empty declines/skips |
| `vault.unlock_prompt`, `vault.save_login`, `vault.code` | Explicit `-32601` |
| `preview.read`, `preview.act`, `terminal.read`, `window.read`, `tour`, `display.install.sudo` | Explicit `-32601`; Android has no matching upstream renderer |

title: fix(android): Secure Link pin path for clients, route UI, TrustManager-only pin

## Summary

## Changes

- Route Secure Link HTTP probes through a request-URL-aware client factory so pin enforcement matches the actual HTTPS URL, not only the candidate host.

- Present Hermes Secure Link (HTTPS) dashboard/Gateway addresses from the proxy candidate instead of plain :9119 LAN fallback when the dashboard surface is present.
- Pin Secure Link solely via the custom X509TrustManager (host+port authority guard). Do not also attach OkHttp CertificatePinner for the same SPKI — some OEM stacks surface Certificate pinning failure / TLS failed while the leaf already matched.

## Summary

Secure Link (`plugin_proxy` on :9443) can pair and serve HTTPS dashboard pages while Gateway chat and dashboard login still fail on the proxy path. This change makes the Secure Link reverse proxy preserve WebSocket auth tickets, avoid nested permessage-deflate failures after `gateway.ready`, keep dashboard auth under `/dashboard`, and advertise a health payload that matches the Android route probe contract.

No linked issue yet; observed on current plugin 1.11.x with Android 1.17.x Secure Link pairs.

title: Fix text-selection handle drag/visuals and onboarding page 1 vibrancy
body:
## Summary
- **Selection handles couldn't be dragged in any direction.** Root cause: the drag gesture's `pointerInput` was keyed on `selectedOcrRanges`, which the gesture itself mutates on every move. The instant a drag moved past touch slop, Compose saw the key change and cancelled + restarted the gesture coroutine mid-drag — the restarted `awaitEachGesture` then waited on a fresh touch-down that never came since the same finger was still pressed. Fixed by reading the live selection via `rememberUpdatedState` instead of keying on it.
- **Handle shape redesigned to match real Android/Chrome/Google Docs handles**: a circle with one sharp corner notched out exactly at the anchor point, asymmetric per side (bulges lean into the selection), replacing a symmetric "balloon on a flat neck" shape. Verified geometrically (numeric assertions + rendered PNG previews of the actual curves) before writing any Kotlin.
- **Highlight band** between the handles is now a fully-rounded capsule instead of a flat, barely-rounded rectangle, so it reads as one selection with the handles instead of two balloons on a rod.
- **Onboarding page 1**: the fanned stack of format-sheets behind the assembled book was permanently washed out (0.20/0.34 fill alpha once landed) — raised to 0.75 card / full-opacity lines, with a deliberate contrast gap kept between the two.

## Test plan
- [ ] Select text and drag each handle in all four directions repeatedly — should never stall.
- [ ] Pinch-zoom with one finger already selecting text — second finger should cleanly cancel the selection.
- [ ] Compare the new handle/highlight look against stock Android text selection (Chrome, Google Docs) for proportion.
- [ ] Step through onboarding page 1 — the sheets fanned behind the book should read as vivid, distinct colors, not pale/grey.

title: Fix recents open failures, viewer flicker/buffering, add fast-scroll UX
body:
## Summary
- **Recents:** files opened via "Open with ClearPDF" from another app (WhatsApp, Gmail, ...) only carry a temporary read grant; once revoked, reopening from Recents failed with "Failed to open PDF" / "Couldn't read this spreadsheet." `LocalDocumentMirror` now saves a durable local copy the first time the file is readable and transparently falls back to it later.
- **PDF/PPT viewer flicker & "buffering":** bitmap cache eviction ran on every scroll tick *and* on every render completion using an undebounced current-page value, recycling pages still transiting the viewport mid-scroll. Eviction is now one debounced sweep, cache radius increased, and pages ahead of/behind the scroll direction are prefetched proactively.
- **PPT last-page flicker:** the empty-page placeholder assumed A4 portrait, collapsing ~2.5x on a landscape (converted .pptx) page and looping the last page in/out of the viewport.
- **xlsx viewer:** dates now render correctly (was showing raw serials — `xl/styles.xml` wasn't read), hidden columns/rows are now honored like Excel, row-number gutter added, stacking fast-flick fling, and a WPS-style row scrubber with a compact liquid-glass "N/Total" badge. Per-cell `border()`+ripple replaced with one `drawBehind()` pass per row (this is what made the fling expose a stall on long sheets).
- **PPTX rendering:** real slide renderer (`PptxRenderer`/`OoxmlNode`) — true slide size, shape geometry inherited from layout/master, theme colors, pictures, tables — replacing a converter that flattened every run of text into a portrait text dump.
- **DOCX rendering:** `DocxWebRenderer` lays the document out with vendored `docx-preview` + `JSZip` (Apache-2.0/MIT, ~48KB total) in an offscreen WebView, rasterized via `PrintDocumentAdapter` with a public-API slice-render fallback; the original hand-written reflow stays as a last resort. Fully offline — no `INTERNET` permission declared.
- **Onboarding:** brightened page 1's book content lines, added a progress-dot row + icon pop to page 4, replaced page 6's generic checkmark-in-a-circle with the same six-format color ring from page 1, and fixed `GlassSearchHeader`'s bounce being springy on open but rigid on close.
- **Localization:** added Spanish (`es`) — full translation, wired into both language pickers, `LocaleHelper`, and the locale allowlist.

## Test plan
- [x] Open a PDF/xlsx via "Open with ClearPDF" from another app, wait, reopen from Recents — should still open.
- [x] Scroll a multi-page PDF and a converted .pptx quickly in both directions — no black flash / re-render stutter.
- [x] Open the xlsx sample with a date column and a hidden column — dates render, hidden column stays hidden.
- [x] Fast-flick the xlsx grid twice quickly in the same direction — scroll distance should stack.
- [x] Drag the new row-scrubber rail on a 500+ row sheet — small circular badge, live scroll.
- [x] Open a .docx and a .pptx — check layout fidelity against the old converter.
- [x] Switch language to Spanish in Settings and in first-run Onboarding.
- [x] Step through onboarding pages 1, 4, 6 for the visual changes; confirm page 5 is untouched.

title: ClearPDF v1.2.0 — text selection, decrypt animation, onboarding polish, crash fix
body:
## ClearPDF v1.2.0

First release after [`v1.1.0-liquid-glass`](https://github.com/Chethan616/ClearPDF/releases/tag/v1.1.0-liquid-glass). Bumps to **versionName 1.2.0 / versionCode 3**.

### ✍️ Text selection — premium rework
- **Drag to select multiple words.** In *Select Text* mode the page no longer scrolls, so a drag now sweeps a real reading-order selection (word → sentence → paragraph) live under your finger, instead of one word per tap. Tap = word, double-tap = line, long-press = paragraph still work.
- **Delete a highlight.** Tapping a word that's already highlighted now shows a **Delete** action in the pill (previously only Copy/Highlight appeared); *Highlight* becomes *Recolor* in that state.

### 🐞 Crash fix — large / encrypted PDFs
- Fixed the app crashing while scrolling large or password-protected PDFs. A big page could throw `OutOfMemoryError` (an `Error`, not an `Exception`) that the renderer's catch let escape; it now catches `Throwable`, recycles partial bitmaps, and guards `openPage`. Text extraction is also serialized behind a `Mutex` so eager loading + fast scrolling can't stack several full-document parses in RAM.

### 🎬 Opening a document
- Removed the loading indicator entirely — opening a PDF is a clean dark fill that dissolves to the first page (no picker flash, no spinner).
- Decrypting a password PDF plays a **blue liquid-glass scan** animation.

### 🎨 Onboarding & Home polish
- **Page 1 (book):** shadow disabled for that page (it used to snap in when the book finished), and the book's lines now take the colours of the sheets that formed it, in sequence.
- **Page 4:** replaced the generic file-kind list with one liquid-glass document card that morphs through PDF → Word → Excel → PPT → Image.
- **Home:** container shadows now fade in *with* their panels instead of snapping in at the end of the entrance.
- **Editor toolbar:** the tool pills bounce with the share capsule's spring when the share button opens.

### 🌍 Community-requested (context for the release)
These drove the release; see the release notes for the user-facing summary: open Office docs, custom background option, PDF e-signing, Portuguese (Brazil).

title: Fix Dokka publish failure on Android library 'release' source set
body:
## Summary
- The `snapshot` workflow's `publishAllPublicationsToMavenCentralRepository` task has been failing on every push to `main` because `:signature-core:dokkaGeneratePublicationHtml` errors with: `Pre-generation validity check failed: Source sets 'androidJvm' and 'release' have the common source roots…`. Dokka 2.x requires every Kotlin file to belong to exactly one source set, but the Android library + per-variant publishing combination registers both `androidJvm` (Dokka's default) and `release` (the variant) with the same `src/main/java` files. Tracked upstream at [Kotlin/dokka#3701](https://github.com/Kotlin/dokka/issues/3701).
- Fix: in each publishable module (`signature-core`, `signature-pad`, `signature-view`), suppress the duplicate `release` Dokka source set so generation runs from `androidJvm` only. The two source sets had identical source roots, so the rendered docs are unchanged.
- This wasn't caught by PR CI because `pr.yml` only runs `./gradlew check`, which doesn't invoke the Dokka publish task. Snapshot publishes have been silently failing for months.

## Test plan
