title: CI: fix access-token scope for get-next-version-code.sh
body:
## Summary
- #685's `access_token_scopes` fix on the `google-github-actions/auth` step was a no-op. Confirmed against the action's own docs: `access_token_scopes` only affects the action's `access_token` *output*, which only exists when `token_format: access_token` is set. Without it, `get-next-version-code.sh`'s `gcloud auth print-access-token` reads the ADC credentials file directly and mints its own token, ignoring that setting entirely — and `gcloud auth print-access-token` has no `--scopes` flag to override it (confirmed against the gcloud CLI reference), so the token stayed scoped to the generic `cloud-platform` default, which the Android Publisher API's `edits.insert` rejects.
- Fix: set `token_format: access_token` on the auth step so it actually produces a scoped `access_token` output, and pass that into `get-next-version-code.sh` via `$ACCESS_TOKEN` instead of shelling out to `gcloud`.
- Also made the script print the actual Play API error response body when edit creation fails, instead of a generic message — the last two real failures both required pulling raw workflow logs to diagnose; this puts the actual cause directly in the log next time.

## Summary

title: Fix stale-voice detection to check download status, not just name/locale
body:
Part of #613 — closes #642.

> [!NOTE]
> **Based on `feature/voice-selection`**, same as #631/#633 — all sub-issue PRs for this feature target it until the whole thing is ready to ship.

## What

- `VocableTextToSpeech.applySelectedVoice()`'s explicit-match check only verified a selected voice's name, locale, and network-required flag — it never checked whether the voice's data was actually downloaded. Android's TTS engine keeps a voice listed in `getVoices()` even after its data is uninstalled (flagged via `KEY_FEATURE_NOT_INSTALLED`, not removed from the list), so a previously-picked voice that later got uninstalled — the literal scenario #619 describes — would still "match" by name and keep being treated as a valid explicit selection.
- Added `isVoiceDownloaded()` (a `Voice` overload plus a `features: Set<String>?` overload, the latter for unit-testability without needing a real `Voice` instance)
- `applySelectedVoice()`'s `availableVoiceNames` now requires both `isVoiceSupportedForLocale()` and `isVoiceDownloaded()` — an uninstalled voice no longer counts as available, so `resolveVoiceSelection()` correctly returns `STALE_FALLBACK_TO_LIVE_DEFAULT` for it instead of `EXPLICIT`
- `getAvailableVoices()` refactored to reuse the same helper instead of inlining the same check twice
- 3 new unit tests on the pure `isVoiceDownloaded(features)` overload
- `Documentation/work-log/642-stale-voice-download-check.md` added per the work-log standard

## Why it's safe

- 46 unit tests, 0 failures (8 in `VocableTextToSpeechTest`, up from 5)
- `./gradlew clean assembleDebug assembleDebugAndroidTest testDebug` succeeds
- **Verified via real on-device reproduction** on a Google Play emulator image (this repo's testing has otherwise been limited by emulators lacking real TTS engines — this is the first time this specific path was actually exercised, not just reasoned about in code):
  1. Selected a downloaded voice (`en-IN-language`) in Vocable's picker — confirmed via log: `applied voice: en-IN-language`
  2. Uninstalled that voice's data through the OS's own TTS voice manager (Settings → Accessibility → Text-to-speech → Install voice data → English (India) → delete)

title: #611: Fix Numbers preset category grid shape and keypad ordering
body:
## Summary

The "123" (Numbers) category rendered as a 6×3 / 3×5 grid with a blank row instead of the 3×4 keypad the designs call for. Fixing the grid shape exposed two further problems behind it: the item order wasn't a keypad either, and the mechanism that seeds preset phrases could never deliver a correction to anyone who had already opened the app.

### Grid shape

- `phraseRows` in `PresetsScreen.kt` had no `USER_KEYPAD` override (unlike `phraseColumns`), so it always fell back to the generic per-breakpoint row count. Added `phrases_rows_one_liner_phrases` to every breakpoint `integers.xml` and branched `phraseRows` on `USER_KEYPAD.id` the same way `phraseColumns` already does.
- Fixed `phrases_columns_one_liner_phrases` in `values-sw600dp-land/integers.xml` (was `6`, needs `3` for the 3×4 target).
- Handset values are unchanged — the new resource values match the generic ones there.
- Added tablet-width `@Preview` specs to `PresetsScreenPreview2` and corrected that preview's phrase list, which had duplicate ids and stale labels.

### Item order

`R.array.category_123` was declared `0 1 2 … 9 Yes No`. The grid fills row-major, so that renders `0 1 2 / 3 4 5 / …`, not a phone keypad. Reordered to `1 … 9 0 No Yes`, which renders `1 2 3 / 4 5 6 / 7 8 9 / 0 No Yes` at the 3-column breakpoints and `1 2 3 4 5 6 / 7 8 9 0 No Yes` at the 6-column ones — both matching the approved designs (Figma 64:2146 / 64:2175).

### Making the arrays authoritative

Reordering an array on its own changes nothing for an existing install, because `sort_order` is only written when a phrase is first seeded:

- `populateDatabase()` was gated behind a `firstTime` shared pref, so it never ran again after the first launch. Removed the gate — seeding is idempotent (`getAllPresetPhrases()` includes soft-deleted rows, so a user-deleted preset is not resurrected), and this is also what reconciles stored phrases against the arrays. A phrase *added* to an array in a past release never reached existing users either; that's fixed by the same change.
- `ensurePopulated()` now resyncs `sort_order` from the array index for rows that already exist.
- Editing a preset soft-deletes its `PresetPhrase` row and stores a "shadow" `Phrase` under the same id, so shadows carry their own `sort_order` and are resynced independently of the preset row — otherwise an install that had already resynced its preset rows would strand its shadows at the pre-reorder index.
- `getPhrasesForCategoryFlow` now sorts by `sortOrder`. Neither DAO query has an `ORDER BY`; `PresetsViewModel` sorted on its way to the grid but `EditCategoryPhrasesState` did not, so after a resync the Presets grid and the Edit Phrases list disagreed on order.

Known limitation, documented in `arrays.xml`: the resync handles additions and reorders, not removals or moves between arrays, since it never deletes or re-parents an existing row.

### Tests

- `PhraseGridResourceInvariantTest` — asserts `columns × rows == max_phrases` for both grids at every breakpoint, which is the invariant #611 violated.
- `KeypadPhraseOrderTest` — pins the array declaration order and asserts the full rendered row matrix against the signed-off layouts, so a column count with no approved layout fails loudly.
- Both discover breakpoint dirs from disk rather than a hardcoded list, so a new `values-*` dir is covered automatically.
- `RoomPresetPhrasesRepositoryTest` — covers reseeding, the `sort_order` resync, shadow resync, and that soft-deleted presets stay deleted across launches.

Closes #611.

## Test plan

- [x] `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest` — 40 tests, all passing
- [x] `./gradlew :app:compileDebugAndroidTestKotlin` compiles
- [x] Tablet portrait/landscape Compose previews render 3×4 with no blank row
- [ ] `./gradlew connectedDebugAndroidTest` on a device/emulator (not run locally — no AVD available)
- [ ] Tablet AVD (`sw600dp`+), portrait + landscape: "123" renders the 3×4 keypad
- [ ] Handset portrait/landscape: "123" renders 3×4 / 6×2, other categories unchanged
- [ ] **Upgrade path** — install a pre-change build, open it, then install this build: "123" shows keypad order in both the Presets grid and Settings → Edit Categories → 123
- [ ] Edit a "123" phrase (creating a shadow), then relaunch: the edited phrase keeps its keypad position
- [ ] Delete a preset phrase, then relaunch: it stays deleted

title: Fix: respect useExactScheduling for repeating alarms on Android
body:
scheduleRepeatingAlarm() previously always used AlarmManager.setRepeating(), which is inexact on API 19+ (equivalent to setInexactRepeating). This ignored the useExactScheduling flag, causing repeating alarms to fire with significant delays (up to 40+ minutes due to Doze mode batching).

When useExactScheduling is true and the app has SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM permission, repeating alarms now use one-shot exact chaining: the first occurrence is scheduled with setExactAndAllowWhileIdle(), and the BroadcastReceiver chains the next occurrence after each alarm fires.

If the permission is revoked between firings, it gracefully falls back to setAndAllowWhileIdle().

title: Use deep link URI hashCode as requestCode in PendingIntent creation - Fixes #24
body:
Use the `deepLinkUri`'s `hashCode` as the `PendingIntent`'s request code. This ensures that whenever a `deepLinkUri` is present, then the `PendingIntent` is unique to that deeplink, so it doesn't overwrite other notification's intents, and if no deeplink if provided, then it will only be opening the app as usual anyway so it's ok to use `0` as the request code.

This fixes https://github.com/Tweener/alarmee/issues/24

title: fix(android): accept wrapped LocalContext in the gallery picker
body:
The Android gallery renderer bails out whenever `LocalContext.current` isn't literally a `ComponentActivity`:

```kotlin
val activity = context
if (activity !is ComponentActivity) {
    onError(Exception(invalidContextMsg))
    return
}
```

In practice `LocalContext` is often a `ContextWrapper` around the activity rather than the activity itself: apps doing per-app language provide a `ContextThemeWrapper`, Hilt wraps fragment contexts, dialog windows provide their own context. In all of those the picker would work fine but never gets to run; `launchGallery()` immediately reports `invalid_context_error`. Hit this in production in a per-app-language app, where the workaround is re-providing the unwrapped activity as `LocalContext` just around the picker.

The activity isn't actually needed here: `activity` is never used after the check, `GalleryPickerConfig` takes the plain `context`, and launching goes through `rememberLauncherForActivityResult`, which resolves the registry via `LocalActivityResultRegistryOwner` regardless of what `LocalContext` is. The check is a leftover from the old public API that took a caller-supplied `context: Any?` and from the CameraX capture flow, both since removed. The camera renderer already has no equivalent gate.

This PR changes the guard to check `LocalActivityResultRegistryOwner.current` instead, which is what `rememberLauncherForActivityResult` itself requires internally (`checkNotNull(LocalActivityResultRegistryOwner.current)`). Wrapped contexts pass, and a host that genuinely can't launch still gets the localized `onError` instead of a crash.

detekt, jvmTest, testDebugUnitTest and koverVerify pass. No new tests: `ui.*` is excluded in the kover config and the launch/error paths are covered by `GalleryPickerStateLaunchTest`.

title: fix(android): guard camera launch when no camera app is present
body:
## Description

On Android, `launchCamera()` fired `MediaStore.ACTION_IMAGE_CAPTURE` unguarded. On devices with no camera app (enterprise/kiosk builds, or the stock camera disabled), the unresolvable intent threw `ActivityNotFoundException` inside the library's own `LaunchedEffect` — crashing the consuming app with no way for callers to catch it. Regression from 1.1.0, when the in-app CameraX preview was replaced by the system camera intent.

This PR guards the camera and gallery launch paths and turns the crash into a reportable outcome:

- A failed launch now reports `onError` then `onDismiss` with a localized message (`camera_unavailable_error` / `gallery_unavailable_error`, all 12 languages), leaving `result` as `ImagePickerResult.Error` — matching the iOS `CameraPresenter` behavior.
- A dismissal that follows an error no longer overwrites the error, so "no camera app" stays distinguishable from "user cancelled". iOS benefits too: an unavailable camera now surfaces as `Error` instead of `Dismissed`.
- Terminal outcomes settle internal state *before* invoking caller-supplied `onError`/`onDismiss` callbacks, so a custom callback can no longer wedge the picker with `result` stuck on `Loading`.

title: Fix JS target ClassCastException on photo capture
body:
## Summary
Fixes #143. On the `js` (non-wasm) target, `PlatformCameraRenderer` crashed with a `ClassCastException` on every photo capture (camera and file-picker paths).

Root cause: the dynamic JS result object stored `fileSize`/`width`/`height` via `.toDouble()`, but the consumer read them back with `result.fileSize as Long` / `as Int`. On Kotlin/JS, `Long` is a boxed class instance rather than a native JS number, so a plain `Double` is never `instanceof Long` and the cast always throws.

## Fix
Write the native `Long`/`Int` values at the point the dynamic object is populated (`blob.size.toLong()`, `canvas.width`, `file.size.toLong()`, etc.) instead of masquerading them as `Double`, matching how `wasmJsMain`'s `PlatformCameraRenderer.wasmJs.kt` already assigns real Kotlin types. Consumer-side casts (`as Long`, `as Int`) are unchanged.

## Test plan
- [x] `./gradlew :imagepickerkmp-photo:compileKotlinJs` passes
- [x] No remaining `.toDouble()` call sites in the touched file

title: fix(ios): optimize gallery picker speed/memory; fix(android): absolut…
body:
…ePath crash

Resolves #135 (iOS gallery slow + memory spike) and #136 (Android absolutePath crash with cropped images).

iOS performance & memory (#135):
- Replace full-resolution UIImage decode + UIGraphics redraw with ImageIO hardware-accelerated downsampling (CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex), decoding directly at target size.
- Process images straight from the file URL (CGImageSourceCreateWithURL), reading only the bytes needed instead of loading the whole file into NSData.
- Add bounded parallelism (3 concurrent) in ImageProcessingQueue to cap peak memory while keeping multi-image selection fast.
- Use lightweight PHPickerConfiguration() instead of PHPhotoLibrary.sharedPhotoLibrary() to avoid the cold-start delay; EXIF is now read directly from the file via CGImageSource.
- Fix DismissalMonitor false-positive dismissal during the presentation animation that released the delegate and froze/cancelled the picker.

Android crash (#136):
- PhotoResult.absolutePath now handles raw absolute file paths (e.g. cropped images saved to cacheDir), not just content:// and file:// URIs, fixing the FileNotFoundException thrown for cropped results.

Cleanup:
- Remove dead NSData-based processing path (processImageFromData, downsampleImage, processViaUIImage) and unused imports.
- Replace unsafe NSURL→CFURLRef cast with CFURLCreateWithFileSystemPath.

title: Fix `createFallbackResult` to persist image to cache file instead of returning content:// URI
body:
## Description

Update `createFallbackResult` to ensure the image is persisted to the cache with a `file://` URI, rather than returning a `content:// `URI.

When both `compression: null` and `includeExif: false` are provided, the code previously fell back to `createFallbackResult`, which returned the original `content://` URI directly. If the user stored this URI in a database, they would later be unable to read the file because `content://` URIs from the media picker are temporary and not persistent across app sessions.

**Old behavior:**
- Returns `content://media/picker_get_content/...` URI
- File cannot be accessed after being stored in local database
- Leads to "File not found" errors when retrieving saved paths

**New behavior:**
- Creates a permanent cached file in app's internal storage
- Returns `file://` URI that persists and remains readable
- Falls back to original URI only if temp file creation fails

**Code change:**
```kotlin
// Before
private fun createFallbackResult(
    uri: Uri,
    originalBytes: ByteArray,
    fileName: String?,
    mimeType: String?,
    exifData: ExifData?
): GalleryPhotoResult

// After
private fun createFallbackResult(
    context: Context,
    uri: Uri,
    originalBytes: ByteArray,
    fileName: String?,
    mimeType: String?,
    exifData: ExifData?
): GalleryPhotoResult
```

Fixes issue where stored image paths become invalid when using default settings (no compression, no EXIF).

title: fix: resolve FileProvider manifest merge conflict
body:
## Description

Rename library's `FileProvider` to `ImagePickerFileProvider` to avoid manifest merge conflict with host app's `androidx.core.content.FileProvider` declaration.

When a host app declares its own `FileProvider`, the manifest merger fails because both use `androidx.core.content.FileProvider` as the component name — Android uses `android:name` as the merge key, causing attribute conflicts on `authorities` and `resource`.

**Error:**
```
Attribute provider#androidx.core.content.FileProvider@authorities value=(com.snsop.grm.provider)
is also present at [io.github.ismoy:imagepickerkmp-android:1.0.35] value=(com.snsop.grm.fileprovider)

Attribute meta-data#android.support.FILE_PROVIDER_PATHS@resource value=(@xml/app_provider_paths)
is also present at [io.github.ismoy:imagepickerkmp-android:1.0.35] value=(@xml/file_paths)
```

**Fix — added internal subclass:**
```kotlin
// data/managers/ImagePickerFileProvider.kt
internal class ImagePickerFileProvider : FileProvider()
```

**Updated `AndroidManifest.xml`:**
```xml
<provider
    android:name=".data.managers.ImagePickerFileProvider"
    android:authorities="${applicationId}.fileprovider"
    android:exported="false"
    android:grantUriPermissions="true">
    <meta-data
        android:name="android.support.FILE_PROVIDER_PATHS"
        android:resource="@xml/file_paths" />
</provider>
```

This gives the library a unique component name so both providers coexist without requiring host apps to add `tools:replace` workarounds.

Fixes #
Fix manifest merge conflict by introducing a dedicated ImagePickerFileProvider.
This avoids clashes with host apps declaring their own FileProvider, enabling zero-config integration.

fix: sign in through the browser so passkeys work
body:
Fixes #183.

## Problem

Choosing "Login with Passkey" on the sign-in page failed immediately with "Authentication failed" and the Android passkey sheet never appeared. `WebViewLoginScreen` loaded the Nextcloud Login Flow v2 page into a bare `android.webkit.WebView`, and a WebView has WebAuthn disabled by default (`WEB_AUTHENTICATION_SUPPORT_NONE`), so `navigator.credentials.get()` rejected inside the page and the IdP rendered its generic error.

Reported against Authentik, but it is not Authentik-specific — it applies to every WebAuthn sign-in, including Nextcloud's own passkey support and hardware security keys.

Configuring the WebView is not an available fix: the non-default WebAuthn support levels require a privileged app. The fix is to stop using a WebView for sign-in.

## What changed

**Chrome Custom Tab instead of a WebView** (`androidx.browser:browser`). Sign-in now happens in the user's real browser, which brings back everything the WebView blocked or degraded: passkeys, security keys, password managers, client certificates, and existing IdP sessions. No Play Services, so the F-Droid `full` flavour is unaffected. `WebViewLoginScreen`, `WebViewLoginViewModel`, `WebViewClient` and `WebViewScreenState` are replaced by `BrowserLoginScreen`, `BrowserLoginViewModel` and `BrowserLoginScreenState`.

**The login URL is validated before it is launched.** Handing a server-supplied URL to an external browser is a wider trust boundary than loading it into a WebView we control, so `getLoginEndpoint` now rejects any scheme that is not `http` or `https` — the same pair the start screen already validates for user-entered server URLs — before anything reaches the `SavedStateHandle` or the state moves to `Loaded`. Not HTTPS-only: cleartext instances are a supported deployment.

**Self-signed certificates** — the setting stays, the silent WebView bypass does not. The Custom Tab shows the browser's own interstitial, and the user proceeds through it. `allowSelfSignedCertificates` still reaches the app's own OkHttp client unchanged; only the navigation argument is gone. `docs/faqs.md` documents manual sign-in as the alternative.

**Return to the app on success** — there is no public API to close a Custom Tab, so `MainActivity` is re-started with `CLEAR_TOP | SINGLE_TOP`, which finishes the tab above it and delivers `onNewIntent` rather than recreating the activity. This is a background activity start, which is why it is its own revertible commit; see Testing for the result. The fallback if it is ever blocked is that Back once lands the user on Home, already signed in.

**Success is detected from a `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` collector**, not a state-keyed effect. While the tab is in front the activity is stopped and its recomposer's frame clock is paused, so a state-keyed effect would not re-fire until the user came back; an already-suspended coroutine resumes regardless, because `AndroidUiDispatcher` also posts to the main-thread `Handler`.

**Surviving process death.** The Custom Tab keeps the app backgrounded for as long as an SSO round-trip takes — minutes with a passkey prompt and possibly 2FA — which is exactly when Android reclaims the process. `pollUrl`, `pollToken`, the login URL and `browserLaunched` are persisted to the `SavedStateHandle`, so a restart resumes polling the *same* token instead of minting a fresh one and orphaning the login the user just completed. `browserLaunched` is part of that set deliberately: without it the restored state would re-open the tab the instant the screen came back. Polling is held in a tracked `Job` so a retry cancels its predecessor instead of leaving a second loop hammering the abandoned token.

## Testing

`BrowserLoginViewModelUnitTest` — 13 cases covering the endpoint request, the rejected non-web login URL, both `browserLaunched` directions, the poll retry and its stop condition, poll cancellation on retry, the saved-token resume path, and the `SavedStateHandle` reads and writes. Full unit suite: 75 tests, 0 failures. `ktlintCheck`, `lint` and `compileFullDebugAndroidTestKotlin` clean; release variant compile-checked with `compileFullReleaseKotlin` + `lintVitalAnalyzeFullRelease`.

**Return-to-app is verified.** The background activity start was the one open question in the spec, and it is settled: the real sign-in flow was driven against a mock Login Flow v2 server on two emulators, and the framework's own verdict read out of logcat.

- **Android 15 / API 35** — `START u0 {flg=0x24000000 cmp=…/MainActivity} with LAUNCH_MULTIPLE from uid 10215 (BAL_ALLOW_FOREGROUND) result code=3`. The background-activity-launch check *allowed* the start, and `result code=3` is `START_DELIVERED_TO_TOP`: `onNewIntent` on the existing instance, no recreation. `CustomTabActivity` CLOSE and `MainActivity` TO_FRONT in the transition log; the tab closed ~3 s after the poll succeeded, and Back from Home exited to the launcher as after a normal sign-in.
- **Android 10 / API 29** — start accepted, `am_on_resume_called` with no `am_on_create_called` and the same pid either side, so the activity was reused rather than recreated.
- Neither run logged anything matching `background activity`.

Both runs were on emulators rather than physical devices; the BAL decision is made by the framework, so this is strong evidence rather than a hardware confirmation.

**Still outstanding**, because the bug itself is only reproducible against a real IdP: the reported Authentik passkey case, a hardware security key, the self-signed end-to-end, and process death mid-sign-in against a real server.

## Notes

The branch also adds `specs/` (spec, three task documents, and the retros). Happy to drop those commits if design docs are not wanted in the repo.

* **New Features**
  * Sign-in now opens in the device’s browser using a secure Custom Tab, supporting passkeys, security keys, password managers, and single sign-on.
  * Added progress, retry, and no-browser error states.
  * Sign-in resumes after the app is closed or reclaimed by the system and returns to the app after authentication.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved compatibility with passkey and WebAuthn authentication.
  * Added validation for unsupported sign-in URLs.
* **Documentation**

title: fix: copy recalculated amount when long-pressing an ingredient
body:
Fixes #208.

## Problem

Long-pressing an ingredient copied the amount for the recipe's *original* yield, even after the
servings were changed. The displayed text was correct; only the clipboard content was stale.

The long-click listener was registered inside `LaunchedEffect(Unit)`. Because the key is `Unit` the
effect never restarts, so the lambda kept the `ingredient` `String` captured during the **first**
composition of that slot. twain's `MarkdownText` builds its `TextView` in the `AndroidView`
**factory** and its `update` block only re-renders the markdown, so changing the servings re-rendered
the row but left the original listener — and its captured string — in place.

## Fix

Two layers, both deliberate:

- **`BindLongClick`** — a private composable that registers the listener via `DisposableEffect` +
  `rememberUpdatedState`, keyed on `viewId`. This is what actually fixes the bug: the helper always
  invokes the newest lambda, so a stale capture is impossible by construction. It also disposes the
  listener (the old code never cleared it) and drops the pointless coroutine around a synchronous
  registration.
- **`RecipeDetailViewModel.getIngredientAt(index)`** — resolves the copy text against live state,
  threaded down through `RecipeDetailLayout` → `Ingredients`. This is what makes the behaviour
  assertable in a JVM unit test that runs in CI.

`findViewById` stays: `MarkdownText` exposes no long-press parameter, and a Compose
`combinedClickable` wrapper is not a substitute because Markwon's `CorePlugin.afterSetText` installs
a `LinkMovementMethod` when none is set, so the `TextView` consumes touch events — and ingredient
values really can contain links (`enrichRecipeLinks` rewrites `#r/123` into markdown links).

Owning the `AndroidView` would be the structural fix and is deliberately out of scope; it means
depending on Markwon directly and reproducing twain's `createTextView` across all four `MarkdownText`
call sites. That's a refactor, not a bugfix.

## Whole-recipe share was already correct

`getShareText()` substitutes `calculatedIngredients` and `currentYield` before formatting, and the
bulk "copy ingredients" button re-captures on every recomposition. Neither is changed — both got
regression coverage instead.

## Tests

`RecipeDetailViewModelUnitTest` is the first ViewModel test in the project, so it also stands up the
`Dispatchers.setMain(UnconfinedTestDispatcher())` harness (new `kotlinx-coroutines-test`
dependency, matching the already-resolved coroutines 1.10.2). Six cases: the recalculated lookup,
an unparsable ingredient, reset-yield, an out-of-range index, and two guarding the share path.

These cover the ViewModel lookup, **not** the Compose binding that actually failed —
`connectedAndroidTest` doesn't run in CI. That gap was closed manually:

- Verified on a real device by @lneugebauer.
- Additionally driven on an API 29 emulator with a throwaway instrumented test (not committed) that
  long-presses the real interop `TextView`: copy before the yield change, after it, `## Dough` and
  `salt` verbatim, and after reset. With the old `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` capture restored it fails
  with `expected:<[5]00 g flour> but was:<[4]00 g flour>` — #208 reproduced — and passes with the fix.

`ktlintCheck`, `test`, `lint`, `compileFullDebugAndroidTestKotlin` (CI never compiles androidTest, so
the `ScreenshotsTestSuite` update is easy to forget) and `compileFullReleaseKotlin` are all green.

title: fix(auth): use /cloud/user endpoint instead of /cloud/users/{id} for login
body:
**Summary**
Switch login from `GET /ocs/v2.php/cloud/users/{id}` (admin-only) to `GET /ocs/v2.php/cloud/user` (current user). This fixes logins for non-admin accounts (e.g., LDAP/IMAP), because the previous endpoint returns 401/403 unless the authenticating user has admin permissions.

**Why**
The app fetched the user profile during login using `/cloud/users/{id}`. On servers where regular users (LDAP/IMAP) are not admins, this endpoint is forbidden and breaks the login. `/cloud/user` returns the authenticated user’s info and works for all accounts.

**How tested**
- Built a debug APK and installed on a Pixel 6a (Android 16).
- Captured logs with `adb logcat` filtered for `okhttp/ocs/auth/token`.
- Second login run (correct credentials flow) shows only 200 responses:
  - `GET /ocs/v2.php/cloud/user` → 200
  - subsequent Cookbook API calls (recipes, categories, version) → 200
- Login succeeds and the app loads data as expected.

**Notes**
- This likely resolves the same login failure reported for IMAP/LDAP users in the linked issue.

title: refactor: Migrate to Room3 and fix Room PagingSource leaking coroutines
body:
`PagingSource` instances created by Room 2 and 3 immediately start a coroutine on the database `CoroutineScope` which is only unregistered if the `PagingSource` is invalidated. If it's not, the coroutine will run forever and memory will never be freed.

To work around this, add code to automatically call `PagingSource.invalidate()` when the `ViewModel` is destroyed. Thanks to the key argument, if another `PagingSource` with the same key was already registered, the `ViewModel` will automatically replace it and make sure the previous one is invalidated if it was not already the case.

title: fix: White Screen Flashing Glitch and add sliding animation
body:
# PR Info

## Issue Details
Navigating from the Home screen to the Detail screen caused a visible white flash due to a slight rendering delay. 

The issue arose because the NavHost composable did not have a background colour set during the transition. When navigating from the Home screen to the Detail screen, there is a delay before the Detail screen renders. During this delay, the NavHost acts as the container for both screens and displays a white background. I’ve set `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background` as a background colour to the NavHost to maintain visual consistency.

### [`v0.33.0`](https://redirect.github.com/slackhq/circuit/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0330)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/slackhq/circuit/compare/0.32.0...0.33.0)

*2026-02-10*

##### New Navigation Architecture:

Circuit now supports **bidirectional navigation** with browser-style forward/backward capabilities!

```kotlin
val navStack = rememberSaveableNavStack(root = HomeScreen)
val navigator = rememberCircuitNavigator(navStack)
navigator.backward() // Move back without removing history
navigator.forward()  // Move forward to a previously visited screen
```

**Navigation changes**:

- `Navigator.forward()`: Move forward in navigation history
- `Navigator.backward()`: Move backward in navigation history
- `Navigator.peekNavStack()`: Immutable snapshot of the current navigation stack state
- `NavigableCircuitContent` is aware of the full navigation stack and provides `NavStackList` to
  decorations, enabling them to render forward stack records.

**SaveableNavStack**:

- New implementation in `circuit-foundation` providing full bidirectional navigation state
- The existing `SaveableBackStack` implementation has been updated to extend `NavStack`

**New `circuit-runtime-navigation` artifact**:

- `NavStack`: Core navigation stack supporting push/pop and forward/backward traversal
- `NavStackList`: Immutable snapshot of navigation state

**circuitx-navigation**:

- `InterceptingNavigator` now supports `forward()` and `backward()` navigation methods
- Updated to use `NavStack` and `NavStackList` instead of `BackStack` and `List<Screen>`
- Rewrite interceptors can now rewrite to any `NavEvent` (not just specific navigation types like `InterceptedGoToResult.Rewrite` or `InterceptedResetRootResult.Rewrite`)
- `FailureNotifier` interface updated with `forwardFailure()` and `backwardFailure()` methods with default implementations

##### New

- Add `mingwX64()` target to `circuit-codegen-annotations`.

##### Fixes

- Fix an issue where `AnsweringResultHandler` was not correctly parceling pending results.

##### Changes

- Compile against kotlin-inject-anvil `0.1.7`.
- `NavigationEventHandler` usage is now disabled by default when no `NavigationEventDispatcherOwner` is available, preventing crashes in environments with dynamic navigation event support. This behaviour can be configured with the `Circuit.lenientNavigationEventDispatcherOwner` option.
- `BottomSheetOverlay` now exposes `contentWindowInsets`, mirroring `ModalBottomSheet`

title: fix: 🐛 Updated setTextSlot function
body:
## Add typed text slot support

Adds two `setTextSlot` overloads so callers can update a text slot either
with just a string or with full styling:

- `setTextSlot(slotId, text: String)` — reads the slot's current document,
  swaps only the text, and writes it back (returns `false` if the slot has
  no value). Fixes #133, where setting a string previously wiped the
  document's font/size/color.
- `setTextSlot(slotId, document: TextDocument)` — sets the full document.

Also adds a `TextDocument` type (text, font, size, colors, etc.) and the
`nativeGetSlotStr` binding to read the current slot value.


Related PR -> https://github.com/LottieFiles/dotlottie-rs/pull/586

body:
# SIGSEGV crash when loading DotLottieDrawable a second time

## Summary

The app crashes with `SIGSEGV` when a `DotLottieDrawable` is disposed and a new one is created —
e.g. navigating away from a page containing `DotLottieDrawable` and then navigating back.

## Fix
DotLottieDrawable.release() now destroys synchronously on the caller's thread instead of launching
  capturedPlayer.destroy() on drawableCleanupScope (IO). This removes the race where the last player's drop could
  concurrently call tvg_engine_term() while the next player's init/tick ran on main. Matches the Compose component cleanup behavior
  
  
  Solves: https://github.com/LottieFiles/dotlottie-flutter/issues/8
  https://github.com/LottieFiles/dotlottie-android/issues/111

title: fix: 🐛 applyConfig triggering 12 JNI crossings
body:
Fixes performance issues with the refactor
- Each DotLottiePlayer constructor does 12 JNI crossings (1 nativeNewPlayer + 11 individual nativeSet* config calls). With
   100 instances, that's 1,200 JNI round-trips on the main thread. The fix batched all config into a single JNI call — 1 crossing  
  per player instead of 12.
  2. Teardown: onDispose used runBlocking { renderMutex.withLock { ... } } which blocked the main thread waiting for the mutex. If a render coroutine was in-flight holding that mutex, the main thread stalled. The fix moved cleanup to a background coroutine so the main thread returns immediately.
  
  Fixes #102  https://github.com/LottieFiles/dotlottie-android/issues/102#issuecomment-4040604405

Fix critical bugs and Android compatibility issues
body:
This PR addresses multiple critical bugs and compatibility issues found throughout the Android Periodic Table codebase:

## 🐛 Critical Logic Bugs Fixed

**Comparator Logic Error**: Fixed a serious bug in `IsotopesActivityExperimental.kt` where the sorting comparator had duplicate conditions:
```kotlin
// Before (broken):
if (lhs.element < rhs.element) -1 else if (lhs.element < rhs.element) 1 else 0

// After (fixed):
if (lhs.element < rhs.element) -1 else if (lhs.element > rhs.element) 1 else 0
```
This bug prevented proper alphabetical sorting of isotope elements.

**Race Condition in Adapter Access**: Fixed potential crashes where `recyclerView.adapter!!.itemCount` was accessed before the adapter was set. The code now properly sets the adapter first and uses safe null checking (`?.`).

**Duplicate View Visibility Setting**: Removed redundant visibility assignments in `UserActivity.kt` where a TextView was set to VISIBLE then immediately to INVISIBLE.

## 📱 Android Compatibility Improvements

**PendingIntent Mutability Flags**: Fixed Android 12+ compatibility by adding proper mutability flags to PendingIntent creation in `ShortCommandWidget.kt`:
```kotlin
val flags = if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.S) {
    PendingIntent.FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT or PendingIntent.FLAG_IMMUTABLE
} else {
    PendingIntent.FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT
}
```

**Deprecated API Usage**: 
- Replaced deprecated `Handler()` constructor with `Handler(Looper.getMainLooper())` across multiple files
- Updated deprecated `capitalize()` method calls to use `replaceFirstChar { it.uppercase() }`

## 🔧 Build System Fixes

**Android Gradle Plugin Version**: Updated from non-existent version `8.11.1` to a stable version `7.4.2` to resolve build failures.

**Hardcoded File Paths**: Removed Windows-specific hardcoded signing configuration path that would break builds on other platforms.

## 🌐 Internationalization

**Hardcoded Strings**: Moved hardcoded text "Go online for emission lines" to proper string resources for better internationalization support.

## Files Modified
- `IsotopesActivityExperimental.kt` - Fixed comparator logic, Handler deprecation, race condition, and capitalize() usage
- `MainActivity.kt` - Fixed Handler deprecation and race condition  
- `UserActivity.kt` - Removed duplicate visibility setting
- `Utils.kt` & `Anim.kt` - Fixed deprecated Handler usage
- `ElementAdapter.kt` - Fixed deprecated capitalize() usage
- `ShortCommandWidget.kt` - Fixed PendingIntent mutability flags
- `ElementInfoActivity.kt` - Moved hardcoded string to resources
- `build.gradle` - Fixed Android Gradle Plugin version
- `app/build.gradle` - Removed hardcoded signing path
- `strings.xml` - Added new string resource

These fixes improve app stability, ensure Android 12+ compatibility, and follow modern Android development best practices.

title: Fix streak validation on sync and add notification permission for Android 13+
body:
Streaks were not validating last play date during Firebase sync, allowing expired streaks to be restored. Android 13+ notification permission was declared but never requested at runtime.

## Streak Validation

**StreakManager.kt**
- `getCurrentStreak()` now validates last play date and auto-resets if >1 day elapsed
- Added `setCurrentStreakWithDate(streak, date)` for atomic updates during sync
- Added `calculateDaysDifference()` for accurate date comparison across year boundaries

**ProgressSyncManager.kt**
- Extended `CloudProgress` with `streakLastPlay` field (ISO yyyy-MM-dd)
- Merge logic now:
  - Selects higher streak value between local/cloud
  - Associates correct last play date with selected streak
  - Validates merged streak freshness before applying locally

```kotlin
// Before: streak restored from cloud without validation
StreakManager.setCurrentStreak(context, cloudStreak)

// After: validates date and resets if expired
StreakManager.setCurrentStreakWithDate(context, mergedStreak, mergedLastPlayDate)
```

## Notification Permission

**SplashActivity.kt**
- Added runtime POST_NOTIFICATIONS permission request for Android 13+ (API 33)
- Uses `ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission()`
- One-time request tracked in SharedPreferences

**AndroidManifest.xml**
- Registered `StreakReminderReceiver` broadcast receiver with `android:exported="false"`

title: [WIP] Improve performance and fix eventual bugs
body:
Performance improvements and bug fixes for Atomic Periodic Table Android app

## Completed:

- [x] Fix deprecated `capitalize()` method (8 files) - replaced with `replaceFirstChar { it.uppercase() }`
- [x] Fix deprecated `Handler()` constructor (4 instances in TableExtension.kt) - added `Looper.getMainLooper()`
- [x] Fix SharedPreferences instantiation in ViewHolders (ElementAdapter, EquationsAdapter) - passed as constructor parameter to avoid repeated instantiation
- [x] Remove redundant text assignment in ElementAdapter - removed duplicate text setting
- [x] Fix JSON parsing in adapter bind methods (EmissionAdapter, IonAdapter) - added caching to prevent repeated file I/O on every bind
- [x] Fix memory leak in MainActivity - cleanup scroll sync runnable in onDestroy to prevent handler leaks
- [x] Fix deprecated resources.getColor() calls - replaced with ContextCompat.getColor() in TableExtension and NuclideActivity
- [x] Remove redundant adapter recreation - filterList already calls notifyDataSetChanged, removed unnecessary adapter recreation in MainActivity and IsotopesActivityExperimental

## Summary:

This PR improves performance and fixes several bugs:

**Performance Improvements:**
1. **Adapter optimization**: Moved SharedPreferences instantiation from ViewHolder bind methods to adapter constructor level, preventing object creation on every item bind
2. **JSON caching**: Added caching for JSON-parsed emission URLs and ionization values to prevent repeated file I/O operations
3. **Removed redundant adapter recreation**: filterList() already updates the adapter, so removed 6 instances where new adapters were unnecessarily created
4. **Removed redundant notifyDataSetChanged**: Removed 3 duplicate calls since filterList() already notifies

**Bug Fixes:**
1. **Memory leak**: Fixed handler leak in MainActivity by properly cleaning up scrollSyncRunnable in onDestroy
2. **Deprecated API**: Fixed 8 usages of deprecated `capitalize()` method with `replaceFirstChar { it.uppercase() }`
3. **Deprecated API**: Fixed 4 usages of deprecated `Handler()` constructor to use `Handler(Looper.getMainLooper())`
4. **Deprecated API**: Fixed 15 usages of deprecated `resources.getColor()` to use `ContextCompat.getColor()`
5. **Code cleanup**: Removed duplicate text assignment in ElementAdapter

**Files Changed**: 13 files
**Lines Changed**: +122, -100

All changes are minimal, focused, and follow Android best practices.

title: Fix double-counting of completed games in statistics
body:
Game completion statistics were incremented twice: once in `LearningGamesActivity.finishWithResults()` when the game ended, and again in `FlashCardActivity.showGameResultsPopup()` when displaying results.

## Changes
- Removed duplicate `completed_quizzes` increment from `LearningGamesActivity.finishWithResults()`
- Counter now increments once in `FlashCardActivity.showGameResultsPopup()` where results are displayed

```kotlin
// LearningGamesActivity.kt - Removed these lines:
if (finishedGame) {
    XpManager.addGameXp(this, xpGameWin)
    if (gameResults.all { it.wasCorrect }) {
        XpManager.addGameXp(this, xpPerfect)
    }
-   val prefs = getSharedPreferences("game_stats", MODE_PRIVATE)
-   val current = prefs.getInt("completed_quizzes", 0)
-   prefs.edit().putInt("completed_quizzes", current + 1).apply()
}

// FlashCardActivity.kt - Kept as single source of truth:
private fun incrementCompletedQuizzes() {
    val prefs = getSharedPreferences("game_stats", MODE_PRIVATE)
    val current = prefs.getInt("completed_quizzes", 0)
    prefs.edit().putInt("completed_quizzes", current + 1).apply()
}
```

title: Fix unresolved reference: migrate to longPressToStartDragging API

title: Fix incorrect setDataChangeListener usage in TableActivity and ToolsActivity
body:
`adapter.setDataChangeListener()` doesn't exist in the DragDropSwipeAdapter API. The library requires setting the listener on the RecyclerView itself.

### Changes
- **TableActivity & ToolsActivity**: Replace `adapter.setDataChangeListener()` with `recyclerView.dragListener = onItemDragListener`
- **TableActivity**: Fix import statements (syntax errors with colons instead of dots)

### Implementation
```kotlin
// Before - incorrect API usage
adapter.setDataChangeListener(object : DragDropSwipeRecyclerView.DataChangeListener {
    override fun onDatasetChanged() {
        saveTableOrder()
    }
})

// After - correct API usage
recyclerView.dragListener = onItemDragListener

private val onItemDragListener = object : OnItemDragListener<TableItem> {
    override fun onItemDragged(previousPosition: Int, newPosition: Int, item: TableItem) {}
    override fun onItemDropped(initialPosition: Int, finalPosition: Int, item: TableItem) {
        saveTableOrder()
    }
}
```

Pattern follows existing OrderActivity implementation. Drag-and-drop reordering now functions correctly when users toggle reorder mode.

title: Fix localized JSON asset loading and user notes persistence
body:
The app was not loading localized JSON assets (always defaulting to English) and user notes could be lost when navigating between elements.

## Changes

### Localization Fix
- **ElementDataLoader**: Added `getAppLanguage(context)` to read user's language preference from SharedPreferences before falling back to system locale
- **LearningGamesActivity**: Changed from `Locale.getDefault()` to `ElementDataLoader.getAppLanguage()`  
- **SettingsActivity**: Clear `ElementDataLoader` cache when language preference changes

All 20+ callsites of `ElementDataLoader.loadElementData()` now respect user language preference automatically.

```kotlin
// Before: Always used system locale
val lang = language ?: Locale.getDefault().language

// After: Checks app preference first
fun getAppLanguage(context: Context): String {
    val prefs = context.getSharedPreferences("settings", Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
    val lang = prefs.getString("app_language", null)
    return if (lang.isNullOrBlank()) Locale.getDefault().language else lang
}
```

### Notes Persistence Fix
- **InfoExtension**: Added `saveCurrentNotes()` called before element navigation and in `onDestroy()`
- Track current element code and EditText reference to enable explicit save operations
- Prevents race conditions with TextWatcher when navigating rapidly

```kotlin
private fun handleNotes(elementCode: String, eText: EditText) {
    saveCurrentNotes()  // Persist previous element's notes
    currentElementCode = elementCode
    notesEditText = eText
    // ... load new element's notes
}
```

Notes are keyed by language-independent `element_code`, so they persist across language changes.

body:
The app crashes on launch in non-English locales because button ID lookup uses localized element names instead of English keys. When locale is German, the code searches for "Wasserstoff_btn" but the XML defines "hydrogen_btn".

**Changes:**
- Use `item.elementKey` instead of `item.element` for button ID construction in `setOnCLickListenerSetups()`
- Add null check before accessing button properties to prevent crash if button not found

```kotlin
// Before
val name = item.element  // "Wasserstoff" in German locale
val btn = findViewById<TextView>(resIDB)
btn.foreground = ...  // NPE: btn is null

// After  
val name = item.elementKey  // "hydrogen" regardless of locale
val btn = findViewById<TextView>(resIDB)
if (btn != null) {
    btn.foreground = ...
}
```

The localized name is still correctly passed to `ElementSend.setValue(item.element)` for display.

title: Release with bug fixes
fix: support fixed scanner orientation
body: # Problem The iOS scanner listens to UIDeviceOrientationDidChangeNotification and rotates its AVCaptureVideoPreviewLayer independently of the host app's supported interface orientations. This causes the camera preview to rotate in apps that intentionally lock their interface orientation. With my old approach of https://github.com/kalinjul/EasyQRScan/issues/33 this got better when holding the iPad toward a wall, but it still had problems with holding the iPad toward the floor. With old approach (holding the iPad toward my desk): With new approach (holding the iPad toward my desk): # Solution Add ScannerOrientation to the public scanner API. Preserve the current device-driven behavior by default. Allow callers to select a fixed orientation such as LandscapeRight. Register the device orientation listener only in device-driven mode. Document the fixed-orientation usage. The fix was verified in a Compose Multiplatform iOS app on a physical device with interface rotation locked and device rotation unlocked and also with the built in scanner demo app. Closes https://github.com/kalinjul/EasyQRScan/issues/22

title: fix(android): remove explicit unbind to prevent dark screen on navigation
body:
## Summary

Removes the explicit `cameraXControllerWrapper.unbind()` call from `CameraSession.dispose()` to fix a dark screen when navigating between screens with cameras. CameraX's `LifecycleCameraController.unbind()` internally calls `ProcessCameraProvider.unbindAll()`, which is a process-wide operation that kills ALL camera sessions — not just the one being disposed. CameraX already manages use case cleanup automatically via lifecycle observation, making explicit unbind unnecessary and harmful in multi-screen scenarios.

Closes #93

title: fix(ios): avoid audio permission in photo capture mode
body:
## Issue
#75

## Summary
  - fix iOS camera startup so photo-only usage no longer requires audio permission
  - move audio input attachment to video recording start/stop instead of session startup
  - add iOS regression tests covering audio attachment during recording and preserving preconfigured mute state

## Problem
  On iOS, starting the camera session could attach audio input even when the developer only wanted to capture photos. That made audio permission necessary in scenarios where it should not be required.

## Solution
  - removed audio input setup from iOS session startup
  - attach audio only when video recording starts
  - detach audio when recording stops or finishes
  - preserve `muteRecording(true)` if it is configured before recording starts

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

  * Mute state is preserved across sessions and applied correctly when recording starts or is toggled.

* **Tests**
  * Added unit tests for audio lifecycle, mute behavior, and stop/cleanup edge cases.

* **New Features**

title: Upgrade to AGP 9 / API 37, fix latent bugs, and draw the sample edge to edge
body:
## Summary

Two commits: a toolchain upgrade that also uncovered a handful of real bugs, and edge-to-edge support for the sample app.

The build tooling was two AGP major versions behind and `jcenter()` was still in the repository list. This moves to AGP 9 with built-in Kotlin and the new DSL, with no opt-out flags, and replaces `buildSrc/Dependencies.kt` with a Gradle version catalog.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| AGP | 8.6.0 | 9.3.1 |
| Gradle | 8.7 | 9.7.0 |
| Kotlin | 2.0.20 | 2.4.10 |
| compileSdk | 35 | 37.1 |
| targetSdk (sample) | 35 | 37 |
| minSdk | 14 / 21 | 23 |
| appcompat | 1.7.0 | 1.7.1 (+ core-ktx 1.19.0, activity 1.13.0) |
| mockito / robolectric / truth / jacoco | 4.5.1 / 4.7.3 / 1.1.3 / 0.8.8 | 5.23.0 / 4.16.1 / 1.4.5 / 0.8.15 |

**`minSdk` 14 → 23 is breaking for library consumers.** androidx.core 1.19 requires it. The library version is bumped to 2.1.0 and the README API badge updated to match.

## Bugs fixed along the way

**The unit tests were not running at all.** JaCoCo's `includeNoLocationClasses` instrumented the JVM's own runtime-generated accessors, so the test worker died at startup with `NoClassDefFoundError: jdk/internal/reflect/GeneratedSerializationConstructorAccessor1`, retried 32 times, and failed after three minutes without executing a single test. Excluding `jdk.internal.*` fixes it; 99 tests now pass. The hand-written `jacocoDebugReport` task is gone too, as it read a classes directory that has not existed since AGP 3 and used `androidTest` as its source directory. AGP's own `createDebugUnitTestCoverageReport` replaces it.

In the library:

- **Views created in code drew nothing.** The one- and three-argument constructors skipped attribute parsing entirely, so `strokeWidth` and `color` stayed at 0. All twelve views now share a single `@JvmOverloads` constructor, which also means `app:*` attributes are no longer ignored when a `defStyleAttr` is supplied.
- **`app:hasHole="true"` enabled the hole on curves that do not support it** (`HeartProgressView`, `CannabisProgressView`, `XProgressView`, the roulettes). The XML path wrote straight through to `CurveSettings` and bypassed the subclass override. That override is replaced by a `supportsHole` flag on the base class.
- **Lowering `precision` below the current starting point hung the UI thread.** `addPointsToCurve` could add nothing and return its input unchanged, so `createNewPoints` looped forever. The starting point is now clamped, with a bail-out if a pass makes no progress. Covered by a new regression test.
- `precision <= 0` and negative `duration` are rejected at the setter instead of failing later.
- `Points.getPoints()` copied the list on every frame, on the drawing hot path.
- Deprecated `readParcelable(ClassLoader)` replaced with `ParcelCompat`.

In the sample: the settings fragment was inflated without its container and lost its layout params, and the precision slider started 10 points off its own mapping.

## Edge to edge

The activities padded their whole root view by the top and bottom insets, which kept content clear of the system bars but stopped the toolbar background from reaching the status bar and ignored side insets. Each view now takes only the edges it owns: the toolbar takes top and horizontal so its background draws behind the status bar and any cutout, the settings `ScrollView` takes bottom and horizontal so the settings scroll behind the navigation bar while the last one stays reachable, and the presentation content container takes all four.

Both activities call `enableEdgeToEdge` with `SystemBarStyle.dark` for the status bar, because the default `auto` style picks dark icons in light mode and those are illegible against the permanently dark blue toolbar.

## Testing

- `./gradlew build` passes, including lint. 99 unit tests, 0 failures.
- The sample was installed on an emulator and checked across several curves before the edge-to-edge commit; the curves render and animate, and the hole checkbox correctly disables itself for curves that do not support it.
- **The edge-to-edge commit has not been verified on a device or emulator yet.** It compiles, but the layout should be eyeballed in both orientations and under both gesture and three-button navigation before merging.

## Targeting `master`

The README asks for pull requests against `development`, but that branch is currently 7 commits behind `master`, so this targets `master` to avoid dragging unrelated commits into the diff.

## Follow-ups, deliberately not in scope

- `FragmentStatePagerAdapter` and `Fragment.retainInstance` are deprecated and still in use. Clearing those means migrating to ViewPager2 and `CircleIndicator3`, which is a refactor rather than a dependency bump.
- `RoundScribbleProgressView.getGraphY` uses `cos(t)` where every sibling curve uses `sin(t)`. It looks like a typo, but scribble curves are deliberate distortions and this is the shape that ships today, so it is untouched.

title: fix: Ensure child is rendered before trying to draw over it
body:
This applies the fix from #136 to the "v2 updates" branch since that seems to be the published version.

Description from that PR:
Fixes #125 

This ensures that we don't have a null child (thus, it is rendered) before trying to draw over it. I had to move away from `parent.getChildAt` because the index can be outside of the page of the underlying RecyclerView. Even if I checked for a null child, the evolution decoration line wouldn't render by using that function.

I found this information at https://stackoverflow.com/a/67710269

> When there is more than one page of data in your recycler view and you're using getChildAt() method, it will throw a null pointer exception. This is because when the position is greater than the number of visible items on the display, getChildAt() won't work as it can only get to the view that is displayed on the screen.
>> 
Therefore, use recyclerView.layoutManager?.findViewByPosition(position) to get the view at the given position.

title: Fix KSP maven artifacts never being pinned or resolved
body:
## Problem

  KSP processors declared via `ksp(...)` in Gradle were computed correctly into
  `WorkspaceDependencies` but never made it through the pinning, dependency
  resolution, or Bazel rule generation steps. This caused three silent failures:

  ### Bug 1 — `ArtifactPinner` skipped `ksp_maven` entirely
  `shouldRunPinning()` and `pinArtifacts()` only iterated over `variantDeps`, so
  `ksp_maven` was never checked for staleness and `ksp_maven_pin.sh` was never
  generated.

  ### Bug 2 — `DependencyResolutionService` missing KSP from maven store
  `populateMavenStore()` only iterated `variantDeps`, so `getMavenDependency()`
  could not resolve KSP artifacts during Bazel script generation, leading to
  unresolvable target references.

  ### Bug 3 — Dangling Bazel target references from dropped KSP processors
  `RootBazelFileBuilder` silently skipped processors with no
  `SymbolProcessorProvider` service entry, but `collectKspPluginDeps` still
  emitted Bazel target references for them, producing targets that don't exist
  in the root `BUILD.bazel`.

  ## Solution

  Introduce `aggregatedRepos` in `WorkspaceDependencies` — a map of repo-name to
  dependency list for artifacts that bypass the per-variant reduction pipeline
  (e.g. `ksp_maven`). This sits alongside the existing `variantDeps` and is
  propagated through all consumers.

  Key changes:
  - **`WorkspaceDependencies`**: Added `aggregatedRepos: Map<String,
    List<ResolvedDependency>>`; renamed `result` → `variantDeps` (with
    `@SerialName("result")` to preserve JSON backward compatibility); removed
    `kspResult`
  - **`ComputeWorkspaceDependencies`**: Writes KSP deps into
    `aggregatedRepos["ksp_maven"]` sorted and deduplicated by max version
  - **`ArtifactPinner`**: Updated `shouldRunPinning()` and `pinArtifacts()` to
    iterate both `variantDeps` and `aggregatedRepos`
  - **`DependencyResolutionService`**: Updated `populateMavenStore()` to also
    populate from `aggregatedRepos`; added `getValidKspProcessorShortIds()` which
    returns only processors that have a valid `SymbolProcessorProvider` service
    entry
  - **`RootBazelFileBuilder`**: Warns and skips processors with no
    `processorClass` instead of silently dropping them
  - **`DefaultDependenciesDataSource.collectKspPluginDeps()`**: Filters KSP
    plugin deps against `getValidKspProcessorShortIds()` so only processors with
    a generated `kt_ksp_plugin` target are referenced

fix(core): track in-flight execute() playback so executeAsync cancels it
body:
Closes #93.

`execute` cleared `currentHandle` before running playback, so during playback no handle pointed at the in-flight vibration. `executeAsync`, which only takes `stateMutex`, then saw a null handle, cancelled nothing, and fired a second vibration over the first.

`execute` now drives its playback through `executeAsync` to get a real motor-stopping handle, publishes it into `currentHandle` under `stateMutex`, then awaits completion; a `finally` under `NonCancellable` cancels the handle and clears the slot with an identity guard so it never wipes a handle a newer caller installed.

This keeps the invariants:

- `executeAsync` never touches `executionMutex` and returns its handle synchronously, so the non-blocking contract holds.
- Lock order is unchanged (`execute` takes `executionMutex` then `stateMutex`; `executeAsync` takes only `stateMutex`), so no new deadlock edge.
- Cancellation propagates; only the motor-stop and slot-clear run under `NonCancellable`.

A handle is required rather than a coroutine `Job` because `executor.execute` does not call `Vibrator.cancel()` on cancellation — only `HapticHandle.cancel()` stops the motor.

## Test

`executeAsync should cancel an execute() playback that is still in flight`: launches `execute` in the background, advances virtual time so it is provably playing, then calls `executeAsync` and asserts the execute-issued handle is cancelled while the async handle survives. Reverting to the pre-fix behavior turns it red. Public API unchanged (internal concurrency only).

title: fix(compose): recompile haptic pattern when Jindong keys change
body:
## Problem

`Jindong(vararg keys)` is documented to recompile and replay its pattern when keys change, like `LaunchedEffect`. It does not.

`rememberHapticPattern` memoizes with a **keyless** `remember { compilePattern(content) }`, and `Jindong` never threads its `keys` into it. The pattern is compiled once on the first frame and cached forever; `LaunchedEffect(*keys)` then replays that stale pattern on every key change.

As a result, state-driven pattern shape does not work. For example:

```kotlin
Jindong(level) {
    val steps = (level * 10).toInt()
    RepeatWithIndex(steps) { Haptic(50.ms) }
}
```

`steps` is frozen at its first-frame value — changing `level` never changes the emitted event count.

## Fix

- `rememberHapticPattern` takes `vararg keys` and memoizes with `remember(*keys)`.
- `Jindong` threads its `keys` through, so `remember(*keys)` (recompile) and `LaunchedEffect(*keys)` (replay) share the same keys.

An empty key list keeps the previous behavior (compile once, replay once on entry).

## Tests

Adds `JindongReactiveTest` (Compose UI test): a key-driven `steps` that changes the emitted event count. The test fails against the current keyless code and passes after the fix.

Pulls in `compose.ui.test` + `kotlinx-coroutines-test` for `jindong-compose` common tests, run on `iosSimulatorArm64` (the module has no JVM target for Robolectric).

No public API change.

title: :thread: fix memory visibility in AndroidHapticHandle
body:
## Issue

  <!-- No specific issue, proactive thread-safety improvement -->

  ## Summary

  Fix memory visibility issue in `AndroidHapticHandle` by using `AtomicBoolean` for thread-safe state management.

  ### Problem
  `isActive` was a plain `var` without volatile semantics, causing potential memory visibility issues when `cancel()` is called from multiple threads:

  ```kotlin
  // Before
  override var isActive = vibrator != null
      private set

  override fun cancel() {
      if (!isActive) return  // Could read stale value
      isActive = false
      vibrator?.cancel()
  }
```

  In Compose environments, concurrent calls can occur from lifecycle callbacks and coroutines simultaneously.

  Solution

  Use AtomicBoolean to guarantee memory visibility and atomic state transitions:

```kotlin
  // After
  private val _isActive = AtomicBoolean(vibrator != null)
  override val isActive: Boolean
      get() = _isActive.get()

  override fun cancel() {
      if (!_isActive.compareAndSet(true, false)) return
      vibrator?.cancel()
  }
```

  Implementation Highlights

  - AtomicBoolean ensures memory visibility across threads
  - compareAndSet provides atomic check-and-update
  - Getter pattern maintains interface compatibility

  Additional Context

  While the practical impact is minimal (vibrator.cancel() is idempotent), this ensures correct multi-threaded behavior per JMM specification. As library code, we should handle edge cases that application code might reasonably trigger, even if rare.

title: fix: prevent resource leak in compilePattern
body:
## Summary

Fix resource leak in `compilePattern()` by implementing `AutoCloseable` pattern.

### Problem
`JindongCompositionHost` was not properly disposed when exceptions occurred during pattern compilation:
```kotlin
// Before
val host = JindongCompositionHost()
host.setContent(content)  // If exception occurs here...
host.sendFrame()          // ...or here...
val pattern = host.collectEvents()  // ...or here...
host.dispose()  // This never gets called
return pattern
```

This caused memory leaks as `Composition`, `Recomposer`, and `CoroutineScope` resources were not cleaned up.

### Solution
Implemented `AutoCloseable` interface and used \`.use\` pattern to guarantee cleanup:
```kotlin
// After
return JindongCompositionHost().use { host ->
    host.setContent(content)
    host.sendFrame()
    host.collectEvents()
}  // close() automatically called even on exception
```

### Implementation Highlights

1. Added `AutoCloseable` interface to `JindongCompositionHost`
2. Implemented `close()` method that delegates to existing `dispose()`
3. Refactored `compilePattern()` to use `.use` block for automatic resource management

## Additional Context

This is a critical bug fix that prevents resource leaks in composition host lifecycle management. The change is backward compatible and doesn't affect the public API.

title: Fix: Clear favourite filter when selecting tags
body:
When switching from "Favourites" to a tag filter, only links that were both favourites AND tagged were shown. Expected: all links with that tag.

## Changes

- Reset `favouriteFilter` to `-1` (All) when adding a tag to the selection in `AccountViewModel.setTagFilter()`
- Intentionally preserve `favouriteFilter` when removing tags (other tags may still be selected)

## Implementation

```kotlin
// In AccountViewModel.setTagFilter()
_selectedTagFilter.update { currentList ->
    if (currentList.any { it.id == tag.id }) {
        currentList.filter { it.id != tag.id }
    } else {
        _favouriteFilter.update { -1 }  // Reset to show all links with this tag
        currentList + tag
    }
}
```

Applies to all tag selection paths: filter chips, content area clicks, and modal sheet.

title: Fix navigation loop when sharing links to Deepr
body:
Users get stuck on the AddLinkScreen when sharing links from other apps - pressing back re-triggers navigation to the same screen in an infinite loop.

## Root Cause

The `LaunchedEffect` in `HomeScreen` detects `sharedText` and navigates to `AddLinkScreen`, but never clears the shared state. When the user backs out, the effect runs again with the same `sharedText` value, re-triggering navigation.

## Changes

- Clear shared text immediately after consuming it for navigation (both success and error paths)

```kotlin
LaunchedEffect(sharedText) {
    if (!sharedText?.url.isNullOrBlank()) {
        val normalizedLink = normalizeLink(sharedText.url)
        if (isValidDeeplink(normalizedLink)) {
            selectedLink = createDeeprObject(link = normalizedLink, name = sharedText.title ?: "")
            resetSharedText()  // Added: prevents re-navigation on back
        } else {
            Toast.makeText(context, "Invalid deeplink from shared content", Toast.LENGTH_SHORT).show()
            resetSharedText()  // Added: prevents stuck state on error
        }
    }
}
```

body:
## Problem

CSV export and import were not handling tags, causing tag data to be lost during backup and restore operations. This was reported in issue where users noted that tags were neither present in exports nor restored during imports.

## Solution

This PR adds full tag support to both CSV export and import functionality by making minimal, surgical changes to the backup system.

### Changes

**Export Side:**
- Modified `CsvWriter.kt` to use `ListDeeprWithTagsAsc` instead of `Deepr` to include tag information
- Updated `ExportRepositoryImpl.kt` to fetch data using `listDeeprWithTagsAsc()` query
- Added "Tags" column to CSV header and output

**Import Side:**
- Updated `ImportRepositoryImpl.kt` to parse tags from the CSV's 6th column
- Added transaction-safe tag import logic that:
  - Creates tags if they don't exist (using `INSERT OR IGNORE`)
  - Links tags to imported links using existing database operations

**Format:**
- Tags are exported/imported as comma-separated values: `"tag1, tag2, tag3"`
- Matches the SQL `GROUP_CONCAT(Tags.name, ', ')` format used throughout the codebase
- Consistent with the markdown sync feature's tag handling

### Backward Compatibility

Old CSV files without the Tags column will continue to import successfully since:
- The header validation only requires the first 3 columns (Link, CreatedAt, OpenedCount)
- Tag parsing uses `getOrNull(5)` which safely returns null for missing columns
- Empty/null tag values are handled gracefully as empty strings

### Testing

The implementation was verified by:
- Code review to ensure it matches existing patterns in `SyncRepositoryImpl.kt`
- Validation that it uses existing database queries and maintains transaction integrity
- Confirmation that the tag separator format matches the database query output

Fixes the issue where tags were not included in CSV export and backup.

title: FIX: DB Schema Generator issues

## Overview
Fix misc database schema generator issues.  See example below

1. **Postgres**: Fix support for double fields/types, double now mapped to `FLOAT8`
2. **Formatting**: The schema ddl generated is messy/unformatted, this formats it 
3. **Migration**: The migration service is updated to handle the formatting above
4. **Grouping**: The migration service can group multiple DDLs into 1 file based for the same model schema.

### Example: Formatting + Float8
```sql
create table if not exists "unit_tests"."sample1" ( 
"id"                  BIGSERIAL    NOT NULL  PRIMARY KEY, 
"test_string"         VARCHAR(30)  NOT NULL  , 
"test_stringOpt"      VARCHAR(30)            , 
"test_string_enc"     VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL  , 
"test_bool"           BOOLEAN      NOT NULL  , 
"test_short"          SMALLINT     NOT NULL  , 
"test_int"            INTEGER      NOT NULL  , 
"test_long"           BIGINT       NOT NULL  , 
"test_float"          FLOAT        NOT NULL  , 
"test_double"         FLOAT8       NOT NULL  , 
"test_enum"           INTEGER      NOT NULL  , 
"test_localdate"      DATE         NOT NULL  , 
"test_localtime"      TIME         NOT NULL  , 
"test_localdatetime"  TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL  , 
"test_zoneddatetime"  TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL  , 
"test_uuid"           VARCHAR(50)  NOT NULL  , 
"test_uniqueId"       VARCHAR(50)  NOT NULL  , 
"test_object_addr"    VARCHAR(40)  NOT NULL  , 
"test_object_city"    VARCHAR(30)  NOT NULL  ,

"test_object_country" INTEGER      NOT NULL  , 
"test_object_zip"     VARCHAR(5)   NOT NULL  , 
"test_object_isPOBox" BOOLEAN      NOT NULL   );
```

### Example: Models
The Account and User models here are both in the `users` schema.
So the migration service will generate both

```sql

...
```

#### 2. 1 File for all models - users.sql
```sql
create table if not exists "users"."account" ( 
...
create table if not exists "users"."user" ( ...
...
```

title: fix: prevent crash when reading malformed JSON from messages DB
body:
Backport of #1301 onto `releases/2.2.1`.

## Problem

A crash was reported originating from `Converters.stringToArray`, called by `MessagesDAO_Impl.getMessagesForWalletFlow`:

```
kotlinx.serialization.json.internal.JsonDecodingException
  at org.greenstand.android.TreeTracker.database.Converters.stringToArray
  at ...MessagesDAO_Impl.getMessagesForWalletFlow$lambda$0
```

`stringToArray` decodes the `survey_response` column (`List<String>?`) on `MessageEntity` with a strict `json.decodeFromString`. A single row holding a malformed/legacy value (anything that isn't a valid JSON array) throws `JsonDecodingException` inside Room's row mapping for the `Flow`, so the exception propagates out and crashes the app — and keeps crashing on every read of that wallet's messages.

## Fix

Wrap the three **read-side** converters (`stringToArray`, `jsonToMap`, `stringToInstance`) in `runCatching { … }.getOrElse { Timber.e(…); null }`. A bad row now logs and degrades to `null` instead of taking down the whole message list. Write-side converters stay strict.

## Verification

Added regression tests for malformed input on each decoder in `ConvertersTest`.

- **Before** (old code): the new tests fail with the exact exception from the crash — `JsonDecodingException: Expected start of the array '[', but had 'n'`.
- **After**: all 11/11 `ConvertersTest` cases pass (verified on this branch).
- **Emulator smoke test**: built/installed the `dev` variant on Pixel_2_API_27, app launches and stays alive with no `FATAL`/`JsonDecodingException` in logcat.

title: fix: re-hydrate OrgRepo on process-death restoration
body:
## Problem

`OrgRepo` keeps its current org **only in memory** and is populated solely by `orgRepo.init()` in the splash screen's `bootstrap()`. When the OS kills the app in the background and restores it directly into a deep screen (e.g. mid capture-setup flow), the splash screen — and therefore `init()` — is bypassed, leaving `currentOrg` null.

The next access then crashes. Building `CaptureSetupNavigationController` reads `orgRepo.currentOrg()` in its constructor, which throws, surfaced by Koin as `InstanceCreationException`:

```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: OrgRepo not initialized. Call init() before accessing currentOrg().
    at OrgRepo.currentOrg(OrgRepo.kt:95)
    at CaptureSetupNavigationController.<init>(CaptureSetupNavigationController.kt:36)
    at org.koin.core.instance.InstanceFactory.create(...)
    at CaptureSetupScopeManager.getNav(SetupScope.kt:72)
    at UserSelectScreenKt$UserSelectScreen$1$1$1.invokeSuspend(UserSelectScreen.kt:34)
```

The org data itself survives process death (the org row is in the DB, the selected org id is in prefs) — only the in-memory cache is lost.

## Fix

Re-hydrate `OrgRepo` **once per process at the composition root** (`Root`), gating `Host()` behind a new idempotent `suspend ensureInitialized()`. This covers every restored destination — `UserSelect`, the capture flow, and the org-picker / add-org screens that also read `currentOrg()` — with a single guard rather than per-screen patches.

- `OrgRepo.ensureInitialized()` — reloads from DB/prefs only when `currentOrg` is null; no-op otherwise.
- `Root` runs it in a `LaunchedEffect`, showing the existing `Splash()` until ready, then composing `Host()`. On a normal cold start it's a fast extra DB read and visually seamless (the gate's splash and the splash route's image are identical); the splash `bootstrap()` is unchanged.

## Verification

Tested end-to-end on an emulator (Android 16 / API 36) with genuine process death (`am kill` while backgrounded):

- **Without this change:** process death → restore into UserSelect → select planter → forward reproduces the exact crash above.
- **With this change:** same steps navigate cleanly to the next setup step; the restored process logs a single `OrgRepo: Org set to …` from the root gate (splash bypassed). Compiles clean; no behavior change on the normal cold-start path.

title: fix: prevent splash drawable resolution crash (#1176)
body:
## Summary

Closes #1176.

Wrap `painterResource(R.drawable.splash)` in a defensive pre-flight via `Resources.getValue(...)` inside `runCatching`, so a missing or unresolvable splash drawable falls back to a solid `AppColors.Gray` `Box` instead of crashing the app at launch with `Resources$NotFoundException`. The failure path is logged via Timber so any recurrence still surfaces in Crashlytics, just non-fatally.

Also drops the unqualified `app/src/main/res/drawable/splash.png` — it was a byte-for-byte duplicate of `drawable-xxxhdpi/splash.png` while `drawable-mdpi/splash.png` was a different (smaller) file. The default-bucket duplicate is the most plausible reason the runtime was failing to materialize the drawable for a slice of long-tail devices under AAB density splits (Crashlytics shows 91 events / 12 users, all on `SplashScreen`).

A follow-up worth filing: migrate to `androidx.core.splashscreen` so the splash is rendered by the system on Android 12+ rather than by a Compose `Image` shown after the permission prompt.

title: fix: resolve tree capture race condition between GPS and camera
body:
## Summary

Fixes a crash where `setImage()` was called before `pinLocation()` completed, because camera capture and GPS pinning run concurrently. The camera could finish first, and `TreeCapturer.setImage()` would throw since `newTreeUuid` was still null.

Split out from #1210 as a focused bug fix (PR 2 of 4). Depends on #1218 (UiEvent system, now merged).

### What changed

**`TreeCaptureViewModel`**:
- `CaptureLocation` creates a `CompletableDeferred<Boolean>` that `OnImageCaptured` awaits before calling `setImage()`
- Double-dispatch guard: if `CaptureLocation` is already in flight, subsequent dispatches are ignored
- 30-second `withTimeoutOrNull` on the GPS wait to prevent indefinite hangs
- On GPS failure or timeout, the bad GPS dialog is shown instead of silently discarding the photo
- Navigation moved from Screen into ViewModel via `triggerEvent(NavigationEvent {...})`

**`TreeCaptureScreen`**:
- `HandleUiEvents(viewModel)` wired up to receive navigation events
- Removed inline `if (state.isLocationAvailable) { navForward() }` from `onImageCaptured` callback — this was the source of the race

### Issues addressed from #1210 review
- Silent photo discard → now shows bad GPS dialog
- Indefinite hang on `await()` → 30s timeout
- No synchronization on deferred → double-dispatch guard
- Navigation from composable callback → moved to ViewModel via UiEvent

## Test plan
- [ ] Tap capture → verify navigation to review screen works
- [ ] From review screen, navigate back → verify no infinite navigation loop
- [ ] Disable GPS / poor signal → verify bad GPS dialog appears (not silent discard)
- [ ] Rapid double-tap capture → verify no crash
