### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>vanniktech/gradle-maven-publish-plugin (com.vanniktech:gradle-maven-publish-plugin)</summary>

### [`v0.33.0`](https://redirect.github.com/vanniktech/gradle-maven-publish-plugin/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0330--2025-06-22-)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/vanniktech/gradle-maven-publish-plugin/compare/0.32.0...0.33.0)

> \[!CAUTION]
> Sonatype OSSRH (oss.sonatype.org and s01.oss.sonatype.org) will be shut down on June 30, 2025.
>
> Migration steps:
>
> 1. Sign in to the [Central Portal](https://central.sonatype.com) with your existing Sonatype account
> 2. Go to [Namespaces](https://central.sonatype.com/publishing/namespaces) and click "Migrate Namespace"
>    for the relevant namespace. Confirm the migration and wait for it to complete.
> 3. Optional: If you want to publish snapshots of your project tap the 3 dots next to your namespace and
>    select "Enable SNAPSHOTs"
> 4. Go to [Account](https://central.sonatype.com/account) and select "Generate User Token". Use the shown
>    "Username" and "Password" as values for `mavenCentralUsername` and `mavenCentralPassword`.
> 5. Configure this plugin to publish to Central Portal. Either update your `SONATYPE_HOST` property from
>    `DEFAULT` or `S01` to `CENTRAL_PORTAL` or call `publishToMavenCentral()`/`publishToMavenCentral(automaticRelease)`
>    without a `SonatypeHost` parameter.

**BREAKING**

- `publishToMavenCentral()` and `publishToMavenCentral(automaticRelease)` without `SonatypeHost` will
  now publish through the Central Portal.
- Deprecated overloads of `publishToMavenCentral` that take a `SonatypeHost` parameter.
- Deprecated `SonatypeHost`.

New

- Basic experimental support for `com.android.fused-library`. There are currently several limitations
  on the Android Gradle plugin side which make signing as well as publishing sources/javadocs not possible.

Improvements

- Added new Gradle properties
  - `mavenCentralPublishing=true` replaces `SONATYPE_HOST=CENTRAL_PORTAL`
  - `mavenCentralAutomaticPublishing=true` replaces `SONATYPE_AUTOMATIC_RELEASE=true`
  - `signAllPublications=true` replaces `RELEASE_SIGNING_ENABLED=true`
  - Note: The old properties continue to work and there are no plans to remove them
- The base plugin is now compatible with isolated projects as long as `pomFromGradleProperties()` is
  not called.
- It's possible to pass a `TaskProvider` to `JavadocJar.Dokka`
- Improved naming of produced `-javadoc` jars (locally, the name of the published artifact is unchanged)
- Resolve issue that caused `version` to be read too early when publishing to
  Central Portal.

Thanks to [@​Goooler](https://redirect.github.com/Goooler), [@​solrudev](https://redirect.github.com/solrudev) and [@​sschuberth](https://redirect.github.com/sschuberth) for their contributions to this release.

##### Minimum supported versions

- JDK 11
- Gradle 8.5
- Android Gradle Plugin 8.0.0
- Kotlin Gradle Plugin 1.9.20

##### Compatibility tested up to

- JDK 24
- Gradle 8.14.2
- Gradle 9.0-rc1
- Android Gradle Plugin 8.10.0
- Android Gradle Plugin 8.11.0-rc02
- Android Gradle Plugin 8.12.0-alpha06
- Kotlin Gradle Plugin 2.1.21
- Kotlin Gradle Plugin 2.2.0-RC3

</details>

# Notes / Description

This pull request introduces enhancements to the dropdown and button components in the Carbon library, focusing on size specifications and platform-specific implementations. Additionally, it includes refactoring and improvements to the `DemoScreen` layout for better modularity and maintainability.

### Dropdown and Button Size Specifications

* Introduced the `getSizeSpecification` function for both `ButtonSize` and `DropdownSize`, providing platform-specific warnings for discouraged sizes. This is implemented for Android (`PlatformSpecifications.android.kt`), with default implementations for desktop and native platforms returning `null`.

* Updated `DropdownDemoScreen` and `ButtonDemoScreen` to use `getSizeSpecification` for determining the interactive state of dropdowns and buttons based on size. This replaces hardcoded logic with a more flexible and reusable approach.

### Refactoring of `DemoScreen`

* Refactored the `DemoScreen` layout to improve modularity:
  - Extracted `VariantsTabList` and `DemoVariantContent` into separate composable functions for better readability and reusability.
  - Renamed variables for clarity (e.g., `layer` to `demoLayer`).
  - Improved layout handling by adding a `modifier` parameter to `ParametersLayout` and ensuring consistent padding and background application.

* Wrapped the variants tab list in with the catalog inline theme to match the UI shell header for better visibility and structural UX.

### Miscellaneous Improvements

* Added missing copyright headers to several files.
* Adjusted dropdown field width for better usability in `DropdownDemoScreen`.
* Removed redundant imports and unused layout wrappers in dropdown demos for a cleaner codebase.

These changes collectively improve the maintainability, platform support, and user experience of the Carbon library's dropdown and button components.

Fix dropped -P overrides in whetstone-gradle-plugin loadParentProperties
body:
## Summary

`whetstone-gradle-plugin/build.gradle.kts:20` (`loadParentProperties`) iterated each property loaded from `../gradle.properties` but queried the Gradle property provider with `name` — which inside a `build.gradle.kts` resolves to `Project.name` (`"whetstone-gradle-plugin"`) — instead of the `key` being processed. As a result, `providers.gradleProperty("whetstone-gradle-plugin")` was always absent, `getOrElse` always returned the file value, and any `-P` override for a parent property (`VERSION_NAME`, `GROUP`, `POM_*`, signing config, etc.) was silently ignored by this module.

The fix is one character: `name` → `key`. Each iteration now queries the property currently being processed, so overrides take effect as the original code clearly intended.

The release workflow's `cat gradle.properties >> whetstone-gradle-plugin/gradle.properties` propagation is left in place — it remains correct (file values still win when no override is provided) and removing it can be a follow-up after this fix has soaked through one release cycle.

## Test plan

- [x] `./gradlew :whetstone-gradle-plugin:properties -q | grep -E "^(VERSION_NAME|GROUP):"` — defaults unchanged (`com.deliveryhero.whetstone` / `1.1.8-SNAPSHOT`).
- [x] `./gradlew :whetstone-gradle-plugin:properties -PVERSION_NAME=9.9.9 -q | grep VERSION_NAME` — prints `VERSION_NAME: 9.9.9` (was `1.1.8-SNAPSHOT` before fix).
- [x] `./gradlew :whetstone-gradle-plugin:properties -PGROUP=foo.bar -q | grep GROUP` — prints `GROUP: foo.bar` (proves the fix is not `VERSION_NAME`-specific).
- [x] `./gradlew build` — green.

title: Fix ProGuard rule propagation for library modules with comprehensive test coverag
body:
## Summary

  Fixes ProGuard rule propagation from Whetstone-annotated library modules to consuming applications by implementing a reliable mechanism to copy Anvil-generated `.pro` files into
  the AAR package. This ensures that classes annotated with `@ContributesViewModel`, `@ContributesFragment`, etc., are properly preserved during ProGuard/R8 minification in
  consuming apps.

  ## Problem

  Previously, ProGuard rules generated by Whetstone's Anvil compiler were not being packaged into library AARs. This caused ClassNotFoundException at runtime when consuming apps
  enabled minification, as the annotated classes were incorrectly stripped out.

  **Root Cause:**
  - Whetstone/Anvil generates `.pro` files in `build/anvil/{variant}/generated/`
  - AGP only auto-discovers ProGuard files from `build/tmp/kotlin-classes/{variant}/META-INF/proguard/`
  - Without copying files between these locations, AGP never packaged the rules into the AAR

  ## Solution

  Implemented a `doLast` hook on KotlinCompile tasks that:
  1. Locates all `.pro` files from Anvil's output directory
  2. Copies them to `kotlin-classes/{variant}/META-INF/proguard/`
  3. Allows AGP to auto-discover and package them into the AAR's `proguard.txt`

  This mimics how KAPT works and integrates seamlessly with AGP's existing consumer ProGuard file mechanism.

  ## Implementation Details

  ### WhetstonePlugin.kt Changes
  - Added `addLocateWhetstoneProguardTask()` method with comprehensive documentation
  - Hooks into KotlinCompile's `doLast` to copy files after compilation
  - Only applies to library modules (app modules don't export consumer ProGuard files)
  - Handles multiple variants correctly with proper task name checking

  ### Test Coverage

  Added comprehensive test coverage across multiple levels:

  #### whetstone-gradle-plugin (14 unit tests)
  - **ProguardFileOperationsTest.kt** (8 tests) - Basic file operations
  - **WhetstonePluginConfigTest.kt** (6 tests) - Plugin copy logic verification

  #### whetstone module (8 E2E integration tests)
  - **ProguardIntegrationTest.kt** (8 tests) - Real code generation tests using `compileAnvil()`
    - Verifies `@ContributesViewModel`, `@ContributesFragment`, `@ContributesActivityInjector`
    - Tests `generateDaggerFactories` flag behavior
    - Validates ProGuard file content format: `-keep,allowobfuscation,allowshrinking class ...`
    - Confirms correct directory structure: `build/anvil/META-INF/proguard/`
    - Tests multiple ViewModels generating separate `.pro` files
    - Handles qualified package names correctly

Tested with real library module build:
  ```bash
  ./gradlew clean :sample-library:bundleMetroReleaseAar
  unzip -p sample-library/build/outputs/aar/sample-library-metro-release.aar proguard.txt

  Result: ProGuard rules correctly packaged in AAR:
  -keep,allowobfuscation,allowshrinking class com.deliveryhero.sample_library.MainViewModel
```

Testing Instructions

  1. Run all tests:
  ./gradlew :whetstone-gradle-plugin:test :whetstone:test
  2. Verify AAR packaging:
  ./gradlew clean :sample-library:bundleMetroReleaseAar
  unzip -p sample-library/build/outputs/aar/*.aar proguard.txt
  2. Should show -keep rules for annotated classes.
  3. Test in consuming app:
    - Build a minified release build of the sample app
    - Verify no ClassNotFoundException for ViewModels/Fragments

title: [REL -1285] Update CI Workflow to Disable Shallow Cloning (Fix "Commit doesn't exist" Error) in Whetstone
body:
:clipboard: Jira Link
-
https://deliveryhero.atlassian.net/browse/REL-1285

:arrows_counterclockwise: Type of change:
-
Maintenance

:dart: What's the purpose of this PR?
- 
To make our CI pipeline more resilient to common git operations like rebasing, resetting, and force-pushing—especially during collaborative pull request workflows. Currently, shallow cloning (fetch-depth: 1) causes CI jobs to fail when a force-push updates a commit that is no longer reachable from the default history fetched by the runner.

This PR will disable shallow cloning by setting fetch-depth: 0 in the actions/checkout step, allowing the CI runner to access the full git history and reliably locate any commit referenced in PRs.

:memo: What is the impact of this change?
- 
- Prevents CI failures due to "Commit doesn't exist" errors after a force-push
- Improves reliability for contributors who rebase or squash commits during PRs
- Ensures tools like danger can access the full history they need

title: Update Anvil to fix gradle build cache issues
body:
Starting from `Kotlin 1.8.20` when [new approach to incremental compilation](https://kotlinlang.org/docs/gradle-compilation-and-caches.html#a-new-approach-to-incremental-compilation) was enabled by default, there is [an issue](https://github.com/square/anvil/issues/693) with Anvil's compiler failing to track changes in the source files with `@ContributesMultibinding` annotation.

Anvil's latest release [2.5.0](https://github.com/square/anvil/releases/tag/v2.5.0-beta01) helps to [fix the issue](https://github.com/square/anvil/pull/836), by offering a new feature that can track such changes in the source files, and available via `com.squareup.anvil.trackSourceFiles=true` config option.

To support this feature, `whetstone` needed to migrate its codegen logic from `Anvil's` `GeneratedFile` to `GeneratedFileWithSources` entity.

Apart from updating the Anvil version, also Dagger, Kotlin, and Compose dependencies were updated for compatibility purposes.

title: Multiplatform worfklow with windows fix
body:
This PR should supercede both of these:
- Closes #147 (that one was missing some test fixes which caused failures on windows)
- Closes #148 (that one is actually the same as the first three commits here, but this PR lets you see everything in action)

I developed this on my fork with the patch from @voczi from #147 as a starting point, picked into a branch where I worked on the workflow.

I made a PR into my fork's main branch to run CI (over and over and over) until I was sure I had it working

Test run showing success: https://github.com/mikehardy/keeper/actions/runs/9686107630

There is nothing fancy about the windows fix itself, it's standard `Path.separator()` and `System.lineSeparator()` stuff - exactly as you would expect

There are two fancy things about the workflow / test fixes:
- zip doesn't work on windows so the build reports artifact uses path declarations in the upload-artifact action instead of a find/zip-then-upload style
- toolchain doesn't work well on windows (I left a comment with reference to upstream issue) so for the test we cannot use gradle toolchain or it fails on windows

End result of all the work is that keeper will run on windows, will be verified working on windows in CI, *and* as a bonus you'll have your emulator tests hardware accelerated

Cheers

This PR replaces #213, which was an earlier attempt at migrating to TurboModules/New Architecture while maintaining backward compatibility with the Old Architecture.

The biggest change in direction: from v6 onward, only the New Architecture is supported. React Native has made New Architecture the default (since 0.76), and the old bridge is deprecated. Maintaining support for both architectures was a significant source of complexity in #213 and dropping Old Architecture support lets us move forward with a cleaner, more maintainable codebase.

title: Fix PriorityQueue type erasure incompatibility with Kotlin 2.2.20+
body:
This PR fixes NoSuchMethodError that occurs in Android/JVM tests when using Kotlin 2.2.20 or later versions.

Problem:
- Android/JVM tests were failing with NoSuchMethodError for methods like push(java.lang.Object) and peek()
- The issue started occurring after upgrading from Kotlin 2.2.10 to 2.2.20

```bash
$ ./gradlew :soil-query-core:jvmTest
Type-safe project accessors is an incubating feature.

> Task :soil-query-core:jvmTest

PriorityQueueTest[jvm] > testClean[jvm] FAILED
    java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: 'void soil.query.core.PriorityQueue.push(java.lang.Object)'
        at soil.query.core.PriorityQueueTest.testClean(PriorityQueueTest.kt:84)

PriorityQueueTest[jvm] > testEmpty[jvm] FAILED
    java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: 'java.lang.Object soil.query.core.PriorityQueue.peek()'
        at soil.query.core.PriorityQueueTest.testEmpty(PriorityQueueTest.kt:77)

PriorityQueueTest[jvm] > testPeek[jvm] FAILED
    java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: 'void soil.query.core.PriorityQueue.push(java.lang.Object)'
        at soil.query.core.PriorityQueueTest.testPeek(PriorityQueueTest.kt:52)
...
```

Root cause:
- Kotlin 2.2.20 changed how type erasure works for generic type parameters with multiple bounds
- With `where E : Any, E : Comparable<E>`, the compiled bytecode had method signatures using Comparable
- However, test code expected Object type signatures
- This mismatch caused NoSuchMethodError at runtime

(Kotlin 2.2.10)

```
$ javap -v PriorityQueue.class
..
Constant pool:
   ...
   #23 = Utf8               push
   #24 = Utf8               (Ljava/lang/Object;)V
   ...
```

(Kotlin 2.2.20)

```
$ javap -v PriorityQueue.class
..
Constant pool:
   ...
   #23 = Utf8               push
   #24 = Utf8               (Ljava/lang/Comparable;)V   
   ...
```

title: Fix implicit dependency error between JS and WASM-JS build tasks
body:
This PR fixes a Gradle build failure that occurred when running the assemble task with both JS and WASM-JS targets enabled. The build was failing with an implicit dependency error because both targets were using the same output module name. 

Error that was occurring:

```
Task ':sample:composeApp:jsBrowserProductionWebpack' uses this output of task
':sample:composeApp:wasmJsProductionExecutableCompileSync' without declaring
an explicit or implicit dependency.
```

Job: https://github.com/soil-kt/soil/actions/runs/18814402347/job/53680543736

Root cause: Both the JS and WASM-JS targets were configured with `outputModuleName = "composeApp"`, causing them to write to the same output directory `/build/js/packages/composeApp`.

title: Fix issue #119 by ensuring the existing runnable is cancelled
body:
## Description

As seen in https://github.com/twilio/audioswitch/issues/119

When switching away from a Bluetooth headset to the speaker (for example), then switching back to the Bluetooth headset, a few seconds later the audio will be switched back to the "earpiece".

After debugging this, I found that this happens because there are multiple `EnableBluetoothScoJob` runnables running, with one of them timing out, therefore causing the `AudioActivationError` state to be set and causing the behaviour of the connection having errored, although this isn't the case and audio is still heard through the BT headset.

This fixes the problem by ensuring that when we start a new `EnableBluetoothScoJob`, we cancel the existing runnable first (if it exists).

## Breakdown

- Added call to `Handler::removeCallbacks` within the `BluetoothScoJob::executeBluetoothScoJob` ensuring only one runnable is running.

## Validation

- Tested on a minimal sample app, switching between audio devices in a call, including powering off/on my BT headset at intervals. Working exactly as intended now.

## Additional Notes

n/a

title: Fix: rootCoverageReport ignores androidTests coverage results when executeAndroidTests is false
body:
# Problem 
In our project we are using gradle managed devices to execute ui tests. Ui tests launch configuration is a bit complicated in our use case, so I had to launch ui tests separately from `Android-Root-Coverage-Plugin`. And then after ui tests have finished it's execution, I am using `:rootCoverageReport"` The problem here, is that coverage results from ui tests are being ignored by `:rootCoverageReport`. This happens only with gradle managed devices, if I manually execute ui tests on connected emulator, and than use `:rootCoverageReport` to create aggregated coverage report, everything works as expected.

I have created new configuration `gradle-managed-device-dont-execute-android-tests.yaml` for `IntegrationTest.kt`, that reproduces the issue above.

# Solution

This pull request also contains fix of that problem. Here are key components of the fix:

1. It turned out that  subProject.getExecutionDataFileTree always received `includeGradleManagedDevicesResults = false`, in case of `executeAndroidTests` is false. Now that is fixed.
2. I had to switch from `project.tasks.findByPath("$path:allDevices${name}AndroidTest")` to `subProject.tasks.configureEach` inside `JacocoReport.addSubProjectVariant`. `project.tasks.findByPath` was always returing null, because task`$path:allDevices${name}AndroidTest` wasn't configured yet at the time `project.tasks.findByPath` is called.
3. The fix introduces explicit dependency between  ":rootCoverageReport" and "coverageReport" tasks of subprojects. Without this change, gradle build sometimes was failing with error like 
```text
Error: gradle Task : "rootCoverageReport" uses the output of task ':nexusoneapi30DebugAndroidTest" without declaring an explicit or implicit dependency.
```

This fixes #90. The root cause of this issue was the combination of `executeAndroidTests=false` combined with not having a Gradle Managed Device setup in the build.gradle file, this would cause the plugin to look for a task that did not exist in the graph:

```
Task with path ':app:allDevicesDebugAndroidTest' not found in project ':app'
```

This PR solves this issue, by checking if the task exists. It also makes sure to not add any Gradle Managed Device execution data to the JaCoCo report when we should be using connected device execution data (and vice versa).

I had to revamp the test setup quite a bit to allow for more flexible test cases, this allowed me to add a regression test for this issue to avoid it in the future.

body:
We should never have been seeing negative values for the size of annotations, as the byte that they
are stored in is unsigned. However, in the process of converting the byte to an int (kotlin has no
bitwise operators available to byte types), we were padding with a bunch of 1s causing it to be read
as a signed number. Forcing it down to an unsigned 8 bit value resolves this issue and lets us read the
values out correctly.

title: Fix reporting for default interface methods and private methods
body:
Previously, we were reporting both default interface methods and private methods that were annotated with @Test
as valid, when in reality neither is true. To fix this, we can take advantage of the differentiation the dex file
format makes in the class_data_item struct, which contains 2 sets of methods: direct_methods and virtual_methods.
For tests, all we really care about are the virtual methods, which are "none of static, private, or constructor"
methods on the class. So this updates our logic for both junit3 and junit4 to only look in the virtual_methods set
for tests.

Previously the padding above the header in the navigation drawer was fixed at 24dp. This works fine for the default Android status bar size, but breaks when the status bar is larger, for example because of a notch or a hole-punch camera.

The changes in this PR allow for the padding to dynamically adjust to the status bar size.

title: [Important] Fix crash due to multiple semaphore releases
body:
The code for deleting blank notes was moved into the `onStart` method in my fix for the note shortcuts. This doesn't make much sense, because `onStart` is going to be called whenever the MainActivity is reopened after being in the background.

As a result of this, the `_deletionFinishedSignal` is being released multiple times, even though the maximum number of permits is set to 1. This causes the app to crash.

Moving the code back to `init` (where it was in the first place) makes sure that the signal is only released once during the viewmodels lifecycle.

fix: bar not working below 128/255 opacity
body:
This is probably a dirty fix but it works for me. Tested on Pixel 9 Pro, latest GrapheneOS (Android 16).

In the code, you're setting the same alpha for both the window parameters and the view.
This means when the color is transparent (alpha = 0), both the window and the view become transparent and apparently on Android 16, transparent windows don't receive touch events.

This fix should ensure that the window itself always has some minimum opacity (at least 128/255) while keeping the actual view transparent.

As I said this is just a dirty fix so feel free to implement this properly if necessary, but this should be the main idea.

title: Lint fixes
Fix state restoration tests
Fix API issues stemming from Android 13/14 changes to location services
body:
# What was the problem

On newer Android 13 and 14 Devices, the startLocationService() function causes a fatal crash, causing the app to exit and show the error mentioned in https://github.com/Almoullim/background_location/issues/200.

# How was it fixed

In the linked issue is a fork that already adresses 1 one of the issues caused by the version change, namely the extra flag for the reicever exported status, but it has some other issues that arise from Android 13 as well.

I fixed the `registerReceiver` call by making a API level check and depending on version code, call the function with or without the flag, in order to still stay compatible with API level 26 and below where the flag does not exist, inspired by [this](https://stackoverflow.com/a/77529595) StackOverflow answer.

```kotlin
if(Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU) {
    registerReceiver(broadcastReceiver, filter, RECEIVER_EXPORTED)
} else {
    registerReceiver(broadcastReceiver, filter)
}
```

There was also another issue, caused be new permission requirements for the foreground service, where now need to more precisely define what kind of foreground service it is, which I added to the manifest.

```xml
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION" />
```

We also need to again change the function call signature of the foreground service to add the new permission type based on API level as before, inspired by [this](https://stackoverflow.com/a/76943772) StackOverflow answer.

```kotlin
if(Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU) {
    startForeground(NOTIFICATION_ID, notification.build(), ServiceInfo.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_LOCATION)
} else {
    startForeground(NOTIFICATION_ID, notification.build())
}
```

title: Fix a potential crash caused by ConcurrentModificationException
body:
### Crash logs

```
java.util.ConcurrentModificationException
  at java.util.ArrayList$Itr.checkForComodification
  at java.util.ArrayList$Itr.next
  at com.linecorp.apng.ApngDrawable.progressAnimationElapsedTime
  at com.linecorp.apng.ApngDrawable.draw
  at android.widget.ImageView.onDraw
```

### Steps to reproduce

If the client registers an animation callback multiple times—potentially due to timing issues or intentional actions by client apps—and then unregisters themselves during the callback execution (a reasonable approach), it triggers a `ConcurrentModificationException`.

#### Sample code

```kotlin
// repeat this action multiple times.
apngDrawable.registerAnimationCallback(object : Animatable2Compat.AnimationCallback() {
    override fun onAnimationEnd(drawable: Drawable?) {
        apngDrawable.unregisterAnimationCallback(this)
    }
})
```

body:
Currently, rendering frame index is calculated from total duration of image. However, APNG can have duration for each frames (fcTL section).

>The `delay_num` and `delay_den` parameters together specify a fraction indicating the time to display the current frame, in seconds. If the denominator is 0, it is to be treated as if it were 100 (that is, `delay_num` then specifies 1/100ths of a second). If the the value of the numerator is 0 the decoder should render the next frame as quickly as possible, though viewers may impose a reasonable lower bound.
>Frame timings should be independent of the time required for decoding and display of each frame, so that animations will run at the same rate regardless of the performance of the decoder implementation.

https://wiki.mozilla.org/APNG_Specification#.60fcTL.60:_The_Frame_Control_Chunk

title: Flutter bug fixes and enhancements
body:
### _Summary_

Why am I opening this PR? I have found an issue on your `felix/isConnected-flutter` branch (which I assume is the one you used to publish the latest Flutter SDK) where you are using the compilation directive `#if DEBUG` on your Swift's side plugin and this is breaking the app on Profile/Release mode.

The affected line is this one => https://github.com/MobileWalletProtocol/wallet-mobile-sdk/blob/71e5e38f46b35efe62485fc4a39bdfb7a0e92900/flutter/ios/Classes/SwiftCoinbaseWalletSdkFlutterPlugin.swift#L70

You have this directive also on branch `2.0` but you don't have in on main branch (the whole guard statement is missing on main branch).

The thing is that by not returning a result() to flutter (because of the compilation directive) on Profile/Release mode the App stucks on `await CoinbaseWalletSDK.shared.configure` call. This is causing a lot of troubles for users.

So, this PR basically merges the changes from `felix/isConnected-flutter` to main (without the compilation directive) and adds a few more valuable things.

Such as:

- Updated dependencies
- Added `ownPublicKey` and `peerPublicKey` methods **(Android side should be checked properly)**
- Added `WatchAsset()` object for rpc request
- Updated example files accordingly

Furthermore, it raise a concern in regards of the whole `CoinbaseWalletSDK.shared.configure` method, which is: Do we really needed? My conclusion is no. 
`configure` method shouldn't be called from Flutter side since the calling could happen too late raising an error when opening the app from terminated state.

So, since Flutter requires anyway iOS platform specific code https://github.com/MobileWalletProtocol/wallet-mobile-sdk/tree/main/flutter#ios-only it makes sense to call configure on native side as well as it is currently done for iOS native SDK https://github.com/MobileWalletProtocol/wallet-mobile-sdk/tree/main/ios#setup
Same situation for Android https://github.com/MobileWalletProtocol/wallet-mobile-sdk/tree/main/android#setup

### _How did you test your changes?_

- Smoke tests and manual tests

title: android: Fix disaster-detection-related bugs
body:
Resolves #36 

Before:
1. Permissions did not refresh on resume
2. Theme primary color on new SDKs used background
3. Service would run even if disaster detection was unavailable
4. It was possible to toggle disaster detection even when unavailable

After:
1. Permissions refresh on resume
2. Theme primary color is static
3. Service doesn't run if disaster detection is unavailable
4. Disaster detection switch is diabled when unavailable

Test:
1. Uninstall the app
2. Run the app with IDE
3. Do not allow permissions
4. Ensure the "SOS" button is red
5. Open the Settings inside the app

title: fix(player): chapter tap while paused starts audiobook playback
body:
## Root cause

`AudiobookPlayerViewModel.seekTo` called `controller.seekTo` but never `controller.play`. Tapping a chapter from the chapter list calls `viewModel.seekTo(chapter.startSec)`, so while playing this worked fine (the seek moved the playhead and playback continued), but while paused it only moved the playhead and left the player paused.

The same bug affected the prev/next chapter transport buttons, which also called `controller.seekTo` directly without resuming play.

## Fix

Extracted `seekAndResumeIfPaused` (in `SkipIntervals.kt`, alongside `resumePositionSec`) which seeks then calls `play()` when `isPlaying` is false. `seekTo` delegates to it and also clears the sleep-stopped flag on resume, matching `togglePlayPause`. `previousChapter`/`nextChapter` now call `seekTo` instead of `controller.seekTo` directly.

## Test

`ChapterSeekAutoPlayTest` in `feature/player/src/commonTest` — two assertions:
- `seekWhilePausedCallsPlayAfterSeek`: verifies `play()` is called after `seek()` when `isPlaying = false`. Fails on revert.
- `seekWhileAlreadyPlayingDoesNotCallPlay`: verifies `play()` is not called a second time when already playing. Fails if the guard is removed.

Runs on JVM and `iosSimulatorArm64` (module is wired in `.github/workflows/ios.yml` line 151).

## Platform parity

Fix is in `commonMain`. Both Android and iOS share the same `AudiobookPlayerViewModel.seekTo` code path. No iOS-specific work needed.

title: fix(player): mark-as-read uses item's own source ID, not the active source
body:
## Root cause

`MarkReadAcrossDimensions.invoke` and `ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl.markFinished` both called `sourceRepository.getActive()?.id` to determine which `library_items` row to write to. When a radio.es podcast was marked as read (via the item-detail sheet or by completing playback from the Riffle source page) while ABS was the active source, every DAO write and progress update targeted `(absSourceId, podcastId)` — a non-existent row — so the writes were silent no-ops. The podcast remained in-progress on the home tab even after reaching 100%.

## Fix

Thread the caller-supplied `sourceId` from `LibraryItemDetailViewModel.markAsRead/markAsUnread` all the way down through `MarkReadAcrossDimensions` → `ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl.markFinished` → the DAO writes. Both `ReadingSessionRepository` interface and `MarkReadAcrossDimensions.invoke` gained a `sourceId` parameter; all call sites updated. The ABS peer PATCH still fires correctly for ABS items (`catalogRegistry.forSourceId(absSourceId)` returns the ABS catalog); for radio.es items the push is gracefully skipped while the local DB write succeeds.

## iOS parity

The fix lives entirely in `commonMain`:
- `MarkReadAcrossDimensions` is `commonMain`; iOS calls it via the same Koin binding.
- `ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl` is `commonMain`; iOS shares the same implementation.
- `MarkReadAcrossDimensionsTest` (regression test added) lives in `commonTest` and runs on iOS via `:core:domain:iosSimulatorArm64Test` (already in `ios.yml`). Confirmed passing.

title: fix(reader): clamp Chromium to maxScrollPx to fix ch-end blank screen (take 3)
body:
## Root cause

JS `HEIGHT_MEASUREMENT_JS` uses `Math.ceil(cssH * dpr)` which gives `contentH=146819` on an S23 (dpr=2.625), so `maxOffset=139259`. Chromium floors its own layout → `maxScrollPx=139258`. The 1-px gap means `wantedPx(139259) > maxScrollPx(139258)`.

**Previous fix (PR #1158) — ADOPT was wrong:** When Chromium drifted to `scrollY=136739`, ADOPT set `translationY=136739`. The WebView's bottom then sat at `136739+7560=144299` — exactly the top of the last viewport of ch01. The entire last screen was blank.

## Fix

New `CLAMP_TO_MAX` correction: call `scrollTo(0, maxSc=139258)` **without** touching `translationY`. The subsequent `onScrollChanged(139258)` hits the existing sub-px ADOPT path (`abs(139258−139259)=1 ≤ tolerance=3`), which sets `windowOffsetPx=139258` and `translationY=139258`. Both stabilise with the invariant restored and the WebView covering the chapter end.

CLAMP_TO_MAX only fires when Chromium has drifted significantly (drift > tolerance) — once it fires and the subsequent ADOPT runs, Chromium is at `maxSc` and the guard `abs(reportedPx - maxScrollPx) ≤ tolerance` blocks CLAMP_TO_MAX from re-firing.

## Verification

Verified on Samsung S23 reading the affected book: footnotes 19–27 at the end of ch01 (including footnote 27 — "Anton Bacaj told me…") are fully visible, immediately followed by the "Chapter 2. Understanding Foundation Models" heading with no blank area.

## Changes

- `ContinuousPositionTracker.kt` — adds `CLAMP_TO_MAX` to `InternalScrollCorrection` enum; changes the 1-px-overshoot-with-large-drift case from `ADOPT` to `CLAMP_TO_MAX`
- `ContinuousWindowController.kt` — handles `CLAMP_TO_MAX` by calling `scrollTo(maxSc)` only, without updating `windowOffsetPx`/`translationY`; removes debug logging
- `ContinuousPositionTrackerTest.kt` — updates large-drift test to assert `CLAMP_TO_MAX`; adds tests for settle guard, sub-px ADOPT at maxSc, and large-overshoot NONE; fixes physically-impossible `reportedPx` in large-overshoot test

## Summary

When completing a radio.es podcast from the Home tab, `readingProgress` was never written to the database — the podcast stayed "in progress" forever.

**Root cause**: `AudiobookPlayerViewModel.positionSaveCoordinator` called `updateReadingProgressUseCase(itemId, progress)` (single-arg overload), which uses `sourceRepository.getActive()?.id` for the SQL `UPDATE`'s `WHERE` clause. When the active source was ABS (the common case when opening from the Home tab), the `UPDATE WHERE source_id = 'abs-id' AND item_id = 'x'` hit 0 rows for a radio.es podcast — leaving `readingProgress` unchanged.

**Fix**: one line in `AudiobookPlayerViewModel.kt` — switch to the two-arg overload `updateReadingProgressUseCase(sourceId, itemId, progress)` so the DB write always targets the correct `(navSourceId, itemId)` row regardless of which source is currently active.

This is the same class of fix as commit `2aad63ac6` which corrected `sourceId` for the position store and ABS sync paths but missed the `updateProgress` lambda.

title: fix(player): sync web-source podcast partial progress via WebDAV
body:
## Root cause

`AudiobookPlayerViewModel` wired `PositionSaveCoordinator` with the single-arg `UpdateReadingProgress.invoke(itemId, progress)` overload (line 143). That overload resolves `sourceId` internally via `sourceRepository.getActive()?.id` — the primary ABS/Komga server, not the web source. For podcast episodes (`isWebSource = true`), the write hit the wrong `(absServerId, podcastItemId)` row in `library_items`, or no row at all.

`WebDavProgressRemote.patch()` reads `readingProgress` from the correct `(webSourceId, itemId)` row of `library_items`. Since that row was never updated during playback, the WebDAV JSON always contained `readingProgress = 0f` for partially played episodes.

On device B: the audio position in seconds **was** synced correctly (stored in `audiobook_positions`), so the player would resume at the right spot. But `library_items.readingProgress = 0f` meant the library always showed the episode as 0% / "not started".

Fully-finished episodes appeared to work because the player reaching `position ≥ duration - ε` on device B causes it to present the episode as ready-to-restart regardless of `readingProgress`.

## Fix

`AudiobookPlayerViewModel.kt` line 143: use the two-arg `UpdateReadingProgress.invoke(sourceId, itemId, progress)` overload with the explicit `sourceId` that is already available as a private field in the ViewModel. This writes to the correct `library_items` row so WebDAV sync uploads the real listen fraction.

## Regression test

`feature/player/src/commonTest/.../WebSourceProgressOnCloseTest.kt` — two tests:

1. `onCloseWritesProgressWithExplicitWebSourceId` — verifies that wiring the coordinator with the fixed lambda results in `LibraryMutator.updateReadingProgress(sourceId, itemId, progress)` (two-arg) being called, not the single-arg path.
2. `onCloseWithSingleArgOverloadWouldWriteToWrongRow` — documents that the old (single-arg) path produces a `SingleArg` call (no sourceId), confirming the route that caused the bug.

The assertion that would flip if the fix were reverted: `assertEquals(webSourceId, call.sourceId)` — after reverting line 143, the call would be a `SingleArg` and the `as?` cast would produce `null`, throwing from `error(...)`.

- [x] No platform-specific copy added

title: fix(reader): fix readaloud sentence highlight after colour change (app restart no longer required)
body:
## Root cause

`PlayerCoordinator` is a Koin `single` (app-lifetime singleton), but `EpubReaderViewModel.onCleared()` was calling `playerCoordinator.dispose()`, which permanently cancels the coordinator's internal `CoroutineScope`.

`AudioClockTicker`'s state-collection coroutine runs in that scope — the one that resolves the audio-clock position to `activeFragmentRef`. Once the scope is cancelled, the coroutine can never restart. Every subsequent reader session sees `activeFragmentRef = null` and no sentence highlight appears, regardless of the stored colour.

The only fix was an app restart, which recreates the Koin singleton and its scope from scratch. The colour-change repro path:

1. Open reader → start readaloud (yellow highlight visible)
2. Navigate back — `onCleared()` fires, `dispose()` cancels the singleton scope
3. Go to Settings → Readaloud → change colour to blue
4. Reopen reader → **no highlight** (scope is dead, `activeFragmentRef` permanently null)

The bug exists after every first reader close, but becomes visible specifically when a colour change is involved, because that's when users compare "before" and "after".

`PlayerCoordinatorScopeTest` already pinned the `single` registration. This PR adds a second test pinning that `onCleared()` never calls `dispose()`.

## Android fix

Remove the `playerCoordinator.dispose()` call from `EpubReaderViewModel.onCleared()`. The singleton's scope must live for the app's lifetime. The `close()` call (nulls `track`, resets ticker) is kept — it is correct and unaffected.

Updated `PlayerCoordinator`'s KDoc (previously said "not a @Singleton", now describes it correctly as an app-lifetime singleton) and the `dispose()` method's KDoc to warn against calling it on a live singleton.

## iOS fix (Cadence highlight colour change)

iOS does not yet have readaloud sentence tracking, so the `AudioClockTicker` / `dispose()` issue does not manifest there. However the same "colour change doesn't take effect" symptom appeared for **Cadence** highlights on iOS.

The initial fix on this branch re-keyed the cadence `LaunchedEffect` on `cadenceHighlightColor`, which had a side effect: restarting the effect reset `followedRef = null`, so the next `combine` emission treated the already-visible sentence as newly changed and called `followCadenceSpan` / `goTo` — an unintended chapter navigation triggered by a plain colour change.

Final fix: split the single effect into two:

1. **Main paint+follow** `LaunchedEffect(cadence, navigator)` — unchanged, `followedRef` is only ever reset when `ref` actually changes.
2. **Colour-repaint** `LaunchedEffect(cadence, navigator, cadenceHighlightColor)` — re-applies the current sentence decoration with the new colour immediately on colour change, without touching `followedRef`.

## Call path — iOS colour-repaint

`SettingsViewModel.updateGlobalFormattingPreferences(prefs)` → `IosFormattingPreferencesStoreImpl.update(prefs)` → `_preferences.value = prefs` → `resolvedPrefs.cadenceHighlightColor` changes → colour-repaint `LaunchedEffect` restarts → `cadence.currentFragment.value` (snapshot) → `navigator.applyDecorations(DECORATION_GROUP_CADENCE, [cadenceDecoration(…, color = newColor)])`.

## Tests

| Test | Platform | What it pins |
|------|----------|-------------|
| `PlayerCoordinatorScopeTest: AppKoinModules registers PlayerCoordinator as a singleton` | Android JVM | `single { PlayerCoordinator(…)` must be in AppKoinModules |
| `PlayerCoordinatorScopeTest: EpubReaderViewModel onCleared does not call playerCoordinator dispose` | Android JVM | No non-comment `playerCoordinator.dispose()` in `onCleared` — fails if the call is reintroduced |
| `ReadiumHighlightRendererTest: applySentenceHighlight re-applies with new color when called again with same ref` | Android JVM | Same ref + different colour → CLEAR + APPLY with new `HighlightTintStyle.tint` |
| `CadenceDecorationTest: changingColourProducesADecorationWithTheNewColour` | commonTest (iOS) | `cadenceDecoration` with BLUE vs YELLOW produces distinct `color` fields |

title: fix(reader): continuous mode reopens at correct position
body:
## Root causes

Three separate bugs combined to produce the wrong reopen position in continuous mode:

### 1. Anchor-based landing for position restoration (`EpubReaderScreen.kt`)

`cfiStringToLocator` places DOM element IDs in `locations.fragments`. The `LaunchedEffect(continuousView)` was unconditionally appending these as `#anchor` to the href, triggering `resolveAnchorThenLand` which places the element top at the viewport top — ignoring the −vh/2 midpoint correction and the progression within the element. This caused a jump of several pages forward. Fix: only use the anchor when `focusId != null` (annotation nav); never for plain position restoration.

### 2. Same anchor issue in `ContinuousPresenter.ToLocatorJson` navigation

Server-sync position jumps were also anchor-landed via `locations.fragments`, so cross-device synced positions had the same drift. Fix: always use progression-based landing in `ToLocatorJson`; strip the anchor entirely.

### 3. Top-chapter height change reverts scroll compensation during landing hold (`ContinuousWindowController.kt`)

When the top chapter (i == 0) changes height after the initial land (e.g. images load and the chapter shrinks), `port.scrollBy(delta)` fires to compensate. `tickLandingHold` then runs on the next animation frame and reverts the scroll back to the stale `landingHoldTargetY`, while `slot.top` for the target chapter has already moved by the same delta. `onPositionChanged` then reads the reverted scroll against the updated slot and reports a progression `delta / targetHeight` higher than saved. The non-top, non-target branch (line 1533) already updates `landingHoldTargetY += delta` before scrolling; the i == 0 path was missing this. Fix: add the same update before `port.scrollBy(delta)` in the i == 0 block.

## Tests

- `ContinuousPresenterTest`: `navigateTo ToLocatorJson ignores fragment anchor — uses progression-based landing` — asserts `href` has no `#anchor` suffix and progression is 0.42f.
- `ContinuousWindowControllerScrollGateTest`: `i==0 height change updates landingHoldTargetY before scrollBy so tickLandingHold does not revert the compensation` — asserts `landingHoldTargetY += delta` precedes `port.scrollBy(delta)` in the i == 0 block.

## Verification

Verified on device (continuous mode): reopening a book returns to the pixel-identical paragraph and progress percentage (21.3%) after images have fully loaded, across multiple close/reopen cycles.

## iOS parity

All three fixes are in Android-specific continuous-mode infrastructure (`EpubNavigatorFragment` / `ContinuousWindowController` / `ContinuousPresenter`). iOS uses the Readium Swift SDK's native position restoration, which does not use CFI fragment anchoring or the `landingHoldTargetY` mechanism. The bug cannot manifest on iOS; no iOS change is required.

title: fix(readaloud): auto-retry transient download failures — bundle and streaming paths
body:
## What

Readaloud downloads from the **books library** (Storyteller bundle path) were failing on transient network interruptions and required up to 20 manual retry taps to complete. The download would resume from the correct byte offset on each retry (`.part` file preserved), but no automatic retry was attempted.

Both download paths now retry on transient network failures with exponential backoff:

| Attempt | Delay |
|---------|-------|
| 1 | 2 s |
| 2 | 4 s |
| 3 | 8 s |
| 4 | 16 s |
| 5 | 30 s |

Up to 5 attempts. Auth failures and explicit HTTP error codes (4xx/5xx) are not retried — they require user action.

## Changes

### `AudiobookBundleDownloader` (books-library Storyteller path)
- Wraps the single `withBundleStream` call in a retry loop
- Each retry recomputes `resumeFrom` from the current `.part` file length so the `Range` header picks up exactly where disk I/O last flushed
- Excludes `HttpStatusFailureException` from retry: `KtorClassifier` maps all `IOException`s to `NetworkResult.Offline` (including HTTP status failures, which extend `IOException`), so 401/403/404 would have been silently retried without this guard

### `StreamingAudioDownloader` (ABS streaming path)
- Wraps each `CacheWriter.cache()` call in a retry loop
- Excludes `HttpDataSource.InvalidResponseCodeException` (ExoPlayer's class for explicit HTTP error codes) from the `IOException` catch

### `IosAudiobookTrackDownloader` (iOS parity)
- Same retry loop added to `downloadOne`
- Excludes `HttpChannelException` (explicit HTTP error codes via `withHttpChannelStream`)

### Test fixes
- `FakeApi.withBundleStream` now maps `IOException` from inside the block to `NetworkResult.Offline`, matching `KtorClassifier`'s real behaviour
- `truncatedStream_isNotFinalised_andPartIsKeptForResume` updated to use `honorRange = false` so retries always see the same truncated body and exhaust the attempt count

## Tests

**Android (new):**
- `AudiobookBundleDownloaderTest.transientNetworkFailure_retriesAndEventuallySucceeds`
- `StreamingAudioDownloaderAndroidTest.download_retries_on_transient_server_error_and_fills_cache`

**iOS (new):**
- `IosAudiobookOfflineTest.download retries on transient network failure and eventually succeeds`

## Emulator OOM note

Verification on emulator-5556 (API-25) produced an `OutOfMemoryError` crash during the bundle download. This is a **pre-existing emulator limitation** — confirmed by reproducing the identical crash with the baseline APK (before this fix). The API-25 emulator has insufficient heap for a large Storyteller bundle. The crash does not occur on modern devices.

title: fix(reader): use postAfterLayout in applyChapterHeight to close ch1-end cutoff
body:
## Root cause

`#1134` added `port.post { syncChapterWindows() }` to `applyChapterHeight` to re-sync the chapter-window after the layout pass updated `wv.height`. But `port.post` is `View.post` — it queues on the Handler and runs **before** the Choreographer-driven layout traversal (VSYNC). The posted sync therefore fired while `wv.height` was still the old placeholder, not the new cap. Chromium then clamped the internal scroll to `contentH − cap` once the layout ran, leaving a gap of `(cap − placeholder)` px — up to ~1576 px on tall-screen Samsung devices — permanently invisible at the end of the chapter.

## Fix

Replace `port.post` with `port.postAfterLayout` (= `doOnNextLayout` on `ContinuousReaderView`). `doOnNextLayout` fires after the full descendant layout traversal, at which point `wv.height == cap`. `syncChapterWindows` then computes the correct offset and both `translationY` and internal `scrollY` are set to `contentH − cap`, closing the gap.

## Why the #1134 test didn't catch this

The regression test in `ContinuousPositionTrackerTest` proved the *algorithm* — it called `chapterWebViewWindowOffset` directly with `webViewHeightPx = cap` and asserted the gap is closed. It didn't (and can't, in a JVM test) verify that `port.post` delivers `wv.height = cap` when it fires on a real Android device. The test was correct; the wiring was wrong.

## New gate test

Adds a source-scanning test to `ContinuousWindowControllerScrollGateTest` (following the same pattern as the `#1109` / `landOnAnnotationOffset` gate) that fails if `applyChapterHeight` reverts to bare `port.post {`. This pins both the algorithm and the scheduling primitive.

title: fix(audio): headphone next/prev skips ±N seconds instead of navigating chapters
body:
## Root cause

On both platforms, the hardware headphone next/previous buttons trigger a different command than the on-screen ⟲/⟳ buttons:

- **Android:** the headphone buttons produce \`Player.COMMAND_SEEK_TO_NEXT\` / \`COMMAND_SEEK_TO_NEXT_MEDIA_ITEM\` (and prev variants), which Media3's default handling routes to \`seekToNextMediaItem()\` — chapter navigation.
- **iOS:** the headphone buttons fire \`nextTrackCommand\` / \`previousTrackCommand\` on \`MPRemoteCommandCenter\`, which were calling \`onTrackDelta(±1)\` — chapter navigation.

The notification/lock-screen ⟲⟳ buttons already used \`CMD_REWIND\`/\`CMD_FORWARD\` (Android) and \`skipBackwardCommand\`/\`skipForwardCommand\` (iOS), so only the headphone path was wrong.

## Fix

**Android** (\`HeadphoneSkip.kt\`, \`AbsolutePositionPlayer.kt\`): extract \`headphoneSkipTargetMs()\` as a testable pure function, then override \`seekToNext()\` / \`seekToNextMediaItem()\` / \`seekToPrevious()\` / \`seekToPreviousMediaItem()\` in \`AbsolutePositionPlayer\` to call it. The behavior is now in the player rather than an \`onPlayerCommandRequest\` callback, so the command proceeds with \`RESULT_SUCCESS\` — Android Auto and Bluetooth HID controllers never see a \`RESULT_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED\` and won't gray out the button.

**iOS** (\`IosAudioPlayerBridgeImpl.swift\`): change the \`nextTrackCommand\` and \`previousTrackCommand\` handlers to call \`onSkip(deltaSec: ±skipIntervals.*Sec)\` instead of \`onTrackDelta(±1)\`, matching what \`skipForwardCommand\`/\`skipBackwardCommand\` already do.

## Design note

The previous Media3 behaviour for \`COMMAND_SEEK_TO_PREVIOUS\` includes a "return to chapter start" threshold (if within a few seconds of chapter start, go back to the previous chapter; otherwise go to the current chapter start). The user's explicit request is "headphone next/prev must do rewind or forward x seconds — same as the player buttons." The in-app player buttons have no such threshold, so intercepting both prev commands for a uniform backward-skip is intentional.

## Tests

- \`HeadphoneSkipTargetTest\` (Android JVM, 9 assertions): forward/backward skip, clamp-at-duration, clamp-at-zero, unknown-duration, zero-duration (edge case where \`TIME_UNSET\` guard would have passed on a 0-duration item), and that non-next/prev commands return \`null\`.
- \`IosAudioPlayerControllerTest\` (Kotlin/iOS): two new tests (\`remoteSkipForwardSeeksWithinTheCurrentTrack\`, \`remoteSkipBackwardSeeksWithinTheCurrentTrack\`) verify that \`onSkip(±N)\` at mid-track position stays on the same track rather than navigating chapters.

\`Parity-skip: HeadphoneSkipTargetTest\` — the Android test exercises routing through androidx.media3 integer constants that have no KMP equivalent. The iOS behavior is covered by the two new \`IosAudioPlayerControllerTest\` scenarios.

title: fix(sync): ABS progress sync — clamp last-page to 100%, send explicit isFinished, fix rounding
body:
## What

Four ABS reading-progress bugs, all reported from a single continuous-mode book:

1. **99% stuck** — last page never pushed 100% to ABS
2. **isFinished not set** — book stayed in Continue Reading even after reaching 100%
3. **ABS finished state not cleared** — reading back to 98% on a finished book left ABS still showing Finished
4. **Display rounding** — 98.6% progress showed as 98% in the detail screen

---

## Root causes and fixes

### 1 & 2 — Paginated/vertical: `totalProgression` never reaches 1.0

Readium's `totalProgression` for the last page of a spine is `(N−1)/N` (positions mark page starts, not ends). The last page of a 100-page book reads as `0.99`, not `1.0`.

**Fix**: `finishAwareEbookProgress()` in `core:domain` compares `totalProgression` against `(total−1)/total` and clamps to `1.0f` when the reader is on the final page. Applied at both close-path call sites in `EpubReaderViewModel` and `IosEpubReaderScreen`.

### 1 — Continuous mode: short final chapter produces 0% progression

When the last chapter is shorter than half a viewport, the midpoint measurement (used by `ContinuousPositionTracker.locatorAt`) falls below the chapter's top at `maxScrollY`, giving `rawProgression = 0.0` and a total below the finished threshold.

**Fix**: `ContinuousPositionTracker.adjustProgressionAtForwardBoundary()` returns `1.0f` when `isLastChapter && maxScrollY > 0 && scrollY >= maxScrollY`. Called from `ContinuousWindowController.handleScrollChange()` before `onRawPosition` fires.

### 3 — `isFinished` flag sticky in ABS

ABS's `isFinished` flag does NOT clear when the field is omitted from the PATCH. The old code passed `isFinished = null` (omitted via `encodeDefaults=false`) for mid-book progress, leaving a previously-finished book in the Finished state forever.

Confirmed via direct API test: `PATCH {isFinished: false}` clears the flag; `PATCH {}` (omitted) keeps it.

**Fix**: Both push sites in `ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl` (`syncProgress` and `runSyncCycle` LocalWins) now pass `isFinished = isFinishedReadingProgress(ebookProgress)` — an explicit `Boolean`. Progress ≥ 1.0 → `true`; progress < 1.0 → `false` (explicitly clears).

### 4 — `toInt()` truncates

`(progress * 100).toInt()` truncates toward zero: 98.6% → 98%.

**Fix**: `roundToInt().coerceIn(0, 100)`. Extracted as `progressPercent()` helper for testability.

---

## Code-review fixes (same PR)

- `finishAwareEbookProgress`: when `totalProgression` is null, the old code compared per-chapter `progression` (0..1) against the book-wide `lastPageThreshold`, falsely returning `1.0f` for early chapters with high within-chapter progress. Fix: return `progression` unchanged when `totalProgression` is absent.
- `adjustProgressionAtForwardBoundary`: added `maxScrollY > 0` guard so books that fit entirely in the viewport (can't scroll) don't immediately fire the boundary override on arrival.

---

## Tests

- `FinishedProgressTest`: 9 tests for `finishAwareEbookProgress` including the null-fallback false-positive multi-spine case
- `ContinuousPositionTrackerTest`: 5 tests for `adjustProgressionAtForwardBoundary` including the `maxScrollY=0` edge case
- `ReadingSessionRepositoryImplTest`: 4 tests verifying `isFinished` Boolean is propagated correctly through both push paths
- `LibraryItemDetailPublicationFactsTest`: 3 tests for `progressPercent` including the rounding regression

---

## iOS parity

- `IosEpubReaderScreen.kt`: close path updated to use `finishAwareEbookProgress` with `spineRef.value.positionCounts`
- Sync changes (`ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl`) are in `commonMain` — both platforms share the implementation
- `finishAwareEbookProgress` and `adjustProgressionAtForwardBoundary` are in `commonMain` / `feature:reader commonMain` — iOS exercises the same code

title: fix(reader): restore exact reading position on reopen
body:
Two bugs caused the reader to open at the wrong position on reopen.

## Root cause A — wrong source in runSyncCycle

`ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl.runSyncCycle` used `sourceRepository.getActive()` to resolve
the catalog. When a book's source is not the active source, `getActive()` returns null →
`Offline` → progress never pushed to ABS → server retains stale old position → next
`pullItem` at open sees server newer → overwrites local position with wrong chapter.

**Fix:** add `sourceId: String? = null` to `runSyncCycle` interface and `ProgressSyncController.sync`.
`EpubReaderViewModel`, `PdfReaderViewModel`, `IosEpubReaderScreen`, and `IosPdfReaderScreen`
pass the book's own `sourceId`, routing around `getActive()` entirely. The null fallback
preserves the existing path for callers that don't have a sourceId (e.g. mark-read flows).

## Root cause B — clock-skew ServerWins jump after every LocalWins push

ABS `PATCH /api/me/progress/:id` does not return `lastUpdate` in the response body (stamp=0).
`runSyncCycle` LocalWins branch fell back to `clock.nowMs()` for `markSyncedAt`. ABS stores
the position with its own server clock, typically 50–100ms ahead of device clock. On the next
30-second heartbeat, `pullProgress` returns `serverLastUpdate > lastSyncedAt` (server-clock
ahead of device-clock fallback) → `!localDirty && serverAdvanced` → ServerWins → reader
jumps to the ABS-stored position even though it's the same content the device just pushed,
causing a visible scroll back on every heartbeat cycle.

**Fix:** after a LocalWins push where stamp==0, do a follow-up `pullProgress` to fetch the
server's actual storage timestamp and use that for `markSyncedAt`. Next cycle sees
`serverLastUpdate == lastSyncedAt` → InSync, no jump.

## Verified on AVD 5554

1. Open "AI Engineering" → navigate to ch03.html 32%
2. Exit reader
3. Reopen → restores to ch03.html 32%, position stable (logcat confirmed no ServerWins fires)

## Regression tests

- `zero-stamp PATCH follow-up GET prevents clock-skew ServerWins on next cycle` — asserts
  `lastSyncedAt` equals the ABS server stamp, not device clock
- `explicit sourceId syncs correctly when getActive returns null` — asserts `runSyncCycle`
  works even when `getActive()` returns null for the book's source
- `runSyncCycle returns Offline when both sourceId is null and getActive returns null`

## iOS parity

`IosEpubReaderScreen` and `IosPdfReaderScreen` updated to pass `item.sourceId` to `runSyncCycle`.
Both bugs are in `ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl` (`commonMain`), tested in `ProgressSyncIntegrationTest`.
The same implementation runs on iOS; the iOS-specific change (adding `item.sourceId` argument)
is compile-time enforced by the updated interface.

## Code review

- *Failed push returns LocalWins* — pre-existing behavior, no change in semantics
- *Follow-up pull may return cached response* — speculative; ABS progress GETs are not cached
- *`ProgressSyncCycleTest` weak assertions on zero-stamp path* — pre-existing; the new `ProgressSyncIntegrationTest` test pins the fix with `assertEquals(serverStamp, positionStore.updatedTimestamp)`
- *`syncSourceId` var race* — no real race; heartbeat starts after `syncSourceId` is set in the same `onOpenReady` coroutine

## Summary

Six `glee` audits covered the whole repo (core cross-platform logic, Android non-UI, Android UI, resources/tests/build config, webruntime/templates, docs/website/root config). This PR fixes what they found.

**Correctness bugs**
- `StateDelegate.clearLog()` no longer wipes AI chat history alongside the logs
- `RetryInterceptor` was fully built and unit-tested but never wired into the production `OkHttpClient` — GitHub API calls got zero retry/backoff. Moved it to the shared source set and wired it into `GithubApiClient`

- "Generate Project Docs (AI)" fired its prompt before project scaffolding finished; now passed as `saveAndInitialize`'s `initialPrompt` so it's dispatched only after scaffolding completes

title: Fix missing web runtime in Releases APKs + crash-reporting & AI-tooling correctness bugs
body:
## Summary

Ten independent fixes from this session's glee audits, stacked on one branch/PR (each commit is self-contained; see commit messages for full detail on any one).

1. **GitHub Releases APKs missing the web preview runtime** — `:webruntime`'s dynamic-feature assets were never fused into the published APK. Fixed via `bundletool build-apks --mode=universal`.
2. **Crash-reporting consent bypasses + dead code** — non-fatal reporting ignored the consent toggle when a Jules key was set; first-run dialog dismiss left reporting on; `LogSanitizer` gaps; hardcoded fake app version; two fully-dead interceptor classes.
3. **`apply_patch` approval-gate bypass + JSON-null corruption** — a chained prefix-strip could drop a deleted file from approval tracking entirely; `contentOrNullSafe()`'s dead branches turned JSON `null` into `"null"`.
4. **`chat()` error strings rendered as normal replies.**
5. **Unconditional WebView hard-reload on every AI turn**, even with zero file changes.
6. **`ideaz-loader.js` deadlocked forever on a direct import cycle** — `inputCache` returned a still-pending promise to itself.
7. **Preview navigated to root `index.html` even when the real entry lived elsewhere** — `findWebEntryPoint`'s result was discarded after the null-check.
8. **The `file:line` tap label's line-number capture was unreachable by construction** — a lazy quantifier before an optional group with nothing mandatory after it. Confirmed independently via `jshell`.
9. **`jsxs()` array children changed shape versus real React** — spreading into `createElement`'s variadic arguments turned an empty list into `undefined` children instead of `[]`, and silenced key warnings.
10. **`data-ideaz-source` on any ancestor silently overrode the accurate per-element source** — checked before the React fiber source and returned immediately, despite the docstring calling it a fallback.

## Verification

- Full local `assembleRelease`/`bundleDebug`/`bundleRelease` + bundletool fuse smoke test (both variants, 21/21 runtime files present).
- `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest` passes throughout, with new regression tests for `LogSanitizer`, `IdeTools.captureToolEdit`, `WebProjectPathHandler`'s SPA fallback, `WebProjectUrlUtils`, and `ContextualChatOverlay`'s label helpers.
- Five new real-execution JS tests (real loader, real vendored React/Babel, or the bridge's own extracted bytes — no mocks of the code under test) wired into `pr-check.yml`: JSX source chain (pre-existing), import-cycle handling, array-children shape, and fiber-vs-declared source priority. Each one fails against the pre-fix code and passes against the fix — verified by temporarily reverting each fix and re-running.
- `./gradlew :app:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` clean after every change.

title: Fix 7 Dependabot Jackson alerts: the pin only reached :app
body:
Closes #56, #57, #58, #59, #81, #83, #95.

## The bug

The 2026-08-21 bump to Jackson 2.18.10 was real and correctly patched `:app`. It just never reached `:webruntime`.

The pin was `configurations.all { resolutionStrategy { ... } }` inside `app/build.gradle.kts` — a **per-project** block, scoped to `:app`'s own configurations. `:webruntime` depends on `:app`, so it inherits the *dependencies* (google-genai, and Jackson through it) but not the *resolution rules* applied to them. Its own `releaseRuntimeClasspath` kept resolving Jackson to whatever google-genai itself requests: **2.17.2**, vulnerable to every one of the seven CVEs the 2.18.10 pin exists to close.

`dependency-submission.yml` submits both modules' release runtime graphs, so the SBOM carried both Jackson versions side by side, and Dependabot correctly kept flagging the 2.17.2 copy — a real vulnerability, not a stale-alert artifact.

Confirmed directly, not inferred:

```
:app:dependencies       → com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind:2.17.2 -> 2.18.10
:webruntime:dependencies → com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind:2.17.2   (resolved, full stop)
```

| Alert | Severity | Affected (per advisory) | 2.17.2 hit? |
|---|---|---|---|
| #56 PolymorphicTypeValidator bypass | High | `<=2.18.7` | ✅ |
| #57 array subtype allowlist bypass | High | `<2.18.8` | ✅ |
| #83 async maxNumberLength bypass | High | `<2.18.8` | ✅ |
| #58 InetSocketAddress SSRF | Moderate | `<2.18.8` | ✅ |
| #59 case-insensitive @JsonIgnoreProperties bypass | Moderate | `<2.18.9` | ✅ |
| #81 Record @JsonIgnore bypass | Moderate | `<2.18.8` | ✅ |
| #95 maxNumberLength (2nd variant) | Moderate | `<=2.18.5` | ✅ |

## The fix

Moved the whole `resolutionStrategy` block to a root-level `subprojects { }` in `build.gradle.kts`, so it applies to every module by construction — `:app`, `:webruntime`, and whatever comes next — rather than by someone remembering to copy it.

Re-verified with `:dependencies` on both modules: every Jackson artifact resolves to 2.18.10, no stray requested-version copies anywhere.

## Why `assembleRelease` specifically

Two earlier attempts at this same Jackson version (2026-08-16, 2026-08-17) reverted after `:app:packageRelease` failures with no diagnosable cause. Neither reproduced when 2.18.10 was pinned in isolation on 2026-08-21, and there's no reason widening the pin's *scope* would cause it either — but `packageRelease` is exactly where they broke, so it's the one task this change could not skip.

Ran it in full (`--stacktrace`, no cache):

```
BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 3m 16s
> Task :app:minifyReleaseWithR8
> Task :app:packageRelease
> Task :app:assembleRelease
```

Clean. Alongside `assembleDebug`, `testDebugUnitTest`, `desktopMainClasses`, `lintDebug`, and the JSX source-chain test.

## Docs

`docs/TODO.md` gets a changelog entry explaining the scope bug and the fix. `docs/build_pipeline.md` had a stale reference to the pin living in `app/build.gradle.kts`; updated to point at the new location.

---

## Summary by Sourcery

Move shared dependency resolution rules to the root project so every module uses patched security dependencies.

Bug Fixes:
- Apply the Jackson 2.18.10 security pin to all modules so both production runtime graphs resolve patched dependencies and the seven Dependabot alerts are addressed.

Enhancements:
- Centralize dependency resolution and security pins at the root project level so current and future subprojects inherit consistent dependency versions.

Documentation:
- Document the multi-module dependency resolution issue, its fix, verification, and the new location of the shared dependency pins.

title: Fix jsxDEV source forwarding, and collapse to one kind of project
body:
Two commits. The first fixes tap-to-source, which was silently a no-op. The second removes every project target except the one the pipeline is actually built for.

---

## 1. Forward jsxDEV's source metadata, and test that it arrives

The re-envisioning (#857) turned on Babel's `jsx-source` transform so that tapping an element could hand the AI `src/App.jsx:42` instead of a CSS selector. It never did.

The vendored `jsx-runtime.js` shim — which the import map points at for **both** `react/jsx-runtime` and `react/jsx-dev-runtime` — was declared `jsxImpl(type, props, key)`, with a comment stating that `jsxDEV`'s remaining arguments were ignored. They were. Babel emitted `{fileName, lineNumber, columnNumber}` as the fifth argument and the shim dropped it one call later. No crash, no warning — `sourceOf()` simply answered `null` every time.

The fix is four lines. The bulk of the commit is an end-to-end test of the four-link chain:

| Link | File | Assertion |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ideaz-loader.js` | still requests `{ runtime: "automatic", development: true }` |
| 2 | vendored `babel.min.js` | emits `jsxDEV` with a `fileName` and `lineNumber` |
| 3 | `jsx-runtime.js` | forwards them |
| 4 | vendored `react.umd.js` | `element._source` is populated, root and nested child |

It runs the *shipped* React and Babel in a `vm`, transpiles real JSX with the loader's exact preset, executes the emitted module against the real shim, and reads `_source` off the result. No mocks — a mock would have passed against the broken shim. Reverting the shim makes it fail with 8 red lines. Wired into `pr-check.yml`; Gradle cannot see any of this.

---

## 2. Collapse to one kind of project

IDEaz previewed exactly one thing and asked about six. `ProjectType` had `ANDROID`, `WEB`, `PWA`, `REACT`, `OTHER`, `UNKNOWN` — and `selectable`, the list of types with a working loop, had **one entry**. The analyzer never returned `REACT` at all; every previewable project reported `PWA` whatever it was. The taxonomy cost branching in a dozen files and bought a label nobody could act on.

It also broke things. `ensureWorkflow` branched on a pre-split enum member, so for `PWA` it fell through to `emptyList()`, wrote no workflow, reported success, and polled GitHub Pages for ten minutes for a site nothing would ever build.

`detectProjectType` → **`isPreviewable`**: is there an `index.html` in one of a few conventional places, or a `package.json`. That is the only question the app ever needed answered.

### Removed with the Android edit target

Already listed as out of scope in `architecture.md`:

- `templates/android` (with its `wasmJsMain` Kotlin), and the placeholder substitution + package-directory relocation only it needed
- `setup_env.sh` — a script that installed a JDK and the Android SDK **into the user's repository**, written on every init
- `ProjectInitializer` — wrote a `CrashReporter.kt` into the user's own source tree with their API key baked into a `Secrets.kt` beside it
- ~200 lines of regex rewriting `versionCode`/`versionName` inside someone else's `build.gradle(.kts)`
- GitHub artifact polling, APK version comparison, installed-APK launch, and the target-package-name setting those hung off. Nothing in the UI ever read the artifact-dialog state they fed.
- the `WASM_COMPILE_SUCCESS` preview path (its compiler was already deleted) and the Android-placeholder screen a web project with a missing entry file used to land on

### On plain HTML

`templates/web` and `templates/pwa` go too, but **a plain HTML project still opens and previews exactly as before**. IDEaz just no longer offers to generate one, and no longer asks which kind you meant. React is the shape the pipeline is built for — `jsx-source` is what makes a tap resolve to a file and line — so the one remaining starter is a React/Vite app.

### AI preamble

Stops naming a project type; describes the preview contract instead — no build step, no dev server, bare specifiers resolve through a bundled import map. That is what an agent editing one of these projects actually needs to know. `AGENTS_SETUP.md` now says the same, replacing an instruction to run a setup script that is no longer written.

### Docs

- `architecture.md` — new section on why there is no `ProjectType`
- `file_descriptions.md` — regenerated against the tree. It described 107 Kotlin files, **39 of which had not existed since the CMP rebuild**, so an agent orienting itself with it opened files that were not there.
- `misc.md` — documented an on-device APK toolchain, a setup script, and three dependencies never in the version catalog (Zipline, LazySodium, Maven Resolver). Now checked against `libs.versions.toml`.
- Five other docs had passages describing removed code as current.

---

## Verification

`assembleDebug`, `desktopMainClasses`, `lintDebug` green; **126 unit tests pass**; the JSX source-chain test passes. Net **−1,959 lines**.

title: Fix build-and-release.yml's opaque IncrementalSplitterRunnable failure
body:
## Summary

The "Merged Build & Release" run for PR #853's merge ([run 32540297681](https://github.com/HereLiesAz/IDEaz/actions/runs/32540297681)) failed at `:app:packageRelease`:

```
Execution failed for task ':app:packageRelease'
> A failure occurred while executing com.android.build.gradle.tasks.PackageAndroidArtifact$IncrementalSplitterRunnable
```

This is the **third time** this exact opaque, stack-trace-free error has appeared — always coinciding with a Jackson-family dependency bump (`:app:packageDebug` in the first two attempts, `:app:packageRelease` this time), always in this one workflow, and **never** locally (I validated PR #853's exact commit with `--stacktrace` on before merging — `packageDebug`, `packageRelease`, and a full `./gradlew build` all passed clean) nor in `pr-check.yml`'s `check` job, which never runs `packageRelease` at all.

### Leading theory

`gradle/actions/setup-gradle`'s cache persists Gradle's own local task-output build cache (not just downloaded dependency jars) across runs via GitHub's Actions cache backend. A dependency bump touching this many jars at once (Jackson core/databind/annotations/datatype-jdk8/jsr310, all together) is a plausible way for a stale cached task output to escape its own cache-key invalidation and feed inconsistent input into the packaging step.

### Fix

- Dropped `--build-cache` from this workflow's default Gradle invocation. Dependency-jar caching (the fast, safe part) is untouched — this only stops packaging-adjacent tasks from potentially reusing a persisted, possibly-stale task-output cache entry.
- Always append `--stacktrace` regardless of where `BUILD_COMMAND` comes from (default or the `BUILD_COMMAND` repo variable override), so if this recurs anyway, it's finally diagnosable instead of a third round of guessing from a bare exception class name.

**Not yet confirmed as the actual root cause** — this is the best-supported theory given the evidence, but the real test is the next `build-and-release.yml` run on master.

## Test plan
- [x] `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"` — YAML parses clean
- [x] Extracted and `bash -n`'d the modified step's script — syntax valid
- [ ] Next `build-and-release.yml` run on master goes green (or, if it still fails, produces an actual stack trace this time)

---

title: Fix two review findings from #851: keep the runtime cacheable, keep root navigation
body:
## Summary

PR #851 got two legitimate review findings from Codex after it was already marked ready for review, and I pushed a fix commit (`47fd33cf`) for both — but a race meant #851 merged at its *first* commit, before that fix commit landed. Master currently has both regressions live. This PR carries that same fix commit (cherry-picked onto current master) as a follow-up.

### What's wrong on master right now

1. **Bundled runtime assets forced non-cacheable.** `#851`'s `Cache-Control: no-store` fix (correctly aimed at project/wasm-preview content) also applied to `WebProjectPathHandler.serveRuntimeAsset()` — the bundled `/__ideaz__/` runtime (React/Babel/etc., ~4.5MB, static per app version). Every reload of *any* web/PWA project now re-transfers that whole runtime for no reason — a real regression against the PR's own "faster preview loop" goal.
2. **Dropped root navigation on wasm-compile-success.** The previous `webView.loadUrl(WebProjectUrlUtils.localProjectRootUrl())` was simplified to a plain `webView.reload()`, which only re-requests whatever URL the WebView is currently on. A Compose Multiplatform app can push its own History API entries via client-side routing, so the WebView may not be sitting at the freshly-mounted output's root by the time a recompile finishes.

### Fix
- `WebProjectPathHandler.response()` now takes a `cacheable` flag; only `serveRuntimeAsset()` sets it (`Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400`). Project content stays `no-store`.
- `WebProjectHost`'s wasm-compile-success handler is back to `loadUrl(localProjectRootUrl())`, dropping only the now-redundant `clearCache(true)`.
- `docs/file_descriptions.md` documents the caching contract.

## Test plan
- [x] `./gradlew :app:compileDebugKotlin` — builds clean
- [x] `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest --tests "com.hereliesaz.ideaz.ui.web.*"` — green
- [x] `./gradlew build -PversionBuild=999 --build-cache` — full build+check green (validates the same task ordering CI runs)
- [ ] CI (`check`, `submit-gradle`) green on this PR
