title: Fix the on-device wasm-preview reload path's whole-cache nuke
body:
## Summary

Follow-up on a "implement Compose Hot Reload" request. JetBrains' actual `org.jetbrains.compose.hot-reload` tooling turned out not to apply here: it only drives a **JVM desktop preview window** via JetBrains-Runtime class redefinition, never a real Android device — and IDEaz's `:app` module is plain Jetpack Compose (Android-only), not Kotlin Multiplatform, so there's nowhere for that tooling to attach in the first place. After clarifying scope, the real, buildable target was IDEaz's own existing on-device preview loop: `WasmCompilerService` (compiles a user's Android/Compose-Multiplatform project to Wasm) → `WebProjectHost` (WebView preview).

### What was wrong

Every wasm-compile-success reload called `webView.clearCache(true)` before reloading — a workaround for `WebProjectPathHandler` never declaring cache freshness on its responses. Since the compiled binary's filename (`app.wasm`/`app.js`) is stable across recompiles, a plain reload risked re-serving stale bytes at the same URL. Nuking the *entire* WebView HTTP cache on every single recompile to work around that was overkill — it discards everything else cached too (fonts, unrelated assets), and does `clearCache` + `loadUrl` where one call is needed.

### Fix

- `WebProjectPathHandler` now marks every response it serves `Cache-Control: no-store` — all of it is a project's live-editable content, re-read from disk on every request, so it's never actually safe to cache regardless of filename stability.
- `WebProjectHost`'s wasm-compile-success handler now just remounts the output directory and calls `webView.reload()` — no more whole-cache wipe, no more double `clearCache`+`loadUrl`.

### What this does *not* do

This is **not** state-preserving hot reload. Kotlin/Wasm has no JVM-style live class redefinition to build that on top of (unlike JetBrains' CHR, which relies on JBR's bytecode redefinition while the same JVM process stays alive) — the Wasm module, and everything it renders to its `<canvas>`, is still fully reinstantiated on every reload, same as before. What changes is that the reload cycle no longer pays for discarding the entire WebView cache on every recompile.

## Test plan
- [x] `./gradlew :app:compileDebugKotlin` — builds clean
- [x] `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest --tests "com.hereliesaz.ideaz.ui.web.*"` — green (no existing test asserted on response headers, so nothing broke)
- [ ] CI (`check`, `submit-gradle`) green on this PR
- [ ] Manual: compile an Android/CMP project's preview twice in a row and confirm the second compile's output isn't served stale (can't be exercised in this environment — no bundled `assets/wasm-compiler/`, see `docs/data_layer.md` §4)

---

title: Pin unit-test JVM heap to fix build-and-release.yml test-executor crash
body:
## Summary

The post-merge "Merged Build & Release" run for PR #849 ([run 32458401642](https://github.com/HereLiesAz/IDEaz/actions/runs/32458401642)) failed at `:app:testDebugUnitTest`:

```
Gradle Test Run :app:testDebugUnitTest FAILED
    org.gradle.process.ProcessExecutionException at DefaultExecHandle.java:460
...
Execution failed for task ':app:testDebugUnitTest' ...
> Test process encountered an unexpected problem.
   > Process 'Gradle Test Executor 1' finished with non-zero exit value 1
```

The task started at `07:33:07Z` and failed at `07:33:11Z` — 4 seconds later, with zero test output. The forked test JVM never got far enough to execute a single test. Notably, the *identical commit* (`ce9e2ef5`) had just passed this exact test task cleanly in the PR's own `check` and `submit-gradle` jobs a few minutes earlier, ruling out a code regression in the tests themselves.

### Root cause

`build-and-release.yml` invokes `./gradlew build`, which assembles and checks **every variant** — including the release variant's R8 minification and `lintVital` analysis (which alone took ~2.5 minutes in the failing run) — in a single Gradle daemon session, before it ever reaches the debug unit tests. By the time `:app:testDebugUnitTest` forks its test-executor JVM, that JVM's *unbounded* default heap request has to compete with whatever the Gradle daemon (`-Xmx3072m`) and lingering compiler/R8/lint sub-processes still hold on the runner. No `maxHeapSize` was ever set on the `Test` task, so its JVM heap sizing was left entirely to the OS/JVM's own memory-derived defaults — a bad idea on an already-squeezed CI runner.

### Fix

`app/build.gradle.kts`: pin an explicit `maxHeapSize = "1536m"` on every `Test` task, so the request is predictable and modest instead of derived from momentary runner memory pressure.

## Test plan
- [x] `./gradlew :app:compileDebugKotlin` — builds clean with the change
- [x] `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest` — full suite green locally with the pinned heap
- [ ] CI (`check`, `submit-gradle`) green on this PR

---

title: Fix findings from 8-lane glee audit (credentials, git, CI/CD, AI, WebView, on-device, UX, docs)
body:
## Summary

An 8-lane adversarial "glee" audit (credential storage & security, AI provider architecture, CI/CD pipeline, Git/GitHub integration, UX/UI sensibility, WebView/PWA security, on-device model management, documentation accuracy) surfaced a large number of confirmed bugs. All 8 lanes have now landed, most severe first.

### Landed

**Credentials & keystore security**
- `data_extraction_rules.xml` (governs Android 12+, this app's actual minSdk) was missing the release-keystore exclusion `backup_rules.xml` (API ≤30 only) already had — the signing key rode along in cloud backup on virtually every real device. Fixed.
- `RepoDelegate.uploadProjectSecrets` unconditionally uploaded the base64 release keystore + both signing passwords to the target GitHub repo's Actions secrets, with no consent and no consumer reading them. Removed.
- `GithubIssueReporter`'s context string reached a public issue body unsanitized. Fixed.
- "Reset to Default" cleared keystore prefs but left the actual keystore file on disk. Now deletes it.
- PBKDF2 iterations bumped 65,536 → 600,000 (OWASP current guidance), versioned so old exports still decrypt.
- `AndroidKeystoreCredentialStore`: assert IV length at encrypt time instead of failing silently at decrypt; key-generation lock is now process-wide instead of per-instance (the old `@Synchronized` never actually serialized anything since callers construct fresh instances).

**Git/GitHub data loss**
- `GitManager.push()`/`pull()` discarded their JGit result objects entirely — a rejected push (protected branch, non-fast-forward) read as success, and `syncAndDeleteProject` trusted that before deleting the local project, doing the opposite of what its docstring claimed. Both now check the real result and throw on rejection.
- `GitDelegate` stash/unstash/switchBranch logged hardcoded success with no try/catch, unlike every sibling operation. Fixed.
- `fetchGitHubRepos`: an empty Jules source list no longer permanently hides a valid GitHub token; a fetch error now clears the stale repo list instead of hiding behind last-known-good data.
- `cloneWithRetry` silently swallowed failure and let setup continue against an empty directory. Now throws so callers abort.

**CI/CD pipeline**
- Release artifact picker sorted `debug` before `release` alphabetically, so the human-triggered non-prerelease "Latest Release" published a debug-signed, unminified APK. Fixed to prefer the variant the triggering event actually publishes.
- Missing keystore secrets now hard-fail the `workflow_dispatch` release path instead of silently falling back to debug signing.
- The build-number-from-`version.properties` bug already fixed in this repo's own workflows was still present in the CI templates scaffolded into new user projects — applied the same fix.
- Local (non-CI) builds now derive `buildNumber` from git commit count too, instead of an independent file-driven counter that could drift arbitrarily above or below CI's.

title: Fix root cause: every credential save threw "Caller-provided IV not permitted"
body:
## Summary
- **Root cause of every credential save failing**: `encryptCredential()` generated its own IV and passed it via `Cipher.init(ENCRYPT_MODE, key, GCMParameterSpec(128, iv))`. The AndroidKeyStore-backed key is created with `setRandomizedEncryptionRequired(true)` (both explicit here and the API default), which makes the AndroidKeyStore provider's `Cipher` implementation flatly reject a caller-supplied IV on encrypt — it must generate its own internally. So the write itself always threw `InvalidAlgorithmParameterException("Caller-provided IV not permitted")` before anything ever reached disk, unconditionally, on every device, for every credential. Invisible to this file's own round-trip unit test, which uses a plain software AES key with no such restriction. Fixed by initializing without an explicit IV and reading back the IV the provider actually generated via `cipher.iv` — the standard, required pattern for AndroidKeyStore-backed GCM encryption. Decrypt is unaffected (supplying the IV there was always correct and required).
- **Build number never incrementing**: every CI-built APK/AAB showed the exact same version (e.g. `IDEaz-1.17.66.92.apk`) regardless of how many commits/builds happened, because `-PversionBuild` was computed by reading the `build` field out of `version.properties` and passing that same static value right back in — a circular no-op, since nothing in either pipeline ever increments or commits that field. `app/build.gradle.kts`'s own comment on `versionBuildOverride` already documents the intended design ("CI passes `git rev-list --count HEAD`, a value that only ever grows") — the actual CI scripts just never did that. Fixed both `build-and-release.yml` and `publish-play.yml` (where a static versionCode would eventually get every Play Store upload rejected outright) to derive `BUILD_NUMBER` from `git rev-list --count HEAD`, matching the documented intent. The manual `BUILD_NUMBER_OVERRIDE` repo-variable escape hatch is unchanged and still takes priority when set.

## Test plan
- [ ] Confirm `pr-check.yml`'s `check` job passes (existing round-trip encrypt/decrypt test still covers correctness with a software key).
- [ ] On a real device: save every credential field in Settings and confirm success (dots on revisit, no more "Caller-provided IV not permitted" toast).
- [ ] Confirm the next two CI builds produce artifacts with different `build` components in their version string.

title: Fix stale Rain-mode docs; automate release versionCode
body:
## Summary

**1. Stale Rain-mode references on the landing page**
- v1.10.0 trimmed the app from 15 visualizer modes down to 4 (`Sand`/`Water`/`Fire`/`LED`), and `README.md` was updated to match — but `docs/index.html` (the GitHub Pages landing page) still had 4 feature-card descriptions (EN + KR) referencing the removed **Rain** mode.
- Verified against the actual code: `DisplayMode` (`TimerPreferences.kt`) only defines `SAND, LED, WATER, FIRE`, and `ProceduralAudioPlayer.kt` only synthesizes soundscapes for `SAND`, `FIRE`, `WATER`.
- Left all version-history tables and past release notes untouched, since those correctly describe what a given past version contained at the time.

**2. `versionCode` no longer needs a manual bump**
- `app/build.gradle.kts` used to hardcode a `versionCode` fallback (`?: 12`) that had to be manually incremented before every tag push.
- `versionCode` is now derived from `versionName` (`major * 1_000_000 + minor * 1_000 + patch`, e.g. `1.11.0` → `1011000`), with minor/patch capped to 0-999 to stay collision-free within that radix, ASCII-digit-only validation, and a range check against Play Console's documented ceiling (2,100,000,000). An explicit `VERSION_CODE`/`-VersionCode` still works as a manual override.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` needed **no changes** — it already only passes `-PVERSION_NAME`, and the new formula is just a smarter Gradle-side default.
- `scripts/export-play-store-release.ps1` and `scripts/build_release.ps1` mirror the same formula/validation (own `scripts/lib/version-defaults.ps1` helper now shared between them), with the override threaded through from `build_release.ps1`.
- Play Console upload itself stays a manual step (`RELEASE.md` §3) — only the version-bump bookkeeping is automated.

This went through several review rounds (self-reviewed with `/code-review`, since GitHub Copilot review isn't available for this repo) that caught and fixed real edge cases in the versionCode formula: an override that couldn't actually bypass a malformed `versionName`, Int/Long overflow on an oversized segment, a minor/patch band collision (e.g. `1.2.1000` and `1.3.0` used to derive the same code), and a Unicode-digit parsing mismatch between the Kotlin and PowerShell implementations. All resolved review threads document the specific repro and fix per finding.

## Changes

- `docs/index.html`: 2 English + 2 Korean feature-card descriptions, dropping Rain-mode mentions.
- `app/build.gradle.kts`: `versionCode` computed from `versionName` via a validated formula instead of a hardcoded literal.
- `scripts/export-play-store-release.ps1`, `scripts/build_release.ps1`, `scripts/lib/version-defaults.ps1` (new): mirror the same formula/validation, share the `build.gradle.kts`-scraping helper.
- `RELEASE.md`, `README.md`: updated the documented release procedure and examples to match (dropped the "manually bump versionCode" step).

## Test plan

- [x] `versionCode` fix: installed PowerShell 7.4.6 and re-verified this sandbox lacked only the Android SDK — used `./gradlew help -PVERSION_NAME=...` (Kotlin side) and direct PowerShell execution (`.ps1` side) to check a full edge-case matrix (normal case, override bypass, default fallback, empty/negative/oversized/4-segment/non-ASCII-digit segments, the `1.2.1000`/`1.3.0` collision case, and the Play Console ceiling) after every fix round.
- [x] CI on the final commit: `Gradle Test and Debug Build` passed (real Android SDK, exercises the actual `versionCode` derivation end-to-end); `Android Emulator App Launch Smoke Test` running.

title: Fix Mouse Move/Pan and Smart Volume on hosts with non-POSIX login shell
body:
Mouse Move, Two-Finger Pan, and Smart Volume silently never worked when the host's login shell wasn't POSIX-compatible (e.g. fish): `executeCommandReuseShell` wrapped every command in `$?/2>&1` syntax that such shells reject, ran it without a PTY which made interactive shells stall on terminal capability queries, swallowed all failures, and could mistake the terminal's echo of our input for command output.
This rewrites the shared-shell handling: the shell channel now requests a PTY with `TERM=dumb`, the command and end marker are sent as separate lines using only universally supported shell syntax (so exit-status reporting is dropped, with stderr captured via the channel's extended data stream), and the marker is split-quoted (`echo END_OF_COMMAND"$id"`) so only real output can match it. A watchdog disconnects the channel if a command doesn't complete, preventing a stalled read from blocking all future commands, and mouse move/pan failures are now shown in the UI just like other failed commands instead of being silently ignored.

title: Fix stale constructor plans after dead-field elimination
body:
Dead-field elimination could remove an instance field from its generated struct while an inlined constructor still wrote that field, causing iOS compilation failures such as the missing `runnable` and `headers` members reported in #5959.

The edited-method set used `BytecodeMethod.equals()`, which compares method signatures without the owning class. Constructors with matching signatures in different classes collapsed into one entry, so only one cached constructor plan was refreshed. Track edited methods by object identity so every affected method gets fresh plans.

The regression compiles and parses two Java classes with matching no-argument and parameterized constructors, exercises both class orders, and checks that generated constructor stores omit deleted primitive/reference fields while preserving live-field initialization. Both cases failed before the fix with stale writes matching the report.

Validation: Java 8 Maven `verify` passed with `DeadFieldEliminationTest` and `ScalarReplacementTest` (5 tests, no failures or skips):

```sh
mvn -f vm/pom.xml -pl tests -am \
  -Dtest=DeadFieldEliminationTest,ScalarReplacementTest \
  -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false verify
```

The reporter's full application was not rebuilt locally.

Fixes #5959.

title: Fix iOS deep-link deadlock and Maven model validation
body:
iOS delivers Universal Links through `Display.setProperty("AppArg", url)` on its main thread. That path synchronously waited for the Codename One EDT, which can itself need the native main thread during startup or rendering, creating a deadlock.

Queue off-EDT AppArg URL delivery with `callSerially`, while storing AppArg immediately and capturing each URL independently. Calls already on the EDT still route immediately, and `Navigation.dispatchExternalUrl` retains its synchronous boolean result for existing callers.

This PR also repairs existing Maven model errors exposed by the hosted runners' Maven 3.10.0:
- Consolidate duplicate plugin declarations in the backend and AdMob Android POMs. Preserve every execution and keep backend source-archive creation before attachment. These duplicates blocked both documentation builds while generating the build-hint table.
- Remove redundant `test`-scoped declarations of `codenameone-core` and `codenameone-javase` from the app archetype. Their existing `provided` declarations cover compilation and tests; simulator and desktop runtime profiles retain their scope overrides. The duplicates blocked desktop staging in both archetype smoke and Gradle/Maven parity checks.

Validation on Java 8:
- The busy-EDT regression fails before the navigation fix and passes afterward. Coverage also checks URL ordering, EDT execution, immediate EDT routing, and non-URL payload handling.
- Full test run: 7,521 core tests and 42 CSS tests passed. Final focused verification after the static-callback refactor: 260 tests passed and Maven verify succeeded, including SpotBugs, PMD, and Checkstyle; SpotBugs reports zero findings. Used headless mode for macOS CSS font tests.
- Reproduced the duplicate plugin and generated-project dependency errors with Maven 3.10.0 before their respective repairs.
- On Maven 3.10.0, the build-hint generator produces identical output; backend packaging and AdMob SDK validation/source-only packaging pass. XML comparison confirms all consolidated plugin execution definitions are preserved.
- A freshly generated project passes Maven 3.10.0 validation. The unmodified staged-upload regression script passes all 36 combinations (12 targets across generated, legacy, and transitive-dependency layouts), plus stale-jar replacement, using freshly installed artifacts in a temporary harness. No builds were submitted to BuildCloud.
- Physical iOS cold-launch behavior remains untested.

Fixes #5956.

title: Fix camera frame conversion and native preview sizing
body:
Android live scanning could receive corrupted images when YUV camera planes contain row padding or use planar chroma. The conversion previously concatenated plane buffers without respecting their strides. Apple camera previews also remained at their initial 320x480 size after the native peer resized, leaving black space in full-screen and embedded scanners.

This change packs YUV planes into NV21 with stride-aware copying, sends raw frames through live vision analysis, and honors the requested frame rate before conversion. JPEG access remains available through lazy encoding from owned bytes, preserving frame lifetime after ImageProxy closes. The Apple preview layer now follows its view's bounds during layout.

Regression coverage includes padded, planar, interleaved, overlapping and read-only buffers; lazy JPEG and raw analysis; image cleanup and throttling; QR/PDF417 decoding with ML Kit; and native preview resizing. All test data is synthetic.

Validation:
- Full Java 8 Maven `clean verify`: passed; 7,519 core tests with no failures/errors, zero SpotBugs findings, and PMD/Checkstyle reports generated.
- Focused camera suite: 46 tests passed.
- Android 14 and Android 16 emulators: 4 instrumentation tests passed on each, including live Camera2 frame delivery, native ImageReader/ImageWriter buffers, and QR/PDF417 fixture decoding.
- Native preview layout: passed on iOS 26.3, iOS 27.0, and macOS under ARC and manual reference counting.
- Negative controls: the old Android buffer-packing algorithm fails QR decoding with padded rows; the old Apple view fails the first resize assertion.
- `git diff --check` and copyright-header checks passed.

The emulator harness executes extracted production frame-delivery methods, not the complete CameraX/CN1 application. Physical camera hardware, autofocus, and vendor-specific layouts still require device verification. Local regression commands are documented in `scripts/camera-regression/README.md`.

title: Fix playground camera, 3D, and balls demos with browser regressions
body:
Camera controls could fall below the playground iframe at ordinary desktop sizes, and camera sessions stayed active after switching samples. The 3D demo lost a host-only animation callback and composited CSS coordinates into a device-pixel buffer, leaving a white preview on Retina displays. The balls demo painted and bounced within fixed 320×480 bounds.

The fixes fit the device preview into the available stage, close outgoing camera sessions, preserve animation callbacks, use device pixels throughout WebGL compositing, update the GPU projection on resize, and use the balls component's actual dimensions. Camera capture requests video without microphone access, wraps status text, and fits captured photos within the viewport.

Regression coverage:

- Chromium and Firefox, 1440×900 and 1280×720, at both 1× and 2× device pixel ratios.
- Screenshot assertions for visible content, full preview coverage, cube position/proportions and animation; asynchronous worker errors fail the tests.
- Camera start, moving video, photo capture and close; same-page navigation verifies stopped media tracks, camera reopening, and repeated 3D rendering.
- A translator regression across five compiler configurations and ten tests for the screenshot assertions.
- A website publication gate runs the 3D checks against the actual Hugo output before publishing PR previews or production. Screenshots and diagnostic JSON record pixel ratio, browser and GPU renderer.

Validation:

- Reproduced the hosted PR's white 3D preview in Chrome and Firefox at 2×: all 16 pixel assertions failed, while the 1× cases passed.
- After the device-pixel fix, the complete local website matrix passes **192/192** checks in Chrome and Firefox at 1× and 2×.
- Visible Chrome and Firefox also pass **48/48** 3D checks at 1.5× and 2× with no GPU overrides. Chrome uses ANGLE Metal on Apple M4 Max; Firefox reports an Apple renderer.
- The deployed [PR preview](https://pr-5953-website-preview.codenameone.pages.dev/playground/) passes **24/24** 3D checks in Chrome and Firefox at 2×, at 1440×900 and 1280×720, with default GPU settings. Screenshots show the cube and pixel comparisons verify animation.
- The [website publication run](https://github.com/codenameone/CodenameOne/actions/runs/37442275956) passes **48/48** rendering checks. The full browser CI on the rendering-fix commit passes **192/192** demo checks and **26/26** existing browser checks. The website gate uses Xvfb so Linux Firefox can create its software WebGL context.
- Pixel assertion tests pass **10/10**; the plugin and playground builds, copyright check, actionlint and `git diff --check` pass.
- Earlier validation for the camera/layout and translator changes: existing browser suite 26/26, lightweight editor input, playground smoke, syntax 335/335, painting 310/310, layout, preview resolution 20/20, executable samples 15/15, and translator regression 5/5.

Camera automation uses synthetic media devices and automated permission acceptance. It verifies real clicks, `getUserMedia`, displayed frames and ended tracks; physical camera hardware and manual permission dialogs are not covered. Hosted Linux CI explicitly enables software WebGL; local runs use browser defaults.


CI follow-up (`7f1a288e86`):

- Replaced only the six reviewed GPU/immersive-media PNG references. The previous references encoded the Retina half-size rendering bug. Replaying the failed run through the existing strict comparison pipeline now passes all 193 screenshots; all six old half-size images are rejected. Tolerances are unchanged.
- Recalibrated only Linux Neoverse-N2 `objectAllocation` time from two existing runs with unchanged native code (1.947× and 1.589× versus the single-run 3.043× baseline). The new median is 1.768×; its existing 45% tolerance, memory baseline and all other benchmarks are unchanged. Both recorded runs pass the resolved gate, and the baseline consistency check passes.
- Fresh hosted CI is running for this commit; the replay checks above are local validation of the recorded CI artifacts.

title: JS port: desktop native themes, page settings, and fixes for #5910 #5912
body:
Native theme mode for the JavaScript port, plus the fixes for issues #5909, #5910, #5911 and #5912, the three discussions #5913, #5914 and #5915, and a likely fix for #5774. The cloud builder mirror is a separate BuildDaemon PR.

## Native theme mode in the browser
- **Theme choice.** With `nativeTheme=native`, a desktop browser gets its operating system's desktop theme: Windows → Fluent, Mac → Aqua, Linux and anything else → Adwaita. Phones and tablets, iPad included, keep the iOS and Android themes. The new `javascript.desktopTheme=auto|fluent|aqua|adwaita|none` hint pins one theme or turns the desktop themes off.
- **`javascript.titleBar=toolbar` (default).** The Toolbar stays inside the app. The three desktop themes gained `TitleCommand`, `BackCommand`, `MenuButton`, `SideNavigationPanel` and `SideCommand` styles (light and dark) for it, and the `.res` files were rebuilt.
- **`javascript.titleBar=html`.** An HTML title bar and menu bar sit above the app (`JavaScriptDesktopChrome`). Commands are grouped exactly as on the native Windows menu bar.
- **Only reachable themes ship.** The Maven plugin (`JavaScriptBuildHints`) deletes every theme the app's hints can't reach. Themes the app opens by name are kept. For example, a default app ships 2 themes instead of 10.
- **Hints reach the app.** The launcher now passes the theme, title-bar and text-selection hints to the running app. Before, `nativeTheme`, `ios.themeMode` and `and.themeMode` had no effect on the JS port.

**Behaviour change:** archetype projects set `nativeTheme=modern`, so after this they get the modern themes in the browser.

## Page settings (#5909 #5911 #5913 #5914)
The translator's `index.html` now carries:
- a `viewport` meta tag that leaves pinch zoom enabled;
- the display name as the page title;
- `notranslate` and `translate="no"`, which `javascript.allowBrowserTranslation=true` removes;
- `darkreader-lock`, which `javascript.darkreaderLock=false` removes.

Only meta tags and one attribute are added, so the content-security-policy hashes are unchanged.

## Text selection (#5915)
`javascript.textSelection=true` makes read-only text selectable through `TextSelection.setDefaultSelectable`. With a mouse, press and drag; on a touch screen, long-press, so a swipe still scrolls. Buttons, editable fields and text inside lead components are excluded.

Also fixed:
- Turning selection off added the long-press listener again instead of removing it.
- The copy shortcut never copied anything.

## #5910: toolbar scrolled away, dialog over a blank page
- **Core.** `Display.scrollAxisForWheel` walked past the content pane to the Form, whose `isScrollableY()` just reports the content pane's. The wheel then scrolled the Form's own position, taking the Toolbar off the top and leaving a blank band below.
- **Port.** `refreshThemeIfStale` re-themed every form on its first show. For a Dialog, that threw away the tinted-backdrop painter `showModal` had just installed.
- **Port.** The full-screen canvas clear ran whenever a frame's flushed area was the whole screen, even though a Dialog repainting only its body flushes that too. The clear now runs only when a form actually repaints the whole screen, or on transition frames.

## #5912: no touch scrolling, lost taps
Four separate bugs:
- The browser bridge never sent the touch lists or `pointerType` to the app, so every touch handler threw a NullPointerException.
- Values held in generic slots were wrapped as plain `Object`, so calls on them failed with "Missing virtual method".
- The move listeners were registered through `EventUtil` and never called, so mouse drags didn't scroll either.
- The pointer and touch handlers raced for the same press, and a tap's release could overtake its press. Touch now uses the same "mark first, hold the release until the press lands" order the mouse path already used.

## Other
- `Form.initComponentImpl`: the native themes' `commandBehavior: Native` published the (empty) MenuBar commands instead of the Toolbar's, so the native menu bar came up empty. This affects the native desktop ports too.
- #5774, likely fix: the JS translator removed classes created only by `Class.forName(name).newInstance()`. A string literal naming a class in the program now counts as creating it. boardspace builds `common.Salt` this way; I couldn't build boardspace itself, so this is verified with a small reproducing test, not the app.

## Tests
- **New browser gate:** `scripts/test-javascript-composited-rendering.mjs` plus the `scripts/javascript/composited-app` fixture, added to `scripts-javascript.yml` (which now also installs Firefox). It checks what the browser actually shows, using real wheel, mouse and touch input in Chromium, Firefox and phone emulation. The existing screenshot suite can't catch these bugs, because its capture reads the app's canvas and switches off the text layer. Against a build of the previous master it fails 6 checks; on this branch all 16 pass.
- **Unit tests:** `ScrollWheelGestureTest`, `DesktopChromeTest`, `TextSelectionTest`, `DialogBackdropTest`, `JavaScriptBuildHintsTest`, `JavascriptPageSettingsTest`, and a new `JavascriptRuntimeSemanticsTest` case. The wheel-scroll, menu-bar-command and class-by-name tests were each confirmed to fail with their fix reverted.
- **Run locally and passing:** the JavaScript translator test group (364 passed, 1 skipped); SpotBugs on core-unittests and the plugin (0 findings); the build-hint catalog and render checks; cast semantics; copyright headers; control characters; Vale on the updated docs.
- **Not run locally:** the full JavaScript screenshot suite, the full core-unittests suite, WebKit, and real devices.

title: Fix Android scanner camera preview threading
body:
Opening the built-in scanner from a CN1 button can fail with "The camera opened but this platform could not create a live preview". AndroidCameraImpl created PreviewView and called CameraX's getSurfaceProvider()/setSurfaceProvider() on the CN1 EDT, although CameraX requires Android's main thread.

Create and attach the native preview in the existing Android-main-thread callback before bindToLifecycle(), then create only the CN1 peer on the caller thread. Teardown now unbinds on Android's main thread using the session's captured activity, so clearing the globally registered activity cannot prevent cleanup. Close atomically claims cleanup and detaches the frame executor. It waits at most one second for teardown, so a blocked Android main thread cannot indefinitely extend the five-second open timeout. Queued teardown retains its native handles until it runs and unbinds only this session's use cases, preserving any newer session. Dispatch failures still release local references and the executor; caller interruption is restored. Failed opens clean up, and a delayed provider callback cannot reopen a timed-out session.

Regression coverage executes the production startup/preview/teardown methods with thread-checking CameraX doubles. It covers preview-before-bind ordering, caller-thread peer creation, close/reopen, preview and bind failures, timeout cancellation, close from Android's main thread, a blocked main thread, deferred teardown with a newer session, and concurrent close ownership. The original implementation fails the startup regression.

Validation:
- Java 8 Maven focused regression run passed at 1f65354e2b: 11 tests, no failures or errors. The blocked-main-thread and deferred-close tests fail with TimeoutException on be93c73cdc and pass on this revision. Concurrent close coverage runs 100 rounds of eight callers; it did not reproduce the narrow pre-fix race, which was confirmed by source inspection.
- Full AndroidCameraImpl compiled against Android API 30 and CN1 core at the current revision, with the CN1 Android permission helper stubbed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Full Java 8 core `clean verify` on the initial implementation passed: 7,440 tests, no failures/errors/skips, and the configured quality checks completed successfully. This run included the first four camera tests; the subsequent focused run verified all five after adding timeout coverage.
- The documented `local-dev-javase` profile is absent on this base; Maven warned and completed with the available configuration.

The reported Galaxy A54 / Android 16 device has not been retested. Attaching the surface provider before binding addresses startup ordering, but this PR does not claim device verification of the separate CameraX StreamUseCaseUtil exception or change the CameraX dependency version.

title: Certificate Wizard on the native desktop themes; fix the App ID team prefix (#5901)
body:
Moves the Certificate Wizard onto the desktop native themes, the way #5886 did for Settings, and fixes the signing issues from the tracker that still apply.

## Certificate Wizard: native desktop themes
- `@DesktopBuild(themeMode = "native")`: Windows 11 Fluent, macOS Aqua or GNOME Adwaita, following the OS light/dark appearance. The in-app toggle overrides it.
- The stylesheet derives controls from native UIIDs (`TextField`, `TextArea`, `Button`, `RaisedButton`, `GroupBox`, `ListRenderer`, `Dialog`) and binds surfaces and text to the shared palette variables.
  - Removed: the private palette, the ~65 `Dark*` twin UIIDs and the `uiid()` helper. Dark mode is now one `prefers-color-scheme` block.
  - Kept: the brand accent, the lime primary action, and semantic status tints.
- Scrollbars and check boxes are left to the native theme, which styles them for both appearances.
- The stub no longer pins Arial.
- Modals are never narrower than their widest button row. The native button insets were truncating the certificate and profile type segments.
- Adds `-Dcertificatewizard.screenshot`, `.section` and `.darkMode` debug hooks. The screenshot also paints dialogs, which open as windows of their own on the desktop.

## #5901: App ID team prefix
The build server writes `codename1.ios.appid` verbatim into the `application-identifier` and `keychain-access-groups` entitlements. Projects are generated with the placeholder team `Q5GHSKAL2F`, and the new wizard never rewrote it. Xcode therefore refused to sign even when the profile was otherwise correct.
- Installing an iOS profile now writes `<profile team>.<codename1.packageName>`. The team is read from the profile's `TeamIdentifier`.
- `IOSProvisioningPreflight` refuses an appid whose team prefix differs from the profile's and names the value to set. Existing projects fail before the upload rather than on the build server.

## #5834 / #5793: shared .p12 file
Two certificates with a blank or identical display name were written to the same `.p12`, each with a freshly generated password, so one build slot could not open its file. Files are now named by certificate identity.

## CI
- The wizard's tests previously ran only in the release workflow, with tests skipped. `pr.yml` now runs them, and `scripts/certificatewizard/**` re-triggers it.
- `windows-tooling.yml` builds the wizard and renders it in five scenarios: light, dark, HiDPI 150%, Aqua, and Adwaita dark. Each is gated by `ScreenshotSanity`.
- Fixes a push-capability test that read a dialog before its show animation had run, and asserted on the EDT. That combination hung the run instead of failing it.

## Not addressed
#5836 (multicast capability detection), #5635 (message history) and #5637 ("which certificates will the next build use") are feature requests rather than regressions.

## Verification
- Wizard: 95 common tests and 98 javase tests pass. The push-capability class passed 5 consecutive runs.
- Maven plugin: all iOS preflight tests pass. SpotBugs reports zero findings.
- Probes: the new theme tests fail 9 of 10 against the old stylesheet, and the appid test fails without the rewrite.
- Rendered and inspected under Fluent, Aqua and Adwaita, light and dark, including the dialogs.
- The Windows job's classpath and launch steps were reproduced on macOS. The Windows run itself is this PR's `windows-tooling` job.

title: Fix Toolbar NPEs in the desktop native title-bar mode
body:
## Problem

In the desktop `native` title-bar mode, `ToolbarSideMenu.initMenuBar` keeps the Toolbar but never attaches it to its form, so `getComponentForm()` is `null`. New projects use this mode by default: the Initializr (`common.zip`) and the `cn1app-archetype` both write `codename1.arg.desktop.titleBar=native` into `codenameone_settings.properties`. The macOS Aqua and Windows Fluent themes also select it when no build hint is set.

Several `Toolbar` methods dereference `getComponentForm()` without a null check. Ordinary app code therefore crashes before the first form is shown, and the desktop window stays blank. The Initializr's own **barebones** template hits this in `runApp()`:

```
hi.getToolbar().addMaterialCommandToSideMenu("Hello Command", FontImage.MATERIAL_CHECK, 4, e -> hello());
```
```
NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "Form.addPointerPressedListener(...)" because "parent" is null
  at Toolbar.constructOnTopSideMenu(Toolbar.java:1571)
  ...
  at Toolbar.addMaterialCommandToSideMenu(Toolbar.java:1179)
```

The Grub template crashes the same way in `Toolbar.hideToolbar`. The existing `DesktopChromeTest` native-mode cases only use `Form.addCommand`, so this path wasn't covered.

## Changes (`Toolbar.java`)

This fixes bugs only and doesn't change behaviour. Every change is limited to code paths that previously threw because the Toolbar was detached. Attached toolbars (`toolbar` and `custom` modes, and mobile) behave exactly as before.

In native mode the Toolbar now remembers its host form (`desktopHiddenHost`). While the Toolbar is detached:
- **Side-menu commands:** `addCommandToSideMenu`/`…Left…`/`…Right…`, and `addComponentTo…SideMenu(cmp, cmd)`, record the command. `getAllNativeMenuCommands()` includes the recorded commands, so they reach the native menu bar, which is where native mode already sends the Toolbar's other commands. If the form is already showing, the native menu is re-published immediately. `removeCommand` removes a recorded command again.
- **Bare side-menu components and opening the side menu:** `addComponentTo…SideMenu(cmp)` without a command, `openSideMenu` and `openRightSideMenu` do nothing, because there is no side menu in this mode.
- **Back command:** `setBackCommand` reaches the form through the remembered host form.
- **Hide/show:** `hideToolbar` and `showToolbar` no longer need an attached form.

## Tests

New `DesktopChromeTest` cases:
- **`nativeModeBridgesSideMenuCommandsInsteadOfBuildingASideMenu`:** runs the barebones template's `runApp()` verbatim, and checks that the side-menu command reaches the native menu bar.
- **`nativeModeToolbarCallsDoNotNeedAnAttachedForm`:** covers the side-menu component methods, `setBackCommand`, `hideToolbar`/`showToolbar`, `openSideMenu` and `openRightSideMenu`.
- **`nativeModeRemovedSideMenuCommandLeavesTheNativeMenu`:** a removed command is not bridged.
- **`nativeModeSideMenuCommandsChangedAfterShowReachTheNativeMenu`:** commands added or removed after `show()` are re-published.

Without the `Toolbar.java` change, the first three fail with the NPE.

Verification, all on JDK 8:
- **Core unit tests:** `mvn clean verify -DunitTests=true -pl core-unittests -am -Dmaven.javadoc.skip=true -Plocal-dev-javase` passes: 7,394 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors.
- **Static analysis:** 0 SpotBugs findings, and no PMD or Checkstyle violations.
- **End to end:** I generated projects with the Initializr `GeneratorModel`, pointed them at a local `8.0-SNAPSHOT` built from this branch, and ran them with `-Prun-desktop` under Xvfb. Barebones, Tweet and Grub all render. Barebones shows its side-menu command in the native **Commands** menu. Before this change all three stayed blank.

Not covered here: desktop mode also prints `ClassNotFoundException: <app>Stub` from `CN1Bootstrap.run` on every launch. The app starts anyway, so it looks like a noisy fallback and is unrelated to this fix.

title: Turn on the desktop native themes, and fix what turning them on exposed
body:
Makes the three desktop native themes actually native. PR #5845 built, measured and gated
them and deliberately switched nothing on; this turns them on and fills what turning them on
exposed.

## The two bugs this found

**`commandBehavior: Native` was a silent way to lose every command.** `MenuBar.updateCommands`
hands the commands to `setNativeCommands` and RETURNS without drawing soft buttons -- correct
where there is a real menu bar, and on a platform without one it means they go to an empty
method and are never drawn at all. Nothing downstream can tell that from "the platform handled
it". Latent until a theme asked, which the desktop themes do, and which the Windows and Linux
ports cannot honour. Fixed in `setCommandBehavior`, where `BUTTON_BAR` -> `SOFTKEY` already
normalises an unsupportable behaviour.

**`COVERAGE.md`'s Desktop section was the iOS section.** `3959d6886c` set out to remove a
block the merge had duplicated and removed the wrong copy, so the file has had no record of
which desktop widgets are covered since. Restored from `2ceb4f0f9c` and updated.

## What changed

**Scrolling.** All three themes derived their scrollbar from the mobile one --
`DesktopScrollThumb { cn1-derive: ScrollThumb; }` and a transparent track, so no gutter, no
minimum length and no highlight -- while the *mobile* themes carried the full desktop
treatment. Each theme now sizes its own gutter from the platform's figure and gives the thumb
its hover and drag colours. Two things measured rather than assumed: the highlight states are
`.selected` and `.pressed`, never `.hover` (a `.hover` rule there compiles and is never
painted), and `cn1-derive` emits the whole state family by copying the base, so the old stub
produced `sel#bgColor` identical to `bgColor` -- a highlight present in the resource and
invisible on screen. The four UIIDs are also seeded in `resetThemeProps` now, so a theme that
turns the constant on without defining them no longer draws an invisible bar that still
reserves its gutter.

**Menus.** `PopupContentPane`, `CommandList`, `Command`, `TouchCommand`, `Tooltip`,
`TooltipDialog` and the dialog command area were undefined in all three themes, so each fell
through to `UIManager`'s blank default -- black on white, on a dark window. Plus a real
right-click menu: `Component.addContextMenuListener` has fired for years and nothing ever
opened one.

**Dialogs.** `defaultNativeWindowModeBool` on the three themes, so a dialog opens as a real
operating system window. Anchored popups never do.

**Keyboard.** Tab and Shift-Tab move focus; Escape cancels. The traversal machinery is old and
could not be wired to Tab as it stood: its filter is opt-in, `preferredTabIndex` defaults to
-1 and `TextArea` is the only class in the framework that opts in, so Tab would have walked
between a form's text fields and skipped every button between them. The desktop order is its
own, filtered on focusability. Escape resolves through one `Dialog.cancel()` that the window
close control and the back gesture already meant separately.

**`desktopTitleBarMode` gained a reader.** The three themes have carried the constant since
they landed and nothing read it.

**Three new components.** `Separator`, `GroupBox`, `Stepper` -- every desktop toolkit has all
three and Codename One had none.

**The flip.** Windows -> Fluent, Linux -> Adwaita, macOS -> Aqua. Java SE stays on legacy
deliberately: that default reaches every desktop application ever built rather than only ours.

**Fidelity: 9 scored controls to 22.** Everything that makes a window look like a desktop
window was unmeasured, including the interactive scrollbar. Three rows are not scored on every
platform, and that is the honest answer rather than a gap -- an `NSScroller` renders nothing
through `cacheDisplay` (measured: correct `usableParts`, correct frame, `isHidden=false`, one
colour in the tile, tried detached and inside a real `NSScrollView` in both styles), `NSMenu`
belongs to the window server, and the AppKit and GTK tooltips are separate windows.

## What is still open

- **Goldens.** The 13 new fidelity rows have none, and the theme flip invalidates the desktop
  screenshot baselines. Both are captured from the runners that score them, never locally, so
  those legs are red until the capture workflows have run and their output has been reviewed.
- **The Windows and GNOME reference apps** are written but have never been compiled -- neither
  toolchain exists on the machine this was written on. CI is the first verifier.
- **Native menu bars on Windows and Linux.** Neither port implements `setNativeCommands`, so
  their commands stay in the now-properly-themed Toolbar, and `isDesktopHideToolbar()` will not
  hide the only place they are drawn. Tracked in `COVERAGE.md`.

control-characters, copyright, build-hint-catalog and the four fidelity gates clean. Vale and
LanguageTool clean on both guide chapters.

title: Fix iOS browser peer hardware keyboard input
body:
Hardware keyboards still could not type into HTML inputs inside `BrowserComponent` after the earlier TextField fix. WebKit owns its editor and never sets `editingComponent`, so the iOS controller continued consuming those presses before UIKit could insert text.

Detect focused native `UIKeyInput` views in the current window and forward their presses to UIKit. Apply the same guard to Catalyst secondary windows, preserving the existing press ownership rules for releases and cancellations across focus changes.

Adds a browser typing step before native TextField editing in the input-validation suite, plus routing checks for nested peers, separate windows, mixed releases, cancellation, and editor startup. The driver now prefers the current app transcript for assertions so earlier test runs cannot contaminate the result.

Validation:

- iPhone 17 Pro simulator, iOS 26.3, hardware events generated with `XCUIApplication.typeKey`: the old guard times out on browser typing while CN1 TextField typing passes; the fix passes all five steps (tap, drag, long-press, browser typing, CN1 typing).
- `python3 scripts/ios/keyboard-peer-tests/check.py`: both controller paths pass. Removing the peer guard makes the regression check fail.
- iOS simulator app build and Catalyst-target Objective-C syntax check pass.
- Shell syntax and `git diff --check` pass.

Physical iPad/Magic Keyboard hardware has not been tested.

Fixes #5740.

title: ParparVM: make the translator self-hosting, and fix what that exposed
body:
Rationale is in the commit message and in code comments; this body is a pointer only.

**What this is.** ByteCodeTranslator now translates itself, and
`.github/workflows/parparvm-selfhost.yml` compares the C it emits against the C
the JVM-hosted translator emits from the same inputs. A 37.6k-line real program
becomes a VM conformance test whose expected value costs nothing to maintain.
Nightly, `workflow_dispatch`, and opt-in on a PR via the `selfhost` label -- a
full run builds the translator twice and translates the corpus several times, so
it does not belong on every PR.

**A real VM bug fell out of it.** Every generated `__STATIC_INITIALIZER_X` was
broken double-checked locking -- `__X_LOADED__` plain-loaded and plain-stored
outside the monitor, and `class__X.initialized` read the same way by inline
guards that skip the initialiser and so never take the monitor. On arm64 a
second thread can see the flag set while the vtable and `classToInterfaceMap`
rows are still invisible. Observed as three identical SIGSEGVs at
`classToInterfaceMap_java_util_NavigableMap[classId] + 0x8` from `TreeSet.clear`.
Acquire/release on both flags across all 391 classes; interface maps `calloc`'d.

**Measured** (5782-class corpus, min of 3 interleaved reps, `phys_footprint`):
62.8s -> 27.4s wall, kernel time 33.4s -> 9.9s. Class-init checks 7.21% -> 0.12%
of mutator self-time; iteration path 25.5% -> 12.4%; `checkConcurrentMod`
2.69% -> 0.00%; `char[]` 1530MB -> 837MB.

**Verified.** Gate D, Gate A and the negative control pass byte-identical on the
797-file corpus. `vm/tests` green. `check-cast-semantics` and
`check-native-signatures` clean. GC heap verifier clean over ~1e9 references.

**Known, not fixed.** A rare (~1/14) crash remains in interface dispatch -- a bad
class id reaching a registered-row lookup. The `calloc` above makes it a clean
NULL-row fault instead of silent garbage. It predates this branch as far as the
evidence goes, and it is not reproducible under a debugger.

**Deliberately not here.** Lowering for-each to an indexed loop in the
translator. The remaining iterator cost is two interface dispatches per element,
each a four-load pointer chase; removing those means not making the calls, which
is a control-flow rewrite and belongs in its own change.

**Not rebased on #5741.** Both touch `cn1_globals.m` GC policy in different
functions (that PR trims the SATB log's retained buffers; this one bounds
run-ahead in `cn1BibopPacingCap`).

title: Fix archetype and Initializr launchers and ship bounded build login
body:
Projects generated through the Maven archetype or Initializr could fail before submission when launched outside their folder, with a spaced Maven cache, or with an apostrophe in the Windows project path. Fix both the archetype launchers and Initializr's independently embedded `common.zip`: anchor the working directory, quote the wrapper command, pass paths to PowerShell as data, clear Maven-distribution credentials before launching Maven, preserve failure exit codes, and repair the Windows aliases/settings goal. Preserve local defaults and explain the explicit `javascript_cloud` submission command.

Initializr also discarded executable modes while assembling its final download. Retain ZipSupport's archive writer and add Unix file attributes to its central directory so `build.sh`, `run.sh`, and `mvnw` extract executable. Update the generated README with Java-version-specific setup, Windows commands, and Eclipse launch imports. A parity guard and `scripts/sync-initializr-launchers.py --write` keep the embedded launchers aligned with the archetype.

Refresh `maven/CodeNameOneBuildClient.jar` from the successful CI build of merged codenameone/BuildClient#5, commit `e68f5cd1350dae2a57037fa0eadd2af8dffe320f` (run 34740172519). SHA-256: `2f29d516620e452fe5a16209b1185f1b5f1cba67432b7f93d9137f54969783bf`. This ships the bounded login and cancellation repair through the existing Maven build-client distribution path.

Validation: archetype packaging and smoke CI passed; the shipped JAR passes all five login regressions. Local tests generate actual Initializr ZIPs across all four IDEs and both Java 8/17 selections, verify CRCs/modes/README, extract normally without chmod, and run the real launchers/wrapper with a Maven recorder from spaced/apostrophe paths, including failure exit codes. The Windows recorder also rejects inherited `MVNW_USERNAME` or `MVNW_PASSWORD`, using synthetic test credentials. The native Windows/Linux CI matrix passed this real-generation test as well as the archetype test. Embedded Maven coordinates, repository declarations, and settings parity pass. Website CI builds Initializr from these sources; generated website artifacts are not committed. The ZIP permissions pass adds one in-memory archive buffer; full browser generation performance is not measured here.

Companion codenameone/BuildCloud#146 repairs the separately vendored onboarding starter and shipped console; codenameone/BuildDaemon#217 repairs the native Linux worker. Merge and normal framework/website releases are required to reach users.

title: Fix native Linux starter linking with optional WebKit
body:
A normal native Linux starter now reaches the final link but fails with `undefined symbol: webkit_web_view_get_type`. `WEBKIT_WEB_VIEW()` expands to a direct WebKit type lookup, bypassing the port's existing dlopen/dlsym implementation.

Use a typed cast for the view already created by `webkit_web_view_new_with_user_content_manager`. This preserves optional WebKit support and removes the three unintended link references in HTML loading, URL navigation, and JavaScript execution.

Add a focused x64/ARM64 CI check that compiles the real browser source against actual GTK/WebKit headers in debug and release configurations, then rejects any unresolved WebKit or JavaScriptCore symbols before dead stripping can hide them. Only generated VM primitive declarations are stubbed.

Validation: shell syntax and diff checks passed. Focused browser compilation and unresolved-symbol checks passed in both debug and release on x64 and ARM64 (workflow run 34755540187). The broader existing Linux native suite is still running. After merge, rebuild/release and deploy BuildDaemon so its embedded nativelinux.jar includes the corrected source. No archetype changes; its publication remains deferred to 7.0.272.

title: fix(YouTube): Decouple flyout buttons and shared hooks from unrelated patches
body:
Flyout menu buttons now show only when the patch that owns them is included, so "Add to Morphe queue" no longer appears without the `Add to queue` patch.

The AiSList filter and its "Report AI channel" button moved out of `Hide layout components` into a standalone `AI channel filter` patch, so a `flyoutPatch` failure can no longer break the hide options.

Shared hooks were moved out of named patches into hidden ones, so including a patch no longer force-enables an unrelated one:

- `DeArrow` no longer pulls in `Restore original titles`. The title hooks now live in a shared patch.
- `Picture-in-picture button` no longer pulls in `Player icon style`. Icon styles are still added when that patch is included.

title: fix(YouTube Music - Third-party lyrics): Validate lyric candidates and display results promptly
body:
### Description

Fix incorrect lyric selection for Chinese metadata and avoid withholding an already usable result while waiting for word timing.

- Normalize Traditional/Simplified Chinese and the common title variant 妳/你 before comparing candidate metadata.
- Apply the existing high-match gate **before** a provider adapter can replace candidate metadata with query metadata. A same-artist, same-duration result with an unrelated title remains ineligible. Preserve that rejection when adding the synchronization score, and exclude low-match results from fallback/candidate queues.
- Publish a validated line-synced/plain result as soon as it arrives while continuing the word-timing search. Ordinary refetches use the same incremental path; a search with explicitly edited terms still waits for all stages.
- Cancel registered provider work on track/query changes, stop stale stage polling/submission, and prevent interrupted providers from opening subsequent HTTP requests. An in-progress blocking HTTP operation may still finish at its configured timeout.
- Preserve the existing view during a refetch, avoid rebuilding identical results, and stop resetting the playback position when duplicate metadata arrives.

For example, querying 王傑 / 幾分傷心幾分痴 at 257 seconds previously favored 一场游戏一场梦 from the same artist at 257 seconds over the actual title at about 251 seconds. The rejected candidate must not be rescued by duration, synchronization rank, or the fallback queue.

### Additional context

Rebased the four existing commits onto `ab122326bfe9502762321673d78cd61a6211a5ca` (`v1.46.0-dev.7`). `git range-diff` confirms that all four commits retain the same changes. The provider list is unchanged; the source diff contains only `LyricsManager`, `LyricsRequests`, and `LyricsPanelView`.

The native action-button issue in #3077 remains separate from this source PR. The test APK also contains a **local, version-specific 9.40.51 native-panel adapter** for full-screen entry, gesture dismissal, and button availability. That adapter is not included in this PR; the UI checks below describe the installed test APK and must not be interpreted as fixes supplied by this source diff. Its obfuscated controller hooks have only been tested on 9.40.51 / Android 16.

### Test results

Physical device: OnePlus Ace6, Android 16. Latest checks completed on 2026-10-06 using YouTube Music **9.40.51**, an upstream-supported experimental version, and patches **1.46.0-dev.7**.

- Compiled the changed production Java classes against the latest installed extension API, converted with D8, and installed with the existing application signature. No compile stubs were packaged. The installed APK, local delivery APK, and phone Download copy have matching SHA-256 hashes.
- On 9.40.51, checked 新长征路上的摇滚, 今天妳要嫁给我, 幾分傷心幾分痴, and 十年（国）: lyrics content, immediate full-screen entry, edge-gesture dismissal, and system Back. Also checked long-press search and playback highlighting after seeking.
- Added four video samples, explicitly confirming that the player was in **video mode**, rather than its audio-only counterpart:

| Video | Video ID | Type | Installed-APK result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 陳淑樺 — 滾滾紅塵 | `qVm3GdOd2P8` | Official MV | Nonempty lyrics, full screen, left/right Back gestures |
| 那英 — 春暖花开 (2013 CCTV Spring Festival Gala) | `UP5CvZlNOKI` | Live performance | Nonempty lyrics, full screen, left/right Back gestures |
| 周杰伦 — 青花瓷 | `Z8Mqw0b9ADs` | Official MV | Nonempty lyrics, full screen, left/right Back gestures |
| Taylor Swift — Blank Space | `e-ORhEE9VVg` | Official MV | Nonempty lyrics, full screen, left/right Back gestures |

- After **each** video sample, switched to the exact negative reproduction, 邓丽君：梅花、中华民国颂 (`eUZhgWZV2JQ`). The lyrics button stayed disabled and tapping it did not open an empty panel. This also checks that the previous song's available state is cleared. The earlier delayed check on this negative sample passed as well.
- All four video lyric panels retained the refetch control. No `MorpheLyricsAccess` or `AndroidRuntime` errors appeared in the collected device log.
- Earlier 9.15.51 device checks covered 16 tracks: all nine tracks on Cui Jian's 新长征路上的摇滚 album, 今天妳要嫁给我, the two distinct Wang Jie titles and an alternate title containing both, 十年 / 明年今日, and 屋頂. A network refetch of 今天妳要嫁给我 took about 0.6 seconds; cache hits took tens of milliseconds. These are device observations, not a controlled benchmark or latency guarantee.
- `git diff --check` passed after rebasing. The [rebased head's Build pull request workflow](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-patches/actions/runs/37341994611) passed for `8ba048ff5d3a8062b126177f1199cd73fa18bc78`, including `./gradlew :patches:buildAndroid --no-daemon` and artifact upload.
- Physical-device validation covers 9.15.51 and experimental 9.40.51. Stable 9.20.53 and the remaining supported versions still need device testing before merge.

title: fix(YouTube): Fix Theme splash screen and Hide layout components startup crash on 21.40
body: ### Description Resolves both remaining TODO items on `feat/yt_21.40` (#3457): 1. **Theme splash screen (`ShowSplashScreenFingerprint`)**: - In 21.40, the branch logic in `MainActivity.onCreate` was inverted from `if-eqz` + `goto` to `if-nez` without `goto`. - Updated opcode pattern in `Fingerprints.kt` to match both branch directions and allow up to one intervening instruction before the constant. 2. **Hide layout components startup crash (`VerifyError: register v0 has type Reference: vuw but expected Float`)**: - In 21.40, instruction reordering placed `applyDimensionIndex - 1` immediately before `move-result v0`, separating the `invoke-interface` call to `co:()F` from its result assignment and passing an uninitialized reference register into `modifyFeedSubtitleSpan`. - Adjusted hook insertion index in `HideLayoutComponentsPatch.kt` from `applyDimensionIndex - 1` to `applyDimensionIndex`. 3. **Target versions**: - Added experimental support for `21.40.160` and `21.40.161` in `Constants.kt`. ### Additional context Builds on top of #3457 (`feat/yt_21.40`). ### Test results - [ ] Tested on both the **minimum** and **maximum** supported versions - [x] Tested on **experimental** supported versions (Optional) Tested on YouTube `21.40.160` and `21.40.161`: - All 91 patches applied with 0 errors. - Runtime verified on Android 16 (Pixel 10 Pro XL): clean startup, feed rendering, Morphe settings, and Hide layout components verified working without crashes.

title: fix(YouTube - Hide layout components): Hide the chapter title next to the timestamp
body:
### Description

Fixes `Hide Chapters and 'In this video' button` not hiding the chapter title shown next to the timestamp on some app versions.

The setting only hid the `time_bar_entry_point_tap_container` view. On YouTube 20.21.37 that view is not the chapter title: the title is its own `time_bar_chapter_title` text view, with the `time_bar_chapter_title_container` chip around it, so the setting did nothing there. The same method that binds the entry point view also binds the title, so the title view and its chip are now hidden under the same setting. The hook is skipped when a version has no such method.

Closes #3359

### Test results

Redmi Note 9S (Android 10), YouTube 20.21.37, `Hide Chapters and 'In this video' button` on, restarted, 3Blue1Brown "But what is a neural network?" (has chapters), player controls shown:

* Before (`dev`): `0:15 / 18:40 • Introduction example >` under the video.
* After: `0:17 / 18:40` only. Pause, next and the chapter segments of the seekbar are unchanged.

Patched 20.21.37, 21.16.256 and 21.39.522 successfully (`Skip silence` already fails on 20.21.37 and is not touched). I did not check the chapter title on 21.16 or 21.39 on the device.

title: fix(YouTube & YT Music - GmsCore support): Fix notification registration for patched apps
body: ### Issue: Google Notification Platform expects the original Google package name in the registration request. Context.getPackageName() supplies Morphe's renamed package instead, causing HTTP 400. #### Companion PR: https://github.com/MorpheApp/MicroG-RE/pull/293 ### description The registration code [reads the package name through `Context.getPackageName()`](https://github.com/zappybiby/morphe-patches/blob/7354168f5827139d72c7178814c3bddb5bbbb76e/patches/src/main/kotlin/app/morphe/patches/shared/misc/gms/Fingerprints.kt#L11-L23). Because Morphe renames the installed app, YouTube sends `app.morphe.android.youtube` to `notifications-pa.googleapis.com/v1/multiloginupdate`, where Google expects `com.google.android.youtube`. Google rejects that registration with HTTP 400. This fix replaces the result of that lookup with `com.google.android.youtube` for YouTube or `com.google.android.apps.youtube.music` for YT Music. ### Test results Tested on MicroG RE 7.2.1-dev.5, Morphe Patches 1.45.0. I used Frida to change only the package name YouTube 21.16.256 put into its GNP registration request, while leaving MicroG RE unmodified. I captured Google’s response in three runs: Morphe’s package name returned HTTP 400, substituting the original Google package returned HTTP 200, and removing the substitution restored HTTP 400. Specifically: 1. Hooked the method that builds the registration data. 2. Changed Context.getPackageName() to return com.google.android.youtube only for that method’s package lookup. 3. Inspected the outgoing request to notifications-pa.googleapis.com/v1/multiloginupdate. 4. Hooked YouTube’s HTTP-response handling to record Google’s actual response: 200 with the substitution, 400 without it. ### companion PR / what is also needed to fix notifications besides this Cloud notifications appear to work with this fix alone for older YT versions (I do not have a specific version range as the testing for real cloud notifications is very time-consuming, but for instance this works as a standalone fix for 21.16.256) With API-key authentication, used by older versions such as 21.16.256, YouTube adds an X-Goog-Api-Key header. It does not ask MicroG for a Spatula header on that path, so MicroG’s Spatula fallback does not block registration. Google can still reject this request because its body contains Morphe’s package name. Correcting that name through this fix was enough to obtain HTTP 200 and restore notifications. With newer versions now requiring Spatula authentication, such as version 21.39.522, YouTube asks MicroG for an X-Goog-Spatula header before completing the request. MicroG normally constructs it using a device key. When that key is unavailable, MicroG builds an alternative using the package identity, certificate digest, and saved check-in Android ID. But in the current implementation, that returns null instead of a completed header. As a result, YouTube reports error 3006 (AUTH_APP_CERT_ERROR). Correcting the package name cannot supply that missing header, so this also needs the MicroG fix. With both fixes implemented, push notifications are now working. #### Related to / (Hopefully!) Closes: https://github.com/MorpheApp/MicroG-RE/issues/17

title: fix(YouTube Music - Hide buttons): Only hide the notification button with Hide Notification button
body:
### Description

Fixes `Hide Notification button` also hiding other buttons in the top bar, such as the Samples and Share buttons on an artist page.

All top bar buttons of a page are built by the same class, and the patch hid the parent of every `top_bar_menu_item_image_view` it created. Only the notification button is created with a notification count key: the page builder passes that key (an `Optional` constructor argument, empty for the other buttons) only for the notification button renderer. The hook now also passes the `Optional` that the class keeps in a field, and the extension hides the button only when it is present. The extension reads it by reflection because the app uses the desugared `j$.util.Optional`.

Closes #3382

### Test results

Redmi Note 9S (Android 10), YouTube Music 9.38.51, `Hide Notification button` on, app restarted, artist page of Taylor Swift:

* Before (`dev`): the Samples and Share buttons are missing; the top bar has no `top_bar_menu_item_image_view` at all.
* After: the Samples and Share buttons are shown. On the Home tab the Activity feed (notification) button is hidden.

Patched 9.15.51 and 9.38.51 successfully for this patch. On 9.15.51 the patch run needs `--continue-on-error` only because `Skip silence` already fails there, which this change does not touch.

title: fix(YouTube - SponsorBlock): Segments may not load for some versions
body:
### Description

On YouTube 21.16.256, SponsorBlock never gets the video ID of a regular video, so no segments are requested and nothing is skipped (#3305). The log only shows `SegmentPlaybackController: Initialized SponsorBlock` and never `New video ID`.

SponsorBlock gets the video ID only from `hookBackgroundPlayVideoId` (`VideoIdBackgroundPlayFingerprint`, `imk.k(fid)` on 21.16), and that method is not reached for normal playback on 21.16. `VideoInformation` already uses both `hookVideoId` and `hookBackgroundPlayVideoId`, so its video ID is still updated there.

This PR also hooks `SegmentPlaybackController.setCurrentVideoId` with `hookVideoId`. Where both hooks run, the second call is ignored (`setCurrentVideoId` returns early for the same video ID). Shorts coming from `hookVideoId` are ignored by the existing `isShortsOpen()` check.

Closes #3305

### Additional context

On 21.16, a regular video opened from a link while the Shorts tab is open is still ignored as a Short (`isShortsOpen()` is true at that moment). That is the existing check and not changed here. Opening a video from the Home feed after watching Shorts works.

### Test results

Redmi Note 9S (Android 10), signed in, default SponsorBlock settings. Linus Tech Tips `1gxnANAbLuE` opened at 0:40 (sponsor segment 44.4 to 64.9 s):

* 21.16.256, current `dev`: no `New video ID` log, no segments requested, playback runs through the sponsor segment.
* 21.16.256, this PR: `New video ID: 1gxnANAbLuE`, segments downloaded, the sponsor segment is skipped.
* 21.16.256, this PR, Shorts tab: `Ignoring Short` for each Short, then a video opened from Home loads its segments.
* 21.39.522, this PR: segments load and the sponsor segment is skipped, as before.

Patched 20.21.37, 21.16.256, 21.38.123 and 21.39.522 successfully.

title: Fix out-of-bounds native read in ShadowNativeImageDecoder.createFromAsset.
body:
Fix out-of-bounds native read in ShadowNativeImageDecoder.createFromAsset.

`ShadowNativeImageDecoder.createFromAsset` copies the asset into a direct `ByteBuffer` with a `while
((bytesRead = ais.read(buf)) != -1)` loop and then calls `ImageDecoder.nCreate(buffer, 0, bytesRead,
...)`. When the loop exits, `bytesRead` is always -1, so the native decoder was always told that the
data ends at -1.

On the native side (`ImageDecoder_nCreateByteBuffer` -> `CreateByteBufferStreamAdaptor` in
`libs/hwui/jni/ByteBufferStreamAdaptor.cpp`), `limit` is converted to `size_t`, so the stream length
becomes `SIZE_MAX`. For direct buffers the buffer address is wrapped in an `SkMemoryStream` of that
length, and Skia codecs that read ahead in fixed-size chunks keep `memmove`-ing bytes past the end
of the allocation. Whether this crashes depends on what memory follows the buffer, so affected tests
fail intermittently: when the next page is protected, the JVM dies with `SIGSEGV (SEGV_ACCERR)` in
`__memmove_avx_unaligned_erms` under `ImageDecoder.nCreate`. Otherwise the decoder silently reads
garbage past the end of the image.

Pass `buffer.position()`, the number of bytes actually copied, as the limit. This affects SDK levels
R and above that decode bitmap drawables from assets or resources with native graphics enabled.

title: Fix NoClassDefFoundError for some shadows on older SDKs
body:
Fixes #11520

### Overview

See the attached issue for explanation of the issue.

I think most occurrences of this issue are actually hidden by the fact that Gradle also puts the compile SDK on the test classpath, so even if a test is running on an older runtime SDK, Java finds the class definition in the compile `android.jar` instead of from the runtime-specific `android-all` jar. I think you would only encounter this if using an older compile SDK.

### Proposed Changes

Use `Object` with the `@ClassName` hint for the new SDK 36 classes following the pattern used in many other shadows.

I validated this against our internal tests which use compile SDK 34.

______

Something interesting, while setting up a regression test for this, I found there are ~70 violations of this kind ( shadow public signature using type only present in newer SDK where its classload would fail). I'm not sure it's worth fixing the problem more generally since I'm not sure how many users are actually affected.

title: Add opt-in fix for stale screenshots on SDK 37.
body:
Add opt-in fix for stale screenshots on SDK 37.

This is a manual fork of #11393.

Robolectric shadows intercept Android Java framework code to use a fixed SystemClock.

This causes mismatch with native graphics code, which uses real system time.

This can cause frame drops and log spam when performing the real native graphics drawing
traverals enabled in SDK 37. These frame drops can then lead to stale or out of date
screenshot captures.

Commit 7bf3c4a partially addressed this by translating
FrameInfo timestamps in HardwareRenderer.syncAndDrawFrame between Robolectric's fixed SystemClock
uptime and the real clock.

However, this commit explicitly skipped adjusting FrameInfo.VSYNC, because doing so caused
existing screenshot tests to fail.

On deeper investigation these screenshot failures actually exposed the incorrect frame dropping
behavior.

This commit addresses the issues by including FrameInfo.VSYNC in this list of indices to adjust.

This behavior is currently opt-in, and can be turned on with
by setting the system property robolectric.enableFrameInfoVsyncOffsetFix=true.

title: Fix jank log spam on SDK 37+ by translating FrameInfo timestamps.
body:
Fix jank log spam on SDK 37+ by translating FrameInfo timestamps.

In SDK 37+, real draw traversals are enabled by default, causing the native
renderer to run and JankTracker to calculate frame durations. However, the
input timestamps in FrameInfo (like IntendedVsync) were in Robolectric's
simulated clock domain, while native completion timestamps were in the host's
real monotonic clock domain. This mismatch resulted in massive calculated frame
durations (e.g., hours/days), spamming the logs with warnings from JankTracker.

This change shadows syncAndDrawFrame(FrameInfo) in
ShadowNativeHardwareRenderer to translate Java-populated timestamps to the host
clock domain before calling native, and translate them (plus native-populated
timestamps) back to Robolectric's clock domain after native execution.

We explicitly exclude Vsync (index 3) from the adjustment to avoid visual
regressions in screenshot tests (e.g., HyphenationScreenshotTest), which
were observed when Vsync was adjusted to large host times.

title: Fix `NoSuchFileException` spam in unit tests logs
body:
When running the unit tests, we often get spammed by stacktraces similar to:
```
java.nio.file.NoSuchFileException: /tmp/robolectric-temp_dir4809833000115193958
    at java.base/sun.nio.fs.UnixException.translateToIOException(UnixException.java:92)
    at java.base/sun.nio.fs.UnixException.rethrowAsIOException(UnixException.java:106)
    at java.base/sun.nio.fs.UnixException.rethrowAsIOException(UnixException.java:111)
    at java.base/sun.nio.fs.UnixFileAttributeViews$Basic.readAttributes(UnixFileAttributeViews.java:55)
    at java.base/sun.nio.fs.UnixFileSystemProvider.readAttributes(UnixFileSystemProvider.java:171)
    at java.base/sun.nio.fs.LinuxFileSystemProvider.readAttributes(LinuxFileSystemProvider.java:99)
    at java.base/java.nio.file.Files.readAttributes(Files.java:1854)
    at java.base/java.nio.file.FileTreeWalker.getAttributes(FileTreeWalker.java:220)
    at java.base/java.nio.file.FileTreeWalker.visit(FileTreeWalker.java:277)
    at java.base/java.nio.file.FileTreeWalker.walk(FileTreeWalker.java:323)
    at java.base/java.nio.file.Files.walkFileTree(Files.java:2792)
    at java.base/java.nio.file.Files.walkFileTree(Files.java:2870)
    at org.robolectric.util.TempDirectory.clearDirectory(TempDirectory.java:158)
    at org.robolectric.util.TempDirectory.destroy(TempDirectory.java:141)
    at java.base/java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.runWorker(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:1144)
    at java.base/java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor$Worker.run(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:642)
    at java.base/java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:1583)
```

It seems that sometimes the temp directory does not exist, so `Files.walkFileTree` throws an exception.
This adds a safety check to ensure that we only call `Files.walkFileTree` when the temp directory exists.

To check this, you can look at the logs of the various `Tests / unit-tests (*)` checks, and make sure that you don't have any stacktrace similar to the one above.

title: Remove Conscrypt's XDH KeyPairGenerator to fix TLS issues
body:
Remove Conscrypt's XDH KeyPairGenerator to fix TLS issues

Conscrypt's implementation of KeyPairGenerator.XDH cannot be initialized with a
NamedParameterSpec, which can cause issues with TLS handshakes in the JVM. This
change removes the KeyPairGenerator.XDH service from the Conscrypt provider
when Robolectric installs it, allowing the JDK's provider to handle XDH key
generation. This is compatible with Conscrypt's other crypto services. A
regression test is added to verify that XDH key generation and agreement work
correctly.

Fixes #11345
